## 1. Reading this reference

This reference complements the narrative report with exact source declarations, type responsibilities, project dependencies and the complete CLI help contract. Source links are pinned to the inspected commit and declaration line where possible. The two fault-related files modified before this task retain working-tree links because a commit link cannot show their uncommitted additions.

**Evidence scope:** catalogue entries establish source presence and declared contracts. They are not a claim that every member was executed, independently validated or checked with a semantic API compatibility analyser. The catalogue is a lexical declaration index: nested public members of internal/private containing types remain internal implementation detail, interface members can omit the `public` keyword, and partial types span multiple files. Follow the source for complete bodies, generic constraints, attributes and accessibility context. Short XML responsibility descriptions below are repository-authored documentation, interpreted alongside the implementation traces in the main report; old roadmap language in those comments is not a current capability guarantee.

The source corpus contains 563 C# files / 152,958 lines at inventory, excluding generated/build directories. Exact methods and constructors appear in file-local C# declaration blocks. They are signatures or declaration excerpts, not runnable replacement classes. Positional record parameters carry their original defaults. Fields/properties are included so option defaults and result structures can be inspected. Inline expression bodies are reduced to signatures where possible. No public stability guarantee is inferred from a declaration being public.

### 1.1 Principal API contracts and usage rules

| Contract | Meaning | Ownership / caution |
|---|---|---|
| `IPowerFlowSolver.Solve(GridModel, PowerFlowOptions?)` | Produces a typed power-flow result | Check convergence and status before downstream calculations. |
| `SteadyStateSolver.Solve(GridModel, PowerFlowOptions?, int)` | Adds bounded tap/control regulation | Retain `RegulatedModel`; electrical convergence and tap settlement differ. One instance per active worker. |
| `ILinearSolver.SolveInPlace(double[,], double[])` | Dense real solve, overwriting RHS with solution | Matrix can also be overwritten; copy for non-mutating use. |
| `ISparseLinearSolver.Solve(CsrMatrix, double[])` | Sparse solve returning vector or null | Null means failure; follow the caller's fallback contract. |
| `IComplexLinearSolver` / factorisation | Complex network solves and repeated RHS | Observe factorisation lifetime and fallback semantics. |
| `WlsStateEstimator.Estimate(GridModel, MeasurementSet, EstimationOptions?)` | Static nonlinear estimation | Check observability, status, method-appropriate statistical fields and size limits. |
| `FrequencyDynamics.Simulate(double, double, IEnumerable<FrequencyEvent>, DynamicsConfig?)` | Reduced frequency trajectory | Inertia is MW.s, demand MW, time seconds; defaults are assumptions. |
| `QstsEngine.Run(GridModel, QstsStudy, CancellationToken)` | Stateful profile/control study | Completion, control settlement and engineering violations are separate dimensions. |
| `HostingCapacity.Run(...)` | Capacity search over snapshot or QSTS studies | Read both capacity bounds and limiting constraints; maximum tested is not infinite capacity. |
| `ReplayValidator.Validate(...)` | Compares no-device baseline with recorded evidence | Only `Reproduced` unlocks the main scenario engine. |
| `IAssetDynamics` and derived interfaces | Per-asset active/passive controllers | Preserve sampling/actuation timestep, units and provenance. |
| `IStorageDispatchPolicy` | Chooses requested battery power | Delivered power is constrained by storage physics. |
| Protocol, relay, physics and audit registries/seams | Composition of supported behaviours | A registry does not imply runtime assembly/plugin discovery. |

For mathematical explanation and worked source-checked examples, see comprehensive report sections 3.3-3.15. Every contract is linked through its declaration below.

## 3. Repository and project inventory

### 3.1 Repository areas

| Area | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `src/` | Numerical library, CLI, ingestion/GPU libraries, shared UI and application heads. |
| `tests/` | Core/integration/CLI/UI test suites and fixtures. |
| `tools/` | Smoke tools, benchmark scripts, cross-validation sidecars, documentation/build utilities. |
| `data/` | Bundled/reference/sample cases and other content; not permission to publish private inferred data. |
| `schemas/` | V1/v2 schemas and kind specifications. |
| `docs/` | Manuals, technical chapters, validation reports and captures; Public submodules not recursively investigated. |
| `python/` | Executable/result wrapper integration. |
| `unity/` | Export-data visualisation consumer. |
| `.github/workflows/` | CI, analysis, release, packaging and documentation automation. |
| Root files | Solution, SDK/build policy, version/changelog, licensing, notices and contributor documentation. |

## 4. Core and CLI source catalogue

### 4.0 Worked API integrations

These examples are checked against source signatures but were not compiled as separate host applications. They use synthetic/reference data and do not bypass the historical-data boundary.

**Frequency excursion:** inertia is MW.s; the event changes net power in MW. The returned finite-window metrics describe the chosen reduced model.

```csharp
using GridSim.Core.Dynamics;

FrequencyResponse response = FrequencyDynamics.Simulate(
    systemInertiaMwS: 200_000,
    baseDemandMw: 30_000,
    events: new[] { new FrequencyEvent(AtSeconds: 1.0, DeltaPMw: -1_000) },
    config: new DynamicsConfig { NominalHz = 50, StepSeconds = 0.02, DurationSeconds = 30 });
Console.WriteLine(response.NadirHz);
```

[Implementation](../../src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/FrequencyDynamics.cs).

**Estimation from a controlled synthetic experiment:** solve the reference network, sample observations, then estimate. This is an internal consistency experiment, not independent validation.

```csharp
using GridSim.Core.Estimation;
using GridSim.Core.IO;
using GridSim.Core.PowerFlow;

var model = IeeeCases.Case14();
var truth = new SparseNewtonRaphsonPowerFlow().Solve(model);
if (!truth.Converged) throw new InvalidOperationException("Reference solve failed.");
MeasurementSet observations = SyntheticMeasurements.Sample(model, truth,
    new SyntheticMeasurementOptions { Seed = 42, NoiseScale = 1.0 });
EstimationResult estimate = new WlsStateEstimator().Estimate(model, observations,
    new EstimationOptions { Method = EstimationMethod.Wls });
if (!estimate.Converged) throw new InvalidOperationException("Estimate failed.");
Console.WriteLine(estimate.Status);
```

[Sampler](../../src/GridSim.Core/Estimation/SyntheticMeasurements.cs), [estimator](../../src/GridSim.Core/Estimation/WlsStateEstimator.cs).

**File-backed QSTS:** compose an existing public case and a real study file. The variables `model` and `studyPath` must refer to the caller's loaded case and existing study JSON.

```csharp
// Continuation inside a host with GridSim.Core.Qsts and GridSim.Core.PowerFlow imported:
var study = GridSim.Core.Qsts.QstsFile.Load(studyPath, model);
var qsts = new GridSim.Core.Qsts.QstsEngine(new SparseNewtonRaphsonPowerFlow());
var series = qsts.Run(model, study);
Console.WriteLine(series.Completed);
```

This is explicitly a host fragment, not a complete runnable application. [QstsFile](../../src/GridSim.Core/Qsts/QstsFile.cs), [QstsEngine](../../src/GridSim.Core/Qsts/QstsEngine.cs).

**Extension recipe:** implement the appropriate interface, test units and failure semantics against its existing CPU/reference implementation, then inject it through the corresponding constructor or registry. For example, `SparseNewtonRaphsonPowerFlow(ISparseLinearSolver?)` accepts an alternative sparse backend; `QstsEngine(IPowerFlowSolver, PowerFlowOptions?)` accepts a whole power-flow engine. Preserve canonical CPU arithmetic when claiming bit identity. A new implementation that rounds differently requires a separately declared numerical contract.


### 4.1 How to use the catalogue

Each file entry gives its namespace, source size, declared types, source documentation for those types and public/internal declaration excerpts. This provides complete primary-file coverage without implying that a raw list replaces the architectural explanation. The comprehensive report explains the significant runtime relationships, algorithm stages, state ownership and failure behaviour. Source bodies are linked for exact implementation.


### src/GridSim.Cli/CliDefaults.cs

### src/GridSim.Cli/CliExit.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Cli`. 143 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Cli/CliExit.cs).

- [`CliExit`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Cli/CliExit.cs#L22) (class): DOC-1 (October 2026, docs-session findings D-DOC-001..015, 053, 085, 130, 159): the one place that names the CLI's exit codes and maps a failure to one of them, so every verb ends with the code the CLI reference (user manual ch. 19, "Parsing rules and exit codes") documents, and never with an unhandled exception or a false exit 0. The codes, in plain words: 0: the run did what was asked and every check passed. 1: input error. A file or case folder that is missing or cannot be loaded, invalid data inside it (for example a generator whose Pmin is above its Pmax), or a requested output that cannot be written. 2: usage error. Something on the command line names nothing that exists or is not allowed: an unknown flag or verb, a bad flag value, an unknown case NAME, a bus id that is not in the case, a forward-inference rejection. 3: a verdict or convergence failure. The study ran and its answer is a failure (did not converge, not reproduced, infeasible, a preflight probe that failed). This file has no dependency on the rest of the CLI, so the test project compiles it in (see GridSim.Tests.csproj) and tests the mapping rules directly, beside the process-level tests that run the real binary.
- [`UnknownCaseException`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Cli/CliExit.cs#L74) (class): D-DOC-130: thrown by the case resolver (Program.cs LoadNamed) when an argument names no case at all. It is an `ArgumentException`, as the old exception was, so every existing handler that caught that still catches this; the handlers that report a load failure use `CliExit.CaseLoadFailure` to tell it (exit 2) apart from a missing or unloadable file (exit 1). The message is built by the resolver: it names the case and lists the built-in names.
- [`FailureTally`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Cli/CliExit.cs#L87) (class): D-DOC-011 / D-DOC-012: a tally of the failures a multi-part run met (the GPU preflight's probes, the benchmark's cases and engines), so the run can print every failure, keep going, and still end with the documented code instead of exit 0. The rule is the batch verbs' rule (manual ch. 19, nminus1-sweep and stress): any part that could not be loaded makes the run an input error (exit 1); otherwise any part that ran and failed (did not converge, threw) makes it a verdict failure (exit 3); a clean run is 0. Skipped parts (an absent GPU, a meshed case for the radial sweep) are not failures and are not recorded here.

### src/GridSim.Cli/CliFiles.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Cli`. 203 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Cli/CliFiles.cs).

- [`CliFiles`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Cli/CliFiles.cs#L32) (class): D-DOC-072 (October 2026, docs-session finding): the ONE overwrite policy of the command line, and the one helper every CLI output goes through. Before, two sites used `GridSim.Core.IO.NeverOverwrite` (refuse, write under a "-dupN" name), the convert verb refused an existing file, the shared result writer replaced, and about 37 sites in Program.cs simply opened the file and wrote over whatever was there, including, with the wrong `--out`, the very case file or measurement set the run had just read. The rule is now written down once (user manual ch. 19, "Output files") and enforced here: An output goes where it is asked to go (or under `results/` by default), and its parent folder is created when it is missing (D-DOC-176: `stability --export` and `trip --export` used to fail on a missing folder). An existing OUTPUT file is replaced. A re-run replaces its own outputs, whether default (under `results/`) or user-named (`--out`, `--export`, `--csv`, ...): naming a file is asking for it, scripts re-run with the same paths, and the shared result writer (F10) has always replaced. NEVER an input. A target is refused, before anything is written, exit 2 (a usage error: the command line names a wrong path), when it is (a) a file the command line names as an input (any existing file named by a token that is not the value of an output flag), (b) an existing file inside a case folder the command line names (a folder holding `system.json`), (c) an existing file inside the bundled `data/` folder next to the executable (the built-in cases and fixtures), or (d) an existing folder. Two deliberate exceptions keep their own, stricter rules and are documented beside the rule: the interposer's window files go through `GridSim.Core.IO.NeverOverwrite` (each window is distinct evidence, so a clash is kept under a "-dupN" name, never replaced), and the case writers (`convert` and the JSON case writer) never write over an existing case. `synth` regenerates its case folder (by default the bundled `data/gb-synthetic`) by design. This file has no dependency on the rest of the CLI, so the test project compiles it in and tests the rule directly (CliFilesTests), beside the process-level tests that run the real binary.
- [`OutputRefusedException`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Cli/CliFiles.cs#L200) (class): D-DOC-072: an output the policy refuses (`CliFiles`): it would replace an input of the run, or it names a folder. Not an `IOException`, so no "could not write" handler swallows it: it reaches the process-wide handler, which prints `error: ...` and exits 2 (a usage error) before anything is written to that path.

### src/GridSim.Cli/ConformanceAllowances.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Cli`. 82 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Cli/ConformanceAllowances.cs).

- [`ConformanceAllowances`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Cli/ConformanceAllowances.cs#L27) (class): D-DOC-039 (October 2026): the explicit, documented list of shipped corpus cases that `gridsim conformance` is allowed to find unconverged, each with its reason. Why a list. Since R220 the verb exits 3 when any case does not converge or cannot be run, so that a case which stops converging cannot vanish from the gate. But three PGLib optimal-power-flow cases in the shipped corpus never converge as power flows, so the verb exited 3 on EVERY run of the shipped corpus and the exit code told a CI job nothing. The allowance list names exactly those cases, so the shipped corpus passes (exit 0) and any NEW failure still fails: a case not on the list that does not converge, any case that cannot be loaded or run, an allowed case that fails in a different way than the list says, or a gate failure on a converged case. What an allowance covers, and what it does not. An allowance matches by the case's file stem AND by the solver status it expects (`PowerFlowStatusName`, "MaxIterations"): the same case ending "NonFinite" (a divergence to NaN) is a different failure and still fails the run. An allowance never covers a load failure or a solve that throws. An allowed case that converges is audited like any other case and a note says the allowance was not needed (a solve that improves is not a regression, so it does not fail the run). `--no-allowances` switches the list off for a run that wants every case to converge. The reasons. All three are PGLib-OPF (IEEE PES Power Grid Library, optimal power flow) benchmark files: each stores an optimisation operating point, not a power-flow start, and plain Newton-Raphson from the stored voltages with reactive limits enforced does not reach the 1e-8 pu mismatch in 100 iterations (status MaxIterations, measured on the shipped files with 1.95.195; manual ch. 30 lists the family). This is a property of the input file, not a solver regression: nothing in the list was ever converged by this verb.
- [`Allowance`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Cli/ConformanceAllowances.cs#L33) (record): One allowed unconverged case: its file stem, the status it is allowed to end with, and why.

Namespace: `GridSim.Cli`. 41 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Cli/CrashReport.cs).

- [`CrashReport`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Cli/CrashReport.cs#L15) (class): F08: the CLI's crash report for an exception nothing handled. Program.cs registers one process-wide UnhandledException handler first thing. Missing input files and unloadable cases are turned into a one-line "error:" and exit 1 there (they are input errors, not defects). Every other unhandled exception arrives here: a defect in GridSim. This writes a crash log (see `CrashLog`) and prints a short message on stderr naming the log, then returns, so the runtime still prints the full stack and ends the process with its non-zero crash code. The crash is never turned into success, and never into exit 1 (which would wrongly blame the user's input).

### src/GridSim.Cli/Gated.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Cli`. 598 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Cli/Gated.cs).

- [`Gated`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Cli/Gated.cs#L20) (class): The CLI's single licence choke point for loading user network models. Every user-facing model load in `Program.cs` goes through `Dir` or `Matpower` instead of calling the Core loaders directly, so the tier's bus limit (LICENSE.md ?2) is enforced in exactly one place. Bundled Networks (LICENSE.md ?1 - the shipped IEEE/CIGRE MATPOWER library and the synthetic/reduced GB cases) are exempt and never counted; a load is "bundled" when its path sits under the repo's `data/` tree. Built-in cases (`case9` ...) never touch these loaders and so are exempt too.
- [`BuiltInCases`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Cli/Gated.cs#L566) (class): The built-in case names that `LoadNamed` in Program.cs resolves (lower case). Kept as a set so a verb can ask "does this free token name a case?" without loading anything (trip and export use it to tell a case from a generator name or an output path). `CliInputHandlingTests` checks that this set and LoadNamed's switch agree.
- [`CaseLoadException`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Cli/Gated.cs#L582) (class): A user case that exists but cannot be loaded (bad content). An `IOException` so existing input-error handling catches it; the CLI's process-wide handler maps an uncaught one to exit 1.
- [`GateRefusedException`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Cli/Gated.cs#L595) (class): GR-190 (November 2026): the loader gate refused a case: the licence's bus limit, or an ambiguous MATPOWER case name. It used to call `Environment.Exit(2)` from inside the loader, so a batch verb could not record the case as a LOAD FAIL row and carry on: the whole batch ended. It is now thrown. Deliberately NOT an `IOException`, so the input-error handlers do not take it for a bad file. A single-case verb lets it through (its catch-alls exclude it) to the process-wide handler in Program.cs, which prints `error: <message>` and exits 2, exactly as the old exit did; a batch verb catches it per case as a LOAD FAIL row.

### src/GridSim.Cli/InterposeTransport.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Cli.Interpose`. 357 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Cli/InterposeTransport.cs).

- [`IRtuTransport`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Cli/InterposeTransport.cs#L10) (interface): A source of delimited protocol frames. Blocking reads are bounded by a timeout so the interposer's console loop stays responsive to a keypress / `--ticks` cap.
- [`InterposeAccessPolicy`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Cli/InterposeTransport.cs#L43) (record): Bug #174 (2026-11-01): who may hold the interposer's single client slot, and for how long while silent. Before, the listener served the first client from anyone, and the Modbus transport never dropped an idle one (a read timeout just looped), so any peer that connected and stayed silent held the only slot and locked the real RTU out indefinitely.
- [`TransportErrors`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Cli/InterposeTransport.cs#L63) (class): Classifies socket read failures for the TCP transports.
- [`TcpFrameTransportBase`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Cli/InterposeTransport.cs#L82) (class): The shared TCP plumbing of the frame transports: bind a listener, accept ONE client at a time, read with a timeout into a reassembly buffer, and drop the client (so the next one can connect) when it goes away. The subclasses supply only the framing rule, `TryExtract`.
- [`TcpDelimitedFrameTransport`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Cli/InterposeTransport.cs#L265) (class): A TCP frame reassembler for start-byte + length-delimited protocols (IEC 60870-5-104: start 0x68, then a one-octet APDU length, then that many octets). It binds a listener, accepts one client at a time, buffers the stream, and yields one whole frame per call. On a bad lead-in it resyncs by discarding bytes up to the next start delimiter. This is the CLI's first socket-binding verb; reads are timeout-bounded so the loop never wedges.
- [`TcpMbapFrameTransport`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Cli/InterposeTransport.cs#L315) (class): A TCP frame reassembler for Modbus TCP, whose MBAP header carries no start delimiter: the frame length is a 2-octet big-endian field at offset 4 counting the unit id + PDU, so a whole frame is 6 + that. Basic resync: if the protocol-id field (offset 2-3) is non-zero the lead-in isn't a valid MBAP header, so drop one octet.
- [`TransportFactory`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Cli/InterposeTransport.cs#L347) (class): Opens the transport a protocol needs. TCP paths exist today (IEC-104 delimited, Modbus MBAP); serial and layer-2 transports register here as their protocols land.

### src/GridSim.Cli/PythonLocator.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Cli`. 111 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Cli/PythonLocator.cs).

- [`PythonLocator`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Cli/PythonLocator.cs#L30) (class): N219 (October 2026): which Python interpreter `gridsim crossval` runs its sidecar with, in a documented order, and which one it actually used. The defect. The verb started the bare command names "python", "py" and "python3" in turn and let the operating system find them. On Windows, CreateProcess searches the folder the CLI was started from, the current folder and the Windows system folders BEFORE the PATH, and the store's "python" alias sits in a folder of its own, so the interpreter that ran was not reliably the one first on PATH: the D1 session found a system Python without pandapower chosen while a virtual environment's Scripts folder was first on PATH (the sidecar then exited 77, "pandapower absent", although the environment the user had set up had it). The verb also never said which interpreter it had used. The rule, in order (the first that applies wins): `GRIDSIM_PYTHON`, when set: that interpreter and no other. A path must exist; a bare name is looked up on PATH. When it names nothing that exists the run fails loud (no fallback: the user asked for that one). An active virtual environment, `VIRTUAL_ENV`: its own interpreter (`Scripts\python.exe` on Windows, `bin/python` elsewhere), when that file exists. The PATH, folder by folder in order: in each folder `python.exe` then `python3.exe` on Windows, `python3` then `python` elsewhere. The search is done here, so PATH order is honoured exactly. On Windows, the `py` launcher by name. Last, the bare names `python` and `python3`, as before, for a setup whose interpreter only the operating system can find (a shim script, for example). A candidate that is the Windows store alias (it exits 9009 without running) is skipped by the caller and the next one is tried. The caller prints the interpreter and where it came from on every run.
- [`Candidate`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Cli/PythonLocator.cs#L39) (record): One interpreter to try: the command (a full path, or a bare name the OS resolves) and why it is here.

- [`IBatchedLinearSolver`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Abstractions/IBatchedLinearSolver.cs#L22) (interface): Solves many independent, equally-sized dense linear systems in one call. Where `ILinearSolver` solves a single `A x = b`, this solves `count` systems `A_s x_s = b_s` (all `n x n`) as a batch - the shape a GPU wants, so a device can factor many small systems in one dispatch instead of paying the per-solve launch + global-lock overhead once per system. The motivating workload is a contingency sweep, where every outage yields a same-sized system that is otherwise solved one-at-a-time. A CPU reference implementation ships now (it just loops the dense LU); a GPU implementation drops in behind this seam. When no device is present the GPU implementation defers to the CPU loop, so this is always safe to construct and call. R071 (October 2026): the contingency sweep now batches its Newton steps (`Analysis.ContingencyAnalysis.ScreenBranchesBatched`) through the SPARSE batched seam, `IBatchedSparseLinearSolver`, because the canonical CPU Newton step is the sparse LU and a dense LU differs from it in the last bits. This dense seam reaches the sweep through `PowerFlow.DenseBatchSparseAdapter` (the GPU route, outside the CPU bit-identity contract).

### src/GridSim.Core/Abstractions/IBatchedSparseLinearSolver.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Abstractions`. 38 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Abstractions/IBatchedSparseLinearSolver.cs).

- [`IBatchedSparseLinearSolver`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Abstractions/IBatchedSparseLinearSolver.cs#L20) (interface): R071 (October 2026): solves many independent SPARSE systems `A_s x_s = b_s` in one call. This is the batched counterpart of `ISparseLinearSolver`, and it is the seam the contingency sweep's Newton steps go through when the sweep is run batched (`Analysis.ContingencyAnalysis.ScreenBranchesBatched`). Why a sparse seam next to the dense `IBatchedLinearSolver`: every CPU Newton power flow takes its step with the canonical sparse LU (`PowerFlow.CpuSparseLuSolver`; N057 routes every size sparse, and the dense engine shares the same sparse step). A dense batched LU pivots in a different order, so its solution differs from the canonical step in the last bits, and a sweep built on it could never be bit-identical to the one-at-a-time sweep. The systems in one batch also need not share a size or a sparsity pattern (each outage removes a different branch, and a Q-limit switch changes the Jacobian's size), which the dense seam cannot carry. The dense seam still reaches the sweep through `PowerFlow.DenseBatchSparseAdapter`, for a GPU backend, outside the bit-identity contract exactly as the single-system GPU solvers are.

### src/GridSim.Core/Abstractions/IComplexLinearSolver.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Abstractions`. 70 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Abstractions/IComplexLinearSolver.cs).

- [`IComplexLinearSolver`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Abstractions/IComplexLinearSolver.cs#L13) (interface): Solves a complex linear system `A x = b` where A is a sparse complex matrix (the natural shape of a harmonic admittance solve `Y(h) V(h) = I(h)`). GridSim's fundamental power flow is real (polar-form Jacobian), so no complex linear solver existed; the harmonic engine needs one, and it is built as a seam with several implementations that cross-validate: a dense direct solve (small cases / oracle), a real 2n-expansion over the tuned real sparse stack (scales to gb-full), and a native complex iterative solve.
- [`IComplexLinearFactorization`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Abstractions/IComplexLinearSolver.cs#L34) (interface): A one-off factorization of a complex matrix that can be solved against many right-hand sides (see `IComplexLinearSolver.Factor`).
- [`ReSolvingComplexFactorization`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Abstractions/IComplexLinearSolver.cs#L64) (class): Fallback factorization for solvers that don't specialise: holds the matrix and re-invokes the solver's one-shot `IComplexLinearSolver.Solve` per RHS. Correct, but with no reuse - so the default never regresses a solver that has nothing to cache (e.g. the iterative BiCGSTAB).

```csharp
public interface IComplexLinearSolver
{
    string Name { get; }

    Complex[]? Solve(ComplexCsr a, Complex[] b);

    IComplexLinearFactorization? Factor(ComplexCsr a) => new ReSolvingComplexFactorization(this, a);
}

public interface IComplexLinearFactorization
{
    Complex[]? Solve(Complex[] b);

    bool SolveInto(Complex[] b, Complex[] x)
    {
        ArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull(x);
        if (ReferenceEquals(b, x)) throw new ArgumentException("x must not be the right-hand side array.", nameof(x));
        Complex[]? r = Solve(b);
        if (r is null) return false;
        if (x.Length != r.Length)
            throw new ArgumentException($"x holds {x.Length} entries; the system has {r.Length} unknowns.", nameof(x));
        Array.Copy(r, x, r.Length);
        return true;
    }
}
```

- [`AcOpfBusResult`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Analysis/AcOpfInteriorPoint.cs#L62) (record): A bus at the optimum: voltage, and the nodal prices (the multipliers of its active and reactive power balance, in cost per MWh and cost per MVArh) and the shadow prices of its voltage limits (cost per pu per hour).
- [`AcOpfGenResult`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Analysis/AcOpfInteriorPoint.cs#L66) (record): A generator at the optimum: its output and the shadow prices of its limits (cost per MW or MVAr per hour). `Index` is its position in `GridModel.Generators`.
- [`AcOpfBranchResult`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Analysis/AcOpfInteriorPoint.cs#L72) (record): A branch at the optimum: the power entering it at each end and, for a rated branch, the shadow price of its MVA limit at each end (cost per MVA per hour; 0 when unrated or not binding). `Index` is its position in `GridModel.Branches`.
- [`AcOpfBinding`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Analysis/AcOpfInteriorPoint.cs#L78) (record): A binding constraint at the optimum: what it is, which element, and its shadow price (in the units of the matching result record).
- [`AcOpfIpmResult`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Analysis/AcOpfInteriorPoint.cs#L83) (record): The result of `AcOpfInteriorPoint.Solve`. When `Converged` is false every number is the state the iteration stopped in, not an optimum: a caller must report the failure (the CLI exits 3 and prints `Log`), never the numbers as a result.
- [`AcOpfInteriorPoint`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Analysis/AcOpfInteriorPoint.cs#L138) (class): A full AC optimal power flow, solved by a primal-dual interior point method (MATPOWER's MIPS, step for step). Unlike `AcOptimalPowerFlow` (a DC dispatch with an AC loss loop, left exactly as it was), this optimises the whole AC state at once. The problem. Variables: every bus voltage angle and magnitude and every in-service generator's active and reactive output (per unit on the system base, angles in radians). Minimise the sum of the generators' polynomial cost curves (`Generator.Cost`, MATPOWER `gencost` model 2; any order) subject to: the AC power balance at every bus (active and reactive), with constant-power loads and the bus shunts and line charging inside the admittance matrix (`YBus`); each rated branch's apparent power at both ends within `Branch.RateAMva` (MATPOWER's default flow limit, on the square of |S|; a rating of 0 means unrated); each bus voltage within its own limits (`Bus.VminPu` / `Bus.VmaxPu`, else the operational band of `VoltageLimits`); each generator within its P and Q limits (an infinite limit is no constraint); every slack bus angle fixed at its case value (the reference). Transformer taps and phase shifts are fixed at their case values; OLTCs are not moved. The method. The Newton step of the perturbed KKT conditions, with the exact analytic Jacobian and Hessian (derived below), solved by the sparse LU (`SparseLu`) on the reduced KKT system, then a fraction-to-boundary step and the barrier update gamma = sigma z'mu / niq. The starting point, the treatment of variable bounds, the convergence conditions and the failure tests are MIPS's. Every loop runs in a fixed order and every trigonometric value comes from `DetMath`, so the result is bit-identical from run to run and from CPU to CPU; there is one linear-algebra path (the sparse LU), so there is no dense/sparse seam to differ across. Refused, naming the cause (never approximated): an in-service generator with no cost curve or a piecewise-linear one, a dispatchable load (MATPOWER's Pmin below 0 with Pmax 0, which it holds at a constant power factor) (none of the repository's MATPOWER cases uses one; MATPOWER handles them with extra variables, not built here), a voltage-dependent (ZIP) load, limits that cross (Pmin above Pmax and so on), a limit that is not a number, a branch with zero impedance, a network with no slack bus, and a network in more than one island. Branch angle difference limits are not part of `GridModel` (the MATPOWER parser notes them when a file has them), so they are not enforced.
- [`Cell`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Analysis/AcOpfInteriorPoint.cs#L186) (record struct): One off-diagonal admittance cell of a bus row: the other bus and G + jB.
- [`FlowLimit`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Analysis/AcOpfInteriorPoint.cs#L190) (record struct): A rated branch's flow limit: the end buses (indices), the end's own admittance (Yaa) and the transfer admittance (Yab) for each end, and the square of the limit in pu.
- [`BoundRow`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Analysis/AcOpfInteriorPoint.cs#L195) (record struct): A bound row of h: h = Sign * (x[Var] - Limit) <= 0 (Sign +1 an upper bound, -1 a lower bound).
- [`Problem`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Analysis/AcOpfInteriorPoint.cs#L197) (class): Declared class; see the source and member declarations for its role.
- [`HessianAccumulator`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Analysis/AcOpfInteriorPoint.cs#L532) (class): Accumulates a symmetric sparse matrix as (row, col, value) triplets in a fixed order.
- [`Evaluator`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Analysis/AcOpfInteriorPoint.cs#L547) (class): The functions of the problem at a point: the objective f (scaled), the equality constraints g (power balance, then the fixed variables), the inequality constraints h (flow limits from, flow limits to, then the bound rows), their first derivatives, the gradient of the Lagrangian Lx = df + dg' lam + dh' mu, and its Hessian Lxx. Shared by the iteration and by the internal derivative check the tests run against finite differences.

The DC-OPF (`DcOptimalPowerFlow`) gives a security-constrained economic dispatch but ignores network losses; this wraps it in an outer loop that inflates the demand by the AC losses, re-dispatches, solves the AC power flow, and repeats until the losses converge - so the returned dispatch pays for its own losses and the AC power flow at it converges. Bus voltages, reactive power, generator reactive limits and AC branch loading are neither optimised nor constrained: the AC solve only measures the losses. It reuses the merit-order LP + PTDF security of the DC-OPF and Newton-Raphson for the loss measurement. A real AC-OPF with voltage and reactive limits is post-1.0 work. N173 (October 2026): when pass 0's DC dispatch is infeasible in a way the loss loop provably cannot repair (the loop only raises demand), the run stops there with `AcOpfFailure.DcDispatchInfeasible` and `AcOpfResult.StoppedAtInfeasibleFirstPass`; see the private StaysInfeasible for the proof and its limits.

Built on `Barrier`: each live lane is a participant; a lane that needs a step posts its system and signals; the barrier's post-phase action (run once, on one thread, after every live lane has signalled and before any is released) solves the whole batch; a lane that is done removes itself. The barrier's phase boundaries are full memory fences, so the posted systems and the answers are visible across threads without further locking.

- [`PvPoint`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Analysis/ContinuationPowerFlow.cs#L9) (record): One converged point of a PV curve: the load multiplier and every bus voltage magnitude (pu) there, aligned with `PvCurve.BusIds`.
- [`PvCurve`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Analysis/ContinuationPowerFlow.cs#L16) (record): The PV curves of a continuation (F18): the largest converged multiplier and every converged point.
- [`LoadabilityWalkEnd`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Analysis/ContinuationPowerFlow.cs#L35) (record): D-DOC-129 (October 2026): how the bisecting loadability walk ended. The walk steps the load multiplier up while the power flow converges and, on a failure, backs off and halves the step. It ends either because the step fell below the minimum step (the nose is then BRACKETED: it lies above the largest converged multiplier and below `LowestFailedLambda`, which is within twice the final step of it) or because the cap on solves ran out first (NOT bracketed: the largest converged multiplier is only a lower bound, and when no solve failed at all the nose was never approached). The cpf verb printed "nose bracketed" in both cases.
- [`LoadabilityGridScan`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Analysis/ContinuationPowerFlow.cs#L44) (record): The result of `ContinuationPowerFlow.ScanGrid` (R072, October 2026): max loadability on a fixed grid of load factors, by the shared loadability walk.
- [`ContinuationPowerFlow`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Analysis/ContinuationPowerFlow.cs#L61) (class): Maximum loadability by load-multiplier stepping and bisection. D-DOC-189 (October 2026): despite the class name (kept, as the API is public), this is NOT a predictor-corrector continuation power flow: there is no tangent predictor, no parameterised corrector and no tracing round the nose onto the lower branch. It scales the system load along a direction until the ordinary power flow can no longer solve - the voltage-collapse "nose" point - and reports the loadability margin. It steps the load multiplier lambda up while the solve converges and bisects the step as it crosses the nose, so the returned margin brackets the collapse point from below (the last multiplier at which a Newton power flow still converges; near the nose the Jacobian becomes singular and Newton fails slightly before the true nose, so the bracket is conservative). The margin is the headline voltage-stability number a low-inertia, high-renewable grid cares about (how much more load before collapse).
- [`IMultiplierWalk`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Analysis/ContinuationPowerFlow.cs#L189) (interface): A walk of the load multiplier: where to start, and where to go next given whether the last solve converged. Returning false ends the walk.
- [`BisectingWalk`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Analysis/ContinuationPowerFlow.cs#L205) (class): Declared class; see the source and member declarations for its role.

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Analysis`. 273 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Analysis/DcOpfCosted.cs).

- [`DcOpfCosted`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Analysis/DcOpfCosted.cs#L36) (class): The DC-OPF on a connected network with each generator's own cost curve (F19, October 2026), and the nodal prices (LMPs) and line shadow prices that come with it. Reached only through `DcOptimalPowerFlow.Solve(GridModel, DcOptimalPowerFlow.DcOpfOptions)` with `DcOptimalPowerFlow.DcOpfOptions.UseGeneratorCosts` set; the fuel-type path is untouched. Formulation. The constraints are exactly those of the linear security LP (`DcOptimalPowerFlow.BuildSecurityLp`): one balance row, and per rated line a thermal row with a slack in [0, 2 RateA]. Each generator becomes one or more LP columns at its bus: a polynomial curve: one column in [Pmin, Pmax] with the linear coefficient b as its cost (and, when a > 0, the quadratic term handled by `DcOpfQuadratic`); a piecewise-linear curve: one column per segment of [Pmin, Pmax] cut at the curve's breakpoints, each costed at its segment's slope (the first column runs from Pmin to the first breakpoint, the others from 0 to their width). Because the curve is convex the slopes rise, so an optimal LP fills the segments in order, and the unit's output is the sum of its columns (the standard LP form of a convex piecewise-linear cost). With only linear and piecewise-linear costs the LP is solved by the existing structured simplex (`DcOpfSecuritySimplex`), and its optimal-basis duals give the prices. With any quadratic term the LP of the linear parts gives a feasible vertex and `DcOpfQuadratic` takes it to the exact optimum; its multipliers give the prices. Prices. With y0 the balance row's dual and y_r thermal row r's (each the change in optimal cost per unit increase of the row's right-hand side), the price at bus k is `LMP_k = y0 + sum_r y_r PTDF[r, k]`: one more MW of demand at k raises the balance right-hand side by 1 and each thermal right-hand side (RateA - f0) by PTDF[r, k] (f0 being the flow the fixed loads cause). y0 is the energy component (the price at the island's reference bus), the sum the congestion component; the DC model is lossless, so there is no loss component. A line's shadow price is the cost saved per MW of extra rating: -y_r when it is held at +RateA, +y_r at -RateA. At a degenerate optimum the duals (so the prices) need not be unique; the ones reported are those of the optimal basis or active set found.
- [`Column`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Analysis/DcOpfCosted.cs#L39) (record struct): One LP / QP column: the generator it belongs to, its bounds, linear cost and Hessian entry (2a).
- [`Attempt`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Analysis/DcOpfCosted.cs#L165) (record): One solve attempt: status, column values, balance dual and one dual per rated line.

### src/GridSim.Core/Analysis/DcOpfHybridColumns.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Analysis`. 207 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Analysis/DcOpfHybridColumns.cs).

- [`DcOpfHybridColumns`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Analysis/DcOpfHybridColumns.cs#L22) (class): A square-ish matrix (m rows, any number of columns) stored column by column, where every column is either a SINGLE (exactly one stored entry, at a known row) or DENSE (a full array of m values). It exists so the security-constrained DC-OPF simplex (`DcOpfSecuritySimplex`) can hold its basis inverse, and the Gauss-Jordan working matrix it is rebuilt from, without an m x m dense array (about 276 MB on gb-full). WHY THIS IS EXACT. The reference (`Numerics.BoundedSimplex`) keeps a dense m x m inverse and updates it with row operations: scale one row, then for every other row with a non-zero multiplier subtract multiplier x pivot row. Each matrix entry is updated independently of every other entry, so the order in which this class visits entries cannot change any value. The only operations this class SKIPS are ones whose result is provably the same value: x - f * 0 and x / d for x = 0. In IEEE 754 arithmetic those can change only the SIGN of a zero (+0 versus -0), never a non-zero value, and a signed zero can never turn into a different non-zero value downstream here: it only ever meets multiplication (giving a zero), addition to a non-zero (no effect), comparison (+0 == -0), Math.Abs, or the refactorisation clamp, which maps both +0 and -0 to the same +clamp. So every non-zero entry here is bit-for-bit the entry the dense reference holds. A single column becomes dense ("promoted") the first time a row operation would give it a second non-zero. Dense columns are never demoted; the simplex rebuilds this object from scratch at every refactorisation.

### src/GridSim.Core/Analysis/DcOpfQuadratic.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Analysis`. 368 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Analysis/DcOpfQuadratic.cs).

- [`DcOpfQuadratic`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Analysis/DcOpfQuadratic.cs#L37) (class): The DC-OPF with quadratic generator costs (F19, October 2026): a small, self-contained, deterministic convex quadratic program solver, used only when at least one generator's cost curve has a non-zero quadratic term. The problem. Variables x (one per generator, or per piecewise-linear segment of a generator). Minimise `sum_j (h_j / 2) x_j^2 + c_j x_j` (h_j = 2 a_j >= 0, a diagonal Hessian) subject to the balance `sum_j x_j = D`, the bounds `lo_j <= x_j <= hi_j` and, for each rated line r, the thermal band `Lower_r <= p_r . x <= Upper_r`, p_r being the line's PTDF entry at each variable's bus. This is the same constraint set as the linear security LP (`DcOptimalPowerFlow`), with the quadratic terms added. The method is the textbook primal active-set method for convex QP (Nocedal and Wright, Numerical Optimization, 2nd ed., Algorithm 16.3), arranged so that the Hessian may be only positive SEMI-definite (units with linear costs have h_j = 0): it starts at a VERTEX (the optimal vertex of the linear part of the problem, found by the existing simplex), where the working set fixes every variable, and it keeps the invariant that the working-set KKT matrix `[H -A^T; A 0]` is non-singular (H positive definite on the working set's null space): Away from the working set's minimiser: solve the KKT system for the step p to that minimiser and take it, shortened at the first constraint it would cross (which then joins the working set). At the minimiser: the same solve gives the multipliers. If every inequality multiplier is >= -tolerance the point satisfies the KKT conditions of the whole convex problem and is optimal. Otherwise the most negative multiplier's constraint j leaves: the direction d with `A d = e_j`, `H d = A^T nu` (the same KKT matrix, another right-hand side) is the best direction off j, its curvature is `d' H d = nu_j` and the slope along it is the multiplier, so the exact line minimum is `t = -lambda_j / nu_j`; with zero curvature (only linear-cost units move) the step runs to the first blocking constraint, which always exists because every variable is boxed. Moving along d keeps H positive definite on the new working set's null space (the curvature along d is decoupled from the old null space because `z' H d = z' A^T nu = 0`), so the invariant holds. Every choice is made in index order with strict comparisons, and only plain IEEE double arithmetic is used (no fused multiply-add, no parallel loop), so the result is the same bits on every run and every CPU tier. The dense KKT solve costs O((n + |W|)^3) per iteration, which is fine for the MATPOWER-sized cases quadratic costs come with (case300: 69 units) and is the documented limit for very large fleets.
- [`Problem`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Analysis/DcOpfQuadratic.cs#L65) (record): The problem. `LineRows` is row-major, Lines x N.
- [`Result`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Analysis/DcOpfQuadratic.cs#L71) (record): The outcome. `LineDuals`[r] is the derivative of the optimal cost with respect to the right-hand side of line r written as in the linear security LP (lambda_lower - lambda_upper), so the nodal prices are formed exactly as from the simplex duals. `Failure` says why a non-Optimal status was returned.

### src/GridSim.Core/Analysis/DcOpfSecuritySimplex.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Analysis`. 534 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Analysis/DcOpfSecuritySimplex.cs).

- [`DcOpfSecuritySimplex`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Analysis/DcOpfSecuritySimplex.cs#L40) (class): The security-constrained DC-OPF linear program solved WITHOUT the dense matrices, giving bit-for-bit the answer of the dense reference (October 2026 review, R005). THE PROBLEM. `DcOptimalPowerFlow` used to build the LP as a dense (1 + L) x (G + L) matrix (one balance row, one thermal row per rated line; G dispatch columns, L line slacks) and hand it to the dense `BoundedSimplex`, which copies it into an m x (n + m) working matrix and keeps a dense m x m basis inverse that it rebuilds by an O(m^3) Gauss-Jordan every 64 iterations. On gb-full (5,876 rated lines, 5,318 generators) that is about 1.9 GB of arrays and hours of arithmetic. THE APPROACH. This class runs EXACTLY the same algorithm as `BoundedSimplex.Solve` - the same two-phase bounded-variable primal simplex, the same Dantzig pricing with the same first-index tie-break, the same ratio test with the same tie margin, the same eta updates, the same refactorisation schedule, pivot choice and clamp - performing the same floating-point operations in the same order on every value that can be non-zero. It only changes how the matrices are STORED: * The constraint matrix is never formed. A dispatch column is the balance-row 1 plus one PTDF entry per rated line, and generators at the same bus share one PTDF column, so the PTDF is held once per distinct generator bus (rated lines x distinct buses, about 73 MB on gb-full). A slack or artificial column is a single +/-1 and is never stored at all. * The basis inverse (and the Gauss-Jordan working matrix it is rebuilt from) is held by `DcOpfHybridColumns`: a column that still has one non-zero is stored as that one value, and only the columns the simplex has actually filled in are stored densely. * Pricing evaluates one reduced cost per (bus, objective coefficient) group of generators: generators with an identical column and identical cost have bit-identical reduced costs, because each is computed by the same sequence of operations on the same numbers. The skipped operations are only multiplications by an exact zero and the additions or subtractions of their zero results. In IEEE 754 arithmetic those change at most the sign of a zero, never a non-zero value, and a signed zero cannot reach a non-zero result anywhere in this algorithm (see `DcOpfHybridColumns`). So the dispatch, the status and every intermediate non-zero are the dense reference's, bit for bit; the tests in `DcOpfSecuritySimplexParityTests` compare the two solvers bit-for-bit on the bundled cases and on randomised degenerate LPs. No floor, tolerance or iteration cap is changed: every constant is read from `BoundedSimplex` (N010: its absolute floors are deliberately left as they are).
- [`Problem`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Analysis/DcOpfSecuritySimplex.cs#L49) (record): The LP, in the DC-OPF's structured form: minimise sum_j C[j] x[j] subject to sum_{i < G} x[i] = B[0] (balance row) sum_{i < G} Ptdf[r, GenColumn[i]] x[i] + x[G + r] = B[1 + r] (thermal row r, r < L) Lo[j] <= x[j] <= Hi[j] with Ptdf row-major (L rows by `DistinctColumns` columns). This is the dense reference's A matrix, row for row and entry for entry.
- [`Diagnostics`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Analysis/DcOpfSecuritySimplex.cs#L63) (record): Counters from the last solve (for tests and the performance notes).
- [`Detailed`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Analysis/DcOpfSecuritySimplex.cs#L125) (record): The outcome of `SolveDetailed`: what `Solve` returns plus the optimal basis's dual values (F19).

### src/GridSim.Core/Analysis/DcOptimalPowerFlow.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Analysis`. 866 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Analysis/DcOptimalPowerFlow.cs).

- [`DcOptimalPowerFlow`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Analysis/DcOptimalPowerFlow.cs#L39) (class): DC optimal power flow / security-constrained economic dispatch: the cheapest generation dispatch that meets demand and keeps every rated line within its thermal limit. It layers on the DC sensitivities of `DistributionFactors` (line flow = PTDF . injection). When line limits are enforced it solves the exact security-constrained LP minimise sum_i cost_i . Pg_i subject to sum_i Pg_i = demand, Pmin_i <= Pg_i <= Pmax_i, -RateA_l <= f0_l + sum_i PTDF[l, bus_i] . Pg_i <= RateA_l for every rated line l, where f0_l is the line's flow from the fixed loads. This is a bounded-variable linear program (one balance row plus a thermal row per rated line; a per-line slack in [0, 2.RateA] carries the two-sided limit), solved to a provable optimum by the self-contained `BoundedSimplex` - so the dispatch is globally cost-optimal across ALL simultaneously-binding constraints, not a one-line-at-a- time redispatch. With limits off it reduces to a plain merit-order (cheapest-first) economic dispatch. Costs are a linear per-generator marginal cost, defaulted from fuel type when a case carries no explicit cost. DC assumptions (reactance-only, 1 pu voltages) are inherited from the PTDF. Scale (R005, October 2026): the LP is solved by `DcOpfSecuritySimplex`, the BoundedSimplex algorithm performed operation for operation without its dense matrices (PTDF held once per distinct generator bus; basis inverse stored column by column, dense only where filled in), so the answer is the dense solver's bit for bit while gb-full fits in memory. The original dense path remains callable as `SolveDenseReference` for the parity tests. Islands (N034, October 2026). A network of several DC islands (see `DistributionFactors.FindIslands`) is dispatched island by island: no power crosses between islands, so each energised island is an independent problem with its own balance (its own generation meets its own demand), its own reference bus (the AC island rule: its slack, else its largest generator) and its own rated lines. Each island is solved by exactly the connected-case code below and the answers are merged back in model order (`DcOpfResult.Islands` reports each island). An island with no generator cannot be supplied: it is reported (with its load) and, when it carries load, the result is not feasible; it is never silently dropped. Before N034 a network with islands threw "DC susceptance is singular" (gb-full could not be dispatched at all). A connected network takes the unchanged single-model path, bit for bit.
- [`GenDispatch`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Analysis/DcOptimalPowerFlow.cs#L68) (record): A generator's dispatched output and its marginal cost.
- [`LineBinding`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Analysis/DcOptimalPowerFlow.cs#L71) (record): A line held at (or over) its thermal limit by the dispatch.
- [`UnrelievableLine`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Analysis/DcOptimalPowerFlow.cs#L94) (record): N109: a rated line that no dispatch can bring within its rating, left out of the security LP and reported here (as the corrective redispatch leaves out an element no generator can move, and as PowerWorld and PSS/E report uncontrollable violations apart from the optimised ones). The reachable range is over every unit anywhere in [Pmin, Pmax] with the balance row dropped, a superset of every dispatch the LP could choose, so a line whose range misses its rating cannot be relieved by any dispatch, and keeping it would only make the whole LP Infeasible.
- [`IslandDispatch`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Analysis/DcOptimalPowerFlow.cs#L105) (record): One DC island's share of a multi-island dispatch (N034).
- [`DcOpfResult`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Analysis/DcOptimalPowerFlow.cs#L109) (record): The dispatch result.
- [`DcOpfOptions`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Analysis/DcOptimalPowerFlow.cs#L156) (record): F19 (October 2026): options of `Solve(GridModel, DcOpfOptions)`. The defaults are exactly the historical `Solve(GridModel, double[], bool)` call: fuel-type costs, line limits on, no prices.

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Analysis`. 268 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Analysis/DcPowerFlow.cs).

- [`DcIslandBalance`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Analysis/DcPowerFlow.cs#L18) (record): One DC island's balance in a `DcPowerFlow` solve.
- [`DcPowerFlowResult`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Analysis/DcPowerFlow.cs#L30) (record): The result of a `DcPowerFlow` solve.
- [`DcPowerFlow`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Analysis/DcPowerFlow.cs#L47) (class): The DC (linearised) power flow (F18, October 2026): bus angles and branch flows from the DC nodal susceptance, the standard textbook linearisation. It REUSES `DistributionFactors` (the same B' build, the same factorisation, the same per-island references and the same flow products as its `DcFlows`, which the DC-OPF and the PTDF / LODF verbs already use), so there is one DC model in GridSim, not two. Convention (that of `DistributionFactors`): only series reactance enters; resistance, line charging, shunts, tap ratios and phase shifts are ignored; voltage magnitudes are 1 pu; there are no losses, so each island's reference bus picks up exactly the island's imbalance. Injections are the in-service generators' Pg minus the bus demand Pd. Nothing here is iterative, so there is no convergence question; a network whose DC model cannot be formed (an in-service zero-reactance branch that is the only link between two islands, or a singular B') throws `InvalidOperationException` from `DistributionFactors.Build`.

- [`ScopfStatus`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Analysis/DcScopf.cs#L38) (enum): How `DcScopf.Solve` ended.
- [`ScopfDispatch`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Analysis/DcScopf.cs#L55) (record): A generator's secured dispatch.
- [`ScopfBinding`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Analysis/DcScopf.cs#L59) (record): A branch at its limit: pre-outage (`Contingency` -1, against RateA) or after the outage of branch `Contingency` (against the post-outage rating).
- [`ScopfBusPrice`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Analysis/DcScopf.cs#L62) (record): A bus's price: the change in optimal cost per extra MW of demand at the bus (the dual of its balance row).
- [`ScopfResult`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Analysis/DcScopf.cs#L66) (record): The result of `DcScopf.Solve`. The dispatch, flows and prices are filled only when `Status` is `ScopfStatus.Optimal`; otherwise they are empty and `Message` says why.
- [`DcScopf`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Analysis/DcScopf.cs#L101) (class): Preventive security-constrained DC optimal power flow: the least-cost generator dispatch that meets demand with every rated branch inside its rating before any outage AND after each listed single-branch outage, with no action after the outage (preventive). Solved as a sparse linear program by `SparseBoundedSimplex`. Formulation. DC model of `DistributionFactors` (reactance only, 1 pu voltages; taps and phase shifts ignored). Columns: the dispatch P_g in [Pmin, Pmax] at cost c_g; an angle psi_i per bus in MW-scaled form (psi = base MVA x theta; the reference bus fixed at 0); a flow f_l per branch, within +/- RateA when rated (free when not). Rows: each bus's balance, sum of its units' P - sum of flows leaving + sum of flows arriving = its demand; each branch's flow, f_l - b_l (psi_from - psi_to) = 0 with b_l = 1 / X_l. After the outage of branch k, branch l carries f_l + LODF(l, k) f_k (`DistributionFactors.LodfColumn`); each secured pair gets a column q in +/- the post-outage rating and the row q - f_l - LODF(l, k) f_k = 0. Every row has a handful of non-zeros, so the LP grows with the network and the secured pairs, not with buses x branches. Constraint generation (the default). The LP starts with no post-outage row. After each solve every pair (outage k, monitored branch l) is checked; the pairs whose post-outage flow exceeds the rating by more than `ViolationToleranceMw` are added (in outage then branch order) and the LP is solved again from scratch. It stops when nothing is broken: the answer then meets every post-outage limit to within that tolerance and is optimal for the LP holding all of them, because the rows left out do not bind. Rows are only added, so it ends within the pair count; `ScopfOptions.MaxRounds` caps it and is reported when reached. Prices. A bus's price is its balance row's dual: the energy price plus the congestion of every binding pre- and post-outage limit. One connected network only (several DC islands are refused, naming the count). Deterministic: every loop runs in a fixed order, and the result is bit-identical from run to run.
- [`Lp`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Analysis/DcScopf.cs#L290) (record): Declared record; see the source and member declarations for its role.

### src/GridSim.Core/Analysis/DistributionFactors.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Analysis`. 496 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Analysis/DistributionFactors.cs).

- [`DistributionFactors`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Analysis/DistributionFactors.cs#L38) (class): DC Power Transfer Distribution Factors (PTDF) and Line Outage Distribution Factors (LODF): the closed-form linear sensitivities of branch flows to nodal injections (PTDF) and to line outages (LODF). Where `ContingencyAnalysis` screens N-1 by physically removing a branch and re-solving, these give the same information from ONE factorisation of the DC nodal susceptance - the workhorses of operations and markets ("which line does each generator load", instant N-1 screening, the basis for redispatch). DC linearisation (the standard convention): only the series reactance is used - R, line charging, taps and phase shifts are ignored, and voltage magnitudes are 1 pu. Branch susceptance b_l = 1/X_l; the reduced nodal susceptance B' (slack row/col removed) is factored once, then PTDF column k (injection at bus k, withdrawal at the slack) is one solve B' x = e_k. LODF for an outage of line k is one transfer solve, LODF[l,k] = Phi[l,k] / (1 - Phi[k,k]); when 1 - Phi[k,k] -> 0 the outage islands the system (line k is a bridge), reported in `RadialOutages` rather than divided. PTDF and LODF are dimensionless (MW per MW); `DcFlows` returns MW. Islands (N034, October 2026). A network made of several electrically separate parts (DC islands: connected components over the branches the DC model uses) has no single reference: B' with one slack removed is singular, and this class used to throw "DC susceptance is singular" (so gb-full, which carries a 3-bus island with its own slack, could not run the security DC-OPF or the CLI `dcopf` verb). Each island now gets its own reference bus, chosen the way the AC power flow's island pre-pass (`PowerFlow.IslandPartition`) chooses one: the island's slack bus if it has one (the first in model order), otherwise the bus of its largest generator by |Pg| (the first in model order among ties). One difference: here any generator on the island counts, even one at Pg = 0, while the AC pre-pass blacks out an island whose generators all have Pg = 0. The island holding the overall slack keeps exactly the reference this class always used. Every reference row and column is removed from B', which is then block diagonal and factored once. A PTDF column means "inject at the bus, withdraw at ITS island's reference"; flows in other islands are zero. An island with no generator at all still gets a reference (its first bus, so B' stays non-singular) and is reported through `Islands` with `DcIsland.HasGeneration` false, so a caller can tell that nothing can supply it. With one island (every connected case) nothing changes: the same reference, the same reduced matrix built in the same order, the same factorisation, bit for bit.
- [`Prepared`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Analysis/DistributionFactors.cs#L112) (record): Everything `Build` derives from a model before the factorisation: the reduced nodal susceptance B' (built in exactly `Build`'s stamp order) and the index maps. `Build` is `FromPrepared(p, SparseLu.Factor(p.BPrime))`, so a caller that factors many B' matrices of one structure together (the batched DC power flow, `DcPowerFlow.SolveBatch`) and hands each factorisation back through `FromPrepared` gets exactly the object `Build` would have made, provided its factorisation is bit-identical to `SparseLu.Factor(CsrMatrix)`'s.
- [`DcIsland`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Analysis/DistributionFactors.cs#L496) (record): One DC island of a network (N034): a connected component over the branches the DC model uses.

### src/GridSim.Core/Analysis/GeneratorCostCurve.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Analysis`. 136 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Analysis/GeneratorCostCurve.cs).

- [`GeneratorCostCurve`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Analysis/GeneratorCostCurve.cs#L27) (class): A generator's active-power cost curve in the form the DC-OPF can optimise (F19, October 2026): a convex quadratic polynomial `C(P) = a P^2 + b P + c` (a >= 0), or a convex piecewise-linear curve through a list of (MW, cost per hour) points. What is accepted, and why. The input is a `GeneratorCost` exactly as a MATPOWER `mpc.gencost` row gives it (or the JSON cost file, which uses the same layout). MATPOWER's own DC OPF accepts polynomial costs up to quadratic and piecewise-linear costs, and needs them convex; this class applies the same limits and refuses anything else, naming the generator, rather than quietly approximating it: Polynomial: NCOST 1 (a constant), 2 (linear) or 3 (quadratic). A longer polynomial is accepted only when every coefficient above the quadratic one is exactly zero (pglib and MATPOWER files often pad that way); a real cubic or higher term is refused. A negative quadratic coefficient (a concave curve) is refused. Piecewise linear: at least 2 points, MW strictly increasing, slopes never decreasing (convex). Outside the points the first and last segments are extended in a straight line, which is what MATPOWER's constrained cost variable formulation does (each segment is an inequality valid on the whole axis). Every number must be finite (the MATPOWER parser already refuses non-finite gencost numbers; the cost-file reader does too). Units are the case's own: cost per hour, MW, so a marginal cost or a nodal price comes out in cost per MWh of the same currency.

### src/GridSim.Core/Analysis/RestorationSequencer.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Analysis`. 180 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Analysis/RestorationSequencer.cs).

- [`RestorationStepResult`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Analysis/RestorationSequencer.cs#L8) (record): One step of a restoration sequence: the branch just energised and the resulting state's health - voltage-band violations and any generator that has run out of reactive capability.
- [`RestorationReport`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Analysis/RestorationSequencer.cs#L26) (record): The health of a whole restoration sequence, step by step.
- [`RestorationSequencer`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Analysis/RestorationSequencer.cs#L48) (class): Evaluates a network-restoration (black-start) sequence for reactive feasibility: it energises the listed branches one at a time, re-solves the growing live network with generator reactive limits ENFORCED, and at each step reports voltage-band violations and any generator that has hit its Qmin/Qmax. This captures the constraint a bare cascade trip does not - as a generator picks up a lightly-loaded EHV line, the line's charging drives a Ferranti over-voltage the machine must absorb, and once it hits its reactive-absorption limit the over-voltage stands: the step is unsafe, and a different ordering (or a shunt reactor) is needed. The power flow already switches PV to PQ at a generator's reactive limit; this wraps it into a sequence checker so an operator can see WHERE a restoration order breaks.

### src/GridSim.Core/Analysis/TapOptimizer.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Analysis`. 222 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Analysis/TapOptimizer.cs).

- [`TapSetting`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Analysis/TapOptimizer.cs#L8) (record): A recommended tap position for one transformer.
- [`TapSchedule`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Analysis/TapOptimizer.cs#L12) (record): A coordinated tap schedule across the network's OLTC transformers, with the voltage-flatness objective before and after.
- [`OltcRegulationCheck`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Analysis/TapOptimizer.cs#L36) (record): D-DOC-046: one OLTC's own regulation at a tap schedule: the voltage of the bus it controls, against the target and deadband its record gives it.
- [`TapOptimizer`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Analysis/TapOptimizer.cs#L54) (class): Finds a coordinated tap schedule across ALL of a network's OLTC transformers at once, to flatten the voltage profile against a solved state - the multi-transformer optimisation the per-transformer deadband regulator (`SteadyStateSolver`) cannot do, since each of its OLTCs chases only its own local target with no coordination. The objective is the sum of squared voltage deviations from `targetVpu`; it is minimised over the tap ratios directly by re-solving the real (nonlinear) power flow for each candidate (a derivative-free downhill-simplex search), so there is no linearisation error, then each tap is snapped to its discrete step grid and the schedule re-evaluated. For the handful of GSP transformers a control-room operator coordinates, this is fast and exact; it reuses the power flow, the `Oltc` bounds, and `NelderMead`.

- [`UcPeriod`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Analysis/UnitCommitment.cs#L101) (record): One period's totals: demand, generation, committed headroom (spinning reserve available), the reserve asked for, and the system marginal price (the balance row's dual in the relaxation with the commitment fixed; NaN when that relaxation did not solve).
- [`UcBinding`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Analysis/UnitCommitment.cs#L105) (record): A branch at its rating in some period: pre-outage (Contingency -1) or after the outage of branch Contingency.
- [`UcResult`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Analysis/UnitCommitment.cs#L109) (record): The commitment's result. `Status` is the branch-and-bound's; the schedules and periods are filled when there is an incumbent (status Optimal or NodeCap with an incumbent), empty otherwise.
- [`UnitCommitment`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Analysis/UnitCommitment.cs#L144) (class): Security-constrained unit commitment (roadmap P0-3): which units run in each period, and at what output, at least total cost, as a mixed-integer linear program solved by `MilpBranchAndBound`. Formulation (per unit g, period t; the standard three-binary form with the output split into segments above Pmin). On/off u, start v (both whole); stop w (continuous, whole whenever u and v are); output P = Pmin u + sum_k s_k with 0 <= s_k <= segment length. Balance: sum_g P = demand(t) (the case's bus loads times the period's scale). Capacity: P <= Pmax u (and P >= Pmin u by construction). Logic: u(t) - u(t-1) = v(t) - w(t), from the unit's initial state. Minimum up / down time (Rajan and Takriti): the starts in the last UT periods <= u(t); the stops in the last DT periods <= 1 - u(t); a unit inside its initial minimum time is held in its state. Ramps: P(t) - P(t-1) <= RU u(t-1) + max(RU, Pmin) v(t), and the mirror for falling output with stops. Spinning reserve: sum_g (Pmax u - P) >= reserve(t). Network: each rated branch's DC flow, PTDF x generation plus the flow the loads alone drive (from the same DC solve as `dcpf`), within +/- RATE_A; for each listed outage k, flow + LODF(l, k) x flow(k) within +/- RATE_A. Cost: the curve's slopes on the segments, its cost at Pmin and the no-load cost per hour on u, the start-up cost on v. One connected network only (several DC islands are refused, naming the count). A committable unit needs a finite Pmax. The answer's integer columns are exactly whole (see `MilpBranchAndBound`); the system price is the balance row's dual in the relaxation with the commitment fixed (the usual pricing of a commitment). Deterministic: every loop runs in a fixed order and the search is bit-identical from run to run.
- [`Unit`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Analysis/UnitCommitment.cs#L504) (record): A unit as the formulation uses it: Pmin, Pmax, the segments above Pmin (length and slope), the fixed cost per hour while on (curve cost at Pmin plus no-load) and the start-up cost.
- [`LpBuilder`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Analysis/UnitCommitment.cs#L574) (class): Columns and equality rows; an inequality gets its own non-negative slack column.
