Every top-level key except `format` is optional (the defaults of `UcOptions` and `UcUnitData`). A unit is named by `unit` (its index among the case's in-service generators, from 0) or by `name` (the generator's name, which must be unique); a unit given twice is refused. A contingency is a branch index (from 0) or a branch name (unique). Throws `InvalidDataException` naming the entry.

### src/GridSim.Core/Analysis/VoltageLimits.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Analysis`. 89 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Analysis/VoltageLimits.cs).

- [`VoltageLimits`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Analysis/VoltageLimits.cs#L22) (class): The one definition of the bus-voltage bands the analysis modules judge a solved state against (R136, October 2026). Before this the band was a bare literal in each module - 0.94/1.06 in the contingency screen, +/-0.04 and +/-0.10 about 1.0 pu in the watch-list, 0.9/1.1 in the restoration checker - so the same state could be secure in one module and violating in another, and an edit to one copy would not reach the rest. Operational band (`OperationalLowPu`..`OperationalHighPu`, 0.94-1.06 pu): the generous operating band a control room holds the transmission system inside. The N-1 contingency screen (violations and its stress score) uses it; the SCADA console's alarm band (`Presentation.ScadaThresholds.VoltageBandLowPu/HighPu`) carries the same values. Statutory band (`StatutoryLowPu`..`StatutoryHighPu`, 0.90-1.10 pu, i.e. +/-`StatutoryBandPu` about nominal): the outer limit. The restoration sequencer checks each energisation step against it, and the watch-list ramps a voltage item's proximity to 1 at it. Watch band (+/-`WatchBandPu` about the reference): the early-warning deviation at which the watch-list starts listing a bus, well inside the operational band. The values are written as literals (not derived, e.g. 1.0 - 0.1) so each is the exact double the modules always used; `VoltageLimitsTests` pins that the bands are consistent with each other.

The score is consequence x proximity - both in [0,1] - so a severe outcome that is close ranks above a severe outcome that is far, or a near-certain event whose consequence is small.
- [`WatchListOptions`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Analysis/WatchList.cs#L34) (record): Options for building the watch-list.

Each source contributes items scored by consequence x proximity: the physics gives the severity, the current state gives how close we are, and the ranking is the product. It reads the solved state (branch loadings, bus voltages, convergence health) and, when supplied, the protection assessment (thermal time-to-trip) and boundary flows.

Inline `dynamicsClass` on an individual asset always wins over a rule. Match is case-insensitive and exact by default; a trailing `*` makes it a PREFIX wildcard (e.g. `"wind*"` matches both `wind-onshore` and `wind-offshore`), which guards against fuel-vocabulary drift silently dropping assets. - [`AssetClassProvenance`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Assets/AssetClassLibrary.cs#L6) (record): The provenance of one authored parameter: where the number came from and a human note.
- [`AssetClass`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Assets/AssetClassLibrary.cs#L18) (record): One authored asset class - a portable, self-contained device description (one element of a v1 case's `asset-classes.json`: a bare JSON array of classes, with no `schema` member and no schema id; D-DOC-230: this comment used to name a schema id, gridsim-asset-classes/1, that no file carries and no reader checks) you bind to a bus. Parameters are a flat name->value bag so the format stays hand-editable and version-tolerant; `Provenance` records, per parameter, whether the value is grounded or a literature-approximated placeholder. Any `ProvenanceTag.CuratedPlaceholder` note MUST carry the literal token `[VERIFY]` (validated at load) - the honesty discipline that keeps assumed control constants labelled as such.
- [`AssetClassLibrary`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Assets/AssetClassLibrary.cs#L60) (class): A named collection of authored asset classes (from `asset-classes.json`). Lookup is by class name; an unknown name is a hard, fail-loud error at bind time - a silent miss would leave an asset mysteriously passive.
- [`AssetClassSupport`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Assets/AssetClassLibrary.cs#L116) (class): Which asset-class kinds GridSim can simulate and which parameters each kind's consumers actually read (rule R073). `AssetClassLibrary` refuses, listing every problem: a class of a kind with no controller (`AssetKind.SynchronousMachine`: a generator bound to it would stay passive), a refused key (`RefusedKeys`), and any key no consumer of the class's kind reads (a misspelt key included). D-DOC-215 (DOC-17): this summary used to narrate the history of R073 ("before this ... now refuses"); it now states the rule as it stands.
- [`AssetParamDefaults`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Assets/AssetClassLibrary.cs#L355) (class): R137 (B4, October 2026; Ruling R1: Mark delegated EE calls 2026-10-04): the ONE table of fall-back values for an asset-class parameter that more than one controller reads. Before, the same authored key fell back to different values in different controllers: an absent `AssetParams.RocofTripConfirmS` was 0.5 s in `GridFollowingInverter`, 1.0 s in `GridFormingInverter` and 0.0 s (an instantaneous trip) in `Protection.ProtectionController`. Now the inverters read the value below, and a protection class must author every dwell its stages need (`Protection.ProtectionController` refuses the class otherwise; see `ProtectionDwellKeys`).
- [`AssetParams`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Assets/AssetClassLibrary.cs#L401) (class): Canonical parameter names for the built-in inverter controllers. ### src/GridSim.Core/Assets/AssetValidation.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Assets`. 220 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Assets/AssetValidation.cs).

- [`RecordedFrequencyTrace`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Assets/AssetValidation.cs#L12) (record): A recorded frequency trace (e.g. NESO 1 s / Gridradar 100 ms) to back-test a simulation against.
- [`ValidationTolerance`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Assets/AssetValidation.cs#L69) (record): Acceptance tolerances for a validation back-test.
- [`ValidationReport`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Assets/AssetValidation.cs#L78) (record): The residuals of a back-test and whether it passes the acceptance gate.
- [`FrozenParameterSet`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Assets/AssetValidation.cs#L92) (record): The parameter set frozen at the ANCHOR event of a blind-prediction protocol (D-DOC-037): every model constant shared across events. A blind prediction of a second event must use exactly these values; `AssetValidation.BlindPredict` refuses anything else. The per-event inputs are not part of it, because they come from the event's own record (`GridEvent.ApplyRecordedServices`): the response services held, the pre-event frequency, the recorded demand effect where the record gives one (N317, LF6 October 2026: it sets the event's DampingPctPerHz, so a frozen damping is compared on the shared set, before the event's record is applied), and the window length (extended to cover the recorded sequence).
- [`AssetValidation`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Assets/AssetValidation.cs#L157) (class): Back-tests a frequency simulation against a recorded event: the acceptance gate that output must pass before it is called evidence. The gate compares three things with a recorded trace: the nadir (Hz), the initial RoCoF (Hz/s, on the trace's own measurement basis) and the time of the nadir (s), each within `ValidationTolerance` (0.05 Hz, 0.05 Hz/s, 2.0 s by default). A credible protocol ANCHORS on one event and then BLIND-PREDICTS a second event with the parameter set frozen at the anchor; only the blind prediction counts as evidence. `BlindPredict` enforces the freeze: it refuses a prediction made with any constant changed since the anchor (`FrozenParameterSet.Differences`), and a "blind" prediction of the anchor event itself. Where it is applied (D-DOC-037, October 2026: it had no caller outside the tests): the credibility gate (`ReplayValidator.Validate`) runs `Compare` whenever a recorded trace is attached, reports it as `ReplayResult.BackTest`, and caps a Reproduced verdict at Marginal when the back-test fails, the same rule the per-sample RMSE applies. SPATIAL (per-node) validation against the four-node Gridradar PMU data (London, Buckingham, Manchester, Strathclyde) - the vector-shift path and the local-vs-COI RoCoF spread - needs the distributed model to carry the asset fleet, and stays UnvalidatedAtScale until that integration and the PMU comparison exist.

### src/GridSim.Core/Assets/ConfirmTimer.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Assets`. 58 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Assets/ConfirmTimer.cs).

- [`ConfirmTimer`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Assets/ConfirmTimer.cs#L26) (struct): N235 (October 2026, found by DOC-4, fixed by DOC-5): how long a condition has held, counted in whole substeps. The grid-following and grid-forming inverters timed their RoCoF trip confirm by adding the substep length to a running total every step (`dwell += dt`) and comparing the total with the confirm time. Repeated addition of a decimal step drifts: ten additions of 0.02 s give 0.19999999999999998, so a 0.2 s confirm at 20 ms substeps was met on the 11th step (220 ms), not the 10th. D-DOC-095 fixed exactly this in the protection relays (`ProtectionEvaluator`); this is the same rule for the inverters, so the two can never disagree. The rule: the time over threshold is (whole substeps) x (substep), one multiplication, not a running sum. A substep of a different length from the ones counted so far first banks those (steps x their length) into a carried total, so a run whose substep changes mid-confirm (the live loop's variable tick) is still exact per run of equal steps. The confirm is met when the elapsed time reaches it, or falls short of it by at most `ProtectionEvaluator.DwellRelativeSlack` of it (2^-49: the representation error of two decimal doubles, under a femtosecond for any confirm below 0.5 s). Plain double arithmetic, identical on every CPU. Effect (steps to trip, before -> after): 0.2 s at 0.02 s 11 -> 10; 0.25 s at 0.02 s 13 -> 13 (0.25 / 0.02 is 12.5, so the 13th step is the first to reach it either way); unchanged for every bundled confirm at the substeps GridSim uses: 0.5 s and 1.0 s at 0.02, 0.01, 0.005 and 0.001 s; 0 s (the first over-threshold step). The exact cases are pinned in Doc5FrequencyEvidenceAssetTests.

### src/GridSim.Core/Assets/DcSource.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Assets`. 185 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Assets/DcSource.cs).

- [`IDcSource`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Assets/DcSource.cs#L11) (interface): What sits behind an inverter's DC link: how much power it can give or take right now, and what it actually delivers when asked. The inverter controllers draw through this seam, so a storage asset's grid response is bounded by its energy store - from the simple state-of-charge bucket to a full chemistry model. Powers are AC-side MW (discharge / injection positive).
- [`SocBucket`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Assets/DcSource.cs#L31) (class): The linear energy bucket the inverters have always carried: `SoC -= P dt / 3600 / capacity`, no losses, no rate limits, headroom closed only at the SoC bounds. A step inside the SoC window is arithmetically as it has always been; the step that reaches a bound delivers only the energy left to it (GR-627).
- [`BatteryDcSource`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Assets/DcSource.cs#L74) (class): A battery pack (`PackModel`) behind a converter of efficiency `eta`: headroom is the pack's instantaneous BMS limit (current, cut-off voltage, SoC window, temperature), and a draw steps the pack's electrochemical and thermal state - so sustained delivery sags, heats and stops exactly where the chemistry says, and charging carries the conversion losses (DC = AC / eta on discharge, AC * eta on charge).
- [`DcSources`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Assets/DcSource.cs#L142) (class): Builds an asset class's DC source: a chemistry pack when `batteryChemistry` is set (with `capacityMwh` as the usable energy), else the SoC bucket when `capacityMwh` is set, else none (unbounded - the historical default).

### src/GridSim.Core/Assets/GridFollowingInverter.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Assets`. 396 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Assets/GridFollowingInverter.cs).

- [`GridFollowingInverter`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Assets/GridFollowingInverter.cs#L21) (class): A grid-following (PLL-behind current-source) inverter as an explicit sample -> compute -> actuate -> protect state machine, integrated on the swing substep. Sample: local (Hz, RoCoF, phase) pushed through a transport delay (`detectionLatencyS`) - modelling PLL/measurement latency and the fact a PLL sees its OWN bus, not the COI. Compute: a deadbanded droop leg (shape shared with `SwingKernel.FastResponseTarget`) plus an optional df/dt leg, capped by SoC/headroom. Actuate: ramp-limit the fast slew, then first-order lag (`actuateTauS`). Protect: on sustained local RoCoF over `rocofTripHzPerS`, a phase step over `vectorShiftTripDeg`, or under-voltage below `lvrtVoltagePu`, the unit trips and its dispatched output `Pg` becomes a deficit (Loss-of-Mains) - the mechanism behind 2019-08-09. In the degenerate regime (zero latencies, df/dt gain 0, SoC/ramp disabled, symmetric headroom, trip disabled) one unit reduces to a `Fleet.FleetUnit` FFR device - "generalises, not forks".
- [`MeasurementDelay`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Assets/GridFollowingInverter.cs#L255) (class): A small transport-delay buffer for a controller's local measurement. Push each step; Read returns the most recent sample at least `latencyS` old (the current sample when latency is 0, so a zero-latency controller is bit-clean). Assumes a roughly constant substep within a run. October 2026 review (R006): the history used to be a `Queue{T}` that `Read` and `PhaseStep` each walked from the oldest sample, so once the 512-entry history was full every controller update visited about 1,024 samples (gb-full binds about 2,000 active assets, and the live loop runs up to 4,000 substeps per tick). It is now a fixed ring buffer of the same 512 samples, and both reads find their sample by binary search over the time stamps: at most 10 probes. The answers are BIT-IDENTICAL to the old scans. Both return a stored sample (no arithmetic is done on it, apart from PhaseStep's one subtraction, which is the same subtraction of the same two stored values), and the sample chosen is provably the same one: `Read` returned the LAST sample of the leading run (oldest first) whose time passes `t <= cutoff + 1e-12`, or the oldest sample when even the oldest fails. When the stored time stamps never decrease, the test is true for a prefix and false after it, so a binary search for the end of the passing prefix finds exactly that sample. `PhaseStep` took as its reference the phase of the LAST passing sample anywhere in the buffer (or the newest sample when none passes, giving latest - latest), and as "latest" the newest sample. With non-decreasing time stamps the last passing sample is the end of the passing prefix, found by the same search. Both arguments need the stored time stamps to be non-decreasing. Every caller's clock only moves forward, but the buffer does not rely on that: each push records whether its time is below the previous one (or either is NaN, which compares false everywhere), and while such a step lies inside the stored window both reads run the original oldest-first scans, so even an out-of-order history gives the old answers.

The synthetic-inertia term lowers initial RoCoF WITHOUT touching E - the codebase's non-negotiable separation of real (1/2)Jw^2 energy from df/dt emulation. There is no detection latency (a voltage source responds essentially instantly) and protection is ride-through biased (a high/disabled RoCoF trip), so a GFM fleet stabilises where a GFL fleet can trip.

### src/GridSim.Core/Assets/Passive/ThermalLag.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Assets`. 41 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Assets/Passive/ThermalLag.cs).

- [`ThermalLag`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Assets/Passive/ThermalLag.cs#L19) (class): The first-order thermal lag shared by the passive plant models (`LineThermalDynamics`, `TransformerDynamics`): `tau dx/dt = drive - x`, stepped by its EXACT discretisation over a tick of `dt` seconds with the drive held constant across the tick: x(t + dt) = drive + (x(t) - drive) * exp(-dt / tau) Bug hunt 2026-11-01 (#190): both models used explicit Euler with `tau = max(dt, 60 * tauMin)`. At the loop tick sizes (LiveSim's default 20 min = 1200 s, GdaReplayLoop's 1800 s) `dt / tau` was then 1 whenever `dt >= tau`, so the state jumped to the drive in one tick and the lag vanished: a 20 min transformer from cold at loading 1 read 1.000 after one 1200 s tick against the exact 1 - e^-1 = 0.632 (0.777 at 1800 s), and a 15 min line read 1.000 against 0.736 (0.865 at 1800 s), so a 1000 MVA line overloaded for one tick was derated to 900 MVA instead of 926.4 MVA; cooling was equally instant. The exact step has no stability limit, so the clamp is gone; it is exact for any tick while the drive is constant over the tick, and it moves every thermal value at every tick size (Euler was first-order accurate even at small ticks).

Unlike the solver's instantaneous OLTC loop, a tap step commits only after the controlled-bus voltage has stayed outside the deadband for `interTapDelayS` (and `initialTapDelayS` before the very first move) - the seconds-to-tens- of-seconds mechanical delay real tap changers have. Thermal state is a first-order lag of loading squared (the I^2 R load loss) vs ambient (top-oil/winding), driving a rating derate. Emits a `PlantStateUpdate`, never a swing-power term - a different (voltage-stability/thermal) timescale from the frequency window.

    TripInfeed,     // -> AssetActuation.TrippedInfeedMw (generator/inverter LoM): remove the protected infeed
    ShedDemand,     // -> +ActivePowerMw step (LFDD): load removed reduces the deficit

### src/GridSim.Core/Diagnostics/AuditAnchorFile.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Diagnostics`. 116 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Diagnostics/AuditAnchorFile.cs).

- [`AuditAnchorFile`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Diagnostics/AuditAnchorFile.cs#L27) (class): D-DOC-062 (October 2026): the anchor of an audit log kept in a small file of its own, so the next run that appends to the log can check the log still holds everything the last run left in it. Why. The hash chain on its own cannot tell a log that lost its last entries (tail truncation) from a log that never had them: the shorter file still verifies. `AuditRunRecorder.Start` used to open the log with no anchor, so the CLI (`--audit-log`) appended new entries to a tail-truncated log without noticing, and the truncation was then buried under fresh, valid entries. Now every run writes the anchor (entry count and head hash) after it appends, and the next run opens the log against it: a log with fewer entries than the anchor, or a different hash at the anchored entry, is refused with `AuditLogTamperException` before anything is appended. Where. By default beside the log (`<log>.anchor`), which catches accidental truncation, a restore of an older copy, and a naive edit. An operator who wants protection against someone who can also edit the anchor keeps it elsewhere (CLI `--audit-anchor <file>`, web `Audit:AnchorPath`: a different account's share, write-once media) and also keeps the anchor line printed at the end of every run. Format (one ASCII line, newline-terminated): `gridsim-audit-anchor/1 count=<N> head=<hash>`, where the hash is `AuditLog.Genesis` for an empty log, else 64 upper-case hexadecimal digits. Anything else is refused (fail loud: a damaged anchor must not silently turn the check off).

### src/GridSim.Core/Diagnostics/AuditEvent.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Diagnostics`. 197 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Diagnostics/AuditEvent.cs).

- [`AuditInput`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Diagnostics/AuditEvent.cs#L11) (record): One named input to an audited run and the SHA-256 of its content, for example the case file or the measurement set an estimate was computed from. Recording the hash (not the content) lets a reviewer later prove which exact input produced a recorded result, without copying the input into the log.
- [`AuditEvent`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Diagnostics/AuditEvent.cs#L80) (class): The small, explicit API a product path (a CLI verb, a service loop) uses to record an event in the persistent audit log: WHO ran it, WHAT was done, WHEN (the run timestamp, plus the grid state time when there is one), WHICH inputs (by SHA-256) and the OUTCOME (R075). The event becomes the entry's summary, in one fixed, unambiguous layout: `actor=<who> action=<what> inputs=<name>:<sha256>,... outcome=<text>` (`inputs=-` when there are none). Because the summary is inside the hash, every one of those fields is covered by the chain. The actor, action and input names are restricted to letters, digits and `. _ - @ /` so the layout can always be split back into its fields; the outcome is free text on a single line and comes last. No secrets. The summary is plain text. Never put a password, key, token or connection string in the actor, action or outcome; record a hash of a sensitive input instead.

### src/GridSim.Core/Diagnostics/AuditLog.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Diagnostics`. 110 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Diagnostics/AuditLog.cs).

- [`AuditLogEntry`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Diagnostics/AuditLog.cs#L15) (record): One tamper-evident audit record: an emitted estimate (or any provenance-bearing output) with the run metadata and a hash that chains it to the previous entry.
- [`AuditLog`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Diagnostics/AuditLog.cs#L36) (class): An append-only, hash-chained audit log for the estimation pipeline - the evidence trail a critical-national- infrastructure service needs (NCSC CAF objective C, "detecting cyber security events"). Each entry records what was emitted, when (run metadata), for which grid instant (present/past state time), its provenance class, and a hash chaining it to its predecessor. Altering any entry after the fact breaks the chain from that point on, so tampering is detectable by `Verify(IReadOnlyList{AuditLogEntry})`. It pairs the estate's existing `ProvenanceTag` (trust class) and run metadata (git commit, host, time) into a single verifiable record. This class is the in-memory log. For a persistent, append-only log on disk (one JSON line per entry, same hash chain) use `AuditLogWriter` to append, `AuditLogFile` to verify or load, and `AuditEvent` to record a product event (who / what / when / input hashes) (R075).

### src/GridSim.Core/Diagnostics/AuditLogFile.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Diagnostics`. 593 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Diagnostics/AuditLogFile.cs).

- [`AuditAnchor`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Diagnostics/AuditLogFile.cs#L19) (record): An externally kept note of how long a log was and what its last hash was at some moment (for example the values printed when a run finished, or stored somewhere the log's writer cannot reach). The hash chain on its own cannot tell a log that lost its last few entries from a log that never had them, and it cannot tell a log rewritten end to end (every hash recomputed) from the original. Checking the file against an anchor closes both gaps for every entry the anchor covers.
- [`AuditLogVerification`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Diagnostics/AuditLogFile.cs#L34) (record): The outcome of verifying an audit log file. A valid result means every line parsed, every entry sits at its own sequence number, every entry links to the hash of the one before it, every stored hash equals the hash recomputed from the entry's fields, and (when an anchor was given) the anchored entries are all present and unchanged. An invalid result names the FIRST broken entry and why; nothing after it can be trusted, because the chain is broken from that point on.
- [`AuditLogTamperException`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Diagnostics/AuditLogFile.cs#L68) (class): Thrown when an audit log file fails verification: an entry was edited, deleted, inserted, reordered, the file was truncated, or it does not match an external anchor. The message names the file, the first broken entry index and the reason. A log in this state must not be appended to; investigate it instead.
- [`AuditLogFile`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Diagnostics/AuditLogFile.cs#L114) (class): The on-disk form of the hash-chained audit log (R075): reading, verifying and saving files. Appending to a live log is done by `AuditLogWriter`. File format (`FormatTag`): UTF-8 with no byte-order mark, one JSON object per line, each line ended by a single LF ('\n'). Each object has exactly these fields, in this order: `format` (always `FormatTag`), `seq` (0-based integer), `runUtc` (round-trip "o" timestamp ending in Z), `stateUtc` (same, or null), `provenance` (a `ProvenanceTag` name), `summary`, `prevHash` and `hash`. The hash is exactly the in-memory `AuditLog` hash, so a file and an in-memory log holding the same records are interchangeable. Canonical lines. The writer always produces the same bytes for the same entry, and the verifier re-encodes every parsed entry and requires the line to match byte for byte. So even a change that the hash does not cover (extra spaces, reordered fields, a timestamp written in a different but equal form) is reported, rather than silently accepted. What verification can and cannot see. Any edit, deletion, insertion or reordering of an entry, and any cut through the middle of a line, breaks the chain at a specific entry and is reported with that index. Removing whole entries from the END of the file leaves a shorter but internally consistent chain, and rewriting the entire file with freshly computed hashes leaves a different but consistent chain; neither can be seen from the file alone. Pass an `AuditAnchor` recorded elsewhere to catch both.
- [`ChainVerifier`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Diagnostics/AuditLogFile.cs#L311) (class): GR-859: the chain state of one verification pass, fed one complete line (without its '\n') at a time. It keeps every entry only when asked to; otherwise just the count, the head hash and the two hashes an anchor check can need (the anchored entry's and the one before it), which are all a result ever reports.

### src/GridSim.Core/Diagnostics/AuditLogWriter.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Diagnostics`. 271 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Diagnostics/AuditLogWriter.cs).

- [`AuditLogWriter`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Diagnostics/AuditLogWriter.cs#L30) (class): The append-only, on-disk audit log (R075). Each `Append` chains a new entry to the current tail with the same hash as the in-memory `AuditLog`, writes it as one JSON line (format in `AuditLogFile`), and flushes it to disk before returning, so an entry the caller has been handed is already durable. Single writer, enforced. Exactly one writer may have a given log open at a time, across threads and across processes. Opening takes an exclusive lock on a companion file (`<log>.lock`, which is left in place and holds no data; the lock is the open handle, not the file's existence) and opens the log itself with write access for this writer only. A second `Open` on the same log, from this or any other process, fails loud with `InvalidOperationException`. Readers (`AuditLogFile.Verify`) may still read the log while it is open. Thread safe. Several threads may call `Append` on one writer; appends are serialised by a lock, so the sequence numbers and the chain stay intact whatever the interleaving. Refuses a damaged log. Opening an existing file verifies it first. A log that does not verify (edited, reordered, truncated, a torn last line from a crash) is never appended to: `Open` throws `AuditLogTamperException` naming the first broken entry, so the damage is investigated rather than buried under new entries. If a write fails part-way, the writer marks itself faulted and refuses every later append for the same reason. No secrets. The summary is stored as plain text (it is hashed, not encrypted). Never put a password, key, token or connection string into it.

### src/GridSim.Core/Diagnostics/AuditRecorderOptions.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Diagnostics`. 88 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Diagnostics/AuditRecorderOptions.cs).

- [`AuditRecorderOptions`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Diagnostics/AuditRecorderOptions.cs#L24) (record): The optional parts of a product audit run (`AuditRunRecorder`): where the entries are forwarded, and how the anchor is signed and checked. Every product path that opens an audit log (the CLI's `--audit-log`, the web host's `Audit:LogPath`) builds one of these from its own flags or settings, so the same controls are reachable from both. The default (`None`) is exactly the plain anchored log. Forwarding (NCSC CAF C1). `Sinks` are notified after each entry is durably on disk, in order. The on-disk chain stays authoritative: a sink that fails never fails the append (see `IAuditSink`). GridSim ships `JsonLinesAuditSink` (an append-only copy for a SIEM collector or a write-once mount) and the incident sinks in `GridSim.Core.Diagnostics.Incident`. Signed anchor (C1, the joint-rewrite limit). With `AnchorSigningKey` (an ECDSA P-256 PRIVATE key) the recorder writes a detached signature over the anchor after every append (`SignedAuditAnchor`, file `SignaturePath`). With `AnchorVerificationKey` (the PUBLIC key) it refuses, before the run does any work, a log whose anchor has no signature or a signature that does not verify: a rewrite of the log and its anchor together, without the private key, is then detected. A host that holds the private key only protects against an attacker who does not; the strongest form keeps the private key off the host and signs at checkpoints (the assurance documents say which applies).

### src/GridSim.Core/Diagnostics/AuditRunRecorder.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Diagnostics`. 486 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Diagnostics/AuditRunRecorder.cs).

- [`AuditRunRecorder`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Diagnostics/AuditRunRecorder.cs#L25) (class): Records ONE product run (a CLI verb such as `estimate`) in the persistent audit log (R075 wiring). Lifecycle. `Start` opens the log BEFORE the run does any work, so a tampered, locked or misplaced log stops the run before it produces anything (fail loud). The run then adds its inputs (`AddInput`), its one-line result (`SetOutcome`) and, when it has one, the grid instant it describes (`StateTimeUtc`). `Finish` writes the single entry and closes the log. `Finish` runs exactly once however it is reached: a normal return, an early return, a process exit from deep inside a flag parser, or an unhandled exception all record the run, and a second call does nothing. A failed run is recorded too: a refused or failed run is an audit event in its own right. Entry layout (via `AuditEvent.FormatSummary`): the outcome is `exit=<code>`, followed by the run's own outcome text when it set one, so the exit code is always in the hashed record. Thread safety. All members are serialised by one lock: `Finish` may be reached from a process-exit handler on another thread while the run is still adding its outcome.

### src/GridSim.Core/Diagnostics/CrashLog.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Diagnostics`. 136 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Diagnostics/CrashLog.cs).

- [`CrashLog`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Diagnostics/CrashLog.cs#L28) (class): Writes a crash log when a GridSim app (the CLI or the desktop app) hits an exception that nothing handled (F08). A crash is a defect, so it must stay loud: the caller still lets the process fail (the CLI keeps the runtime's non-zero crash exit; the desktop app shows the message and closes). What this adds is evidence that survives the crash: one plain-text file holding the exception (type, message, stack, every inner exception), the exact build (`BuildInfo.InformationalVersion`), the runtime, the OS, the command-line arguments and the time, so a bug report can quote it instead of a half-remembered screen. Where the file goes, in order: the folder named by the `GRIDSIM_CRASH_DIR` environment variable, when it is set (used by the tests, and by anyone who wants crash logs somewhere specific); otherwise `%LOCALAPPDATA%\GridSim\crash` on Windows (`~/.local/share/GridSim/crash` on Linux, `~/Library/Application Support/GridSim/crash` on macOS), next to the licence file; otherwise, if that cannot be created, the system temporary folder. On Linux and macOS a folder created there is owner-only and the file is created new and owner-only (GR-839), so another user of a shared `/tmp` cannot read it or redirect it. Writing the log must never throw: a failure to write it returns `null` and the caller still reports the crash.

A file written to a temporary name, flushed and then moved over the old one is durable only once the directory entry that names it is on disk too; POSIX gives that only through fsync on the directory, which .NET has no API for (it refuses to open a directory as a file), hence the two libc calls. On Windows the rename is a journalled metadata change on NTFS and there is no directory handle to flush, so this is a no-op there. Fail loud: a directory that cannot be opened or flushed throws `IOException` naming it and the error number.

The mark is an entry in `Exception.Data`, so the exception keeps its type and message and every caller that catches or asserts the type sees exactly what it did before. The real-time DSE engine counts a marked `InvalidOperationException` as a failed window when it continues on error; an unmarked one (a programming fault) fails the run loudly instead of being counted.

### src/GridSim.Core/Diagnostics/ForwardInferenceGuard.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Diagnostics`. 157 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Diagnostics/ForwardInferenceGuard.cs).

- [`ForwardInferenceReason`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Diagnostics/ForwardInferenceGuard.cs#L4) (enum): Why a `ForwardInferenceException` was thrown.
- [`ForwardInferenceException`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Diagnostics/ForwardInferenceGuard.cs#L25) (class): Thrown when data newer than the historical horizon (or with no date at all) is fed to the engine.
- [`ForwardInferenceGuard`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Diagnostics/ForwardInferenceGuard.cs#L56) (class): The hard "no forward inference" invariant. GridSim is a historical state estimator: it may only ever process data that is at least `HorizonHours` old. Anything newer - recent OR future - is rejected at the ingestion boundary, so the engine is structurally incapable of nowcasting or prediction. It can only ever lag reality. Every dated input (event onsets, GDA time-series stamps, NESO frequency samples) passes through here, so "it can only ever lag" is enforced by construction, not policy. Why SEVEN DAYS + ONE HOUR (widened from 25 h, 2026-07-14, owner decision): the horizon is a defence, and widening it strengthens the defence twice over. First, forward-inference defence in depth: a state that is at least a week old cannot be mistaken for - or repurposed as - a nowcast under ANY publication-lag or clock-skew argument; every data source the project consumes has fully published well inside a week, so the guard margin is no longer comparable to the lag of the slowest feed. Second, reduced operational constraint space: a week-lagged state carries no operationally actionable information (unit commitment, outage windows, market positions and constraint patterns have all rolled over), so the system's entire output space sits outside the envelope an operational or market-sensitive reading could attach to. The extra hour keeps a full settlement week strictly behind the boundary across DST transitions.

### src/GridSim.Core/Diagnostics/IAuditSink.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Diagnostics`. 62 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Diagnostics/IAuditSink.cs).

- [`IAuditSink`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Diagnostics/IAuditSink.cs#L22) (interface): A secondary observer of audit entries as they are durably appended to an `AuditLogWriter` (NCSC CAF C1: forwarding the evidence trail to a monitoring function). A deploying party supplies an implementation to forward entries to a SIEM / SOC, a syslog collector, or a write-once (WORM) or remote append-only store, so a rewrite of the local log and its anchor together can still be caught against an independent copy (see `AuditLogFile` section 6.2 of `docs/assurance/caf-mapping.md`). The on-disk chain is authoritative; a sink is secondary. A sink is notified only AFTER the entry is durable on disk and the hash chain has advanced, so a sink can never affect what is recorded. A sink that throws does NOT fault the log or fail the append: the authoritative record must not depend on an external forwarder being reachable (a syslog outage must not stop estimation). The writer keeps the first sink error for inspection (`AuditLogWriter.LastSinkError`); it does not hide it, but it does not let it corrupt the durable trail. This is the one deliberate departure from the fail-loud rule in the audit path, and it is deliberate: durability of the primary record outranks delivery to a secondary. No secrets. An entry's summary is plain text (hashed, not encrypted). A sink that forwards it off the host must treat it as it would any audit record; it must never be used to carry a credential, which the writers already forbid.
- [`NullAuditSink`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Diagnostics/IAuditSink.cs#L32) (class): A sink that does nothing. The default when no monitoring forwarder is configured.
- [`BufferedAuditSink`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Diagnostics/IAuditSink.cs#L45) (class): A sink that keeps every observed entry in memory, in order. For tests and for an in-process consumer such as `SecurityEventMonitor` that aggregates the trail without a disk round trip.

GR-363 (November 2026): the burst monitor is wired with a sliding window of `DefaultBurstWindow` (one hour), so a burst of one kind that clears re-arms the latch and a later burst raises its own incident, instead of the first burst of a long-running host silencing that kind for good. The window is read only from the entries' own timestamps, so the same trail always gives the same incidents.

Every series the evidence engine emits carries one of these so a reviewer can trust the provenance. `Interpolated`/`Synthetic` data may improve replay fidelity but must never be fed to the forward integrator as if it were a recorded input. The trust order Recorded > DerivedFromRecorded > Interpolated, Synthetic > CuratedPlaceholder, the rule that trust only moves down (a datum gains a stronger tag only by being re-sourced from a primary record), and the rule that a `Counterfactual` is never an input to another replay are rules for authors and reviewers: each tag is fixed at the site that creates the datum, and no code ranks tags or refuses an input by its tag. The one combinator that merges two tags, `AvoidedCost.Weakest`, never returns a tag stronger than either input (pinned by `Doc17TextHygieneTests`), and the model-output records default to non-recorded tags (FrequencyExportMeta: Synthetic, H0StudyMeta: Counterfactual, a storage replay: Counterfactual). Technical chapter 8 lists every site that assigns or computes a tag. CF5 (N327 part 2): the checkable parts are now code, in `ProvenanceTrust`: the trust ranks, the refusal of an output tag (Counterfactual, UnvalidatedAtScale) as an input (at the replay entry and the case editor's save gate) and a downgrade-only check for combinators. What stays a reviewer rule is listed there.

### src/GridSim.Core/Diagnostics/ProvenanceTrust.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Diagnostics`. 158 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Diagnostics/ProvenanceTrust.cs).

- [`ProvenanceTrust`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Diagnostics/ProvenanceTrust.cs#L35) (class): N327 part 2 (CF5): the provenance trust rules of technical chapter 8 ("Trust order and the downgrade-only rule"), in code. Until CF5 they were reading rules for authors and reviewers only (D-DOC-212); these are the parts that can be checked mechanically without changing what any valid input does: The trust order Recorded > DerivedFromRecorded > Interpolated = Synthetic > CuratedPlaceholder (`Rank`). `ProvenanceTag.Counterfactual` and `ProvenanceTag.UnvalidatedAtScale` are OUTPUT tags (`IsOutputOnly`): they label a conclusion and have no place in the input order. An output tag is never an input (`RequireInput`): a counterfactual is never an input to another replay, and an unvalidated-at-scale result is never fed back as data. Enforced at the replay entry (`ReplayValidator.Validate`, every tag of the event) and at the case editor's save gate (any provenance tag in a case file). Trust only moves down (`RequireNotRaised`): a value computed from inputs may carry at most the weakest input's trust. For combinators that merge tags. N359 (CF6): the three rules CF5 left to reviewers are now code too: an event is replayed as a reproduction of history only when its effective tag (the weakest of its parts, `ReplayValidator.EffectiveProvenance`, `Weakest`) is Recorded or DerivedFromRecorded (`ReplayValidator.RequireRecordedReplay`, called by replay-event, refusing by name); the study verbs (scenario, fleet, evidence, h0-study) accept a placeholder or synthetic event and their outputs inherit the weaker tag (main's ruling on CF6-F3 / F4); a VoLL figure keeps its policy tag (`AvoidedCost.VollBaseProvenance`): `--voll-source` records the citation but no longer raises the tag, and `AvoidedCost.FromLfddAvoided` refuses a raised VoLL tag through `RequireNotRaised`; the harmonic export headline is the weakest of its sources' tags among Recorded / DerivedFromRecorded (else CuratedPlaceholder), checked by `RequireNotRaised` (`HarmonicExport.HeadlineProvenance`); it used to read Recorded when some sources were only DerivedFromRecorded.

Shared by the audit trail and the incident router so there is one scale.
- [`SecurityEventKind`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Diagnostics/SecurityEvent.cs#L27) (enum): The kind of security event recorded in the audit trail and routed as an incident. Each value names a detection GridSim can make from inside the engine; mapping a kind to an OES incident category and severity is the incident router's job (CAF C1 security monitoring, C2 threat hunting, D1 response).
- [`SecurityAudit`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Diagnostics/SecurityEvent.cs#L81) (class): Records ONE security event in the persistent audit log, so the trail carries one entry per security event with its reason, not only one entry per run (NCSC CAF C1; closes the 6.1 (b)-(f) gap in `docs/assurance/caf-mapping.md`). The entry's outcome is a fixed, parseable layout so a `SecurityEventMonitor` can read the kind and severity back: `event=<kind> severity=<severity> reason=<free text>`, written through `AuditEvent.FormatSummary` with `action=security`. Restriction aware. A security entry carries no future-dated grid claim: a horizon-violation event records the horizon and the rejected stamp inside its free-text reason, never as the entry's `StateTimeUtc`. The optional `stateTimeUtc` is for an event that genuinely concerns a permitted-age (present/past) grid instant; leave it null for a refusal. No secrets. The reason is plain text (hashed, not encrypted): never put a credential in it.

### src/GridSim.Core/Diagnostics/SignedAuditAnchor.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Diagnostics`. 264 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Diagnostics/SignedAuditAnchor.cs).

- [`SignedAuditAnchor`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Diagnostics/SignedAuditAnchor.cs#L26) (class): An ECDSA signature over an `AuditAnchor`, kept in a detached file beside the log (`<log>.anchor.sig` by default). This closes the honest limit stated in `docs/assurance/caf-mapping.md` section 6.2: the plain hash chain and the `AuditAnchorFile` are tamper-EVIDENT, but an actor who can rewrite both the log and its anchor can recompute a consistent pair. Signing the anchor with a key the host does not hold makes that joint rewrite detectable: the attacker can forge the chain and the anchor, but not the signature. Trust model (the same as licensing). The signature is made with an ECDSA P-256 private key held OFF the host (an offline station, an HSM, or an OS keychain reached through an `ISecretStore`); the host keeps only the PUBLIC key and verifies. The strongest form signs the anchor offline at a checkpoint or rotation; a host that signs continuously must hold the key and then only gains protection against an attacker without that key. This class provides the primitive; the deployment decides where the key lives, and the assurance document states which protection applies to a given deployment. Format (one ASCII line, newline-terminated): `gridsim-audit-anchor-sig/1 count=<N> head=<hash> sig=<base64>`. The signed bytes are the exact `AuditAnchorFile.Format(AuditAnchor)` line, so the signature is bound to that precise anchor. The signature is ECDSA P-256 / SHA-256, IEEE-P1363 fixed 64 bytes, as the licence keys use.

### src/GridSim.Core/Diagnostics/SupplyChain/BuildProvenance.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Diagnostics.SupplyChain`. 177 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Diagnostics/SupplyChain/BuildProvenance.cs).

- [`BuildProvenance`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Diagnostics/SupplyChain/BuildProvenance.cs#L28) (record): What a running GridSim binary can attest about how it was built (NCSC CAF A3 asset management, A4 supply chain, and A4.b "secure software development and support", which at Achieved requires a supplier to attest to the authenticity and integrity of its software). It correlates an emitted result or audit entry to the exact build that produced it, and is the input the `ComplianceAttestation` binds the compliance manifest to. Everything here is deterministic: the version and commit come from the assembly's informational version (`BuildInfo`), the toolchain from the .NET SDK version stamped into the assembly at build time (assembly metadata `GridSimBuildSdk`, not the runtime the binary happens to run on), and the SBOM hash from a build-time assembly metadata attribute the release workflow injects. There is no wall-clock read, so two builds of the same commit with the same SDK and SBOM produce the same `BuildHash`, on any machine. What the build hash is, and is not. It is an IDENTITY LABEL: a short, deterministic name for "this version, this commit, this SDK, this SBOM", to correlate a result or an audit entry with the release it came from. It is NOT an integrity proof: it is computed from metadata strings, not from the bytes of the shipped files, so a modified binary that keeps the same metadata reports the same hash. Integrity of a download comes from outside the binary: the signed build-provenance attestation over every Release file (`gh attestation verify`), the SHA256SUMS list, and the Authenticode signature of the Windows binary.

### src/GridSim.Core/Diagnostics/SupplyChain/ComplianceAttestation.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Diagnostics.SupplyChain`. 102 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Diagnostics/SupplyChain/ComplianceAttestation.cs).

- [`ComplianceAttestation`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Diagnostics/SupplyChain/ComplianceAttestation.cs#L30) (record): What a running GridSim binary states about its own build and control set (NCSC CAF A4.b). It binds the build identity (`BuildProvenance`) to the compliance manifest (`ComplianceManifest`): the version, the commit, the build hash (an identity label, not an integrity proof: see `BuildProvenance`), the SBOM hash and the manifest hash, plus how many in-scope controls the manifest records as Achieved. A reviewer reads it from a running binary (`gridsim compliance verify` or the web endpoint). Whether a downloaded binary is the released one is checked outside it: the signed build-provenance attestation and SHA256SUMS of the Release. The verdict. `IsCompliant` needs BOTH (1) a release build (`IsReleaseBuild`: a well-formed SBOM hash was injected, the commit is known and the source tree was clean at build time) and (2) every in-scope control recorded as Achieved. Bug #196: a release build does NOT by itself prove that the full test matrix passed. release.yml injects the SBOM hash only after the matrix, but anyone can build with an SBOM hash outside it, as the 2.1.000 RC-1 release was; that is why supply-chain and secure-sdlc-attestation are recorded PartiallyAchieved until a release is published through release.yml. The manifest's statuses are maintained by hand in source, so (2) is an inventory, not a measurement: a control whose product wiring is missing is recorded PartiallyAchieved, and the verdict then reads NOT COMPLIANT. A local or development build never attests compliance, whatever the manifest says.

The statuses are maintained BY HAND, here, from what the product paths actually do: a control is Achieved only when a shipped path (a CLI verb, the web host) exercises it and a test evidences that path; a primitive that no host uses yet is PartiallyAchieved with the gap in its description. The gate then refuses to call a build compliant until the gap is closed - the same doctrine the estimator applies when it reports `Unobservable` rather than a plausible lie. A release build is produced only after the full test matrix passed, so every named evidencing test was green for it (`ComplianceAttestation`); `ComplianceAttestationTests` checks every named test class exists and pins exactly which controls are not yet Achieved, so a status change is always deliberate.

### src/GridSim.Core/Diagnostics/UtcTime.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Diagnostics`. 75 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Diagnostics/UtcTime.cs).

- [`UtcTime`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Diagnostics/UtcTime.cs#L14) (class): The one rule GridSim uses for turning an input `DateTime` into UTC. .NET's `DateTime.ToUniversalTime` treats a `DateTimeKind.Unspecified` value as machine-local time and shifts it by the local offset. Every GridSim timestamp is UTC by contract, so an Unspecified stamp (a parsed naive string, a `new DateTime(y, m, d)` without a kind) is UTC that simply lost its label. Converting it as local made the same input give a different answer on a BST machine than on a UTC server: a bridge start or seek time moved by an hour, and an audit-log hash computed on one machine failed to verify on another. `ForwardInferenceGuard` and `RestrictionReview` already read Unspecified as UTC; this helper is that same rule in one place so every caller agrees.

- [`Dispatcher`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dispatch/Dispatcher.cs#L18) (class): Turns capacities into a balanced dispatch. Non-slack generators run at their chosen output (from `OutputMw`, or capacity x capacity-factor); the slack generator - the marginal plant, gas in GB - is set to make total generation meet demand plus an allowance for losses. The power flow then balances it exactly (the slack bus absorbs the true losses), but starting balanced gives a clean, fast, "natural" steady state and lets us sanity-check the slack stays within its capacity: `BalanceDetailed` reports a marginal target outside the marginal plant's [Pmin, Pmax] (R076; the check was promised here but never made). Multi-slack models: only the FIRST slack bus (in bus order) carries the marginal plant; any other slack bus keeps its generators at their chosen outputs, and the result says how many slack buses there were.

### src/GridSim.Core/Distribution/BranchCurrentDsse.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Distribution`. 275 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Distribution/BranchCurrentDsse.cs).

- [`BranchCurrentEstimate`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Distribution/BranchCurrentDsse.cs#L10) (record): A branch-current DSSE result: per-bus phase voltages plus the estimated per-branch phase currents.
- [`BranchCurrentDsse`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Distribution/BranchCurrentDsse.cs#L36) (class): A branch-current distribution state estimator (Baran-Kelley formulation): the state is the per-phase branch currents rather than the node voltages. On a radial feeder that is simpler, faster and better-conditioned than the node-voltage formulation. It WLS-combines the redundant current-phasor measurements per branch, then recovers the node voltages by a single forward sweep down the radial tree (V_to = V_from - Z * I_from). It cross-validates the node-voltage `ThreePhaseWlsEstimator` to machine precision. A static, measurement-only filter (no review-gate entry). N167 (October 2026): every N062 element is modelled. A measured current is the current into the branch at its From bus; across a regulator and a charged line the forward sweep undoes the regulator ratio and the From-end half of the charging before the series drop, and a lateral drops only on its phases (the others are exactly zero, as in the sweep). Validated on the IEEE 123 Node Test Feeder (N167ExtendedElementSolversTests).

### src/GridSim.Core/Distribution/MultiPhaseGridModelAdapter.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Distribution`. 153 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Distribution/MultiPhaseGridModelAdapter.cs).

- [`MultiPhaseGridModelAdapter`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Distribution/MultiPhaseGridModelAdapter.cs#L30) (class): N062 / R059 (October 2026): an adapter from a positive-sequence `GridModel` to a balanced `MultiPhaseFeeder`, so a radial distribution case held as a GridModel (a MATPOWER feeder such as case33bw, a JSON case) can be solved by the three-phase stack. The lift is exact for a balanced network: in per-unit on the three-phase base, a positive-sequence quantity is the per-phase quantity on the per-phase base, so each phase carries exactly the positive-sequence data. So: a branch r + jx becomes a diagonal 3x3 series impedance (r + jx on every phase, no mutual coupling), and its line charging B a diagonal shunt jB (half at each end, the same pi model); a bus load Pd + jQd becomes the per-phase load (Pd + jQd) / BaseMva on every phase; a bus ZIP load P(V) = Pd (Ap V^2 + Bp V + Cp) becomes three loads, constant-impedance Ap Pd + j Aq Qd, constant-current Bp Pd + j Bq Qd and constant-power Cp Pd + j Cq Qd, which draw exactly the same power at every voltage; a generator at a PQ bus is a constant-power injection (a negative load) Pg + jQg; a bus shunt capacitor Bs above 0 becomes a capacitor bank of Bs / BaseMva per phase; the slack bus is the source, at its voltage setpoint (`VoltageSetpoint`, else its Vm) and its angle VaDeg, rotated by -120 and +120 degrees on phases b and c. What the three-phase sweep cannot represent is REFUSED (an `ArgumentException` naming it), never approximated: a voltage-controlled (PV) bus, an off-nominal tap or a phase shift, a bus shunt conductance or a shunt reactor (Bs below 0), a model that is not one radial tree from a single slack. Out-of-service branches are left out (they carry nothing), as the power flow leaves them out.

### src/GridSim.Core/Distribution/MultiPhaseJsonLoader.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Distribution`. 1170 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Distribution/MultiPhaseJsonLoader.cs).

- [`MultiPhaseFeeder`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Distribution/MultiPhaseJsonLoader.cs#L25) (record): A `MultiPhaseModel` loaded from a `gridsim-dist3ph/1` file, together with the engineering context the per-unit model itself does not carry: the feeder's name and cited source, the three-phase MVA base, each bus's line-to-line kV base, and the authored id of every branch and load (aligned by index with `MultiPhaseModel.Branches` and `MultiPhaseModel.Loads`), so a report can speak in volts and amps and name the elements the author wrote.
- [`MultiPhaseMeasurementSet`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Distribution/MultiPhaseJsonLoader.cs#L78) (record): A measurement set for the three-phase estimators, read from a `gridsim-dist3ph-measurements/1` file.
- [`MultiPhaseJsonLoader`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Distribution/MultiPhaseJsonLoader.cs#L134) (class): EXPERIMENTAL. Strict loader for the `gridsim-dist3ph/1` JSON format, the first way to build a `MultiPhaseModel` from a file (R059). It is a plain System.Text.Json reader in the style of JsonGridLoader, kept deliberately strict: it will move under the v2 schema family (technical chapter 28) later. What the format holds (see user manual ch. 7 and technical ch. 18, "The gridsim-dist3ph/1 feeder file", for a full example; D-DOC-155: this used to cite "technical chapter 18.5", a section number that no longer exists): - "schema": exactly "gridsim-dist3ph/1" (no other version or spelling is accepted); - "name", "description" (cite the data source here), "baseMva" (three-phase MVA base); - "buses": id, baseKvLL, and on exactly one bus a "source" block (the infinite-bus voltage); - "lineCodes": a 3x3 series phase-impedance matrix (r and x) per unit length, in ohm/mile or ohm/km, and optionally (N062) a 3x3 shunt susceptance "b" with "bUnit" uS/mile or uS/km (the line charging); - "lines": from, to, code, length and lengthUnit (ft, mile, m, km), and optionally (N062) "phases" ("abc" by default; "ab", "ac", "bc", "a", "b" or "c" for a lateral, whose code must be zero on the other phases); - "transformers": grounded-wye/grounded-wye, or (1.95.251 / 1.95.252) delta / grounded-wye, at rated ratio (see below); - "switches" (N062): from, to, optional phases, and "closed" (true or false). A closed switch is a branch with no impedance; an open one is not a branch (it is recorded, so a normally-open tie never closes a loop); - "regulators" (N062): from, to, optional phases, "tapStepPercent" and "taps" (one integer per phase, 0 on a phase the regulator does not have): an ideal step-voltage regulator from the From bus to its output bus, voltage ratio 1 + step * tap per phase (`PhaseBranch.StepRegulatorRatio`); - "capacitors" (N062): bus and "kvar" per phase at the bus's nominal voltage (wye, constant susceptance); - "loads": kW and kvar per phase at nominal voltage, "connection" wye or (N062) delta (then the three entries are a-b, b-c, c-a) and "model" constant-power or (N062) constant-current or constant-impedance. A ZIP load is up to three loads on one bus, one of each model. - buses may carry an optional display "name" (N062), for nodes the published data names, such as RG1. Per-unit conversion. Voltages are per-unit of each bus's line-to-neutral base (kV_LL / sqrt 3). Per-phase power is per-unit of BaseMva / 3. So the impedance base is kV_LL^2 / BaseMva ohm and the current base is BaseMva / (sqrt 3 kV_LL). A line's per-unit matrix is (r + jx) * length / Zbase of its (shared) bus kV base. Transformers (1.95.251 / 1.95.252: "d-gy", a delta / grounded-wye at rated ratio with the delta on the From side, step-down or step-up by the rated voltages, is also modelled; see `PhaseBranch.DeltaWyeStepDown` and `PhaseBranch.DeltaWyeStepUp`). A grounded-wye/grounded-wye transformer whose rated kV equal the kV bases of the buses it joins is, in per-unit, exactly its leakage impedance on every phase (the ideal transformer becomes 1:1 and all three sequences pass), so the loader turns it into a diagonal `PhaseBranch` with z = (r% + j x%) / 100 * (BaseMva * 1000 / kVA). That needs no new solver element. N334 (CF5): "oy-od" (open wye / open delta: primaries on From-side phases A and B to earth; the step-down connection only, a step-up is refused, N357) and "od-od" (open delta / open delta) banks are modelled (`PhaseBranch.OpenWyeOpenDelta`, `PhaseBranch.OpenDeltaOpenDelta`). N335 (CF5): "y-d", "d-d", "oy-od" and "od-od" take an optional "windings" array of per-winding {"rPercent", "xPercent"} on the bank's kVA (three, ab / bc / ca, for "y-d" and "d-d"; two, ab / bc, for the open banks) in place of the bank's rPercent / xPercent, for unequal winding impedances (see `TransformerWindings`). Every other connection and magnetising branches are REFUSED with a message saying the sweep does not model them yet, rather than approximated. Strictness. Member names are case-sensitive; an unknown member, a duplicate member, a missing required member, a wrong JSON type, a non-finite or out-of-range number, a matrix that is not 3x3, a duplicate id, an unknown bus or line-code reference, a branch joining a bus to itself, a line joining buses of different kV base, and a network that is not one radial tree from the single source are all errors. Every error names the file and the JSON path of the offending value. Comments are allowed (for annotation); trailing commas are not.
- [`Ctx`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Distribution/MultiPhaseJsonLoader.cs#L1059) (class): Per-file reading context: every accessor checks the type and range and fails with file + path.

The solver-authoritative per-unit model, written exactly: every per-unit number (series impedance and shunt admittance matrices, regulator and transformer ratios, source voltages, load powers, capacitor ratings) as the double the model holds, so `MultiPhaseV2Writer` followed by this reader gives back the same model bit for bit, and the physical context (BaseMva in MVA, each bus's kV base) beside it. That follows the v2 rules: closed unit vocabulary (pu@system, MVA, kV, dimensionless ratios; nothing is converted at load, so no unit outside the vocabulary is ever needed, unlike the v1 file's ohm/mile, ft and kW), provenance on every value (a document default and optional per-element entries; a CuratedPlaceholder note must carry [VERIFY]), unknown members refused, and a byte-stable writer. The v1 file stays the authoring format in physical units. Checks. First the bundled schema (every structural error at once, with JSON pointers); then, with the v1 reader's own context and messages (file and JSON path on every error), what the schema subset cannot say: exact vector and matrix sizes, finite numbers, unique ids (branches and open switches share one id space), bus references, exactly one source, the branch kind rules (see the schema's branch description), lines, switches and regulators joining one kV base, and then the v1 reader's own network checks unchanged: one radial tree, the gy-gy three-wire rule, bus phases from the source outward, and loads and capacitors only on phases their bus has.

### src/GridSim.Core/Distribution/MultiPhaseModel.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Distribution`. 642 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Distribution/MultiPhaseModel.cs).

- [`Phase`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Distribution/MultiPhaseModel.cs#L9) (enum): The phases a bus or branch carries. A full three-wire feeder is `Abc`; single- and two-phase laterals use the subsets (N062, October 2026: `PhaseBranch.Phases` carries them and the three-phase sweep solves only the phases each bus has; a bus's phases are those of the branch feeding it).
- [`PhaseImpedance`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Distribution/MultiPhaseModel.cs#L28) (class): A 3x3 complex phase-impedance (or admittance) matrix - the untransposed series impedance of a distribution line segment, with self terms on the diagonal and mutual coupling off it. A balanced positive-sequence line is `Diagonal` with zero mutuals.
- [`PhaseBus`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Distribution/MultiPhaseModel.cs#L93) (record): A bus in the unbalanced model. A source (substation) bus holds a fixed three-phase voltage; every other bus's voltage is solved.
- [`PhaseBranch`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Distribution/MultiPhaseModel.cs#L149) (record): A radial branch: a series 3x3 phase impedance (per-unit), and, since N062 (October 2026), optionally the phases it carries, a shunt (line-charging) admittance and an ideal step-voltage regulator at its From end. The element, from the From bus to the To bus, is: an ideal per-phase regulator (when `RegulatorRatio` is set; otherwise a straight connection), then a pi section: half of `ShuntY` to earth, the series `Z`, and the other half of `ShuntY` to earth at the To end. With the three optional parameters at their defaults it is exactly the v1 line (three phases, series impedance only), and the sweep does exactly the arithmetic it did before.
- [`PhaseLoadModel`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Distribution/MultiPhaseModel.cs#L310) (enum): How a `PhaseLoad`'s current depends on its voltage (N062, October 2026).
- [`PhaseLoadConnection`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Distribution/MultiPhaseModel.cs#L324) (enum): How a `PhaseLoad` is connected (N062, October 2026).
- [`PhaseLoad`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Distribution/MultiPhaseModel.cs#L345) (record): A load: per-phase complex power at nominal voltage (per-unit), and since N062 (October 2026) how it depends on voltage and how it is connected. With the defaults it is the v1 constant-power wye load. A ZIP load is written as up to three loads on the same bus (one constant-power, one constant-current, one constant-impedance), which is what a ZIP load is: the sum of the three.
- [`PhaseCapacitor`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Distribution/MultiPhaseModel.cs#L360) (record): A wye-connected shunt capacitor bank (N062, October 2026): a constant susceptance per phase. QPerPhase[p] is the reactive power (per-unit of BaseMva / 3) it delivers at 1 pu line-to-neutral voltage, so its susceptance is B = QPerPhase[p] (per-unit) and it injects I = j B V; at a voltage V it delivers QPerPhase[p] |V|^2.
- [`MultiPhaseModel`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Distribution/MultiPhaseModel.cs#L371) (class): An unbalanced three-phase distribution network: per-phase buses, 3x3-impedance radial branches, and loads. A separate model path from the positive-sequence `GridModel` - the transmission engine is untouched. v1 covered radial three-phase line networks with wye constant-power loads; balanced diagonal impedances reduce it to three decoupled positive-sequence sweeps (the non-regression bridge). Since N062 (October 2026) a branch may carry fewer than three phases, a line-charging shunt and an ideal step-voltage regulator, a load may be constant-current or constant-impedance and delta-connected, and shunt capacitors may be added; with none of those the model is exactly the v1 model.
- [`MultiPhaseElement`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Distribution/MultiPhaseModel.cs#L569) (enum): N167 (October 2026): the element kinds of a `MultiPhaseModel` beyond three-phase series-impedance lines and constant-power wye loads (see `MultiPhaseModel.ElementsPresent`).

### src/GridSim.Core/Distribution/MultiPhaseV2Writer.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Distribution`. 425 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Distribution/MultiPhaseV2Writer.cs).

- [`MultiPhaseV2Writer`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Distribution/MultiPhaseV2Writer.cs#L33) (class): N339 (October 2026): writes a `MultiPhaseFeeder` as a `gridsim-dist3ph/2` document (`schemas/v2/dist3ph.schema.json`) that `MultiPhaseJsonLoader.ParseV2` reads back to the same model, bit for bit. Byte-stable. The text is a pure function of the feeder and the provenance: members in a fixed order, every number in its shortest round-trip form (System.Text.Json), two-space indentation, "\n" line ends on every OS and one final newline. Writing the loaded-back feeder again gives the same bytes (pinned by tests). Exact. Every per-unit double the model holds is written as that double; the order of buses, branches, capacitors and loads is the model's (the solver sums in that order). Optional members are written only when they differ from the reader's absence rule (phases abc, no shunt, no regulator, transformer ratio 1), so absence and presence read back to the same record. A model the v2 form cannot hold is REFUSED by name (`InvalidDataException`), never written in part: a non-finite number, a branch with two transformer flags, a transformer ratio on a branch that is not a transformer element, or a branch kind the format does not know. Whatever the reader would refuse (for example a line with a regulator) is refused by the reader on the round trip, which is why the CLI and the tests always read the written text back and compare (`FirstDifference`). Provenance. A feeder read from a v2 file carries its provenance and it is written back as read. A feeder from a v1 file or a lifted case carries none, and the caller MUST then say what it is (`provenanceForUnprovenanced` of `ToJson`): GridSim never invents a tag. Giving one for a feeder that already has its own is refused too (which one would win would be a guess).

### src/GridSim.Core/Distribution/SequenceFaultStudy.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Distribution`. 277 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Distribution/SequenceFaultStudy.cs).

- [`SlgFaultResult`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Distribution/SequenceFaultStudy.cs#L14) (record): The result of a single-line-to-ground fault study at a bus.
- [`SequenceFaultStudy`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Distribution/SequenceFaultStudy.cs#L31) (class): Sequence-network fault study on a radial three-phase model - the earth-fault analysis a positive-sequence phasor model declines. It derives each line's sequence impedances (z1 = z2 = z_self - z_mutual, z0 = z_self + 2 z_mutual) from its 3x3 phase impedance, accumulates the Thevenin sequence impedances along the radial path from the (infinite-bus) source to the fault, and applies the classic single-line-to-ground connection I0 = I1 = I2 = E1 / (Z0 + Z1 + Z2 + 3 Zf), fault current = |3 I1|. N167 (October 2026): shunt elements are neglected - loads of every kind (constant power, constant current, constant impedance, wye or delta), shunt capacitors and line charging - so the fault current is that of the series path alone, from the given prefault E1. That was always the study's treatment of loads; it now also applies to the N062 shunt elements instead of refusing them. (The matching rule of IEC 60909-0, which neglects line capacitances and non-rotating loads in the positive- and negative-sequence networks, is [VERIFY]: the standard is not in docs/reference, N136.) A closed switch is a zero series impedance. A single- or two-phase branch or a step-voltage regulator on the path to the fault is refused, naming the branch.
- [`FaultSummary`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Distribution/SequenceFaultStudy.cs#L90) (record): All four shunt-fault current magnitudes (per-unit) at a bus, for a bolted (or Zf) fault.

### src/GridSim.Core/Distribution/ThreePhaseSigmaChecks.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Distribution`. 71 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Distribution/ThreePhaseSigmaChecks.cs).

- [`ThreePhaseSigmaChecks`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Distribution/ThreePhaseSigmaChecks.cs#L17) (class): N264 (October 2026): the measurement-sigma check shared by the three-phase estimators (`ThreePhaseWlsEstimator` and `BranchCurrentDsse`). Both weight a measurement by 1 / sigma^2. A sigma of 0 gave an infinite weight (and NaN everywhere it met a zero), a negative sigma a valid-looking positive weight from a meaningless input, a NaN sigma a NaN weight, and an infinite one a weight of 0 (the measurement silently ignored). The JSON loader (MultiPhaseJsonLoader) already refuses a sigmaPu that is not above 0, so only Core callers could pass such a value; they are now refused here too, by name, before any arithmetic. A sigma so small or so large that 1 / sigma^2 is not a finite positive number (below about 1e-154 or above about 1e154) is refused for the same reason: its weight would be infinite or 0. Every sigma that worked before is accepted unchanged and nothing is computed differently, so every accepted estimate is bit for bit what it was.
