- [`IMultiPhaseSolver`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Distribution/ThreePhaseSweep.cs#L88) (interface): The three-phase power-flow solver seam (parallel to the positive-sequence IPowerFlowSolver), so alternative unbalanced solvers can slot in behind one contract.
- [`ThreePhaseSweepOptions`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Distribution/ThreePhaseSweep.cs#L95) (record): Knobs for the three-phase sweep.
- [`ThreePhaseSweep`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Distribution/ThreePhaseSweep.cs#L128) (class): A three-phase backward/forward-sweep power flow for radial distribution networks - the matricial generalisation of `PowerFlow/BackwardForwardSweep.cs`. Backward sweep accumulates per-phase branch currents from the constant-power wye loads (I = conj(S/V) per phase); forward sweep drops voltage across each 3x3 series impedance (V_child = V_parent - Z * I_branch). On a balanced diagonal model it reduces to three decoupled positive-sequence sweeps - the non-regression bridge to the transmission engine. N062 (October 2026) elements, each added only where the model has it, so a v1 model is solved with exactly the arithmetic it always was: single- and two-phase laterals (only the phases a bus has are solved; the others are exactly zero); line charging as a pi section (half the shunt admittance at each end, a constant-admittance node current); ideal step-voltage regulators at a branch's From end (output voltage ratio times input, input current ratio times output); constant-current and constant-impedance loads, wye or delta (defined at nominal voltage); and wye shunt capacitors (constant susceptance). A closed switch is a branch with zero series impedance. Validated against the IEEE 123 Node Test Feeder's published results (docs/reference S289; see MultiPhaseIeee123Tests).

- [`ThreePhaseWlsResult`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Distribution/ThreePhaseWlsEstimator.cs#L30) (record): The solved three-phase estimate: per-bus complex phase voltages and convergence metadata.
- [`ThreePhaseMeasurementResidual`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Distribution/ThreePhaseWlsEstimator.cs#L64) (record): D-DOC-217 (October 2026): the residual of one measurement at a three-phase WLS estimate.

State is the per-phase rectangular voltage [Vre, Vim] of every non-source bus (the source voltage is the fixed reference). Per-phase voltage magnitudes fix the magnitudes (nonlinear rows); per-phase branch current phasors - linear in the rectangular state via the 3x3 series admittance Y = Z^-1 - anchor the angles the magnitude-only telemetry cannot. A Gauss-Newton loop resolves the state; on a network solved by `ThreePhaseSweep` a full consistent measurement set recovers the truth to machine precision. A static, measurement-only filter - no Dynamics/ process model, so no review-gate entry (see `GridSim.Core.Diagnostics.RestrictionReview`).

### src/GridSim.Core/Distribution/TransformerWindings.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Distribution`. 198 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Distribution/TransformerWindings.cs).

- [`TransformerWindings`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Distribution/TransformerWindings.cs#L37) (class): N335 / N334 (CF5): the series (leakage) impedance of a transformer element whose To side is a delta (full or open), from its PER-WINDING impedances, as the 3x3 line-to-neutral equivalent the three-phase sweep's forward pass drops across (V_to = TransformerOutput(V_from) - Z I_to). Derived from Kersting's generalised-matrix construction (W. H. Kersting, Distribution System Modeling and Analysis, the delta / delta, ungrounded wye / delta and open wye / open delta sections), written out here in full because no published reference result is on disk: The To-side delta windings ab, bc, ca carry the winding currents I_D = (I_ab, I_bc, I_ca); the line currents are I_a = I_ab - I_ca, I_b = I_bc - I_ab, I_c = I_ca - I_bc. Each winding's terminal voltage is its ideal EMF less its own drop, V_xy = E_xy - Zw_xy I_xy, so the line-to-line drop is Zw_D I_D (Zw_D = diag of the winding impedances). The line currents fix I_D only up to a common circulating current k (the three-wire To side has I_a + I_b + I_c = 0): I_D = M I_abc + k (1, 1, 1) with the particular solution M I_abc = (0, I_b, -I_a). The connection fixes k: - delta / delta: the HV delta's EMFs sum to zero, so KVL round the LV delta gives sum Zw_xy I_xy = 0: k = -(z . M I) / sum z, the circulating current that unequal windings carry (zero when they are equal); - ungrounded wye / delta: each primary winding current is its secondary winding current over the ratio, and the floating neutral makes them sum to zero, so sum I_D = 0: k = -(sum M I) / 3; the neutral-point shift then adds (z . I_D) / 3 to every winding EMF, so the line-to-line drop is (Zw_D - (1/3) 1 z^T) I_D; - open (two windings ab, bc; no ca winding): I_ca = 0, so I_D = (I_a, -I_c, 0) exactly, and the open side's line-to-line voltage closes the triangle: drop_ca = -(drop_ab + drop_bc). The line-to-line drop d is turned into the line-to-neutral equivalent of zero zero-sequence (the convention every voltage on a three-wire GridSim bus uses) by Kersting's W = (1/3) [[2, 1, 0], [0, 2, 1], [1, 0, 2]], so Z = W d / I. Units: each winding impedance is given in per-unit on the bank's per-phase power base and the To side's voltage base, exactly the number the equal-winding element puts on its diagonal (PhaseImpedance.Diagonal(z) in the loader). A delta winding sits across a line-to-line voltage, so on the line-to-neutral impedance base it is three times that number (Zw = 3 z); with all three equal the equivalent is z on every phase, which is the existing element. The equivalent holds for three-wire To-side currents (I_a + I_b + I_c = 0), which the sweep guarantees below a delta secondary (it refuses wye loads, capacitors, charging and regulators there). [VERIFY] against Kersting's worked examples once the book section is on disk; self-consistency is proved in Cf5OpenAndUnequalTransformerTests (the equal-winding limit is the existing element bit for bit, the winding losses equal the equivalent's, power balances).

- [`AssetFrequencyResult`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/AssetFrequencyDynamics.cs#L15) (record): The excursion plus what the authored-asset fleet did: trips, net FFR at the nadir, per-class rollups.
- [`AssetFrequencyDynamics`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/AssetFrequencyDynamics.cs#L38) (class): The batch (pre-computed-trace) swing solve WITH the authored per-asset dynamics fleet - the centre-of-inertia twin of `FrequencyDynamics.Simulate` plus the `pAssetFleet` term. It is a faithful copy of `FrequencyDynamics.Simulate` with two additions appended last in the imbalance sum: the fleet's net swing power, and the cumulative Loss-of-Mains trip deficit (lost dispatched Pg). With an empty fleet both are identically `0.0`, so the trajectory is bit-for-bit the baseline (`x + 0.0 - 0.0 == x`) - the reduction gate. Local frequency is sampled from the COI at the PREVIOUS step's RoCoF/phase (a one-step measurement latency), which also avoids an algebraic loop with the very term it forms.

### src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/ConverterDefaults.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Dynamics`. 115 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/ConverterDefaults.cs).

- [`ConverterDefaults`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/ConverterDefaults.cs#L38) (class): The default control parameters GridSim's three converter representations fall back to when an asset class (or a caller) does not author them (October 2026 review, WS13: R138, R140, R164, R172). One device, three models. A grid-following converter appears as an average-value EMT model (`Emt.ThreePhaseConverter`), as a dq admittance in the impedance scan (`Impedance.GridFollowingImpedance`) and as a linear block in modal analysis (`SmallSignal.LinearInverterModel`). Before this table each model carried its own bare literals. They are named here, side by side, WITHOUT changing any value, so the differences are visible in one place. One PLL default (R138, October 2026 review; stream B5; Ruling R1: Mark delegated EE calls 2026-10-04). The three models used to fall back to three differently tuned PLLs (EMT 20 Hz, impedance 5 Hz, small-signal 5 Hz; damping 0.707, 0.707 and 1.0), so an EMT run, an impedance scan and a modal result of one unauthored device were not comparable. All three now take `PllBandwidthHz` (20 Hz) and `PllDampingRatio` (0.707), and the small-signal block reads the class's authored PLL damping as the impedance model does. Why 20 Hz and not 5 Hz: (1) it is the value the EMT model, the only one that integrates the PLL itself, was built and validated with; (2) an SRF-PLL of a transmission-connected converter is commonly tuned to a few tens of Hz (zeta = 1/sqrt(2), Kaura and Blasko, "Operation of a phase locked loop system under distorted utility conditions", IEEE Trans. Ind. Appl. 33(1), 1997; Teodorescu, Liserre and Rodriguez, Grid Converters for Photovoltaic and Wind Power Systems, Wiley, 2011, ch. 4 [VERIFY the bandwidth range quoted there]), while a few Hz is a weak-grid retuning; (3) a faster PLL widens the negative-resistance band that destabilises a weak grid (Wen, Boroyevich, Burgos, Mattavelli and Shen, "Analysis of D-Q small-signal impedance of grid-tied inverters", IEEE Trans. Power Electron. 31(1), 2016; Harnefors, Wang, Yepes and Blaabjerg, "Passivity-based stability assessment of grid-connected VSCs - an overview", IEEE JESTPE 4(1), 2016), so for an UNAUTHORED device the screen must not assume the forgiving slow loop: the placeholder errs on the conservative side, and a class that authors its own bandwidth is used as authored. One exception is kept on purpose: the small-signal block's stand-in for the time-domain controller's detection DELAY (bandwidth 1/(2 pi latency), used when a class gives a latency and no PLL bandwidth, as every bundled class does) is critically damped, `SmallSignalDelayEstimatorDampingRatio`, because it represents a pure delay, which has no overshoot, not a PLL. Every value here is a CuratedPlaceholder (literature-typical, not a measured setting). R140 (stream B5): the grid-forming impedance's two unit-inconsistent scalings are replaced by a per-unit derivation on the converter's rating (see `Impedance.GridFormingImpedance`).

### src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Distributed/ClassicalInit.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Dynamics.Distributed`. 692 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Distributed/ClassicalInit.cs).

- [`ClassicalInit`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Distributed/ClassicalInit.cs#L24) (class): Builds the reduced classical-model inputs (`ClassicalMultiMachine`) from a solved power flow. Follows the standard classical transient-stability preparation: 1. loads -> constant shunt admittances `y = conj(S)/|V|^2` folded onto the bus diagonal; 2. each generator -> an internal node behind its transient reactance X'd (added as a reactance branch to its terminal bus); 3. Kron-reduce the augmented network to the generator internal nodes -> the reduced admittance Y; 4. internal EMF `E' = V_t + jX'd*I_t` gives |E'| and the initial rotor angle delta0; 5. mechanical power set to the electrical output at delta0, so an undisturbed run is stationary. Everything is placed on the system base: X'd, H convert from the machine base by the MBase/BaseMva ratio. This is deliberately kept separate from the kernel so the kernel stays validatable against closed-form references without a solve.
- [`Prepared`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Distributed/ClassicalInit.cs#L26) (record): Declared record; see the source and member declarations for its role.
- [`Augmented`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Distributed/ClassicalInit.cs#L342) (class): R007 (stream P, October 2026): the fault-independent part of a classical preparation (see `Augment`): the augmented network's cells, the kept internal nodes, the machine quantities and the unfaulted reduction.
- [`FaultScreen`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Distributed/ClassicalInit.cs#L397) (class): R007 (stream P, October 2026): a classical preparation reused across fault buses. The CCT screen (CLI `stability --screen`) and the single study (which prepares, then searches the CCT at the same bus) used to call `FromSolvedCase` once per fault bus, rebuilding the augmented network and redoing the identical UNFAULTED reduction every time; only the faulted reduction depends on the bus. `ForFault` returns exactly `FromSolvedCase(model, result, xdpMachineBase, faultBusId, holdNonMachines)`, bit for bit, with its own fresh arrays: the fault-independent part is computed once, on the first call, by the very code FromSolvedCase runs, and only the faulted reduction (the same code again) is done per bus; the latest bus's faulted reduction is kept, so asking for the same bus again (the single study) costs a copy. A call that fails leaves nothing cached, so a later call fails again with the same exception, as every FromSolvedCase call would. Making the screen computes nothing and cannot fail on the model, so a caller that never asks for a fault (a model with no generator bus) behaves as before. The model and the solved result must not change while the screen is in use (they are read when the first fault is asked for); the X'd array is copied when the screen is made. Safe to use from several threads (a lock). Not done, because it is not bit-identical: a bolted fault changes one diagonal entry, so the faulted reduction could be had from the unfaulted one by a rank-one (Sherman-Morrison) update, or by resuming a saved elimination state at the fault bus; both round differently from the full reduction.

### src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Distributed/ClassicalMultiMachine.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Dynamics.Distributed`. 285 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Distributed/ClassicalMultiMachine.cs).

- [`ClassicalMultiMachine`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Distributed/ClassicalMultiMachine.cs#L32) (class): Classical multi-machine transient-stability kernel - the per-generator backbone reserved for the small canonical validation cases (WSCC-9, Kundur two-area, IEEE-39), distinct from the domain-reduced COI kernel (`MultiDomainSwing`) that carries GB scale. Each machine is the classical model: a constant voltage `E'angle delta` behind its transient reactance, swinging over the network reduced (Kron) to the generator internal nodes. The electrical power out of machine i is Pe_i = sum_j |E_i||E_j| ( G_ij cos(delta_i-delta_j) + B_ij sin(delta_i-delta_j) ) with the reduced admittance `Y = G + jB`, and the swing per machine (per-unit, H in seconds): ddelta_i/dt = omega_s * omegabar_i domegabar_i/dt = ( P_m,i - P_e,i - D_i*omegabar_i ) / (2 H_i) integrated with classical RK4 for first-swing accuracy - the refinement the domain-reduced kernel defers. A fault is a window [`Fault.OnSeconds`, `Fault.ClearSeconds`) during which a different reduced admittance `Fault.YFaulted` applies (e.g. all-zero for a bolted terminal fault => Pe = 0), after which the network returns to `yReduced`. The window's edges are read with the RMS integrator's R249 tolerance (N047): an RK4 sample within a millionth of a step of an edge counts as having reached it, so the one-ulp rounding of an edge formed as onset + clearing never decides whether a sample sees the fault. This kernel takes ALREADY-REDUCED inputs (H, D, Pm, |E'|, Y_red) so it is validatable in isolation against exact analytic references - the single-machine-infinite-bus mode frequency, the equal-area critical clearing time, and undamped energy conservation - without depending on a power-flow solve. `ClassicalInit` builds those inputs from a solved `Model.GridModel`.
- [`Fault`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Distributed/ClassicalMultiMachine.cs#L35) (record): A three-phase fault as a temporary reduced admittance over a time window.
- [`MachineTrace`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Distributed/ClassicalMultiMachine.cs#L38) (record): Per-machine trajectory: rotor angle delta(t) (rad) and per-unit speed deviation omegabar(t).
- [`Result`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Distributed/ClassicalMultiMachine.cs#L43) (record): Declared record; see the source and member declarations for its role.

- [`CouplingReport`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Distributed/DomainCoupling.cs#L40) (record): R025 (October 2026 review, stream B1): how the inter-domain coupling was obtained, so a report can say whether the per-domain nadirs and RoCoFs rest on the network or on the uniform heuristic. Before R025 the fallback was silent.
- [`DomainCoupling`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Distributed/DomainCoupling.cs#L58) (class): Derives the inter-domain synchronising-stiffness matrix K (MW/rad) from the network. Kron-reduces the bus admittance matrix onto the generator buses (`KronReduction`), then reads the reduced synchronising susceptance (Im Y x base MVA at flat 1 p.u. voltage) across every cross-domain bus pair. This replaces the M1 MVP target-mode heuristic with physically-derived coupling: a stiffer line (smaller reactance) between two domains gives a larger K. Falls back to the M1 uniform target-mode stiffness when the model carries no branch reactance (bare test models) or the reduction yields negligible coupling. The matrix is symmetric, so the tie power it drives is antisymmetric and never moves the centre of inertia (the T1 invariant is preserved).

### src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Distributed/MultiDomainSwing.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Dynamics.Distributed`. 251 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Distributed/MultiDomainSwing.cs).

- [`MultiDomainSwing`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Distributed/MultiDomainSwing.cs#L30) (class): The domain-reduced multi-area centre-of-inertia swing kernel (M1 MVP). Each synchronous speed domain is a coherent mass (E_d) with its own frequency and rotor angle, coupled to the others by antisymmetric tie synchronising power. The system-level forcing (event, governor droop, load damping, TSGB fast response, recorded system response services) is computed from the inertia-weighted COI frequency EXACTLY as the lumped `FrequencyDynamics` does, then distributed across domains so the per-domain updates re-aggregate to the identical COI trajectory. Two provable properties follow from the construction: - the tie power is antisymmetric (sum over domains = 0), so it moves energy between domains without changing the COI - the COI frequency equals the lumped frequency to rounding (T1); - with a single domain there is no tie and the forcing is the whole imbalance on the one mass - identical to the lumped model (T0). (The single-domain case is delegated to FrequencyDynamics by `DistributedInertiaModel` so that reduction is exact, not merely to rounding.) Semi-implicit (symplectic) Euler on the same 20 ms step as the lumped model - energy-bounded, so it stays stable under the stiff physically-derived (Kron-reduced) coupling where plain forward Euler would blow up. The degenerate single-domain path delegates to the lumped forward-Euler model, so the reduction stays exact. Inter-domain synchronising coefficients come from `DomainCoupling` (Kron reduction of the network); RK4 for absolute first-swing accuracy vs published curves is a future refinement alongside the per-machine classical model.
- [`Result`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Distributed/MultiDomainSwing.cs#L32) (record): Declared record; see the source and member declarations for its role.

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Dynamics.Distributed`. 135 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Distributed/PropagationDelay.cs).

A disturbance does not reach the whole system at once: it spreads at a finite wave speed, so distant domains respond later. tau_ij = physical distance / wave speed, with the wave speed derived from the local inertia density (slower where inertia is dense, per the LOS thesis) and CLAMPED to the electromechanical-wave literature band (~500-1500 km/s). PROVENANCE: this overlay is EXPERIMENTAL and UNVALIDATED AT SCALE. The clamp is the honest statement - we assert only that the wave speed lies in the published band; the absolute GB-scale value is not validated (it needs PMU/DFR field data). It is off by default (`DistributedConfig.EnablePropagation`).

This single linear form unifies the trapezoidal and backward-Euler R-L and C rules (see `EmtCompanionStamp`). A pure resistor has `Geq=1/R` and no history (both coefficients zero).

Pure functions of the element parameters and the timestep - validated to machine epsilon against the closed-form RLC transient. All values are per-unit (`L`, `C` in seconds via `X/omega0`, `B/omega0`); the step `dt` is in seconds.

### src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Emt/EmtElement.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Dynamics.Emt`. 64 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Emt/EmtElement.cs).

- [`EmtElement`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Emt/EmtElement.cs#L9) (record): A passive EMT network element addressed by integer node ids (a bus, or `EmtNetwork.Ground` for the reference). Elements are immutable; per-step history lives in the engine, keyed by `Id`. Series capacitance (series compensation, a branch with X < 0) is a `SeriesCapacitorBranch` (R078); line charging and bus shunts are `ShuntElement`s.
- [`SeriesBranch`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Emt/EmtElement.cs#L21) (record): A series R-L branch between two nodes (a line's series arm, a source's internal impedance, or a pure resistor when `L = 0`). Positive current is From->To. Values per-unit; L in seconds (X/w0). `Tap` (R078) is an ideal off-nominal transformer of ratio `Tap : 1` on the From side, in the MATPOWER / `PowerFlow.AdmittanceStamp` convention: the series arm sees `v_From / Tap` at its From end and the From bus carries `i / Tap`, which gives exactly the power-flow stamp `Yff = ys/Tap^2`, `Yft = Ytf = -ys/Tap`, `Ytt = ys` for a real tap. The default 1 is a plain line and leaves every untapped run bit-identical. A branch current probe on a tapped branch reads the series-arm current `i` (the To-side current, before the To-end charging); the From-bus current is `i / Tap`. The engine refuses `L < 0` (use `SeriesCapacitorBranch`), `R = L = 0` (an infinite conductance) and a non-positive or non-finite tap.
- [`SeriesCapacitorBranch`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Emt/EmtElement.cs#L31) (record): A series R-C branch between two nodes (R078): the EMT model of a series-compensated branch, which the phasor data carries as a negative series reactance `X < 0`. The capacitance is `C = 1/(|X|*w0)` (per-unit, in seconds), so at the system frequency its reactance is exactly `-1/(w0*C) = X`. The R and C are in series inside one companion (see `EmtCompanionStamp.SeriesRc`), so no internal node is needed. `Tap` is the same From-side ideal transformer as on `SeriesBranch`. Positive current is From->To. The engine refuses a non-positive or non-finite C or tap.
- [`ShuntElement`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Emt/EmtElement.cs#L36) (record): A shunt to ground at one bus, carrying any of a conductance `G`, a capacitance `C` (line charging half-each-end, or a bus capacitor) and an inductance `L` (a reactor) in parallel. Each non-zero part becomes its own companion branch to ground.
- [`VoltageSource`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Emt/EmtElement.cs#L42) (record): A voltage source at a bus with time-varying EMF `Emf`. A The?venin source (`Rs` > 0) is stamped as its Norton equivalent (a conductance 1/Rs plus a current source Emf/Rs) and provides the network's ground reference; an ideal source (`Rs` = 0) makes its bus a Dirichlet node whose voltage is imposed directly.
- [`CurrentSource`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Emt/EmtElement.cs#L46) (record): An independent current source injecting `Inj`(t) into a bus (returned from ground). Also the seam a future converter/machine Norton model injects through.
- [`BergeronLine`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Emt/EmtElement.cs#L56) (record): A lossless distributed (travelling-wave / Bergeron) transmission line. Unlike a lumped pi section it models finite wave-propagation speed: each end is a surge-impedance resistance (`SurgeImpedance` Zc) to ground plus a history current source carrying the wave that left the OTHER end one travel time (`TauSeconds`) ago. There is no instantaneous coupling between the ends - that is the whole point of a travelling-wave model - so it stamps only a diagonal conductance at each end. Captures reflections (open-end voltage doubling), matched-line absorption and propagation delay exactly.
- [`SwitchElement`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Emt/EmtElement.cs#L63) (record): An ideal switch between two nodes: a conductance that toggles between `Ron` (closed) and `Roff` (open). It stays permanently in the matrix pattern (open = a tiny conductance, not removed), so a switching event changes only the numeric matrix - the fill-reducing ordering is computed once. A shunt fault is a switch from a bus to `EmtNetwork.Ground`: pass `To = EmtNetwork.Ground`, `Ron = R_fault`, and close it with a `SwitchEvent`.

### src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Emt/EmtEngine.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Dynamics.Emt`. 1126 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Emt/EmtEngine.cs).

- [`EmtEngine`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Emt/EmtEngine.cs#L29) (class): The EMT time-domain engine: a Dommel nodal companion-model solver. Each fixed timestep it assembles the real nodal conductance matrix G (constant between switching events) and solves `G | v = i_history` for the instantaneous node voltages, then advances each reactive element's history. The matrix is factored once and back-substituted every step - the amortization that makes microsecond stepping affordable. Governing constraint. An EMT run is Solving under `UnderstandingRestrictions.md`: a forward simulation about the MODEL, not forward inference about reality. Its output is a model trajectory, never a claim about the real grid's future. It sits in the `Dynamics/` seam beside the swing/harmonic tools and does not engage the estimator's restriction-review gate. Any assumed element parameter (e.g. a future converter model) must be tagged `CuratedPlaceholder [VERIFY]`; the passive R/L/C/source/switch elements here are grounded in the model's per-unit data. One engine, one network, one timestep (R077). The network and dt are fixed at construction; `Simulate` refuses an `EmtCase` naming a different network or dt, and refuses a second run on an engine whose state has already advanced unless `Reset` is called first. Branch models (R078). A series arm may carry an off-nominal tap (an ideal From-side transformer, `SeriesBranch.Tap`) and a series-compensated branch is a series R-C arm (`SeriesCapacitorBranch`); with the tap they reproduce the power flow's branch stamp exactly at the system frequency. Untapped branches take the original stamping code path, unchanged.
- [`Kind`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Emt/EmtEngine.cs#L31) (enum): Declared enum; see the source and member declarations for its role.

A build needs at least one source to provide the ground reference.
- [`EmtBuildOptions`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Emt/EmtNetwork.cs#L20) (record): Options for building an EMT network from a `GridModel`.

Why it matters: a load is modelled as a constant impedance, `G = Pd/BaseMva`. For `Pd < 0` that is a NEGATIVE conductance, an element that generates energy in proportion to the voltage across it. It is not passive, so it feeds the network's natural modes and the time-domain run grows without bound (IEEE 145, IEEE 300, several pglib and PEGASE cases; case533mt_hi reached 1.16e75). A negative-impedance load is therefore never built, in either mode.
- [`EmtNetwork`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Emt/EmtNetwork.cs#L57) (class): A resolved EMT network: a node count and the passive elements addressed by node id (0..NodeCount-1, or `Ground` for the reference). This first cut is single-phase (one node per bus); the node indexing is deliberately kept indirect so a later three-phase build can widen each bus to a 3-node block without changing the engine. Built directly for unit tests, or from a `Model.GridModel` via the Slice-2 `FromGridModel` factory.

### src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Emt/EmtUnits.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Dynamics.Emt`. 43 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Emt/EmtUnits.cs).

- [`EmtUnits`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Emt/EmtUnits.cs#L14) (class): Per-unit  <->  physical conversions the EMT engine needs. GridSim stores branch impedance as per-unit R/X/B (no henries/farads), so inductance and capacitance are derived at build time: `L = X/omega0`, `C = B/omega0` (per-unit, in seconds), with `omega0 = 2pi | FrequencyHz`. This mirrors the `w0 = 2pi f0; l = x/w0` derivation in `Dynamics.Impedance.GridImpedanceAssembler`. Physical henries/farads are only recoverable where a bus carries a non-zero base voltage (`Zbase = kV^2/MVA`); per-unit EMT is fully self-consistent, so a case with `BaseKv = 0` runs per-unit-only (physical volts/amps simply aren't reported).

The positive-/negative-sequence impedance is (Rs-Rm)+jomega(Ls-Lm); the zero-sequence is (Rs+2Rm)+jomega(Ls+2Lm).
- [`ThreePhaseShunt`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Emt/ThreePhaseEmt.cs#L24) (record): A per-phase (uncoupled) shunt to ground at a bus: conductance G, capacitance C, inductance L on each of the three phases - a balanced load or shunt.

A single-line-to-ground fault is `Phases = new[]{0}`.

Voltages and currents are per-unit peak phase quantities (a phasor's magnitude is the waveform amplitude), so the RMS and EMT models share one per-unit system.
- [`EmtConverterTrace`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Emt/ThreePhaseEmt.cs#L58) (record): One converter's EMT trajectory, sampled every step: the PLL-measured terminal voltage magnitude, the fundamental active/reactive power and current, and the dip state.

Each bus is three phase nodes; a coupled branch stamps the 3 x 3 companion of its (R,L) matrices, so inter-phase mutual coupling is handled exactly - the difference between this and three independent single-phase circuits, and what lets it reproduce unbalanced faults. Method, guard and CDA-free trapezoidal integration mirror the single-phase `EmtEngine`; this is the abc generalization the scalar engine's node model was designed to allow. Same governing constraint: forward simulation about the model, not inference. Status (R077 decision, October 2026): programmatic and test-only. No CLI verb, web page or desktop view drives this engine, and none is planned in the current programme; it is reached from code (the validation tests EmtConverterTests and ThreePhaseEmtTests are its only callers). It has no `GridSim.Core.Model.GridModel` builder, so it cannot be pointed at a bundled case. Exposing it would need a three-phase network builder from a model (winding connections, zero-sequence data) and a verb with its own validation; until that is specified it stays a library engine. One engine is one run (R077): `Simulate` may be called once. A second call would continue from the end state while restarting time at zero, so it throws `InvalidOperationException`; build a new engine for a new run.

### src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Forming/FormingKernel.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Dynamics.Forming`. 89 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Forming/FormingKernel.cs).

- [`FormingKernel`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Forming/FormingKernel.cs#L20) (class): The single source of truth for the grid-forming (voltage-source) swing step - the forming twin of `Dynamics.SwingKernel`. A grid-forming converter imposes its internal angle on the network, so the grid frequency `f` IS the converter's virtual-rotor frequency; the unified forming swing over the real synchronous COI mass `E` and the virtual former `Ev` (both locked to the same `f`) is (2*(E+Ev)/f0) * df/dt = pForcing - Dtot*(f - f0) with `pForcing` = every imbalance term NOT proportional to `(f-f0)` and `Dtot` = load damping + former damping Dv. The `(f-f0)` damping term is integrated implicitly (A-stable, closed form); the explicitly-integrated proportional responders (governor / FFR / services) remain in `pForcing`, so callers bound the internal step by `SubStepCount` to keep fast, high-gain responders inside their stability region at small `E+Ev`.

### src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/FormingMode.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Dynamics`. 32 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/FormingMode.cs).

- [`FormingMode`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/FormingMode.cs#L19) (enum): Grid-forming frequency-FORMATION mode. `None` is today's floored centre-of-inertia path and is byte-identical to the pre-forming behaviour. Under `Vsm` / `Droop` the grid frequency is BUILT by a voltage-source (grid-forming) converter whose internal angle the network follows, rather than measured off a floored synchronous COI. The forming denominator is `E_real + E_virtual` with NO `Math.Max(1,.)` floor: a genuine (droop-damped) trajectory even at zero real inertia, or a fail-loud error when nothing forms the frequency (E_real == 0 AND E_virtual == 0). `Droop` sets the virtual inertia Ev = 0, so a true power STEP into an islanded (E_real == 0) grid is ill-posed - that specific case fails loud via `Forming.FormingKernel.EffectiveFormingInertiaMwS`. With synchronous mass present (E_real > 0) Droop is perfectly well posed (finite, A-stable). For islanded steps use `Vsm` (Ev > 0).

### src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/FrequencyBands.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Dynamics`. 124 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/FrequencyBands.cs).

- [`FrequencyBands`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/FrequencyBands.cs#L42) (class): N273 (October 2026 review, stream B2; D2 open item O1; Ruling R1: Mark delegated EE calls 2026-10-04): the frequency band set a study or a live display grades a frequency against, for ONE system nominal frequency. The GB set (`Gb`) holds exactly the `FrequencyLimits` constants; `ForNominal` gives the same GB bands about another nominal. Why offsets in hertz about the nominal (the decision, benchmarked). The live loop, the web dashboard and the desktop used the absolute GB edges (49.8 / 50.2 operational, 49.5 / 50.5 statutory, 48.8 LFDD, 49.9 / 50.1 SCADA) for every case, so case9 (60 Hz since D2) sat 10 Hz "above statutory" for ever. The question is how a non-50 Hz system's bands should be expressed. How the reference tools and codes express them: PSS/E: one base frequency per case (the BASFRQ option, 50 or 60 Hz); dynamic models carry speed and frequency as a per-unit DEVIATION from it, and its frequency-relay and load-shedding models take pickups in Hz for the system they protect [VERIFY model names and units against the PSS/E Model Library]. PowerFactory: the nominal frequency is a project / grid setting (50 or 60 Hz); RMS results report frequency in per unit of it and the deviation in Hz, and relay frequency elements are set in Hz [VERIFY against the PowerFactory User Manual, "Nominal frequency" and the frequency-relay element]. ENTSO-E System Operation Guideline (Commission Regulation (EU) 2017/1485, Annex III, Table 1): the standard frequency range, maximum instantaneous and maximum steady-state frequency DEVIATIONS are given in mHz about the 50 Hz nominal (e.g. +/-50 mHz, 800 mHz, 200 mHz for Continental Europe) [VERIFY table number]. NERC (60 Hz): frequency response is measured in MW per 0.1 Hz of deviation (BAL-003-2) and UFLS first stages are set in Hz per region (PRC-006); deviations, again, in Hz about 60 Hz [VERIFY standard versions]. GB itself: ESQCR 2002 (SI 2002/2665) regulation 27(3)(a), "a variation not exceeding 1 per cent above or below the declared frequency", with 27(2) declaring 50 Hz (+/-1 % of 50 Hz, the statutory 49.5 / 50.5 Hz; confirmed on legislation.gov.uk 2026-10-11, N292); the operational +/-0.2 Hz and the 48.8 Hz LFDD first stage (Grid Code OC6.6) are written in Hz. So the common form is a band in HERTZ ABOUT THE SYSTEM'S NOMINAL. A proportional rescale (x 1.2 at 60 Hz) has no support beyond ESQCR's one percentage, and would move the operational and LFDD edges, which every code writes in Hz. GridSim's live loop is a GB tool (GB demand curve, GB SCADA bands, GB services), so its bands are the GB ones, expressed as offsets about the model's nominal: case9 at 60 Hz is graded against 59.8 / 60.2, 59.5 / 60.5, 58.8 and 59.9 / 60.1 Hz. A per-model band set read from case data (a system's own grid code) would need a model field and a schema change; it is recorded as a follow-up in the B2 notes. Every 50 Hz case gets `Gb` itself, so every 50 Hz output is byte-identical. Exactness: for any GB edge e (all between 25 and 100 Hz) the difference e - 50 is exact (Sterbenz: two doubles within a factor of two subtract exactly), and at 50 Hz the edge is returned as the constant itself, never recomputed.

- [`FrequencyFitResult`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/FrequencyConstantsFitter.cs#L22) (record): The outcome of fitting the swing model's nadir/recovery constants to a measured trace.
- [`FrequencyConstantsFitter`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/FrequencyConstantsFitter.cs#L46) (class): Fits the swing model's nadir/recovery constants (`DynamicsConfig.DampingPctPerHz` and, optionally, `DynamicsConfig.ResponsiveFraction` / `DynamicsConfig.GovernorTimeConstantS`) to a measured loss-of-infeed frequency trace, by least-squares over the trajectory that `FrequencyDynamics.Simulate` produces for a known lost infeed at known inertia and demand. This is the tool, not a fitted value. The default `DampingPctPerHz = 1.0` stays UNFITTED until a real GB trip trace (a clean dip to a nadir and recovery, with the concurrent lost infeed and the system inertia both known) is supplied here. The bundled NESO sample is ambient normal operation - it contains no trip to fit against. Fitting `Damping` alone (the default) is well-identified from one trace; jointly fitting all three from a single trace is weakly identified (they trade off against each other), so supply the responsive headroom and governor lag from the operational record and fit only `Damping` unless multiple events are available.

### src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/FrequencyDynamics.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Dynamics`. 341 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/FrequencyDynamics.cs).

- [`DynamicsConfig`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/FrequencyDynamics.cs#L29) (record): Settings for the centre-of-inertia frequency model. PROVENANCE / CALIBRATION STATUS (see `FrequencyCalibrationTests`): `DroopPu` = 5% is the GB Grid Code governor droop - a firm, documented figure, not a fitted one. `DampingPctPerHz` (~1%/Hz), `ResponsiveFraction` (~20% headroom) and `GovernorTimeConstantS` (~8 s) are literature-typical GB values, NOT yet fitted to a measured trip. They set the nadir and the recovery shape (the initial RoCoF depends only on inertia and the loss, so it is unaffected by them). Their uncertainty is roughly a factor of two. The bundled NESO sample (`data/neso/frequency-sample.csv`) is ambient normal-operation data (band ~+/-0.1 Hz, max |RoCoF| ~0.01 Hz/s) - it contains no clean trip step, so it cannot pin the governor/damping constants. It IS enough to confirm the swing-equation RoCoF scale (the calibration test drives an ambient-sized imbalance through `FrequencyDynamics.Simulate` and matches the measured ambient RoCoF). Calibrating the nadir constants against a real loss-of-infeed trace (a genuine dip to a nadir and recovery) is PENDING; do not treat the nadir/settle values as validated until that trace is in hand.
- [`SystemResponseService`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/FrequencyDynamics.cs#L158) (record): One recorded frequency-response service as the swing model integrates it: the published delivery curve - zero inside the deadband, a low-gain segment to `KneeFraction`*`Mw` at `KneeDeviationHz`, the steep segment to full output at `FullDeliveryDeviationHz`, capped beyond - first-order-lagged by `TimeConstantS`. DC: deadband 0.015, knee (0.2, 5%), full at 0.5 Hz. DM/DR have no low-gain segment: knee at the deadband with fraction 0 gives their ramp-from-deadband shape (DM 0.1->0.2 Hz, DR 0.015->0.2 Hz). Knee <= 0 falls back to a droop line through zero.
- [`FrequencyEvent`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/FrequencyDynamics.cs#L170) (record): A power step at a moment in time (negative MW = a generation loss / deficit).
- [`FrequencyResponse`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/FrequencyDynamics.cs#L188) (record): The shape of a frequency excursion: the headline numbers plus the full trajectory.
- [`FrequencyDynamics`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/FrequencyDynamics.cs#L241) (class): A single-mass (centre-of-inertia) swing-equation model of system frequency: df/dt = f / (2E) deltaP , E = HS (the spinning kinetic energy, MWs) After a generation loss deltaP, frequency falls at a rate set entirely by the inertia E - that's the RoCoF. Governor droop (ramping in over a few seconds) and load damping then arrest the fall, producing a nadir and a settling point. Halve the inertia and the RoCoF doubles and the nadir deepens - the whole "98 vs 260 GVAs" argument, runnable. Output is on the same 20 ms timeline as the NESO data, so it can be replayed/visualised alongside the real trace.

### src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/FrequencyIntegrator.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Dynamics`. 78 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/FrequencyIntegrator.cs).

- [`FrequencyIntegrator`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/FrequencyIntegrator.cs#L21) (class): A stateful, incremental centre-of-inertia swing-equation integrator - the running-clock twin of `FrequencyDynamics.Simulate`. Where `Simulate` pre-computes a fixed trace, this advances one `Step` at a time by an arbitrary deltat, so the live dashboard can drive system frequency at whatever time-step the user chooses (1 ms -> 20 min) and watch a real RoCoF/nadir/recovery play out instead of a canned animation. The per-step physics are identical to `Simulate`, because both take them from the one swing kernel, `SwingResponders` (October 2026 review, R080, stream B1): `df/dt = f0/(2E)*deltaP` with governor droop (lagged), load damping, the optional TSGB fast response, the recorded system response services (`DynamicsConfig.SystemResponseServices`) and an equilibrium start at the recorded pre-event frequency (`DynamicsConfig.InitialFrequencyHz`). Before R080 this integrator silently ignored the services and the pre-event frequency, and floored the demand at 1 MW where Simulate did not; the demand is now used as given (the live loop floors it itself, so no live result moves). Large deltat is integrated in bounded internal sub-steps so explicit Euler stays stable - a 20-minute step doesn't blow up, it just settles.

### src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Impedance/GridFollowingImpedance.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Dynamics.Impedance`. 200 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Impedance/GridFollowingImpedance.cs).

- [`GridFollowingImpedance`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Impedance/GridFollowingImpedance.cs#L39) (class): The small-signal dq admittance of a grid-following (current-source-behind-PLL) converter, derived from its authored control law plus the inner-loop parameters the behavioural time-domain model lacks. This is the device whose interaction with a weak grid produces the classic PLL / sub-synchronous instability the screen is built to catch - a phenomenon that is IDENTICALLY ABSENT from the behavioural P-f droop model (`Assets.GridFollowingInverter` has no PLL, no current loop), so it is genuinely new physics. Transfers. The PLL is the STANDARD SRF-PLL closed loop from the terminal q-axis voltage perturbation to the estimated angle: `G_pll(s) = (k_p s + k_i) / (s^2 + Vd0 k_p s + Vd0 k_i)`, with the PI gains derived from the natural frequency `wn = 2 pi f_bw` and damping `zeta` so the closed-loop denominator is `s^2 + 2 zeta wn s + wn^2`: `k_p = 2 zeta wn / Vd0`, `k_i = wn^2 / Vd0`. There is NO free integrator - `G_pll(0) = 1/Vd0` is finite - so the return ratio has no pole at the origin and the minor-loop `P = 0` assumption holds (no Nyquist-contour indentation needed). The current loop is `G_ci(s) = w_ci / (s + w_ci)`, or unity when the detail level omits it. Full 2x2 admittance (drawn), system dq frame. A constant-P/Q outer loop sets the converter-frame current reference from the measured d-axis voltage, and the PLL rotates both the reference and the injected current; the two mechanisms populate all four entries: Y_dd = G_ci * Id0/Vd0 Y_dq = Iq0 * G_pll Y_qd = G_ci * Iq0/Vd0 Y_qq = -Id0 * G_pll Both off-diagonals are proportional to `Iq0`, so a unity-power-factor unit (`Iq0 = 0`) decouples - the honest decoupled limit the property test asserts. The `-Id0 * G_pll` term gives `Y_qq` a NEGATIVE real part around the PLL bandwidth: the negative-resistance band that destabilises a weak grid. Positive-sequence reduction. The modified-sequence (Rygg/Molinas) transform `Y_pp = 1/2[(Y_dd + Y_qq) + j(Y_qd - Y_dq)]`, which for this matrix collapses to the clean `Y_pp = 1/2 (G_ci/Vd0 - G_pll)(Id0 + j Iq0)`.

### src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Impedance/GridFormingImpedance.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Dynamics.Impedance`. 197 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Impedance/GridFormingImpedance.cs).

- [`GridFormingImpedance`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Impedance/GridFormingImpedance.cs#L45) (class): The small-signal dq admittance of a grid-forming converter - a voltage source behind a virtual impedance with a power-synchronisation loop. Where the grid-following unit presents a negative-resistance band that can trip a weak grid, the GFM presents a POSITIVE-REAL (passive) impedance over the sub-synchronous band, which is why a grid-forming fleet stabilises where a grid-following fleet destabilises - reproduced here as a MEASURED impedance property, not an assertion. Inertia invariant. The synthetic-inertia coefficient (`AssetParams.SynInertiaMwsPerHz`) enters ONLY as a labelled control transfer inside the power-loop impedance `Z_p(s)`; it is never summed into a swing energy E. The (1/2)Jw^2-vs-df/dt separation is preserved by construction - this model is small-signal about a fixed operating point and touches no machine H or EMF. Impedance. The virtual impedance is an RL element in the dq frame, `Z_v(s) = (R_v + s L_v) I + w0 L_v J` (`L_v = X_v / w0`, `J = [[0,-1],[1,0]]`); the power loop adds a first-order synchronising resistance `Z_p(s) = D_p / (1 + s tau_p)` on the diagonal (droop `D_p` from `dampingMwPerHz`, time constant from the power-loop bandwidth and the labelled synthetic inertia). The admittance is the 2x2 inverse of the total. Per-unit power loop (R140, October 2026 review; stream B5; Ruling R1: Mark delegated EE calls 2026-10-04). Every quantity of the loop is now on the converter's own rating S (MVA), the base the impedance itself is on. The grid-forming law is a P-f droop with a virtual inertia, which in per unit on S reads `2 H_v d(dw)/dt = -dp - k_d dw` with the per-unit droop gain `k_d = D f0 / S` (D the damping in MW/Hz) and the virtual inertia constant `H_v = J f0 / (2 S)` (J the labelled synthetic inertia in MW.s/Hz; the same `Ev = J f0 / 2` MW.s the frequency model's former uses, `Forming.FormingAggregate.FromFleet`). As a frequency response to power this is `dw = -m_p dp / (1 + s 2 H_v m_p)` with the per-unit droop `m_p = 1 / k_d = S / (D f0)`: a droop with a first-order lag, the VSM / droop equivalence of D'Arco and Suul ("Equivalence of virtual synchronous machines and frequency-droops for converter-based microgrids", IEEE Trans. Smart Grid 5(1), 2014, pp. 394-395). So the loop's synchronising resistance is the per-unit droop, `D_p = m_p` (linearised at unit voltage), and its time constant is the power-loop filter `1 / (2 pi f_pl)` plus the inertia lag `2 H_v m_p`, which with an authored damping is `J / D` seconds (rating- and frequency-free, as a time constant must be). Before R140 the code used `D_p = 0.01 D` (MW/Hz read straight as pu, so a 1000 MW/Hz fleet got 10 pu whatever its size) and `tau += 1e-4 J` (MW.s/Hz read as seconds); both scaled with the absolute MW size of the unit instead of its per-unit control law. A unit with no authored damping keeps the placeholder `ConverterDefaults.GfmDefaultSyncResistancePu` as its per-unit droop (unchanged), and a unit with neither damping nor synthetic inertia (every flag-built model) is bit-identical to before.

### src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Impedance/GridImpedanceAssembler.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Dynamics.Impedance`. 159 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Impedance/GridImpedanceAssembler.cs).

- [`GridImpedanceAssembler`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Impedance/GridImpedanceAssembler.cs#L28) (class): Assembles the grid-side driving-point impedance an inverter sees, reusing the harmonic Y(h) stack (`FrequencyDependentYBus.Build` takes a real-valued h) and the driving-point solve seam (`HarmonicImpedanceScan`: solve `Y(h) x = e_k`, take `x[k]`). It generalises that solve to any real - and any SIGNED - frequency ratio, which is exactly what the dq +/-w0 sequence transform needs. Conjugate symmetry (FIX 5). Passing the SIGNED h (not `|h|`) to `FrequencyDependentYBus.Build` makes `Y(-h) = conj(Y(h))` - the series term `1/(R+jhX)`, the line charging `jhB`, and BOTH shunt rules (`Bs*h` for a capacitor, `Bs/h` for a reactor) are odd in h - so the driving-point solve satisfies `Z(-f) = conj(Z(f))` exactly. The naive `|h|` mirror does NOT (it loses the sign the reactor rule needs), which is why this always solves at the true signed h. DC arm (FIX 5). The dq negative arm lands on `h = 0` when the perturbation frequency equals f0. At h=0 the network is singular (a lossless branch is a short, a reactor shunt blows up), so a null driving-point solve is raised as an EXPLICIT error, never silently returned as Z = 0, and the scan skips `f_p ~ f0`.

### src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Impedance/MinorLoopNyquist.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Dynamics.Impedance`. 247 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Impedance/MinorLoopNyquist.cs).

- [`NyquistVerdict`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Impedance/MinorLoopNyquist.cs#L18) (record): The verdict of a minor-loop / generalised-Nyquist test.
- [`MinorLoopNyquist`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Impedance/MinorLoopNyquist.cs#L51) (class): The minor-loop Nyquist test (SISO Middlebrook) and the generalised (MIMO) Nyquist test. P = 0. Both the grid and the converter are individually stable in these models (the SRF-PLL closed loop is Hurwitz, with NO free integrator, so the converter admittance has no open right-half-plane pole and no pole on the imaginary axis). The return ratio therefore has `P = 0` open-loop RHP poles, and by the argument principle the unstable closed-loop mode count equals the net encirclements of (-1,0) - no Nyquist-contour indentation is required. If a future model introduces a legitimate imaginary-axis pole, this class must indent the contour and count P explicitly rather than assume P = 0. Counting. Both criteria reduce to winding a scalar return-difference around the origin: SISO winds `1 + L(jw)` with `L = Z_grid * Y_conv`; MIMO winds the return-difference determinant `det(I + T(jw))` with `T = Y_conv * Z_grid` (the generalised Nyquist criterion is the encirclements of the return-difference determinant, equivalent to summing the characteristic loci but free of eigenvalue branch-swap). The negative-frequency arm is the conjugate mirror (`L(-jw) = conj(L(jw))`).

Because the very first RoCoF sample is taken before governors or fast response have moved, the estimate is clean: at t=0 the only imbalance is deltaP itself.

### src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/AcExciter.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Dynamics.Models`. 216 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/AcExciter.cs).

- [`AcExciterVariant`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/AcExciter.cs#L4) (enum): Which alternator-rectifier excitation system an `AcExciter` is.
- [`AcExciter`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/AcExciter.cs#L36) (class): The alternator-rectifier excitation systems of the IEEE AC1 family (EXAC1, ESAC1A): a field-controlled alternator whose output is rectified by non-controlled diodes, so the field voltage falls as the field current loads the rectifier. Structure (all per-unit; IFD the machine's field current in the non-reciprocal Xad base, equal to Efd in steady state): VFE = VE*(KE + SE(VE)) + KD*IFD (exciter field demand: self-excitation, saturation, armature reaction) VF = sKF/(1+sTF) * VFE (rate feedback) x = leadlag_{TC/TB}(Verr - VF) (Verr = Vref - Vt + Vs) EXAC1: VR = lag_{KA, TA, [VRMIN, VRMAX]}(x) ESAC1A: VA = lag_{KA, TA, [VAMIN, VAMAX]}(x), VR = clamp(VA, VRMIN, VRMAX) TE dVE/dt = VR - VFE (ESAC1A: VE >= 0) IN = KC*IFD / VE, Efd = VE * FEX(IN) FEX = 1 (IN <= 0), 1 - 0.577 IN (IN <= 0.433), sqrt(0.75 - IN^2) (IN <= 0.75), 1.732 (1 - IN) (IN <= 1), 0 above SE is the quadratic saturation through (E1, SE1) and (E2, SE2): VE*SE(VE) = B*(VE - A)^2 above A, else 0, with A and B from the two points (no saturation when SE1 = SE2 = 0). The FEX constants and the quadratic form are the IEEE 421.5 ones (its rectifier regulation annex). Each step reads VFE at the start-of-step VE (as `Ieeet1` reads its feedback), advances the lead-lag and the regulator with the exact zero-order hold, then the exciter with the exact zero-order hold of its start-of-step linearised pole (SE frozen, KD*IFD held), the same operator splitting `Ieeet1` uses; the field current is held across the step like every other input.

### src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/BusFrequencyMeter.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Dynamics.Models`. 187 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/BusFrequencyMeter.cs).

- [`RmsBusTrace`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/BusFrequencyMeter.cs#L17) (record): The voltage angle of a set of buses through an RMS run, one sample per integration step (inertia placement study, October 2026). Recorded by `RmsTransientStability.StudyEventsMeasured` from the same committed network solve the machines integrate against; reading it changes no number of the run.
- [`BusFrequencyResult`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/BusFrequencyMeter.cs#L24) (record): Per-bus frequency measures of one run (see `BusFrequencyMeter.Measure`).
- [`BusFrequencyMeter`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/BusFrequencyMeter.cs#L51) (class): Bus frequency, RoCoF and angle jump from recorded bus voltage angles, the way a relay at that bus would see them (inertia placement study, October 2026). Angle jump. At an event the network changes between two samples while the machine EMFs cannot, so a bus voltage angle steps. The jump at an event at sample `ke` is the angle change across the event less the change over the step before it: `(u[ke] - u[ke-1]) - (u[ke-1] - u[ke-2])`, so the steady drift of the angle is not counted as a jump. The jump is then taken out of the angle (subtracted from every later sample) before the frequency is formed, so the frequency and RoCoF below are those of the rotor-driven motion, and the jump is reported on its own. (A real loss-of-mains relay sees both together; the two are kept apart here so each can be judged against its own limit.) Frequency. `f[k] = f0 + (u[k] - u[k - nc]) / (2 pi nc dt)` over about one nominal cycle (`nc` is the whole number of steps nearest `1/(f0 dt)`, at least one: the shortest window a zero-crossing or phasor measurement uses; 4 steps of 5 ms at 50 Hz, exactly one cycle); before the first full window the first full estimate is held, so a bus that starts off nominal does not read a step from nominal. RoCoF. `(f[k] - f[k - nw]) / (nw dt)` over a sliding window (`nw dt` = 500 ms by default, the window GB loss-of-mains protection measures RoCoF over under the Distribution Code / G99), and the worst magnitude of it over the run. The same window applied to a centre-of-inertia frequency gives the system figure the bus figures are compared with. Pure arithmetic in one fixed order: the same input gives the same bits on every CPU and operating system.

### src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/CctSearch.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Dynamics.Models`. 134 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/CctSearch.cs).

- [`CctSearch`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/CctSearch.cs#L42) (class): The step-grid search for a critical clearing time (CCT), shared by the RMS engine (`RmsTransientStability.CriticalClearingBracket`) and the classical model (`Distributed.ClassicalInit.CriticalClearingBracket`), so the two can never search differently. What it reports (N048, October 2026). The CCT is defined as the FIRST loss of synchronism from below: the largest whole number of steps m such that clearing after every step count from 0 to m holds synchronism, so clearing after m + 1 steps is the first clearing time on the grid that loses it. A plain bisection finds that only when stability is monotone in the clearing time (every clear shorter than a stable one is stable too). Multi-swing cases break that: on WSCC-9 bus 2 (classical, CLI setup) clearing after 171 steps (342 ms) holds, 172 to 174 (344 to 348 ms) lose synchronism, 175 (350 ms) holds again, and 176 to 187 (the probe window) lose it (D-DOC-191: this comment used to say 174 / 348 ms held, the pattern before N047; re-measured at 1.95.203 with `stability case9 --fault-bus 2 --clear N`, and `stability case9 --screen` reports the pocket at 350 ms); bus 8 and bus 9 have stable pockets 5, 11, 13 and 14 steps above their first loss. A bisection can land on a pocket's upper edge and report a CCT above a clearing time that already loses synchronism. How (bounded cost). Three stages, every trial memoised (a step count is never simulated twice): The unchanged integer bisection (R106 / N042): trial 0, trial M (the whole window), then halving until the stable and unstable step counts are adjacent. For a monotone case this alone is the answer, exactly as before. Downward verification: the `scanSteps` step counts just below the stable end are simulated. If one of them loses synchronism, the bisection landed on a stable pocket: the search re-bisects between 0 and that lower unstable step and verifies again. After `MaxRefinementRounds` such rounds it stops guessing and walks up from step 1 to the lowest unstable step found, which gives the exact first loss (at most that many trials). Upward probe: the `scanSteps` step counts just above the unstable end are simulated. Any that holds synchronism is a stable pocket above the first loss; the CCT does not move (it is the first loss), but the result says so (`CctBracket.NonMonotone`, `CctBracket.PocketStableSteps`). Guarantee: the reported stable end is the first loss from below provided no stable pocket is wider than `scanSteps` steps (a pocket that wide would hide the losses below it from the downward verification). Only a linear scan from 0 removes that proviso, at about 170 to 380 trials per WSCC-9 bus instead of about 10. Cost: at most `2 * scanSteps` trials above the bisection when the case is monotone near its CCT (fewer when bisection trials are reused); with the default 16 steps that is 32 trials (64 ms of clearing time either side at 2 ms). `CctBracket.Trials` reports the exact count of simulations a search ran. A scan depth of 0 gives the bisection alone, the pre-N048 search, trial for trial.

### src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/ControlBlocks.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Dynamics.Models`. 290 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/ControlBlocks.cs).

- [`ControlBlocks`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/ControlBlocks.cs#L24) (class): The common block-diagram integrator: the standard control-system transfer-function blocks that every IEEE excitation / turbine-governor / PSS standard model is wired from. This is the foundation of the standard dynamic-model library (P0-1) - a machine model, an AVR and a governor are each a small wiring of these primitives, so validating the blocks once, hard, de-risks every model built on them. The linear dynamic blocks (`FirstOrderLag`, `LeadLag`, `Washout`) integrate by the exact zero-order-hold discretisation of their pole, not by an Euler/RK step: for an input held constant across the step the state advance `x <- a*x + (1-a)*K*u` with `a = exp(-dt/T)` is the closed-form solution of the block's ODE, so a step response reproduces the analytic `K(1-e^{-t/T})` to machine epsilon at every sample and is unconditionally A-stable at any step. The pure `Integrator` (a marginally-stable pole at the origin) advances by the forward-Euler rule `x <- x + K*u*dt`, which is likewise exact for a held input (a ramp). Every block is a pure function of (state, input, dt) with no shared or static state, so a study is bit-for-bit reproducible run to run, matching the whole-app determinism contract (technical manual ch. 11). Two structural degeneracies are exact by construction and are pinned as reduction identities (the same discipline used across GridSim - collapse the general model onto a known one and demand field-for-field agreement): a `LeadLag` with equal numerator and denominator time constants is an exact pass-through, and a `FirstOrderLag` with zero time constant is an exact gain.
- [`FirstOrderLag`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/ControlBlocks.cs#L77) (class): First-order lag `K / (1 + sT)` with optional non-windup output limits - the workhorse block (an AVR forward gain, a governor valve/steam bowl, a measurement transducer). The state is the output `x`; its ODE is `T dx/dt = K u - x`, advanced by the exact zero-order hold. When limits are set the state is clamped to `[min, max]` each step - a non-windup position limit, so the output leaves the limit the instant the input reverses, with no wound-up integral to unload. A time constant at or below `ControlBlocks.InstantThresholdSeconds` makes the block the pure gain `y = K u`.
- [`LeadLag`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/ControlBlocks.cs#L147) (class): Lead-lag compensator `(1 + sTa) / (1 + sTb)`, unity DC gain - the phase-shaping block of PSS and AVR transient-gain-reduction stages. Realised as a direct feedthrough plus an internal lag: `y = c*u + xL` where `c = Ta/Tb` and `xL` is the lag `(1-c)/(1+sTb)` of the input, integrated by the same exact zero-order hold as `FirstOrderLag`. The denominator time constant Tb must be positive. When `Ta == Tb` the feedthrough coefficient is exactly 1 and the internal-lag gain exactly 0, so the block is a bit-exact pass-through (`y = u`) - a reduction identity, not an approximation.
- [`Washout`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/ControlBlocks.cs#L186) (class): Washout (high-pass) `sT / (1 + sT)` - the derivative-with-memory block at the front of every PSS, so a sustained (DC) input produces no steady output and only the change is passed. Realised as `y = u - xL` where `xL` is the unity-gain lag of the input, integrated by the exact zero-order hold. In steady state `xL -> u` so the output decays to exactly zero. The time constant must be positive.
- [`Integrator`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/ControlBlocks.cs#L224) (class): Pure integrator `K / s` with optional non-windup limits - the integral path of a PI regulator, an over/under-excitation timer, a valve position. The state is the output; `dx/dt = K u`, advanced by forward Euler (`x <- x + K u dt`), which is exact for an input held across the step (a ramp). Clamping the state itself to `[min, max]` makes the limit non-windup: the output cannot integrate past the limit, so it releases immediately when the input reverses.
- [`PiController`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/ControlBlocks.cs#L262) (class): Proportional-integral regulator `Kp + Ki/s` with a non-windup limit on the integral state - the core of a bus-voltage or governor load regulator. The proportional path is a direct feedthrough; the integral path is an `Integrator` whose non-windup limits stop the integral winding up while the plant is against a limit. The integral limits default to the (optional) overall output limits.

### src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/Esst4b.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Dynamics.Models`. 152 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/Esst4b.cs).

- [`Esst4b`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/Esst4b.cs#L31) (class): ESST4B - the IEEE 421.5-2005 type ST4B static excitation system (PSS/E ESST4B): a potential- and/or compound-source controlled rectifier exciter with an outer voltage PI regulator and an inner field-voltage PI regulator. Structure (all per-unit on the machine base; VT and IT the terminal voltage and current phasors, IFD the field current in the non-reciprocal Xad base): VE = | KP e^(j THETAP) VT + j (KI + KP e^(j THETAP) XL) IT | (the power source voltage) IN = KC IFD / VE, VB = min(VE FEX(IN), VBMAX) (FEX the IEEE 421.5 rectifier regulation) VR' = PI_{KPR, KIR, [VRMIN, VRMAX]}(Verr) (Verr = Vref - Vt + Vs) VR = lag_{TA}(VR') VM = PI_{KPM, KIM, [VMMIN, VMMAX]}(VR - KG Efd) (solved with the step's own Efd = VM VB) Efd = VM VB The outer PI regulator is a `PiController` (non-windup limits on the integral and on the output) and the lag a `FirstOrderLag`, with the inputs held across the step. The inner loop's algebraic loop through KG Efd = KG VB VM is solved exactly each step (linear in VM, then clamped, the integral held inside the same limits): closing it through the start-of-step field instead is a one-step-delay loop of gain KPM KG VB, which diverges once that passes 1, as ordinary data do. The PSS/E data have no VGMAX (the 2005 limit on KG Efd), so none is applied; the under- and over-excitation limiter gates are not modelled. Initialisation needs the terminal quantities, so `Initialize` only records the field and the first `Step` sets every state from that step's measurements (the undisturbed network at t = 0, as the kernel guarantees): VB0 from VT, IT and IFD = Efd0, then VM0 = Efd0 / VB0, and with KIM above 0 the inner error 0 so VR0 = KG Efd0 (KIM = 0: VR0 = KG Efd0 + VM0 / KPM). The outer integrator then holds VR0 with zero voltage error when KIR is above 0; KIR = 0 needs KIM above 0 and holds the error KG Efd0 / KPR. KIR = KIM = 0 would need the measurements to find the steady error before the first step, so it is refused. Any state outside its limits, or a VB0 that is not above 0, fails loud.

### src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/Gast.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Dynamics.Models`. 110 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/Gast.cs).

- [`Gast`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/Gast.cs#L25) (class): GAST - the standard simple gas-turbine governor (PSS/E GAST; CGMES GovGAST), in GridSim's turbine-governor library beside `Tgov1`. Data R, T1, T2, T3, AT, KT, VMAX, VMIN, DTURB (the PSS/E order). The block diagram, as published for PSS/E GAST and reproduced by NEPLAN's turbine-governor reference and the ANDES GAST model: pd = Pref - dw/R (load reference less the droop on the speed deviation) limit = AT + KT*(AT - x3) (exhaust temperature load limit) u = min(pd, limit) (low value gate) x1 = lag_{T1, [VMIN, VMAX]}(u) (fuel valve, non-windup position limits) x2 = lag_{T2}(x1) (turbine power) x3 = lag_{T3}(x2) (exhaust temperature measurement) Pmech = x2 - DTURB*dw All quantities are per-unit on the machine base. Each step the gate reads the exhaust temperature state x3 of the START of the step (the measurement the limit sees while the step's input is held), then the three lags advance in signal order with the exact zero-order hold of `FirstOrderLag`, each seeing its upstream block's new output (the same sequencing as `Tgov1`). With Pref set to the initial mechanical power, dw = 0 is an exact equilibrium provided the temperature limit is not binding there: at equilibrium x1 = x2 = x3 = Pmech0, so the limit is AT + KT*(AT - Pmech0), which is at least Pmech0 exactly when Pmech0 <= AT (KT >= 0). In steady state on the temperature limit x = AT + KT*(AT - x), so the turbine settles at AT whatever KT: AT is the most power the ambient temperature allows, and Pmech0 above it cannot be an equilibrium (refused, as R252 refuses any start outside a limit).

This is the first study that closes a standard control model around the machine dynamics, and it is built with no second kernel - it drives the trusted classical integrator through its per-step mechanical-power hook, so: when every governor is absent the result is bit-for-bit the constant-Pm classical swing (the reduction identity, pinned by test); the machine-epsilon numerics of the classical kernel are inherited unchanged - this layer adds only the governor state advance. Each present governor is initialised to its machine's initial mechanical power `pm0` so an undisturbed run is stationary; on a disturbance it acts on the machine's own speed deviation. For an islanded machine set the steady speed deviation settles to the analytic droop `omegabar_ss = deltaP / sum(1/R)`, the second, independent oracle this layer is validated against.

### src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/HydroGovernor.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Dynamics.Models`. 130 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/HydroGovernor.cs).

- [`HydroGovernor`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/HydroGovernor.cs#L22) (class): The classic transient-droop (dashpot) hydro turbine-governor with the ideal water column - the standard hydro-plant model, alongside the steam `Tgov1` / `Ieeeg1`. Two features distinguish a hydro governor: the transient droop (a washout of gate position that temporarily opposes gate motion, so the slow water column is not over-driven), and the non-minimum-phase water column, whose power initially moves the wrong way when the gate opens (water inertia). Structure: err = Pref - dw c = (err - Rt*washout_{Tr}(g)) / Rp (permanent droop Rp, transient droop Rt over Tr) g = lag_{Tg, [gmin,gmax]}(c) (gate servo) Pmech = (1 - sTw)/(1 + 0.5 sTw) * g (ideal water column) All quantities are per-unit. The water column is realised exactly as `Pmech = 3*lag_{0.5Tw}(g) - 2*g` (the partial-fraction form of `(1 - sTw)/(1 + 0.5sTw)`), so a gate opening of `dg` makes the power first drop by `2*dg` before recovering to `+dg` - the water-hammer inverse response, exact to machine epsilon. With `dw = 0` and `Pref = Rp*Pmech0` the model is stationary, and the steady (permanent) droop is `dPmech/dw = -1/Rp`. The dynamics are the exact-discretised `Washout` and `FirstOrderLag` blocks.
