### src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/Ieeeg1.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Dynamics.Models`. 240 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/Ieeeg1.cs).

- [`Ieeeg1`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/Ieeeg1.cs#L37) (class): IEEEG1 - the IEEE type 1 steam turbine-governor (IEEE Committee Report, "Dynamic Models for Steam and Hydro Turbines in Power System Studies", IEEE Trans. PAS-92, 1973, Fig. 1 and 5; the PSS/E IEEEG1 model), the standard steam-plant model above the compact `Tgov1`. It has the governor phase-shaping lead-lag, a rate- and position-limited valve, and the four-stage steam train (chest, reheater, crossover, second crossover) whose power fractions tap the high-, intermediate- and low-pressure stages of a high-pressure (HP) shaft and, for a cross-compound unit, a low-pressure (LP) shaft. A direct wiring of the common control blocks: e = -(1/R) * dw (droop on speed deviation, K = 1/R) s1 = leadlag_{T2/T1}(e) (governor phase shaping) dPgv/dt = clamp((Pref + s1 - Pgv) / T3, Uc, Uo), (valve servo: rate limited ...) Pgv in [Pmin, Pmax] (... and position limited, non-windup) y4..y7 = cascade of lags T4, T5, T6, T7 from Pgv (steam chest -> reheat -> crossover -> second crossover) PmechHP = K1*y4 + K3*y5 + K5*y6 + K7*y7 (HP shaft: the value Step returns) PmechLP = K2*y4 + K4*y5 + K6*y6 + K8*y7 (LP shaft: LowPressureShaftPowerPu) All quantities are per-unit on the machine base. The eight fractions are fractions of the TOTAL turbine power and must sum to 1 (the 1973 report's definition; checked in the constructor). With `Pref` at the valve power at synchronous speed, `dw = 0` is an exact fixed point: the valve holds Pgv = Pmech0, the HP shaft carries (K1 + K3 + K5 + K7) * Pmech0 and the LP shaft the rest. A tandem-compound unit (one shaft, the usual case and the default K1 = 1) puts every stage on one machine: its shaft power is the sum of the two outputs, which is Pmech0 at equilibrium. The steady droop of the total is `dPmech/dw = -1/R` in the unlimited region. It collapses onto a single-stage governor when `K1 = 1` (all power from the chest stage) and `T2 = T1` (no phase shaping). The dynamics are the exact-discretised `FirstOrderLag` and `LeadLag` blocks, plus the exact piecewise solution of the rate-limited valve servo (below). R083 (October 2026 review, stream B3; Ruling R1: Mark delegated EE calls 2026-10-04). Before, the model had no valve opening / closing rate limits (Uo / Uc) and no LP-shaft fractions (K2 / K4 / K6 / K8), so IEEEG1 data whose response is rate-limited (most published steam data: Uo about 0.1 pu/s, Uc about -1 pu/s) could not be reproduced, and a data set with LP fractions silently lost that share of the power. Both are now in. With the new arguments at their defaults (Uo = +infinity, Uc = -infinity, K2 = K4 = K6 = K8 = 0) every expression of the old model runs unchanged, so every existing result is bit for bit what it was. A governor lag T1 of zero with no lead (T1 = T2 = 0, common in PSS/E data) is the pure gain the transfer function then is, instead of an exception.

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Dynamics.Models`. 99 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/Ieeet1.cs).

It carries the features SEXS omits: the exciter's own self-excitation constant `Ke` and open-circuit saturation `Se(Efd)`, and the rate (stabilising) feedback loop. Structure: Verr = (Vref - Vt + Vs) - Vf (regulator error less the rate feedback) Vr = lag_{Ka, Ta, [Vrmin,Vrmax]}(Verr) (voltage regulator) Te dEfd/dt = Vr - (Ke + Se(Efd)) * Efd (exciter, Se = Aex*exp(Bex*Efd)) Vf = (Kf/Tf) * washout_{Tf}(Efd) = sKf/(1+sTf) * Efd All quantities are per-unit. The exciter ODE advances by the exact zero-order hold of its (start-of-step linearised) pole - `Se` frozen across the step, the same operator splitting used for machine saturation - so it is A-stable and, with `Se = 0, Ke = 1, Kf = 0`, collapses to a two-lag AVR whose steady field is `Efd = Ka*Verr` (the SEXS behaviour). Saturation (`Aex > 0`) raises the regulator voltage needed to hold a given field; the rate feedback adds transient damping and washes out in steady state (`Vf -> 0`), so it does not bias the setpoint.

Two implementations: `LegacyRmsConverterModel`, the historical REGC_A/REEC-style converter (`RmsConverterState`), forwarded call for call with exactly the arguments the kernel passed before this interface existed, so its numbers are bit for bit unchanged; and `Wecc.WeccConverterState`, the WECC second-generation model chain bound from a DYR file.

From the second pass of each step's iteration on, the kernel passes each such unit `a = V - Zdd I_own` (the node voltage of the last solve with the unit's own last injection removed) and `Zdd` (the driving-point impedance of the network at the unit's node, from one solve with a unit injection, once per network); the unit returns the injection that satisfies `V = a + Zdd I(V)` for its own model. Other units in the same pass are held (block Jacobi), and the kernel's convergence test is unchanged. A model whose `SolvesWithNetwork` is false takes the historical path, call for call.
- [`LegacyRmsConverterModel`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/IRmsConverterModel.cs#L79) (class): The historical converter (`RmsConverterState`) behind `IRmsConverterModel`: each call is the call the kernel made before, with the same arguments (the magnitude and the DetMath phase of the same phasor), so every number is the same bits.

### src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/MachineAdmittanceColumns.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Dynamics.Models`. 133 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/MachineAdmittanceColumns.cs).

- [`MachineAdmittanceColumns`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/MachineAdmittanceColumns.cs#L30) (class): The machine-only reduced admittance of a dense RMS network, held for a fast and BIT-IDENTICAL product `I_m = Y E` (R116, October 2026 review, S5). The historical product (`DenseMachineNetwork.MultiplyMachineInto`) walks `Complex[,]` one element at a time and accumulates each machine current over the columns in ascending order: `sr += g*Er - b*Ei; si += g*Ei + b*Er`, starting from +0. The summation order of a row is what the bits depend on, so the usual vectorisation (splitting a row's sum across lanes) would change them. This class instead vectorises ACROSS ROWS: the real parts G and imaginary parts B are copied once, column-major, into two flat arrays, so the entries of column j for consecutive rows sit side by side, and each vector lane carries one row's own running sums through the columns in the same ascending order. Every lane does, per column, exactly the scalar operations in the scalar order - multiply, multiply, subtract (or add), then add to the running sum - with a separate rounding at each step (never a fused multiply-add), so every machine current is the scalar result to the bit at every vector width (AVX-512, AVX2, SSE, and the scalar loop for the rows left over and on CPUs without vector units). The tiers are selected once by `SimdCapabilities.Tier`; each arm is exercised on any machine through the explicit-tier overload (a test seam, as for `SimdKernels`). The copy is taken at construction: the network multiplies by the admittance it was built with, as every caller assumes (the RMS integrator builds one network per admittance stage and never edits the matrix).

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Dynamics.Models`. 49 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/MachineBase.cs).

- [`MachineBase`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/MachineBase.cs#L25) (class): The one rule for the MVA base a machine's per-unit dynamic data (inertia H, reactances X'd, X''d, ...) is written on, shared by the classical (`Distributed.ClassicalInit`) and the subtransient (`SubtransientInit`) initialisations (D-DOC-055, docs-session finding, Ruling R1: Mark delegated 2026-10-04). The rule: a positive `Generator.MBase` is the machine base; a zero or negative MBase means "not given" and the SYSTEM base (`GridModel.BaseMva`) is used instead, which is the MATPOWER convention (its parser already reads a non-positive mBase as the system base, and the MATPOWER writer notes it). A NaN or infinite MBase is not a base at all and is refused (fail loud): it used to turn every reactance and the inertia of that machine into NaN or zero without a word. Why one rule: before D-DOC-055 the two initialisations disagreed. SubtransientInit already fell back to the system base; ClassicalInit floored the divisor at 1e-6 MVA (so a zero MBase made X'd on the system base 1e8 times the machine value) and scaled H by the raw MBase (so a zero MBase gave H = 0 on the system base, which the swing divides by). No bundled case reaches the fallback: every bundled generator with a non-positive capacity has H = 0, so the classical study holds it as a constant injection (or refuses the case for want of inertia) before its MBase is read, and the MATPOWER parser has already replaced a non-positive mBase with the system base.

### src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/MultiMachineFluxDecay.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Dynamics.Models`. 170 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/MultiMachineFluxDecay.cs).

- [`MultiMachineFluxDecay`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/MultiMachineFluxDecay.cs#L55) (class): The multi-machine varying-`E'q` (flux-decay) model - the network generalisation of the SMIB `OneAxisMachine`. Every machine's transient EMF `E'q` is a state driven by its field voltage through the field flux-linkage decay, and the machines are coupled through the reduced network rather than a single infinite bus. It is the varying-`E'q` step up from the constant-`E'` `ClassicalMultiMachine`, and reuses that trusted swing kernel through its flux-decay hook - there is no second integrator (the same "no second kernel" discipline as `GovernedMultiMachine`). Per machine (per-unit on the system base, angles in rad, times in seconds): ddelta_i/dt = omega_s * omega_i (rotor angle) domega_i/dt = (Pm_i - Pe_i - D_i*omega_i) / (2 H_i) (swing) T'do_i dE'q_i/dt = Efd_i - E'q_i - (Xd_i - X'd_i) * Id_i (field flux-linkage decay) This first multi-machine slice is round-rotor at the network interface (`Xq = X'd`), so each machine presents to the network as a simple internal voltage `E'q_i&#8736;delta_i` behind its transient reactance `X'd` - exactly the classical interface, with the reduction reactance already folded into the reduced admittance `Y` by `ClassicalInit`. The electrical power is then the classical form `Pe_i = sum_j |E'|_i |E'|_j (G_ij cos(delta_ij) + B_ij sin(delta_ij))` (no saliency reluctance term), and the d-axis current that drives the flux decay is recovered from the network reactive injection at the internal node, Qe_i = sum_j |E'|_i |E'|_j (G_ij sin(delta_ij) - B_ij cos(delta_ij)), Id_i = Qe_i / |E'|_i so there is no iterative network solve: given the rotor angles and internal voltages, one reduced matrix-vector product gives both `Pe` and `Id` in closed form. The field flux state advances on the same exact zero-order-hold `FirstOrderLag` as the rest of the library (input `Efd_i - (Xd_i - X'd_i) Id_i` held across the step), and the rotor swing advances by the classical kernel's RK4 with `E'q` frozen across the sub-steps - operator splitting, matching both the SMIB machine and the governor. Deliberately out of this slice. Saliency in the network interface (`Xq != X'd`), the subtransient two-axis reactances of GENROU/GENSAL/GENTPJ and magnetic saturation need a dq-frame solve that carries a d- and q-axis reactance separately - the same oracle-backed care at network scale that the SMIB slice established, taken up in the next slice. Multi-machine AVR is likewise deferred: the reduced internal-node network does not expose terminal voltages (Kron reduction eliminated the terminal buses), which an AVR regulates, so the field is held constant per machine here; AVR-in-the-loop is already validated at SMIB scale on `OneAxisMachine` and returns to the multi-machine model with the terminal-voltage-preserving solve. It collapses onto the classical model as a reduction identity - with `Xd_i = X'd_i` the flux-decay driver term vanishes and a matched held field keeps every `E'q_i` at its initial value, so the run is the constant-`E'` classical swing - and an open (disconnected) machine's field response is the analytic flux-decay exponential to machine epsilon. These, with equilibrium stationarity and bit-for-bit determinism, are the oracles it is validated against (`tests/GridSim.Tests/MultiMachineFluxDecayTests.cs`).
- [`MachineTrace`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/MultiMachineFluxDecay.cs#L59) (record): Per-machine trajectory: rotor angle delta(t) (rad), per-unit speed deviation omega(t), and the varying transient EMF magnitude E'q(t) (pu).
- [`Result`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/MultiMachineFluxDecay.cs#L65) (record): Declared record; see the source and member declarations for its role.

### src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/MultiMachineSubtransient.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Dynamics.Models`. 851 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/MultiMachineSubtransient.cs).

- [`IRmsFieldController`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/MultiMachineSubtransient.cs#L15) (interface): A per-machine field controller (AVR, optionally with a stabiliser) for the subtransient multi-machine kernel (R061). The kernel calls `Initialize` once with the machine's initial held field, then, once per step, `Step` with the regulator error `Vref - Vt` and the machine's speed deviation (pu), and uses the returned field voltage across the step. `RmsExciter` is the standard implementation (SEXS, IEEET1, EXAC1, ESAC1A or ESST4B, each with an optional PSS1A).
- [`IRmsFieldCurrentController`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/MultiMachineSubtransient.cs#L41) (interface): A field controller that also reads the machine's field current (an alternator-rectifier exciter whose rectifier regulation and armature reaction depend on it, such as `AcExciter`). When `NeedsFieldCurrent` is true the kernel calls the four-argument `Step` with the start-of-step field current in the non-reciprocal Xad base, IFD = E'q + (Xd - X'd) Id + the d-axis saturation increment: the quantity the E'q equation balances against Efd, so IFD = Efd at every equilibrium (which is how such a controller initialises from the field alone). Otherwise the kernel takes the three-argument path, unchanged.
- [`IRmsTerminalFieldController`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/MultiMachineSubtransient.cs#L59) (interface): A field controller that also reads the terminal voltage and current phasors (a static exciter fed from a potential and/or compound source, such as `Esst4b`). When `NeedsTerminalQuantities` is true the kernel calls the six-argument `Step` with the start-of-step field current (as for `IRmsFieldCurrentController`), the terminal voltage V_t = E'' - jX'' I (pu) and the machine current I (pu on the SYSTEM base, generator convention), both in the network frame; the controller converts the current to its machine base itself.
- [`RmsMachineTrip`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/MultiMachineSubtransient.cs#L79) (record): R061 rest (CF4, October 2026): machine `Machine` (its index in the kernel's machine list) is disconnected from `AtSeconds` on (a generator trip). The network stage in force from that time must already leave the machine out (no Norton admittance, zero admittance in the machine list, so it carries no current); the kernel then sets its mechanical power to zero (the unit is off the system, its turbine shut), holds its field, and leaves it out of the synchronism verdict (a disconnected rotor cannot lose synchronism with the system). The trip takes effect at the same step a network stage at the same time does (the shared stage tolerance).
- [`MultiMachineSubtransient`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/MultiMachineSubtransient.cs#L123) (class): The salient / subtransient multi-machine transient-stability model - the network generalisation of the SMIB `SubtransientMachine`, built on the validated dq current-injection core `SubtransientNetworkInterface`. Every machine carries the full six-state set (rotor angle and speed, the transient EMFs `E'q`, `E'd` and the subtransient EMFs `E''q`, `E''d`) with its own d- and q-axis reactances and time constants, and the machines are coupled through the reduced admittance (with the round subtransient reactance `X''` folded in, as `ClassicalInit` folds `X'd`). Per machine, on the system base (angles in rad, times in seconds): ddelta_i/dt = omega_s * omega_i domega_i/dt = (Pm_i - Pe_i - D_i*omega_i) / (2 H_i) T'do_i dE'q_i/dt = Efd_i - E'q_i - (Xd_i - X'd_i)*Id_i - E''q_i*Se_i(|E''_i|) T''do_i dE''q_i/dt = E'q_i - E''q_i - (X'd_i - X''d_i)*Id_i T'qo_i dE'd_i/dt = -E'd_i + (Xq_i - X'q_i)*Iq_i - E''d_i*Se_i(|E''_i|)*(Xq_i - Xl_i)/(Xd_i - Xl_i) T''qo_i dE''d_i/dt = E'd_i - E''d_i + (X'q_i - X''q_i)*Iq_i Each step, one `SubtransientNetworkInterface.Inject` gives every machine's air-gap power and its dq stator currents from the subtransient EMFs and rotor angles; the four flux states advance on the exact zero-order-hold `FirstOrderLag` (currents and transient EMFs frozen across the step), and the coupled rotor swing advances by RK4 with the subtransient EMFs frozen, the network injection recomputed at each sub-step as the angles move - the same operator splitting the SMIB and round-rotor models use. It collapses onto the trusted `ClassicalMultiMachine` as a reduction identity: with every reactance equal to `X'd` and a matched held field, all four flux drivers vanish, the subtransient EMF stays at its initial `E'q&#8736;delta`, and the fleet is the constant-`E'` classical swing - so a fault-free run follows the classical kernel to 8 or 9 decimal places (only the Pe rounding differs). A faulted run does not: the classical kernel reads the fault window at each RK4 stage time, while this one picks its network once at the step start and holds it for all four stages. With no exciters the field is held per machine. Per-machine AVRs are supported (R061): the terminal voltage is recovered each step as `V_t = E'' - jX'' I` and fed either to a SEXS list (`exciters`, with an explicit voltage reference) or to a general `IRmsFieldController` list (`fieldControllers`: SEXS, IEEET1, EXAC1, ESAC1A or ESST4B, optionally with a PSS1A on the rotor speed, see `RmsExciter`), whose voltage reference is set from the measured initial terminal voltage so the fleet starts at equilibrium. Converter plant. Converter-interfaced units (battery, PV, wind, VSC HVDC) have no rotor and no EMF behind a reactance. When `converters` are passed, their terminal buses are kept as retained nodes after the machine internal nodes (`ConverterNetwork`), each is an `RmsConverterState` phase-locked current source, and the machines see the effective admittance plus the coupling current the converters drive. With none, the kernel is exactly the machine-only one.
- [`Machine`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/MultiMachineSubtransient.cs#L129) (record): One machine's reactances and open-circuit time constants, all per-unit on the system base (so directly comparable to the reduced admittance), with an optional saturation curve. The round subtransient reactance `X''d = X''q` that the network interface requires is the value folded into the reduced admittance; the per-axis `Xdpp`/`Xqpp` here drive the damper flux decay.
- [`MachineTrace`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/MultiMachineSubtransient.cs#L143) (record): Per-machine trajectory: rotor angle, speed and the four flux states through the run.
- [`Result`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/MultiMachineSubtransient.cs#L154) (record): The run: per-machine traces, the synchronism verdict, and (when the fleet includes converter plant) per-converter traces.
- [`Fault`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/MultiMachineSubtransient.cs#L170) (record): A temporary reduced admittance applied over a fault window (onset, cleared), as in the classical kernel.
- [`NetworkStage`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/MultiMachineSubtransient.cs#L176) (record): One entry of a piecewise-constant network schedule: from `AtSeconds` the reduced admittance becomes `YReduced` (until the next stage). This carries the general event timeline an RMS study needs - a fault applied then cleared, a branch tripped (and left out), a switching sequence - where the single `Fault` window only reverts to the base network.
- [`SwingWorkspace`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/MultiMachineSubtransient.cs#L797) (class): The RK4 stage buffers of `SwingStep`, allocated once per run (R115: SwingStep used to allocate fourteen n-vectors plus four acceleration arrays every step).

### src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/OneAxisMachine.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Dynamics.Models`. 220 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/OneAxisMachine.cs).

- [`OneAxisMachine`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/OneAxisMachine.cs#L43) (class): The first varying-`E'q` synchronous machine of the standard model library - a one-axis (flux-decay) machine on a single-machine-infinite-bus (SMIB) network, the step up from the classical constant-`E'` model (`Distributed.ClassicalMultiMachine`). The transient EMF `E'q` is now a state driven by the field voltage `Efd` through the field flux-linkage decay, so an AVR finally has a field circuit to act on (see the `Sexs` coupling below). Three states per machine (per-unit, angles in rad, times in seconds): ddelta/dt = omega_s * omega (rotor angle) domega/dt = (Pm - Pe - D*omega) / (2 H) (swing, omega = pu speed deviation) T'do dE'q/dt = Efd - E'q - (Xd - X'd) * Id (field flux-linkage decay) The stator is algebraic (Rs = 0, no stator transients): `Vd = Xq*Iq`, `Vq = E'q - X'd*Id`, and against an infinite bus `Vinf&#8736;0` through the external reactance `Xe` the dq currents have the closed form Id = (E'q - Vinf*cos(delta)) / (X'd + Xe) Iq = Vinf*sin(delta) / (Xq + Xe) so there is no iterative network solve - the SMIB interface is a two-line linear solve, exact and deterministic. The air-gap power is `Pe = E'q*Iq + (Xq - X'd)*Id*Iq`, the second term the salient- pole reluctance power (zero for a round rotor `Xq = X'd`). The field flux-decay equation is, over a step with `Id` and `Efd` held, exactly a first-order lag `T'do dE'q/dt = u - E'q` with input `u = Efd - (Xd - X'd)*Id`, so it advances on the same exact zero-order-hold `FirstOrderLag` as the rest of the library - the open-circuit field response is machine-epsilon exact. The rotor swing advances by RK4 with `E'q` frozen across the sub-steps (operator splitting, the same discipline the governor uses in `GovernedMultiMachine`). It collapses onto the classical model as a reduction identity: with `Xd = X'd` the flux-decay driver term vanishes, so a held field keeps `E'q` constant, and with `Xq = X'd` as well the reluctance term vanishes and `Pe = E'q*Vinf*sin(delta)/(X'd + Xe)` is the classical SMIB power-angle curve. That constant-`E'`, undamped swing conserves its energy and oscillates at the analytic mode frequency, the oracles this model is validated against.
- [`Parameters`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/OneAxisMachine.cs#L50) (record): Machine and SMIB-network parameters, all per-unit on the machine base (times in seconds). Single-field constraints are enforced on construction (fail-loud); the derived reactance sums `X'd + Xe` and `Xq + Xe` are then positive by construction.
- [`Trace`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/OneAxisMachine.cs#L87) (record): Trajectory: one entry per sample of each state and the derived terminal quantities.

### src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/Pss1a.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Dynamics.Models`. 102 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/Pss1a.cs).

- [`Pss1a`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/Pss1a.cs#L37) (class): PSS1A - the IEEE single-input power-system stabiliser, the first entry in GridSim's PSS library. It adds damping to the rotor oscillation by feeding a phase-compensated speed (or power) signal into the AVR summing junction. Like `Tgov1` and `Sexs` it is a direct wiring of the common control blocks: a stabiliser gain `Ks`, a washout `sTw/(1+sTw)` that blocks any steady signal, two phase-lead stages `(1+sT1)/(1+sT2)` and `(1+sT3)/(1+sT4)`, and output limits `[Vsmin, Vsmax]`: g = Ks * u (u = speed deviation or power input) w = washout_{Tw}(g) (no output for a sustained input) v1 = leadlag_{T1/T2}(w) Vs = clamp( leadlag_{T3/T4}(v1), Vsmin, Vsmax ) (added to the AVR error) All quantities are per-unit. Its defining property is that it contributes nothing in steady state: the washout drives any DC input to zero output, so a PSS never shifts the regulated voltage - it acts only on the swing. The model owns no numerics of its own beyond routing the signal: the dynamics are the exact-discretised `Washout` and `LeadLag` blocks. A subset of the IEEE 421.5 PSS1A it is named after (R083, October 2026). The standard's block diagram also has an input transducer lag 1/(1 + sT6) ahead of the gain, and a second-order low-pass filter in A1 and A2 after the washout that stands for the low-frequency effect of the torsional filters. The filter has the two coefficients A1 and A2 only (an earlier note here said "A1 to A6", which is wrong for PSS1A). Order: transducer T6, gain Ks, washout T5 (Tw here), filter A1 / A2, lead-lags T1 / T2 and T3 / T4, limits. Sources (public implementations of 421.5-2005 / 2016, checked 2026-10-11, N338): CGMES 2.4.15 PssIEEE1A ("IEEE 1A 421.5-2005 Section 8.1"; attributes a1, a2, t1 to t6, ks, vrmax, vrmin; typical T6 0.01 s, A1 0.061, A2 0.0017), MathWorks Simscape PSS1A (421.5-2016: "Second-Order Low-Pass Filter" with "denominator constants A1 and A2", T6 "transducer time constant"), and PSCAD's 2016 stabiliser models. This model has neither block, so it cannot reproduce data whose response depends on them (a non-zero T6, A1 or A2). The exact filter polynomial and a response-level check still need IEEE 421.5 itself, which is not in docs/reference [VERIFY]; the two blocks can be added around the gain and washout in a new constructor, leaving this one unchanged. A lead-lag stage with BOTH time constants zero is the unity transfer function (1 + 0s)/(1 + 0s) = 1, the way published PSS1A data switches a stage off (T3 = T4 = 0 for a single-stage stabiliser); since R083 such a stage is bypassed exactly instead of being refused. A stage with a zero lag but a non-zero lead is a pure derivative (improper) and is still refused, loudly.

### src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/RmsConverter.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Dynamics.Models`. 589 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/RmsConverter.cs).

- [`RmsConverterParameters`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/RmsConverter.cs#L37) (record): Parameters of the RMS grid-following converter model, after the WECC second-generation renewable models: the REGC_A generator/converter interface (current-command lags, low-voltage active current management) under a REEC-style electrical control (constant P/Q in normal operation, K-factor reactive-current boost and active-current freeze during a voltage dip, a current limit with reactive priority, and a ramp-limited active-current recovery). Currents are per-unit on the unit's own rating. Defaults are typical published values for a large grid-following plant.
- [`RmsConverterUnit`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/RmsConverter.cs#L69) (record): A converter-interfaced unit as the RMS engine sees it: where it sits among the retained nodes, its rating, its operating point from the solved power flow, and its control parameters.
- [`RmsConverterTrace`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/RmsConverter.cs#L128) (record): Per-converter trajectory: terminal voltage, active and reactive power and current (system pu).
- [`RmsConverterState`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/RmsConverter.cs#L161) (class): The dynamic state of one RMS grid-following converter (see `RmsConverterParameters`). Per step, given the terminal voltage phasor from the network solve: Vf = lag(|Vt|, Tr) measured voltage normal : Ip* = P0 / Vf, Iq* = Q0 / Vf constant power dip (Vf < Vdip, or within HoldSeconds of one): Iq* = Iq0 + Kqv (V0 - Vf), Ip* = Ip frozen at dip entry limit : Iq* clamped to +-Imax; Ip* <= sqrt(Imax^2 - Iq*^2) reactive priority REGC_A : Ip = lag(Ip*, Tg) with any rise held to RampUp, Iq = lag(Iq*, Tg) output : Ip_out = Ip * LVACM(|Vt|) (0 at LvPnt0, 1 at LvPnt1, linear between) injected : I = (Ip_out - j Iq) e^{j angle(Vt)} (a phase-locked current source; exporting Q positive) All currents are held in system pu (scaled by the rating), so the network sees them directly. The initial state reproduces the power-flow injection exactly, so an undisturbed run is stationary.
- [`ConverterNetwork`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/RmsConverter.cs#L444) (class): The reduced network with converter terminal buses retained next to the machine internal nodes. Partitioning the retained admittance `[Ymm Ymc; Ycm Ycc]` (machines first), the converter bus voltages and the machine currents follow in closed form from the machine EMFs `E` and the converter currents `Ic`: Vc = Ycc^-1 (Ic - Ycm E) I_m = Ymm E + Ymc Vc = Yeff E + Ymc Ycc^-1 Ic, Yeff = Ymm - Ymc Ycc^-1 Ycm `Yeff` is the usual machine-only reduced admittance (converter nodes eliminated at zero injection), so with no converter current the machines see exactly the network they always did.

- [`RmsTransientStability`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/RmsEventCct.cs#L10) (class): Declared class; see the source and member declarations for its role.

Events are separated by commas; each is `kind:arguments@seconds`: `fault:BUS@t` a bolted fault at bus BUS (`RmsBusFault`); `clear:BUS@t` its clearance; `trip:K@t` branch K (0-based index into the case's branch list) trips; `reclose:K@t` it closes again; `load:BUS:P:Q@t` a load step of P MW and Q Mvar at bus BUS (negative to shed); `gentrip:G@t` generator G (0-based index into the case's generator list) trips. Numbers are invariant-culture. Anything else is refused (FormatException) naming the item and the expected form; the physical checks (bus exists, branch in range, ...) are `RmsTransientStability.StudyEvents`'s.

### src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/RmsEvents.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Dynamics.Models`. 371 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/RmsEvents.cs).

- [`RmsEvent`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/RmsEvents.cs#L21) (record): R061 rest (CF4, October 2026; Ruling R1): one scheduled disturbance of an RMS event study (`RmsTransientStability.StudyEvents`). Every event takes effect at the first integration step whose time has reached `AtSeconds` (the network-stage rule of the kernel, with its millionth-of-a-step tolerance) and stays in effect for the rest of the run unless a later event undoes it (only a bus fault can be undone, by a `RmsFaultClear`). The kinds are the ones PSS/E dynamic simulation and PowerFactory RMS studies offer as their basic switching events: a bolted bus fault and its clearance, a branch trip, a load step and a generator trip.
- [`RmsBusFault`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/RmsEvents.cs#L33) (record): A bolted three-phase fault to ground at bus `BusId` (the same near short circuit the single-fault study uses, `SubtransientInit.BoltedFaultShuntPu`), in place until a `RmsFaultClear` on the same bus.
- [`RmsFaultClear`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/RmsEvents.cs#L42) (record): The clearance of the bolted fault at bus `BusId` (the fault's shunt is removed; the network is otherwise as it then stands). Clearing by tripping the faulted branch is a clearance plus an `RmsBranchTrip` at the same time.
- [`RmsBranchTrip`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/RmsEvents.cs#L50) (record): Branch `BranchIndex` (its index in `model.Branches`) opens at both ends and stays out: its series admittance, line charging and tap leave the network.
- [`RmsLoadStep`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/RmsEvents.cs#L63) (record): A load step at bus `BusId`: `DeltaPMw` + j`DeltaQMvar` more (or, negative, less) load. The RMS network carries load as constant admittance converted at the solved voltage (`SubtransientInit`), so the step is the admittance `conj(dS / Sbase) / |V0|^2` with V0 the bus's solved voltage: it draws exactly dS at the pre-event voltage and scales with |V|^2 after, as the base loads do (the PSS/E and PowerFactory constant-impedance load convention). Steps on one bus add.
- [`RmsBranchReclose`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/RmsEvents.cs#L73) (record): N351 (CF5): branch `BranchIndex` (its index in `model.Branches`), tripped by an earlier `RmsBranchTrip`, returns to service (auto-reclose). A reclose of a branch that is not tripped at that time is refused. After the last reclose the network is the base network's own cells again.
- [`RmsGeneratorTrip`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/RmsEvents.cs#L83) (record): Generator `GeneratorIndex` (its index in `model.Generators`) is disconnected: its Norton admittance leaves the network, it carries no current, its mechanical power is zero, its field is held and it is no longer judged for synchronism (see `RmsMachineTrip`). Only a unit integrated as a synchronous machine can be tripped (converter plant and held units are not machines of the RMS fleet).
- [`RmsTransientStability`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/RmsEvents.cs#L89) (class): Declared class; see the source and member declarations for its role.

### src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/RmsGovernor.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Dynamics.Models`. 115 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/RmsGovernor.cs).

- [`IRmsGovernor`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/RmsGovernor.cs#L11) (interface): A per-machine turbine-governor for the RMS transient-stability study (R061, governor part; October 2026 review, stream B3). The study calls `Initialize` once per run with the machine's initial mechanical power (pu on the MACHINE base), then `Step` once per integration step with the machine's start-of-step rotor speed deviation (pu), and holds the returned mechanical power (pu, machine base) across the step's swing integration. `Tgov1` and `HydroGovernor` implement it directly; `Ieeeg1` through `Ieeeg1Data` (a tandem-compound unit: both shafts' power on the one machine).
- [`GovernorData`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/RmsGovernor.cs#L29) (record): The parameters of one machine's turbine-governor: immutable data (machine base, seconds), carried on `SubtransientInit.MachineData.Governor` and turned into a FRESH stateful governor for every run by `Create`, so a critical-clearing-time search that runs the study many times never leaks state from one trial into the next. The three standard models are `Tgov1Data`, `Ieeeg1Data` and `HydroGovernorData`. Their parameter names follow the model classes' constructors exactly.
- [`Tgov1Data`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/RmsGovernor.cs#L39) (record): TGOV1 parameters (see `Tgov1`'s constructor; per-unit on the machine base).
- [`Ieeeg1Data`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/RmsGovernor.cs#L55) (record): IEEEG1 parameters (see `Ieeeg1`'s constructor; per-unit on the machine base). The RMS study treats the unit as TANDEM-COMPOUND: one shaft carries both the HP and the LP output (the eight fractions sum to 1, so the shaft holds the initial power at equilibrium). GridSim does not model cross-compound pairs (two machines on one governor); their LP machine would need its own entry.
- [`Tandem`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/RmsGovernor.cs#L73) (class): One shaft: the HP output plus the LP output of the same step. With the default fractions the LP output is exactly +0.0, so the shaft power is the HP output itself.
- [`GastData`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/RmsGovernor.cs#L87) (record): GAST parameters (see `Gast`'s constructor; per-unit on the machine base): the simple gas-turbine governor with its exhaust temperature load limit.
- [`HydroGovernorData`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/RmsGovernor.cs#L105) (record): Hydro governor parameters (see `HydroGovernor`'s constructor: permanent and transient droop, the dashpot reset time, the gate servo and the ideal water column; per-unit on the machine base). The v2 governor kind names this model "HYGOV"; it is GridSim's classic transient-droop governor with the ideal (inelastic, lossless) water column, which is the PSS/E HYGOV structure without HYGOV's turbine gain At, no-load flow qNL, turbine damping and gate-velocity limit (those are not modelled; a data set that relies on them is approximated, see the notes).

The kernel (`MultiMachineSubtransient`) needs nothing else from the network, so a dense Kron-reduced admittance and a sparse full network are interchangeable.
- [`RmsNetworkBuffers`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/RmsNetwork.cs#L48) (class): Shared argument checks for `IRmsNetwork.SolveInto`.
- [`RmsNetworkStage`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/RmsNetwork.cs#L63) (record): From `AtSeconds` on, the run integrates against `Network` (until the next stage whose time has arrived) - a fault applied, cleared, a branch tripped.
- [`DenseMachineNetwork`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/RmsNetwork.cs#L72) (class): The classic machine-only reduced admittance: `I_m = Y E`. The product is formed with exactly the arithmetic of `SubtransientNetworkInterface`, so a run through this network is bit-for-bit the historical kernel. Since R116 (October 2026) it runs on the vector units through `MachineAdmittanceColumns`, which keeps each row's summation order and so every bit; the admittance is copied at construction (the network multiplies by the matrix it was built with).
- [`SparseRmsNetwork`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/RmsNetwork.cs#L149) (class): The full (unreduced) network as a sparse system - the RMS network at every size (N271, October 2026: it was the large-case network only, gb-full, with a dense Kron reduction below 1,500 buses). Every machine is a Norton source at its terminal bus: admittance `y_i = 1/(jX''_i)` on the diagonal and current `E_i y_i` injected. Loads and held units are constant shunts, converters inject their currents at their buses. One solve `Y V = sum E_i y_i + Ic` then gives every machine current `I_i = (E_i - V_t,i) y_i` and every converter bus voltage. The network is linear, so this is exactly the Kron-reduced model without forming it: it is factored once per stage (sparse LU) and each evaluation is one back-substitution.
- [`Scratch`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/RmsNetwork.cs#L162) (class): Declared class; see the source and member declarations for its role.

```csharp
public interface IRmsNetwork
{
    int Machines { get; }

    int Converters { get; }

    (Complex[] MachineCurrents, Complex[] ConverterVoltages) Solve(Complex[] emf, Complex[] converterCurrents);

    void SolveInto(Complex[] emf, Complex[] converterCurrents, Complex[] machineCurrents, Complex[] converterVoltages)
    {
        ArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull(machineCurrents);
        ArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull(converterVoltages);
        (Complex[] im, Complex[] vc) = Solve(emf, converterCurrents);
        RmsNetworkBuffers.Check(im.Length, vc.Length, machineCurrents, converterVoltages);
        Array.Copy(im, machineCurrents, im.Length);
        Array.Copy(vc, converterVoltages, vc.Length);
    }
}
```

### src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/RmsNetworkSolvedIteration.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Dynamics.Models`. 133 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/RmsNetworkSolvedIteration.cs).

- [`RmsNetworkSolvedIteration`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/RmsNetworkSolvedIteration.cs#L23) (class): One pass of the RMS kernel's converter / network iteration for the units that solve their own network interface (`IRmsNetworkSolvedConverterModel`, the WECC REGC_B voltage source: DECISIONS D36 of the WECC expansion). Each such unit u at converter node c sees its node as `V = a + Zcc I_u`, with `a = V_last - Zcc I_u,last` the voltage of the last network solution without its own injection, and returns the injection phi_u(a) that solves its own model exactly. With ONE such unit that is the whole pass (the network is linear, so the next solution reproduces it and the iteration ends). With several, each unit's a depends on the others' injections through the network, `a_u = a_u,last + sum over w != u of Z_uw dI_w`, and holding the others fixed (block Jacobi or Gauss-Seidel) converges only linearly, slowly when two terminal-frame sources are electrically close (measured on WSCC-9 with two units: about 13 passes per step, and the 50-pass cap hit at a fault). So the pass takes one Newton step on the injections instead: `dI_u - S_u(sum over w != u of Z_uw dI_w) = phi_u - I_u,last`, where S_u, the real 2 x 2 sensitivity of phi_u to a, comes from two extra solves with a moved by 1e-7 |a| (real and imaginary). The linear system (2 x units reals) is solved by Gaussian elimination with partial pivoting; a singular system falls back to the Jacobi update. The kernel's convergence test (the change of the network solution) stays the judge, so the Newton step only decides how fast it is met.

### src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/RmsTransientStability.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Dynamics.Models`. 712 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/RmsTransientStability.cs).

- [`RmsTransientStability`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/RmsTransientStability.cs#L30) (class): RMS transient-stability study on the salient/subtransient multi-machine model (backlog P1-2) - the production step above the classical critical-clearing-time screen (`Distributed.ClassicalInit`). It seeds the fleet from a solved power flow with `SubtransientInit`, applies a bolted three-phase bus fault over a window through the integrator's network schedule (faulted reduced admittance during the fault, base network on clearing), and integrates the full six-state machines with `MultiMachineSubtransient`. This is the RMS engine the standard-model library was built for: real cases, the standard machine models, and a scheduled disturbance, with per-machine angle/speed/flux output and a synchronism verdict. By default the field is held (the classic first-swing assumption). Optional per-machine exciters (R061: `RmsExciter`, SEXS, IEEET1, EXAC1, ESAC1A or ESST4B, each optionally with a PSS1A) can be passed to `Study` and `CriticalClearingTimeSeconds`; their voltage references are set from the initial terminal voltages so the undisturbed fleet stays at equilibrium. With no exciters passed, every number is bit-for-bit the held-field study. Governors (R061, governor part, October 2026 stream B3) come with the machine data: `SubtransientInit.MachineData.Governor` (TGOV1, IEEEG1 or the hydro governor, `GovernorData`) drives that machine's mechanical power from its own rotor speed each step, initialised at the solved operating point; with no governor in the data every number is bit-for-bit the constant-Pm study. It reduces to the trusted classical critical-clearing time when the reactances are collapsed to `X'd`. Converter-interfaced plant enters as REGC_A/REEC-style current sources on retained buses (`RmsConverterState`), not as machines; the result's `Converters` carries their traces.
- [`FleetStudy`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/RmsTransientStability.cs#L102) (record): N246 rest (CF2, October 2026): a `Study` run together with what its synchronism test was judged on, so a caller can score law 9 from the same trajectory on the same machine set (`Physics.SynchronismFromTrajectory.Subtransient`).
- [`GovernorPlan`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/RmsTransientStability.cs#L142) (record): R061 (governor part; October 2026 review, stream B3; Ruling R1: Mark delegated EE calls 2026-10-04): the governors of one study, by machine slot of the prepared fleet. `BySlot` holds each machine's governor data (null: constant mechanical power); `MachineToSystem` is MBase / BaseMva per slot, the factor that turns a governor's machine-base power into the system base the swing integrates on.
- [`CctBracket`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/RmsTransientStability.cs#L497) (record): The step-quantised critical-clearing bracket of `RmsTransientStability.CriticalClearingBracket` (R106, ruling Q15) and of the classical `Distributed.ClassicalInit.CriticalClearingBracket` (N042, the same contract). Clearing after `StableSteps` whole integration steps keeps synchronism; clearing after `UnstableSteps` steps loses it (null when the whole search window survived). With the default iteration cap the two are adjacent steps, so the true boundary of the discretised model lies between them. N048: `UnstableSteps` is the FIRST loss from below (see `CctSearch` for the search and its guarantee), and `NonMonotone` says whether a stable pocket was seen above it.
- [`RmsExciter`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/RmsTransientStability.cs#L546) (class): A standard exciter for the RMS transient-stability study (R061): a `Sexs` or an `Ieeet1` AVR, optionally with a `Pss1a` stabiliser on the rotor speed deviation whose output is added to the AVR summing junction (`Verr = Vref - Vt + Vs`). Build one per machine with `FromSexs` or `FromIeeet1`; the parameters are the AVR's own constructor parameters. The wrapper owns the AVR (built here from the parameters, so it can also report the steady regulator error the kernel needs for the voltage reference) and only routes the signals; all dynamics are the existing blocks'. It is stateful: one instance per machine. `Initialize` resets every state, so one instance can be reused across separate runs (the CCT bisection does this).

### src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/Sexs.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Dynamics.Models`. 70 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/Sexs.cs).

- [`Sexs`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/Sexs.cs#L19) (class): SEXS - the Simplified Excitation System, the IEEE compact AVR and the first entry in GridSim's standard excitation library. It maps a voltage error to a field voltage and, like `Tgov1`, is a direct wiring of the common control blocks: a transient-gain-shaping lead-lag `(1+sTa)/(1+sTb)` followed by the exciter gain-lag `K/(1+sTe)` with non-windup ceiling/floor limits `[Emin, Emax]`: Verr = Vref - Vc + Vs (regulator error: reference - measured terminal + PSS signal) v1 = leadlag_{Ta/Tb}(Verr) Efd = lag_{K, Te, [Emin,Emax]}(v1) All quantities are per-unit. The steady field voltage is `Efd = clamp(K*Verr, Emin, Emax)`, so the high open-loop gain K holds the terminal-voltage error small - the defining behaviour of an AVR. The model carries no numerics of its own beyond routing the signal: the dynamics are the exact-discretised `LeadLag` and `FirstOrderLag` blocks.

### src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/SubtransientInit.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Dynamics.Models`. 680 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/SubtransientInit.cs).

- [`SubtransientInit`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/SubtransientInit.cs#L57) (class): Builds the `MultiMachineSubtransient` inputs from a solved power flow - the subtransient analogue of `ClassicalInit`. It computes the self-consistent six-state fixed point so an undisturbed run seeded from a real dispatch is stationary: 1. each generator's terminal voltage and current come from the solved case (`I_t = conj(S_gen/V_t)`); 2. the rotor angle is the angle of the q-axis phasor `V_t + jXq*I_t` - the classic salient-machine construction, which forces `Vd = Xq*Iq` and hence makes every flux-decay derivative vanish; 3. the dq terminal quantities then give the transient and subtransient EMFs directly (`E'q = Vq + X'd*Id`, `E'd = Vd - X'q*Iq`, `E''q = Vq + X''d*Id`, `E''d = Vd - X''q*Iq`); 4. the field voltage is set to hold `E'q` (`Efd = E'q + (Xd - X'd)*Id + E''q*Se(|E''|)`, the GENROU d-axis saturation increment since N045; it used to read `Se(E'q)`), and the mechanical power to the electrical output (`Pm = Vd*Id + Vq*Iq`). With saturation the q-axis behaves as the saturated reactance (scale `(Xq - Xl)/(Xd - Xl)`, see the N045 note below), so step 2 uses that reactance; 5. each machine is folded into the network by its round subtransient reactance `X''` and the augmented admittance is Kron-reduced to the internal nodes - the reduced admittance the swing uses. Reactances and inertia convert from the machine base by the `MBase/BaseMva` ratio. Converter plant. A converter-interfaced generator (`Generator.IsConverterInterfaced`) is not a machine: it has no rotor, inertia or EMF behind `X''`. By default it is taken out of the machine fleet and its terminal bus is retained after the machine internal nodes, as an `RmsConverterUnit` current source initialised on its share of the solved bus injection (co-located converters are aggregated into one unit per bus). Its `MachineData` entry is ignored. `convertersAsCurrentSources: false` restores the old treatment (every generator a machine). Power-flow-only units (`Generator.PowerFlowOnly`: a slack balancer, a voltage-control device) are neither machines nor converters: their solved injection becomes a constant admittance at their bus. So is a synchronous-typed unit with no inertia (`H <= 0`), which cannot be integrated; those are listed in `Prepared.HeldUnits`. An island with no integrable machine but a slack or PV bus gets a stiff synthetic reference source at that bus (`Prepared.IslandReferences`) - otherwise the converter current sources and held admittances there would have no voltage reference and float. One network engine at every size (N271, October 2026; ruled by main under Mark's determinism rule 2026-10-04, Ruling R1: Mark delegated EE calls 2026-10-04). Every case is prepared on the sparse full network (`SparseRmsNetwork`: machines as Norton sources behind `X''`, factored once per stage with the same sparse LU as the fault network, N233). Before, a case of up to 1,500 buses was prepared on a Kron-reduced dense admittance and only larger ones (gb-full) on the sparse network. The two are the same linear model, but they are different arithmetic, so a 9-bus case and gb-full did not run the same engine and their answers differed in the last bits: two answers to one question, which the determinism rule forbids. The size switch is gone, exactly as the fault network lost it at N233 and the power flow at N057; cases above 1,500 buses were already sparse and are bit for bit unchanged. The dense Kron path survives only as a TEST ORACLE (`DenseKronReferenceScope`): an independent algorithm the tests cross-check the sparse answers against; no production code can select it. A unit's `Generator.UnitTransformerXPu` is added to every machine reactance (the machine referred to the HV bus).
- [`RestoreDenseKronFlow`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/SubtransientInit.cs#L81) (class): Declared class; see the source and member declarations for its role.
- [`MachineData`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/SubtransientInit.cs#L94) (record): Per-machine dynamic data on the machine's own base (aligned to `model.Generators`); the round subtransient reactance folded into the network is `Xdpp` (= `Xqpp`). `Governor` (R061, governor part; October 2026, stream B3): the machine's turbine-governor parameters, or null for a constant mechanical power (the historical study). The RMS study builds a fresh governor from it for every run (`RmsTransientStability`); this initialisation does not read it. `Xl` (N045): the stator leakage reactance (machine base), read only by the GENROU q-axis saturation scale `(Xq - Xl) / (Xd - Xl)`; 0 (the default) is the leakage-free limit. It must be below X''d (checked when the machine is saturated).

- [`SubtransientMachine`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/SubtransientMachine.cs#L42) (class): The subtransient synchronous machine on a single-machine-infinite-bus (SMIB) network - the GENROU/GENSAL-class model, the step up from the two-axis machine (`TwoAxisMachine`). It adds the fast subtransient EMFs `E''q` and `E''d` behind the subtransient reactances `X''d`, `X''q`: the damper-winding flux linkages that dominate the first cycle or two after a disturbance, cascaded off the transient EMFs by the short subtransient time constants `T''do`, `T''qo`. Six states per machine (per-unit, angle in rad, times in seconds): ddelta/dt = omega_s * omega (rotor angle) domega/dt = (Pm - Pe - D*omega) / (2 H) (swing) T'do dE'q/dt = Efd - E'q - (Xd - X'd)*Id (d-axis field flux decay; with saturation also - E''q*Se(|E''|), N045, see SaturationCurve) T''do dE''q/dt = E'q - E''q - (X'd - X''d)*Id (d-axis damper flux, cascaded off E'q) T'qo dE'd/dt = -E'd + (Xq - X'q)*Iq (q-axis flux decay; with saturation also - E''d*Se(|E''|)*(Xq - Xl)/(Xd - Xl), N045) T''qo dE''d/dt = E'd - E''d + (X'q - X''q)*Iq (q-axis damper flux, cascaded off E'd) The stator (Rs = 0) sees the subtransient EMFs behind the subtransient reactances, `Vd = E''d + X''q*Iq`, `Vq = E''q - X''d*Id`, so against the infinite bus Id = (E''q - Vinf*cos(delta)) / (X''d + Xe) Iq = (Vinf*sin(delta) - E''d) / (X''q + Xe) - a closed-form network solve - and `Pe = E''d*Id + E''q*Iq + (X''q - X''d)*Id*Iq`. Every flux state rides the same exact zero-order-hold `FirstOrderLag`: over a step with the currents and the transient EMFs held, each subtransient equation is a first-order lag on its (constant) input, the same as the transient equations. The rotor swing advances by RK4 with the subtransient EMFs frozen - the operator splitting used throughout the library. It collapses onto `TwoAxisMachine` as a reduction identity: with `X''d = X'd` and `X''q = X'q` the damper drivers vanish and the fixed points give `E''q = E'q`, `E''d = E'd`, so the subtransient stator, currents and power are exactly the two-axis machine's.
- [`SaturationCurve`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/SubtransientMachine.cs#L54) (record): The open-circuit magnetic-saturation curve, the standard scaled-quadratic form `Se(x) = B*(x - A)^2 / x` for `x > A` (else 0), fitted to the two tabulated points `Se(1.0) = SatAt1Pu` and `Se(1.2) = SatAt12Pu` - the PSS/E S(1.0), S(1.2) saturation FACTORS (dimensionless fractional extra field current over the air-gap line at 1.0 and 1.2 pu air-gap flux). The field-current increment that enters the field balance is `FieldIncrement` = `x * Se(x)` (R251, ruling Q9). The fit is closed-form: `k = sqrt(1.2*S12/S1)`, `A = (k - 1.2)/(k - 1)`, `B = S1/(1 - A)^2`. A curve with `SatAt1Pu = 0` is the unsaturated machine (`Se == 0`).
- [`Parameters`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/SubtransientMachine.cs#L157) (record): Machine and SMIB-network parameters, all per-unit on the machine base (times in seconds). Constraints are enforced on construction (fail-loud). `Saturation` is optional: null (the default) is the unsaturated machine, solving bit-for-bit as before. `LeakageReactance` (N045) is the stator leakage Xl, used only by the q-axis saturation scale; 0 (the default) is the leakage-free limit.

### src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/SubtransientNetworkInterface.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Dynamics.Models`. 155 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/SubtransientNetworkInterface.cs).

- [`SubtransientNetworkInterface`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/SubtransientNetworkInterface.cs#L44) (class): The salient / subtransient multi-machine network interface - the dq-frame current-injection core that carries the two-axis machine (`TwoAxisMachine` / `SubtransientMachine`) into a coupled network. It is the generalisation of `MultiMachineFluxDecay.NetworkInjection` from a round-rotor internal voltage `E'q&#8736;delta` to a full two-axis internal voltage with both a d- and a q-axis component, so a machine that is not a simple voltage-behind-one-reactance still enters the network in closed form. Each machine presents at its internal node the subtransient EMF `(E''q, E''d)` in its own rotor frame; rotated into the common network frame by the load angle `delta` it is the phasor Vr_i = E''q_i*cos(delta_i) + E''d_i*sin(delta_i) Vi_i = E''q_i*sin(delta_i) - E''d_i*cos(delta_i) (so a pure q-axis EMF, `E''d = 0`, is exactly `E''q&#8736;delta` - the round-rotor case). With the subtransient reactance `X''` folded into the reduced admittance `Y` (as `Distributed.ClassicalInit` folds `X'd`), the injected current is one matrix-vector product `I_i = sum_j Y_ij V_j`, the air-gap power is `Pe_i = Re(V_i * conj(I_i))`, and the dq currents that drive the flux decay are recovered by the inverse rotation Iq_i = Ir_i*cos(delta_i) + Ii_i*sin(delta_i) Id_i = Ir_i*sin(delta_i) - Ii_i*cos(delta_i) so there is no iterative network solve - the whole interface is closed form and deterministic. This interface requires a round subtransient reactance (`X''d = X''q`, folded into `Y`); the internal saliency (`Xd`, `Xq`, `X'd`, `X'q` all distinct) lives in the per-machine flux dynamics, exactly as at SMIB scale. It reduces to `MultiMachineFluxDecay.NetworkInjection` field-for-field when every `E''d = 0`: both `Pe` and the recovered `Id = sum_j E''q_j (G_ij sin(delta_ij) - B_ij cos(delta_ij))` agree with the round-rotor closed form. For a lossless reduced network the per-machine air-gap powers sum to zero (the machines only exchange power). These are the oracles it is validated against. An optional `extraCurrent` adds a current to each machine's injection before the power and dq currents are formed - the coupling term `Ymc Ycc^-1 Ic` through which converter current sources on retained buses (`ConverterNetwork`) act on the machines. Null leaves the closed form as is.

### src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/Tgov1.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Dynamics.Models`. 96 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/Tgov1.cs).

- [`Tgov1`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/Tgov1.cs#L21) (class): TGOV1 - the standard steam turbine-governor, the simplest of the IEEE governor family and the first entry in GridSim's standard turbine-governor library. It maps rotor speed deviation to mechanical power and is a direct wiring of the common control blocks: a droop gain `1/R`, a valve/steam-bowl lag `1/(1+sT1)` with non-windup position limits `[Vmin, Vmax]`, a reheat lead-lag `(1+sT2)/(1+sT3)`, and a turbine-damping term `Dt*dw`: valveCmd = Pref - dw/R Pgv = lag_{T1, [Vmin,Vmax]}(valveCmd) (mechanical valve/gate position) Pt = leadlag_{T2/T3}(Pgv) (turbine power after reheat shaping) Pmech = Pt - Dt*dw All quantities are per-unit on the machine base. With `Pref` set to the mechanical power at synchronous speed, `dw = 0` is an exact fixed point (the undisturbed run is stationary, matching the classical-model initialisation), and the steady droop is `dPmech/dw = -1/R - Dt` in the unlimited region. The model owns no numerics of its own beyond this arithmetic - the dynamics are the exact-discretised `FirstOrderLag` and `LeadLag` blocks.

### src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/TwoAxisMachine.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Dynamics.Models`. 249 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/TwoAxisMachine.cs).

- [`TwoAxisMachine`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/TwoAxisMachine.cs#L44) (class): The two-axis synchronous machine on a single-machine-infinite-bus (SMIB) network - the step up from the one-axis flux-decay model (`OneAxisMachine`). It adds the q-axis transient EMF `E'd` as a fourth state, driven by the q-axis flux-linkage decay, so both axes now carry transient dynamics and the stator sees the transient reactances on both axes (`X'd`, `X'q`) rather than `X'd` on the d-axis and the synchronous `Xq` on the q-axis. Four states per machine (per-unit, angles in rad, times in seconds): ddelta/dt = omega_s * omega (rotor angle) domega/dt = (Pm - Pe - D*omega) / (2 H) (swing, omega = pu speed deviation) T'do dE'q/dt = Efd - E'q - (Xd - X'd) * Id (d-axis field flux-linkage decay) T'qo dE'd/dt = -E'd + (Xq - X'q) * Iq (q-axis flux-linkage decay) The stator is algebraic (Rs = 0, no stator transients), `Vd = E'd + X'q*Iq`, `Vq = E'q - X'd*Id` (Anderson & Fouad two-axis form), and against an infinite bus `Vinf&#8736;0` through the external reactance `Xe` the dq currents have the closed form Id = (E'q - Vinf*cos(delta)) / (X'd + Xe) Iq = (Vinf*sin(delta) - E'd) / (X'q + Xe) so there is no iterative network solve - the SMIB interface is a two-line linear solve, exact and deterministic. The air-gap power is `Pe = E'd*Id + E'q*Iq + (X'q - X'd)*Id*Iq`, the last term the transient-saliency reluctance power. Each flux state advances, over a step with `Id`/`Iq` and `Efd` held, exactly as a first-order lag on the same exact zero-order-hold `FirstOrderLag` as the rest of the library: `E'q` with input `Efd - (Xd - X'd)*Id`, and `E'd` with input `(Xq - X'q)*Iq`. The rotor swing advances by RK4 with both EMFs frozen across the sub-steps (operator splitting, the same discipline the governor and one-axis models use). It collapses onto `OneAxisMachine` as a reduction identity: with `X'q = Xq` the q-axis flux-decay driver vanishes, so an `E'd` started at its equilibrium `0` stays `0`, the stator q-axis reduces to `Vd = Xq*Iq`, and both the currents and `Pe = E'q*Iq + (Xq - X'd)*Id*Iq` are exactly the one-axis machine's. Its steady state reproduces the one-axis synchronous q-axis: `E'd_eq = (Xq - X'q)*Vinf*sin(delta)/(Xq + Xe)` makes `Iq = Vinf*sin(delta)/(Xq + Xe)`, the same current the one-axis model carries.
- [`Parameters`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/TwoAxisMachine.cs#L51) (record): Machine and SMIB-network parameters, all per-unit on the machine base (times in seconds). Constraints are enforced on construction (fail-loud); the derived reactance sums `X'd + Xe` and `X'q + Xe` are then positive by construction.
- [`Trace`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/TwoAxisMachine.cs#L96) (record): Trajectory: one entry per sample of each state and the derived terminal quantities.

### src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/Wecc/CurrentSourceNetworkSolver.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Dynamics.Models.Wecc`. 133 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/Wecc/CurrentSourceNetworkSolver.cs).

- [`CurrentSourceNetworkSolver`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/Wecc/CurrentSourceNetworkSolver.cs#L21) (class): Exact network-interface solution for a current source injected along its own terminal-voltage angle whose current in that frame depends only on the terminal voltage MAGNITUDE x and is affine in x between known break points (REGC_A: `g(x) = Ip LVACM(x) - j max(Iqx - Khv max(x - Volim, 0), Iolim)`). DECISIONS D38 of the WECC expansion. The kernel gives the Thevenin view of the unit's node, `V c1 = a + c2 I` (`Regcb.SolveWithNetwork` explains a, c1, c2). With `V = x e^{j phi}` and `I = g(x) e^{j phi}` the frame condition is the scalar equation `|x c1 - c2 g(x)| = |a|`, `phi = arg a - arg(x c1 - c2 g(x))`; on each affine piece it is a quadratic, solved in closed form. Of the roots with x above `RmsConverterState.PllLockMinVoltagePu` the one whose angle is nearest the last committed angle is taken. With no root (for example active current into a near-terminal bolted fault: no terminal angle is consistent) the frame is held at the last angle, as the converter holds it below the lock voltage: then `V c1 = a + c2 g(|V|) e^{j theta}`, again a scalar quadratic per piece in x = |V|, and the root nearest the last committed magnitude is taken.

### src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/Wecc/DerA.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Dynamics.Models.Wecc`. 416 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/Wecc/DerA.cs).

- [`DeraParameters`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/Wecc/DerA.cs#L12) (record): DER_A, the WECC aggregated distributed energy resource model, after P. Pourbeik, "Proposal for DER_A model", memo to the WECC REMTF (10/11/16, revised to 6/19/19; public on wecc.org), Fig. 2 (block diagram), Fig. 3 and the Appendix (partial voltage tripping, Vrfrac logic), Table 1 (the 48 parameters, in this order). Per unit on the unit's MBASE.
- [`DerAState`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/Wecc/DerA.cs#L166) (class): DER_A dynamics (see `DeraParameters`), all states advanced from start-of-step inputs (`WeccBlocks`): s0 Vt_filt = lag(Vt, Trv); vp = max(Vt_filt, 0.01); Iqv = clamp(Kqv db(Vref0 - Vt_filt, dbd1, dbd2), Iql1, Iqh1) s1 = lag(Pord, Tp) (the power feedback is the power order, memo item g) s2 = lag((Pflag ? tan(pf0) s1 : Qref) / vp, Tiq); Iqcmd = clamp(s2 + Iqv, -Iqmax, Iqmax) s5 Frq_filt = lag(f, Trf); df = db(1 - Frq_filt, fdbd1, fdbd2); droop = Ddn min(df, 0) + Dup max(df, 0) s6: PI(Kpg, Kig) on clamp(Pref - s1 + droop, femin, femax) in [Pmin, Pmax]; input = Freq_flag ? PI out : Pref s7 = that input rate limited to [dPmin, dPmax]; s8 Pord = lag(s7, Tpord) in [Pmin, Pmax]; Ipcmd = clamp(Pord / vp, Ipmin, Ipmax) current limit: Q priority Iqmax = Imax, Ipmax = sqrt(Imax^2 - Iqcmd^2); P priority Ipmax = Imax, Iqmax = sqrt(Imax^2 - Ipcmd^2); Ipmin = -Ipmax for storage (typeflag = 0), else 0 s4 = lag(Vrfrac multiplier of Vt_filt, Tv); m = Vtripflag ? s4 : 1; m = 0 once the frequency trip has acted s3 Iq = lag(m Iqcmd, Tg); s9 Ip = lag(m Ipcmd, Tg), rise limited to rrpwr while Ip >= 0 (and the charging rise to -rrpwr while Ip <= 0, memo footnote 2) Partial voltage tripping is the memo's Appendix pseudo code, on Vt_filt (memo note 10), with the low side (vl0, vl1, tvl0, tvl1, Vmin) and the same logic on the high side (vh1, vh0, tvh1, tvh0, Vmax); the two multipliers are multiplied (DECISIONS D26). A timer "exceeds" its setting when the time since it started is above the setting by more than a millionth of a step (the engine's event-time convention). Frequency tripping (Ftripflag): the filtered frequency, read as nominal while Vt_filt <= Vpr, below fl for more than tfl or above fh for more than tfh trips the whole model for the rest of the run (its current commands become 0 and the Tg lags take its current to 0). Network interface. The memo places a voltage source behind Xe at the terminal as a numerical device; with its EMF recomputed from the model's currents it injects the model's current at the solved voltage. GridSim solves the current-source interface to its algebraic fixed point (1e-10 pu) every step, so the injected current is exactly the model's current and Xe has no effect; it is range-checked and named in the DYR notes (DECISIONS D24). Frequency is the backward difference of the terminal voltage angle over the step, `1 + wrap(dtheta) / (2 pi f0 dt)`, into the Trf transducer lag. Initialisation from (P0, Q0, V0): Pref = P0 and every P state at P0, Qref = Q0 (or tan(pf0) = Q0 / P0), s2 = Q0 / V0, the multiplier at 1; refused unless vl1 < V0 < vh1 (memo note 9), V0 - Vref0 is inside the deadband when Kqv is not zero (memo note 4a: GridSim refuses rather than move Vref0), P0 is inside [Pmin, Pmax] and the initial currents inside the current limit; then every state residual must be under 1e-9.

- [`ReecOutputs`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/Wecc/Reec.cs#L26) (record struct): What a REEC model computes from its states for one step: the current commands and the block inputs the state advance needs.
- [`IReecModel`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/Wecc/Reec.cs#L43) (interface): An electrical control model as the composed WECC unit drives it (REEC_A/B/C in `Reec`, REEC_D in `Reecd`): the same four calls per step, in the same order.
- [`Reec`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/Wecc/Reec.cs#L89) (class): REEC_A / REEC_B / REEC_C (PSS/E REECA1 / REECB1 / REECCU1), the renewable energy electrical controls, after EPRI 3002006525 Figs. D-1, D-2, D-3, Fig. 3-2 (state transitions), Fig. 3-4 (storage) and App. B (current limit logic). Per unit on the unit's MBASE; reactive current exporting positive. s0 Vt_filt = lag(Vt, Trv) s1 Pe_filt = lag(Pe, Tp) vp = max(Vt_filt, 0.01) Voltage_dip = Vt < Vdip or Vt > Vup (raw Vt, DECISIONS D6) Qsel = PfFlag ? tan(pf0) Pe_filt : Qext; Qlim = clamp(Qsel, Qmin, Qmax) VFlag=1: Vsel = clamp(Kqp (Qlim - Qgen) + s2, Vmin, Vmax), s2' = Kqi (Qlim - Qgen) in [Vmin, Vmax] VFlag=0: Vsel = clamp(Vref1 + Qlim, Vmin, Vmax) (REEC_B/C: no Vref1, DECISIONS D8) QFlag=1: Iqv_path = clamp(Kvp (Vsel - Vt_filt) + s3, Iqmin, Iqmax), s3' = Kvi (Vsel - Vt_filt) in [Iqmin, Iqmax] QFlag=0: Iqv_path = s4, s4 = lag(Qlim / vp, Tiq) Iqv = clamp(Kqv db(Vref0 - Vt_filt, dbd1, dbd2), Iql1, Iqh1) Iqinj: 0 normal; Iqv in a dip; after the dip (REEC_A) Iqfrz for Thld s (Thld > 0) or Iqv for -Thld s (Thld < 0) Iqcmd = clamp(Iqv_path + Iqinj, -Iqmax, Iqmax) prl = Pref rate limited to [dPmin, dPmax]; Psel = PFlag ? prl Wg : prl; s5 Pord = lag(Psel, Tpord) in [Pmin, Pmax] Ipcmd = clamp(Pord / vp, Ipmin, Ipmax) current limit (App. B): Q priority Iqmax = min(VDL1, Imax), Ipmax = min(VDL2, sqrt(Imax^2 - Iqcmd^2)); P priority Ipmax = min(VDL2, Imax), Iqmax = min(VDL1, sqrt(Imax^2 - Ipcmd^2)); Ipmin = 0 (REEC_C: -Ipmax); REEC_A Thld2 holds Ipmax at its dip value after the dip. REEC_C: SOC = SOCini - (1/T) integral(Pe dt); SOC <= SOCmin -> Ipmax = 0; SOC >= SOCmax -> Ipmin = 0. s2, s3, s4, s5 are frozen while Voltage_dip = 1.
- [`WeccEquilibrium`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/Wecc/Reec.cs#L322) (class): The fail-loud equilibrium gate every WECC model runs at initialisation.

### src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/Wecc/Reecd.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Dynamics.Models.Wecc`. 370 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/Wecc/Reecd.cs).

- [`ReecdParameters`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/Wecc/Reecd.cs#L21) (record): REEC_D: the renewable energy electrical control model of the WECC REMWG memo Rev. 27b (Pourbeik, 2/16/23, section 3.1, Figure 3 and Table 3; approved by the WECC MVS in August 2020): REEC_A with ten-point VDLq / VDLp tables (Iqmin = Iqmax when Iqmax is negative; Ipmin = -Ke Ipmax), local current or reactive-droop compensation (rc, Xc, Kc, Tr1, Vcmpflag), an always-active reactive injection arm with the Iqcmd_bl hold (Thld), the Ipcmd/Ipmax hold (Thld2), converter blocking (vblkl, vblkh, Tblk_delay), qvmax/qvmin on the incoming reference, Paux, the dip flag from Vt_filt, and the linked non-windup PI limits of the memo's page 10-11 pseudo code. Per unit on MBASE; reactive current exporting positive. GridSim reads a `'REEC_D'` record (no public source gives the PSS/E record order; DECISIONS D30): six flags PfFlag VFlag QFlag PFlag PqFlag Vcmpflag, then the 78 values in the order of the EPRI REGC_B/REEC_D test protocol's Table 5 (EPRI memo to WECC REMTF, 8/17/2020): mvab Vdip Vup Trv dbd1 dbd2 Kqv Iqh1 Iql1 Vref0 Iqfrz Thld Thld2 Tp qvmax qvmin Vmax Vmin Kqp Kqi Kvp Kvi Vref1 Tiq dPmax dPmin Pmax Pmin Imax Tpord rc Xc Tr1 Kc Ke vq1 iq1 .. vq10 iq10 vp1 ip1 .. vp10 ip10 vblkl vblkh Tblk_delay.
- [`Reecd`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/Wecc/Reecd.cs#L173) (class): REEC_D (see `ReecdParameters`). The equations, beyond REEC_A (`Reec`): s0 Vt_filt = lag(Vt, Trv); Voltage_dip = Vt_filt < Vdip or Vt_filt > Vup (from Vt_filt, memo item 6) s6 Vcomp = lag(Vcmpflag ? |Vt - (rc + j Xc) It| : Vt + Kc Qgen, Tr1) Qsel = PfFlag ? tan(pfaref) Pe_filt : Qext; Qlim = clamp(Qsel, qvmin, qvmax) Vsel = clamp(VFlag ? Kqp (Qlim - Qgen) + s2 : Vref1 + Qlim, Vmin, Vmax) QFlag 1: clamp(Kvp (Vsel - Vcomp) + s3, Iqmin, Iqmax); QFlag 0: s4 = lag(Qlim / vp, Tiq) Iqinj = clamp(Kqv db(Vref0 - Vt_filt), Iql1, Iqh1) always active (memo item 2c) Iqcmd_bl = Q path + Iqinj, held after a dip for |Thld| s (Thld > 0: its last dip value; < 0: Iqfrz) Iqcmd = clamp(Iqcmd_bl, Iqmin, Iqmax); Iqmin = Iqmax < 0 ? Iqmax : -Iqmax Ipcmd = clamp((Pord + Paux) / vp, -Ke Ipmax, Ipmax); Ipcmd and Ipmax held at their last dip values for Thld2 s blocked (Vt_filt <= vblkl or >= vblkh, and Tblk_delay after it returns): every limit 0, so Ipcmd = Iqcmd = 0 linked non-windup: s3 at a limit with its derivative pushing out stops, and stops s2 too when s2 pushes the same way Paux is 0 (GridSim has no external auxiliary-control models). The baseload flag of the North American tools is not a REEC_D parameter (it belongs to the generator record) and is not modelled (baseload 0).
