All quantities are per unit on the unit's own MVA base (MBASE). Reactive current is held EXPORT-positive (DECISIONS D2): the diagram's `-1/(1+sTg)` block gives the network-convention `Iq = -Iq_export`. states Ip = lag(Ipcmd, Tg), rise limited to Rrpwr, upper limit LVPL(Vf) (s1, non-windup) Iqx = lag(Iqcmd, Tg), export fall limited to Iqrmax when Q0 > 0, export rise limited to -Iqrmin when Q0 < 0 (s0) Vf = lag(|Vt|, Tfltr) (s2) network Ip_out = Ip * LVACM(|Vt|) LVACM = 0 below Lvpnt0, 1 above Lvpnt1, linear between Iqx_out = max(Iqx - Khv max(|Vt| - Volim, 0), Iolim) (HVRCM, DECISIONS D3) LVPL(Vf) = 0 at or below Zerox, Lvpl1 (Vf - Zerox)/(Brkpt - Zerox) between, no limit at or above Brkpt The two network blocks (LVACM, HVRCM) are algebraic in the terminal voltage and are evaluated inside the converter / network fixed point; the three states advance once per step from the start-of-step voltage with the current commands held (see `WeccBlocks`).

Values per unit on the unit's MBASE. The record order GridSim reads is the memo's Table 1 order: Tg Iqrmax Iqrmin Tfltr rrpwr RateFlag Te Imax pqflag re Xe.
- [`RegcbNetworkSolution`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/Wecc/Regcb.cs#L60) (record struct): REGC_B's exact solution against the Thevenin view of its node (`Regcb.SolveWithNetwork`): the node voltage, the terminal current (machine base, network frame), the converter frame angle and whether that frame is held.
- [`Regcb`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/Wecc/Regcb.cs#L84) (class): REGC_B, the voltage-source generator/converter (see `RegcbParameters` for the source). Reactive current is held EXPORT-positive, as in `Regca` (DECISIONS D2). s0 Iqx = lag(Iqcmd, Tg), rate limits Iqrmax / Iqrmin on the side Q0 selects (as REGC_A) s2 Vf = lag(|Vt|, Tfltr); vp = max(Vf, 0.01) (the 0.01 floor is on Vt itself) s1 RateFlag 0: lag(Ipcmd, Tg), Ip = s1; RateFlag 1: lag(Ipcmd vp, Tg), Ip = s1 / vp rrpwr bounds a RISING magnitude of s1 (both signs: a store charging recovers at -rrpwr; memo footnote 4) E target in the terminal-voltage frame (d along Vt, so Vtd = |Vt|, Vtq = 0 and id = Ip, iq = -Iqx, as the memo's "Id (= Ip)" fixes the frame): Ed = |Vt| + id re - iq Xe, Eq = iq re + id Xe, i.e. |Vt| + (re + j Xe)(Ip - j Iqx) s3, s4 Ed, Eq = lag(target, Te) network: the source (Ed + j Eq) e^{j theta} behind re + j Xe, theta the angle of the terminal voltage OF THE SAME network solution (DECISIONS D36: the frame the memo defines; solved exactly with the network by `SolveWithNetwork`, so it converges on weak nodes and a steadily turning terminal leaves no error); the frame is held at the last angle only while no consistent terminal frame exists (a phase-locked loop freezing). The Norton admittance y = r / (re + j Xe) is stamped on the bus; terminal current I = (E - V) / Z, limited to Imax in magnitude on the frame axis with the priority pqflag (DECISIONS D31) The states advance once per step from the start-of-step terminal voltage with the commands held; Ed and Eq are constant over the step, so a change of the terminal voltage MAGNITUDE moves the current at once (the voltage-source behaviour the memo introduces REGC_B for), while a rotation of the terminal angle carries the source with it exactly.

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Dynamics.Models.Wecc`. 265 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/Wecc/RegfmA1.cs).

- [`RegfmA1Parameters`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/Wecc/RegfmA1.cs#L15) (record): REGFM_A1: the droop-controlled grid-forming inverter model approved by the WECC MVS on 27 September 2023 (W. Du et al., "Model Specification of Droop-Controlled, Grid-Forming Inverters (REGFM_A1)", PNNL-35110, September 2023: Fig. 1-5, Table 1, Eq. 1-9). Per unit on the inverter rating (MBASE). GridSim reads a `'REGFM_A1'` record (the PSS/E record order is not public; DECISIONS D30) with the 22 data values of Table 1 in its order, the three set points that the power flow initialises (Vref, Qref, Pref) left out: XL mq kpv kiv Emax Emin mp Pmax Pmin kppmax kipmax omega0 TPf TQf TVf Qmax Qmin VFlag QVFlag kpqmax kiqmax ImaxF.
- [`RegfmA1State`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/Wecc/RegfmA1.cs#L111) (class): REGFM_A1 in the RMS engine (see `RegfmA1Parameters`). A voltage source E at angle delta behind j XL, stamped as its Norton admittance on the bus (spec Eq. 8, 9). Per unit on MBASE; the network sees system per unit. Pinv = lag(P, TPf), Qinv = lag(Q, TQf), Vinv = lag(|V|, TVf) (Eq. 4-6, P and Q at the terminal) dPmax = min(0, kppmax (Pmax - Pinv) + xPmax), xPmax' = kipmax (Pmax - Pinv), xPmax <= 0 dPmin = max(0, kppmax (Pmin - Pinv) + xPmin), xPmin' = kipmax (Pmin - Pinv), xPmin >= 0 d omega = omega0 (mp (Pref - Pinv) + dPmax + dPmin) (rad/s); delta' = d omega; omega = omega0 + d omega dQmax, dQmin likewise with kpqmax, kiqmax on Qinv Vcmd = Vref + mq (Qref - Qinv) + dQmax + dQmin VFlag 1: Edroop = clamp(kpv (Vcmd - Vinv) + xV, Emin, Emax), xV' = kiv (Vcmd - Vinv) in [Emin, Emax] VFlag 0: Edroop = clamp(Vcmd, Emin, Emax) network: I = (Edroop e^{j delta} - V) / (j XL); |I| > ImaxF -> I = ImaxF I / |I| (Fig. 4: same angle phi) Initialisation: I0 from the solved P0, Q0, V0; E0 = V0 + j XL I0, delta0 = angle(E0); Pref = P0; Qref = 0 (QVFlag 1) or Q0 (QVFlag 0); Vref so that Vcmd = V0 (VFlag 1) or |E0| (VFlag 0); xV = |E0|. Refused, naming the quantity: P0 outside [Pmin, Pmax], Q0 outside [Qmin, Qmax], |E0| outside [Emin, Emax], |I0| at or above ImaxF. Integration (the WECC rule, `WeccBlocks`): lags by exact ZOH, integrators and delta by forward Euler, all from the start-of-step measurements; E is constant over a step except through the algebraic current limit. The spec says nothing of freezing the controls while the current limit acts, so nothing is frozen (DECISIONS D33).

Two independent paths: the reactive path regulates a voltage (RefFlag = 1; with line drop compensation or reactive droop) or a branch reactive power (RefFlag = 0) and gives Qext to the REEC model; the active path (Fflag = 1) gives Pref with primary frequency response (separate droops Ddn / Dup and a deadband). All P and Q quantities are per unit on the unit's MBASE (DECISIONS D16); voltages in per unit.
- [`RepcInputs`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/Wecc/Repca.cs#L137) (record struct): The measured inputs of REPC_A for one step (machine base for P and Q).
- [`Repca`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/Wecc/Repca.cs#L154) (class): The REPC_A dynamics (see `RepcaParameters`, EPRI 3002006525 Fig. 3-5): Vmeas = VCFlag ? Vcomp : Vreg + Kc Qbranch; s0 = lag(Vmeas, Tfltr); s1 = lag(Qbranch, Tfltr) err = RefFlag ? Vref - s0 : Qref - s1; e = clamp(db(err, dbd1, dbd2), emin, emax) s2 : PI Kp + Ki/s on e, integral and output in [Qmin, Qmax], integral frozen while Vreg < Vfrz Qext = leadlag(PI out, Tft, Tfv) (s3) s4 = lag(Pbranch, Tp); df = db(Freq_ref - Freq, fdbd1, fdbd2); droop = Ddn min(df, 0) + Dup max(df, 0) ep = clamp(Plant_pref - s4 + droop, femin, femax); s5: PI Kpg + Kig/s on ep in [Pmin, Pmax]; Pref = lag(s5 out, Tg) (s6) Initialised so the plant output, the regulated voltage and the frequency are their initial values with zero error: Vref = the initial Vmeas, Qref = the initial Qbranch, Plant_pref = the initial Pbranch, Freq_ref = 1, the PI integrals and the lead-lag at the REEC model's initial Qext and Pref. With Fflag = 0 the Pref output is the REEC model's initial Pref, held.

### src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/Wecc/WeccBlocks.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Dynamics.Models.Wecc`. 97 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/Wecc/WeccBlocks.cs).

- [`WeccBlocks`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/Wecc/WeccBlocks.cs#L19) (class): The block primitives the WECC renewable models are drawn with, beyond `ControlBlocks`: pure static functions of (state, input, step) with no hidden state, so every model built on them is a pure function of its inputs and bit-for-bit reproducible. Integration rule (shared by every WECC model, the same as the converter model it extends). A step evaluates every block input from the start-of-step states and measured quantities, then advances every state: a first-order lag by the exact zero-order hold of its pole (`Lag`: for an input held across the step `x <- u + (x - u) exp(-dt/T)` is the closed-form solution, A-stable at any step), an integrator by forward Euler (`Integrate`, exact for a held input). A limit on a state is a non-windup limit: the state itself is clamped, so it leaves the limit on the first step its input reverses. A rate limit bounds the change of the state over the step to rate x dt.
- [`HoldTimer`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/Wecc/WeccBlocks.cs#L83) (struct): A post-event hold timer (REEC_A Thld / Thld2, the DER_A reconnection delays): armed at a time, it is active while the simulation time is before the arm time plus its duration. Times are compared with a millionth-of-a-step tolerance, the engine's convention for event times (MultiMachineSubtransient.StageTimeToleranceSteps), so a hold of exactly n steps lasts exactly n steps despite the rounding of t = k dt.

### src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/Wecc/WeccConverterState.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Dynamics.Models.Wecc`. 354 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/Wecc/WeccConverterState.cs).

- [`WeccConverterState`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/Wecc/WeccConverterState.cs#L37) (class): One converter-interfaced unit driven by its WECC model chain (`WeccPlant`: REGC_A with an optional REEC_A/B/C and an optional REPC_A plant controller) in the RMS engine. The models work per unit on the unit's MBASE; the network sees system per unit, so currents are scaled by the unit's rating (`RmsConverterUnit.RatingPu` = MBASE / system base). Each step (the kernel's sequence): the current is iterated with the network to the algebraic fixed point (`TrialCurrent`: REGC_A's LVACM and HVRCM at the trial voltage, states held), committed at the converged voltage (`Commit`, which also measures the unit's P and Q), then `Step` runs the dip state machine, takes the plant controller's Pref and Qext from its start-of-step states and measurements, evaluates the REEC commands, advances REGC_A with those commands held, then advances the REEC and REPC states and the frequency measurement. Without a REEC the current commands stay at their initial values; without a REPC the REEC's Pref and Qext stay at the values that hold the initial point. Plant controller measurements. The regulated bus voltage and the flow-branch current come from the retained converter nodes the network solves at the start of the step (`RmsConverterUnit.WeccMeasurement`); with no branch the plant output is the unit's own P, Q and current. The frequency is the backward difference of the regulated bus voltage angle over the step, `1 + wrap(theta_k - theta_k-1) / (2 pi f0 dt)`, through a first-order lag of `RepcaParameters.FrequencyFilterSeconds` (default 0.02 s, DECISIONS D15); the controller reads the filter state at the start of the step. Initialisation from the unit's solved operating point (P0, Q0, V0) and, for a plant controller, the solved voltages of its measurement buses; every model checks its own start (`Regca`, `Reec`, `Repca`) and the composed unit then requires every REGC_A state residual to be zero for the commands the controls give at t = 0 (`WeccEquilibrium`). The current is injected along the terminal voltage angle (REGC_A has no PLL dynamics); when the terminal voltage collapses below `RmsConverterState.PllLockMinVoltagePu` the last angle is held, as the legacy converter does.

- [`WeccCheck`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/Wecc/WeccParameters.cs#L18) (class): Small helpers shared by the parameter checks.
- [`RegcaParameters`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/Wecc/WeccParameters.cs#L75) (record): REGC_A (PSS/E REGCA1): the renewable energy generator/converter interface. The current commands pass through the converter lag Tg (with the reactive-current recovery rate limits Iqrmax/Iqrmin and the active-current rise limit Rrpwr and the low-voltage power logic LVPL on the active current), and the network interface applies the low-voltage active current management (LVACM, Lvpnt0..Lvpnt1) and the high-voltage reactive current management (HVRCM, Volim, Khv, Iolim). EPRI 3002006525 Fig. D-4.
- [`ReecVariant`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/Wecc/WeccParameters.cs#L142) (enum): Which renewable energy electrical control model a `ReecParameters` set describes. REEC_B and REEC_C are documented as subsets of REEC_A (EPRI 3002006525 section 3.3), REEC_C adding the storage path.
- [`ReecParameters`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/Wecc/WeccParameters.cs#L157) (record): REEC_A / REEC_B / REEC_C: the renewable energy electrical controls, which turn the active and reactive power references into the current commands Ipcmd and Iqcmd for the REGC model. EPRI 3002006525 Figs. D-1, D-2, D-3. Fields a variant does not have are ignored by it and must stay at their defaults (the DYR reader never sets them).
- [`WeccPlant`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/Wecc/WeccParameters.cs#L317) (record): The WECC dynamic model chain of one converter-interfaced unit, as bound from a DYR file (or built by a test): the generator/converter model (REGC_A), its electrical control (REEC_A/B/C) and its plant controller (REPC_A, `Repc`). Later slices add the wind turbine mechanics and DER_A. `Source` names where the data came from, for reports.
- [`WeccMeasurement`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/Wecc/WeccParameters.cs#L407) (record): Where a WECC plant controller measures (REPC_A): its regulated bus and the branch whose flow is the plant output, resolved against the case when the RMS study is prepared. Bus 0 means the unit's own terminal (and no branch: the unit's own P, Q and current). The branch current at the from end is `I = Y11 V(from) + Y12 V(to)` (system per unit, the branch's own pi-model stamp with its tap and phase shift, oriented from BUS1 to BUS2). The initial voltages are the solved power flow's, for the initialisation.

### src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/Wecc/WindMechanics.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Dynamics.Models.Wecc`. 444 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/Wecc/WindMechanics.cs).

- [`WtgtaParameters`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/Wecc/WindMechanics.cs#L14) (record): WTGT_A (PSS/E WTDTA1): the two-mass drive train. H total inertia (s), DAMP generator-side damping (pu power per pu speed), Htfrac turbine share of H (0 = one lumped mass), Freq1 first torsional mode (Hz), Dshaft shaft damping.
- [`WtgaraParameters`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/Wecc/WindMechanics.cs#L38) (record): WTGAR_A (PSS/E WTARA1): Pm = Pm0 - Ka theta (theta - theta0), with the pitch theta and the initial pitch theta0 in degrees, so Ka is pu power per degree squared (EPRI 3002006525 section 3.1 quotes a typical 0.007).
- [`WtgptaParameters`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/Wecc/WindMechanics.cs#L53) (record): WTGPT_A (PSS/E WTPTA1): the pitch controller (EPRI Fig. C-3). Angles in degrees, rates in degrees per second.
- [`WtgtrqaParameters`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/Wecc/WindMechanics.cs#L91) (record): WTGTRQ_A (PSS/E WTTQA1): the torque controller (EPRI Fig. C-4). Tflag 1 = power (torque) control on (Pref0 - Pe_filt)/omega_g, 0 = speed control on omega_g - omega_ref; the speed reference is a four-point power-speed table (p1..p4 pu power, spd1..spd4 pu speed) of the filtered power. TRATE (MW) is the turbine rating; GridSim requires it to equal the unit's MBASE (or be 0 for "the MBASE"), since the scaling between the two bases is not publicly specified.
- [`WindParameters`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/Wecc/WindMechanics.cs#L125) (record): The wind turbine mechanics of a unit: a drive train, and for a type 3 turbine the aerodynamics, pitch and torque controllers. Either the drive train alone (type 4) or all four (type 3).
- [`DriveTrain`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/Wecc/WindMechanics.cs#L166) (class): WTGT_A drive train (EPRI Fig. C-1). Speed deviations from the initial speed omega0 (pu), shaft twist in pu.s: 2 Ht dwt/dt = Pm / omega_t - K theta - Dshaft (wt - wg) 2 Hg dwg/dt = -Pe / omega_g + K theta + Dshaft (wt - wg) - DAMP wg dtheta/dt = wt - wg, omega_t = omega0 + wt, omega_g = omega0 + wg Ht = Htfrac H, Hg = H - Ht, K = 2 Ht Hg (2 pi Freq1)^2 / H (DECISIONS D11: the undamped mode is Freq1 Hz) With Htfrac = 0 it is one mass: `2 H dw/dt = (Pm - Pe)/omega - DAMP w`. The torques Pm/omega_t and Pe/omega_g are held across a step and the linear part is advanced by its exact zero-order hold `x <- Phi x + Gamma [Tm; Te]`, with Phi = exp(A dt) and Gamma = integral_0^dt exp(A s) ds B from the matrix exponential of the augmented matrix [[A, B], [0, 0]] (scaling and squaring of its Taylor series, plain IEEE arithmetic in a fixed order), computed once per step size. Forward Euler would grow the undamped torsional mode by |1 + j w dt| per step (DECISIONS D14).
- [`Aerodynamics`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/Wecc/WindMechanics.cs#L332) (class): WTGAR_A aerodynamics (EPRI Fig. C-2): Pm = Pm0 - Ka theta (theta - theta0), pitch in degrees.
- [`PitchController`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/Wecc/WindMechanics.cs#L348) (class): WTGPT_A pitch controller (EPRI Fig. C-3), degrees: ew = omega_t - omega_ref + Kcc (Pord - Pref); s0' = Kiw ew in [tmin, tmax]; a = clamp(Kpw ew + s0, tmin, tmax) ec = Pord - Pref; s1' = Kic ec in [tmin, tmax]; b = clamp(Kpc ec + s1, tmin, tmax) theta = lag(a + b, Tp) in [tmin, tmax], rate in [RTetaMin, RTetaMax] (s2) Pord is the REEC power order; Pref the REEC's power reference after the speed multiplication (Psel), so the compensation path acts when the power order is held below the reference (DECISIONS D20). Initialised with s0 = theta0, s1 = 0 and theta = theta0 (any split of theta0 between the two integrals is an equilibrium; DECISIONS D20).
- [`TorqueController`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Models/Wecc/WindMechanics.cs#L402) (class): WTGTRQ_A torque controller (EPRI Fig. C-4): s1 = lag(Pe, Tp); omega_ref = s0 = lag(f(s1), Twref) (f: the p -> spd table, flat beyond its ends) Tflag = 1: e = (Pref0 - s1) / omega_g; Tflag = 0: e = omega_g - omega_ref Tref = clamp(Kpp e + s2, Temin, Temax), s2' = Kip e in [Temin, Temax], frozen in a voltage dip Tref is a torque; REEC_A with PFlag = 1 multiplies it by omega_g (the PSS/E convention, EPRI 3002006525 section 3.3).

### src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/MultiDeviceFrequencyIntegrator.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Dynamics`. 101 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/MultiDeviceFrequencyIntegrator.cs).

- [`MultiDeviceFrequencyIntegrator`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/MultiDeviceFrequencyIntegrator.cs#L33) (class): The stateful, live twin of `Fleet.FleetDynamics` - the multi-device analogue of `FrequencyIntegrator`. A base system inertia plus N `FleetUnit`s, each with its own FFR state, deadband, lag and onset stagger, all seeing one system frequency. Intrinsic inertia is summed into E (N-additive real (1/2)J*omega^2); the fast response is the sum of independently-clamped, independently-staggered unit outputs, which is strictly less than Nx a single unit at full tilt - the emergent non-additivity. R080 (October 2026, stream B1): the governor, the recorded system response services and the equilibrium start are the one swing kernel's (`SwingResponders`) and the unit loop is the one shared with the batch twin (`FleetUnitBank`). Before R080 this integrator ignored the recorded services, the pre-event frequency and every grid-forming field, and floored the demand at 1 MW; R080 then refused grid-forming here, as its batch twin refused it (R263), instead of silently running the non-forming swing. Grid-forming (N291, October 2026 review, stream B5; Ruling R1: Mark delegated EE calls 2026-10-04). Under `DynamicsConfig.Forming` = Vsm or Droop this integrator now runs the grid-forming step of its single-mass twin `FrequencyIntegrator` (`FormingKernel`, the config's aggregate virtual former over the base plus unit inertia) with the fleet's summed fast response in the device slot of the forcing, exactly as the batch twin `Fleet.FleetDynamics.Simulate` does (the model and its sources are documented there). A one-unit, zero-stagger forming fleet is bit for bit `FrequencyIntegrator` with that device; with Forming = None every number is the old one (the forming flag is false, the forming denominator equals the floored E, so the sub-step count and the swing step are the pre-N291 ones). Internal use (N314, LF5, October 2026; F stream R079, Ruling R1): the live twin of FleetDynamics, pinned equal to it by B1; users reach the fleet through `gridsim fleet` (the batch twin). No front door of its own, so the type is `internal` (its tests reach it through InternalsVisibleTo); nothing outside Core used it.

- [`PlacementMinimum`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Placement/InertiaPlacementStudy.cs#L102) (record): The smallest scanned budget meeting a criterion, for one placement (NaN when none of the scanned budgets meets it), with the linear estimate between the last budget that fails and the first that passes.
- [`InertiaPlacementReport`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Placement/InertiaPlacementStudy.cs#L106) (record): Everything the study produced.
- [`InertiaPlacementStudy`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Placement/InertiaPlacementStudy.cs#L136) (class): The inertia placement study (October 2026): with the synchronous inertia of GB in ideal places, can the system run on less of it? What is fixed. The case, its dispatch and its power flow. Today's synchronous fleet keeps `InertiaPlacementOptions.ResidualFleetFraction` of its inertia (each machine's H scaled, nothing moved). The rest of each budget is synchronous condensers of one inertia constant (`InertiaPlacementOptions.CondenserH`) that inject no power and no reactive power at the solved state (so the power flow is that of the case), placed by the placement under test. So between placements only the location of the added inertia (and of the condenser MVA that comes with it) changes. What is measured. For each loss (a step of constant admittance drawing the loss's MW at the bus's solved voltage, the RMS engine's load-step event, at the transmission bus nearest the named site), the RMS engine (`RmsTransientStability.StudyEventsMeasured`, mechanical power held: no frequency response) gives the centre-of-inertia frequency and every measured bus's voltage angle. From them: the centre-of-inertia RoCoF and the worst bus RoCoF (both over 500 ms, `BusFrequencyMeter`), their ratio K (the spatial penalty), the worst voltage angle jump, the north-south inter-area oscillation, and the time the centre-of-inertia frequency takes to fall to 49.8 Hz. The lumped model (`FrequencyDynamics`, with the default GB response) gives the same time with frequency response, which does not depend on placement. Deterministic: every list is walked in a fixed order and every function is the deterministic one, so the same inputs give the same bits on every CPU and operating system.
- [`OptimisedSites`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/Placement/InertiaPlacementStudy.cs#L469) (record): The result of `Optimise`: the site weights found, the objective (the worst bus RoCoF over every loss, Hz/s) they give, and the objective of the equal weights it started from.

### src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/PostTripModel.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Dynamics`. 43 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/PostTripModel.cs).

- [`PostTripModel`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/PostTripModel.cs#L22) (class): The network after one generator trips: the same model without that unit. N158 (October 2026, H hygiene stream of the inertia re-appraisal; the remainder of N094): the CLI `trip` verb built this copy twice by hand (once for the asset-dynamics run, once for the distributed-inertia run), listing the properties itself. Both copies took the in-service list (`GridModel.Generators`) as the whole fleet, so every out-of-service unit vanished from the copy (`GridModel.AllGenerators`), and the distributed copy also dropped the asset bundle and the protections. This one helper goes through `GridModel.CopyWith`, which carries every property and keeps the out-of-service units. Bit-identity: the copy's in-service list is exactly the old one (the original in-service units minus the tripped one, in the same order; `GridModel.CopyWith` returns that very list when the model has out-of-service units, and an equal list otherwise), and every engine reads only that list. The base, buses, branches, OLTCs, boundaries, frequency and name are the same objects as before. The only differences are the out-of-service units now kept in `GridModel.AllGenerators` (no engine reads it) and, on the distributed path, the asset bundle and protections now carried (the distributed model reads neither; the CLI refuses `--asset-dynamics` together with `--inertia-model distributed`). So no trip result moves.

A tripped unit hurts twice - its output becomes the deficit AND its rotating mass leaves the system, so the remaining inertia is lower exactly when it's needed most. This is the security view: which single loss is the binding RoCoF case, and does it breach 0.125 Hz/s or the 49.5 Hz floor.

These are the linear archetypes of the nonlinear time-domain controllers - the nonlinear code (`GridFormingInverter`, `GridFollowingInverter`) is UNTOUCHED; the correspondence is documented per term. Deadband, arming, SoC clamps and trips are nonlinearities dropped about an armed / unsaturated / untripped operating point, which is exactly the pre-trip small-signal (in)stability question.

Both archetypes floor the actuator time constant with `max(1e-3, actuateTauS)`, mirroring the code's `Math.Max(dt, actuateTauS)` guard, so a zero-tau class never divides by zero.

- [`ModalResult`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/SmallSignal/ModalAnalysis.cs#L24) (record): The modal-analysis result: the sorted modes, the state labels, the RHP eigenvalue count (the small-signal instability count) and the minimum damping ratio over the oscillatory modes.
- [`ModalAnalysis`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/SmallSignal/ModalAnalysis.cs#L52) (class): Modal (small-signal) analysis of an assembled `SmallSignalModel`: eigenvalues, damping ratios, modal frequencies, participation factors and the right-half-plane count. Eigenvalues come from the robust Francis-QR path (no eigenvectors needed). Participation needs biorthonormal left/right vectors; when A is DEFECTIVE (the default undamped swing system's rigid-body COI Jordan block) the right-eigenvector matrix is singular, so we DEFLATE the rigid mode first - a reference-relative reduction onto the electromechanical subspace - and compute participation there. We never fabricate a participation vector for a defective mode.

### src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/StabilityMetrics.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Dynamics`. 112 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/StabilityMetrics.cs).

- [`StabilityMetrics`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/StabilityMetrics.cs#L17) (class): The forward "situational awareness" quantities the NESO RP1 control-room panel is built on, derived from the swing equation and the TSGB Minimum Intrinsic Floor (MIF) framework. The single most important quantity is purchased time: the seconds a system will ride a credible loss, inside its frequency band, on real stored energy alone. From the swing equation RoCoF = f0 . dP / (2 . E), and t = (f_now - f_threshold) / RoCoF so purchased time is (proportional to) the intrinsic energy and inversely proportional to the loss. See `Proposals/MIF/0001 - The Minimum Intrinsic Floor (MIF).md` s.5, and the largest-credible-loss correction in `Policy/0021 - The 1,800 Megawatt Fiction.md` s.6. These are pure numeric helpers. The generator -> intrinsic/proxy inertia reduction (which needs the synchronous-vs-converter fuel classifier) is done by the caller and fed in as GVA.s.
- [`GroupLoss`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/StabilityMetrics.cs#L90) (record struct): A named cluster of infeeds that can be lost together (shared converter/landfall/route), e.g. Sellindge = IFA+ElecLink, or the North-Sea corridor = NSL+Viking.

### src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/SwingResponders.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Dynamics`. 265 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/SwingResponders.cs).

- [`SwingResponders`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Dynamics/SwingResponders.cs#L43) (class): THE one swing kernel of the centre-of-inertia frequency family (October 2026 review, R080; stream B1; Ruling R1: Mark delegated EE calls 2026-10-04). It owns every responder state of the swing equation and the order in which their powers are added, so the seven engines of the family compute the same physics from one copy: `FrequencyDynamics.Simulate` (batch, lumped); `AssetFrequencyDynamics.Simulate` (batch, lumped, plus the authored asset fleet); `FrequencyIntegrator` (live, lumped); `AssetAwareFrequencyIntegrator` (live, lumped, plus the authored asset fleet); `Fleet.FleetDynamics.Simulate` (batch, a fleet of devices); `MultiDeviceFrequencyIntegrator` (live, a fleet of devices); `Distributed.MultiDomainSwing.Simulate` (batch, the distributed model's per-domain swing). What it holds, per run: the governor droop lag (GB Grid Code 5 % droop through a first-order lag), the TSGB device's fast frequency response (a capped droop with a deadband, through its own lag), the recorded system response services (Dynamic Containment / Moderation / Regulation on their published delivery curves, each through its own lag), the standing imbalance of an equilibrium start at a recorded pre-event frequency, and the load self-damping. The swing itself (df/dt = f0 / (2E) * deltaP, Kundur, Power System Stability and Control, 1994, section 3.9 and section 11.1; or the grid-forming semi-implicit step of `FormingKernel`) is integrated by each engine, because the engines legitimately differ there (a fixed batch trace, a live clock, one mass or several). Why it exists (the R080 finding): the five hand-copied loops had drifted. The two live integrators ignored the recorded services and the pre-event frequency (`DynamicsConfig.SystemResponseServices`, `DynamicsConfig.InitialFrequencyHz`) although their documentation said "the per-step physics are identical to Simulate"; the multi-device integrator ignored the grid-forming fields; and the live integrators floored the demand at 1 MW while the batch ones did not (the R163 demand-floor inconsistency). All of them now take every one of those terms from here, so they cannot drift again. Engines that cannot model a feature refuse it loudly instead of ignoring it. (The fleet engines refused grid-forming from R263 / R080 until N291, stream B5, routed them through the forming step with the fleet's summed fast response in the device slot.) Bit-identity (Mark's determinism rule): every state update and every sum below is the expression the engines used, operand for operand and in the same order (the B1 notes and `B1SwingKernelTests` carry the verbatim old loops and compare them bit for bit). Where an engine used to leave a term out (the live integrators had no standing imbalance and no services), the kernel adds an exact +0.0 in its place: x + (+0.0) is x for every x except -0.0, and no sum here can be -0.0 because the governor state is never -0.0 (it starts at +0.0 and an update that cancels exactly gives +0.0 in round-to-nearest), so those engines are bit-identical too when the terms are absent.

### src/GridSim.Core/Estimation/BadDataAnalysis.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Estimation`. 247 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Estimation/BadDataAnalysis.cs).

- [`BadDataAnalysis`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Estimation/BadDataAnalysis.cs#L14) (class): Largest-normalized-residual bad-data machinery. At a converged estimate the residual covariance diagonal is Omega_i_i = sigma_i^2 - h_i^T*G^-1*h_i (h_i = the measurement's Jacobian row, G = H^TWH), and the normalized residual r^N_i = |r_i|/sqrtOmega_i_i identifies the gross error the chi-square test detected. A measurement with Omega_i_i ~ 0 is critical: it is the only observation of some state direction, its residual is structurally zero, and removing it would make the system unobservable - so it is flagged, never removed. The gain matrix is factored once and back-substituted per measurement (O(s^3) + m*O(s^2)), the dense-M1 cost profile.
- [`LuFactorization`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Estimation/BadDataAnalysis.cs#L172) (class): Plain LU with partial pivoting that keeps its pivot record, so one O(s^3) factorization serves the m per-measurement back-substitutions. Throws like the LU solvers on a pivot collapsed below the relative floor (callers only reach here at a converged, observable estimate, so this is a genuine anomaly).

### src/GridSim.Core/Estimation/ChiSquare.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Estimation`. 84 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Estimation/ChiSquare.cs).

- [`ChiSquare`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Estimation/ChiSquare.cs#L13) (class): Dependency-free chi-square quantiles for the bad-data consistency test. Uses the Wilson-Hilferty cube approximation chi-square(k,p) ~ k*(1 - 2/(9k) + z_p*sqrt(2/(9k)))^3 with an Acklam-style rational approximation for the standard-normal quantile z_p. Accurate to well under 1% for k >= 3 - ample for a detection gate. At k = 1 and k = 2, where Wilson-Hilferty sags (2.5 % and 0.9 % low at p = 0.95) and which reduced-redundancy sets such as `--prior solve` meet, the exact closed forms are used instead (GR-539): chi-square(1,p) = z_((1+p)/2)^2 and chi-square(2,p) = -2 ln(1 - p). Deterministic by construction (pure arithmetic, no tables loaded at runtime).

### src/GridSim.Core/Estimation/DenseEstimationLimits.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Estimation`. 65 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Estimation/DenseEstimationLimits.cs).

- [`DenseEstimationLimits`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Estimation/DenseEstimationLimits.cs#L19) (class): The one place that states how large a system each DENSE estimation method accepts (October 2026 review, WS11 R119/R107). Before this, the concept "the largest system we run a dense O(s^3) solve for" had a different value in every file and two methods had no cap at all: the QR step allocated two dense m x s matrices on any case (about 3.9 GB on gb-full), and the Kalman filter, reachable from `serve --method ekf` on any case, holds and inverts dense s x s covariances every window (about 3 GB and tens of minutes per window on gb-full). Every dense method now checks one of these named limits and FAILS LOUD above it instead of exhausting memory or running for hours. The limits are not collapsed into a single number on purpose: the methods differ in what they hold and how often they pay for it, and moving an existing value would silently change which bundled cases a method accepts. The existing values are kept exactly (so no case that ran before is refused, and none that was refused now runs) and the two new caps reuse an existing value of the same kind. Units differ for the same reason they always have: the constrained-family cap was defined in buses, the others in states (about two states per bus: the non-slack angles plus every magnitude).

### src/GridSim.Core/Estimation/DistrustedSources.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Estimation`. 94 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Estimation/DistrustedSources.cs).

- [`DistrustedSources`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Estimation/DistrustedSources.cs#L18) (class): A response control that marks one or more measurement sources distrusted, so their rows are forced to pseudo-measurement treatment: their sigma is inflated, driving their weight (1/sigma^2) toward zero, so a poisoned or suspect feed can no longer pull the estimate while the system stays observable. This is the containment step the incident runbook calls on when a source is suspected of carrying bad or injected data (NCSC CAF D1 response, feeding the FDIA screen's C1 story). Pure and deterministic. It is a side-effect-free transform over a measurement or a set: same input, same output, so a quarantined re-run is still bit-reproducible. It does not log or decide policy; the hosting layer records a `SecurityEventKind.DistrustedSource` audit entry when it applies one. It only ever weakens a row, never strengthens one. It inflates sigma, never shrinks it, and never changes a value, so it cannot be used to forge confidence in a source; and it leaves a distrusted row in the set (down-weighted) rather than deleting it, so observability and the audit record are preserved.

### src/GridSim.Core/Estimation/Dse/EnsembleKalmanStateEstimator.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Estimation.Dse`. 419 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Estimation/Dse/EnsembleKalmanStateEstimator.cs).

- [`EnsembleKalmanStateEstimator`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Estimation/Dse/EnsembleKalmanStateEstimator.cs#L26) (class): A recursive Ensemble Kalman Filter network-state tracker - a Monte-Carlo sibling of the EKF/UKF. It carries an ensemble of state members, propagates each through the `IProcessModel` predict step (with sampled process noise), and corrects them with the perturbed-observation update using the ensemble's own sample covariances. The estimate is the ensemble mean. Deterministic for a fixed seed (all random draws are ordered), so it is testable like the estate's other seeded machinery. N264 (October 2026, stream LF4; Ruling R1 and Mark's determinism rule): every window draws its random numbers from its OWN stream, `new Random(WindowSeed(seed, k))`, where k counts the windows the filter has COMMITTED so far (the first window is k = 0 and uses the seed itself, so its numbers are unchanged). Before N264 one `Random` ran across all windows, and draws taken by a step that then failed could not be given back, so every later window saw different noise from a run in which the failed window never arrived. Now a failed step does not advance k: the next window uses exactly the stream it would have used had the failed window never been seen, and the filter (ensemble and stream) is exactly as before the failure. The cost is that every EnKF number from the second window on moved once. Same restriction posture as the EKF/UKF and gated the same way: the predict step integrates a process model, the method is registered in `RestrictionReview` and asserted at construction, and the emitted mean is the filtered present, stamped at the window time; inputs stay guard-limited upstream.
- [`ProcessNoiseSampler`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Estimation/Dse/EnsembleKalmanStateEstimator.cs#L345) (class): D-DOC-113 (October 2026): draws one process-noise sample w ~ N(0, Q) and adds it to a predicted ensemble member, for `EnsembleKalmanStateEstimator`. Before, the filter drew each state's noise independently with variance q_ii, so any correlation in Q (off-diagonal q_ij) was silently dropped. The rule, which is fully deterministic for a fixed random stream: Diagonal Q (every off-diagonal entry exactly zero, either sign: the default random-walk model and any other uncorrelated model): x_i += sqrt(max(q_ii, 0)) * g_i for i = 0, 1, ..., s - 1, one standard normal draw g_i per state in state order. This is the pre-October-2026 statement, verbatim, so every result with a valid diagonal Q is unchanged to the bit. N264 (LF4): a diagonal entry that is not a variance (negative, NaN or infinite) used to be read as 0 (negative) or carried into the ensemble (NaN, infinity); it is now refused before any draw, naming the process model and the entry, as the correlated path refuses a negative pivot (the streaming engine counts the window failed). Correlated Q: Q must be exactly symmetric and finite. Its lower Cholesky factor L (Q = L L^T) is formed by `DseLinAlg.CholeskySemiDefinite` (column by column, a zero pivot allowed for a direction with no variance, a negative one refused); then s standard normal draws g_0 .. g_{s-1} are taken in state order and x_i += sum_{k = 0..i} L[i, k] g_k, the sum accumulated from k = 0 upwards starting at +0. The draw count per member (s) and order are the same as on the diagonal path. An invalid Q (not symmetric, not finite, not positive semi-definite) throws `InvalidOperationException` naming the process model, so the streaming engine counts the window as failed instead of sampling a covariance that does not exist. The factor of the last Q seen is kept and reused while each member's Q is the same to the bit (the usual case: Q does not depend on the member), so a correlated Q costs one O(s^3 / 6) factorisation per window, not one per member.

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Estimation.Dse`. 111 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Estimation/Dse/FrequencyRocofFilter.cs).

Estimating RoCoF as a filter state is more reliable than differentiating a PLL frequency - erroneous PLL RoCoF is what mis-tripped ~6,200 MW of solar in the 2016 Blue Cut event - and it degrades gracefully under measurement noise. It is a recursive filter with a predict step, so it is gated by `RestrictionReview` and asserted at construction; the emitted (frequency, RoCoF) is the FILTERED PRESENT, never a future-dated claim, and frequency measurements arrive guard-limited upstream. Experimental (R062, October 2026): Core API and tests only; no CLI verb or production caller. Still needs: a frequency feed (GDA system frequency, or PMU FREQ/DFREQ once the decoder applies FNOM scaling), a CLI or replay surface, and validation of its tuning against a recorded event.

- [`DseEstimate`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Estimation/Dse/KalmanStateEstimator.cs#L7) (record): One filtered present-state estimate from a recursive DSE step, with per-bus 1-sigma bounds.
- [`KalmanStateEstimator`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Estimation/Dse/KalmanStateEstimator.cs#L37) (class): A recursive (Extended Kalman Filter) network-state tracker - Dynamic State Estimation at the network-state level. Unlike the snapshot `WlsStateEstimator`, it carries a state estimate and its covariance across measurement windows: each step predicts the state forward through an `IProcessModel` (persistence by default), then corrects it against the window's measurements. The correction is done in information form - the posterior information matrix is the prior information plus the WLS gain H^T R^-1 H - so it reuses exactly the same measurement Jacobian the snapshot estimator does and there is no dense m x m innovation inverse. This is the boundary case `UnderstandingRestrictions.md` gates: the predict step integrates a process model a step ahead, so the method is registered in `RestrictionReview` and asserted at construction. The emitted estimate is the FILTERED PRESENT state, stamped at the window time - a filter, not a predictor. Inputs remain guard-limited upstream (the loader / streaming engine refuse any window newer than the horizon).
- [`DseLinAlg`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Estimation/Dse/KalmanStateEstimator.cs#L320) (class): Small dense linear algebra for the recursive filters (invert, matrix-vector, F P F^T, add).

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Estimation.Dse`. 51 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Estimation/Dse/RandomWalkProcessModel.cs).

The state is expected to hold from one window to the next, with a per-unit-time process-noise variance capturing how fast it can drift. This is the standard forecasting-aided / tracking state-estimation model (Debs-Larson): no dynamics, just "the grid state changes slowly between telemetry snapshots." The state-transition Jacobian is the identity, so it makes no forward claim about the real grid - it only sets how much the filter trusts the previous estimate as a prior for the present one.

### src/GridSim.Core/Estimation/FeasibleWlsStep.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Estimation`. 544 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Estimation/FeasibleWlsStep.cs).

- [`FeasibleWlsStep`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Estimation/FeasibleWlsStep.cs#L37) (class): The physics-feasible estimation backend (`EstimationMethod.Feasible`): the equality-constrained KKT of `ConstrainedDenseWlsStep` PLUS an ACTIVE SET that enforces the state-coupled operational inequalities at SOLVE time - generator reactive capability (Qg in [Qmin,Qmax]), across-branch angle difference (|theta_f - theta_t| <= limit), and branch apparent-power rating (|S_end| <= RateA). Where the acceptance gate (Ring C) would reject a converged state that breaches one of these, the active set instead pulls the solve onto the boundary as it iterates, so the estimate converges to a feasible state rather than being thrown away. Each Gauss-Newton major iteration linearises every currently-violated inequality at the current point and appends its row to the augmented system's constraint block alongside the zero-injection equalities. The Jacobian rows come straight from the measurement model - injection-Q partials (`MeasurementModel.InjectionQRow`) for Q-capability, the two +-1 angle entries for the angle difference, and the branch flow partials (`MeasurementModel.BranchFlowRow`) for the thermal limit, whose nonlinear |S| <= RateA is enforced through its squared form S^2 = P^2 + Q^2 (row 2P*dP + 2Q*dQ) - so there is no copy-drift. A constraint no longer violated at the next point simply drops out (re-evaluated each iteration); the active set converges with the state. The constraint block is row-equilibrated (every constraint row, its C^T column and its right-hand side scaled by an exact power of two near sqrt(max diag G)) so constraint pivots are not lost under the relative pivot floor beside a gain of 1e6-1e8; this rescales only the multipliers. The angle-difference rows carry a hysteresis band like the thermal rows (R257 follow-up, ruling Q12). The generator-Q rows carry a band too and are released on the sign of their previous multiplier (N043), so a Qg at its limit is neither cycled nor frozen. Load-bearing invariant: with no equality constraint and no active inequality the augmented system IS the free normal equations, so the step matches `DenseWlsStep` to solver tolerance - the feasible method costs nothing on a state that is already feasible. Dense backend only; the estimator selects it under the same 3,000-bus fail-loud guard as the constrained method. Observability and residual covariance delegate to `ConstrainedDenseWlsStep` (equalities enter both; inequalities only add information, never remove it).

- [`HtiEstimationResult`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Estimation/HtiBadDataEstimation.cs#L62) (record): The outcome of an estimate whose bad-data stage is Hypothesis-Testing Identification.
- [`HtiBadDataEstimation`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Estimation/HtiBadDataEstimation.cs#L102) (class): Runs the state estimator with `HypothesisTestingBadData` as the bad-data method in place of the sequential largest-normalised-residual (LNR) removal loop (R062, October 2026 review: HTI was designed to replace LNR but nothing called it). The loop, in plain terms: Estimate with the WLS loop's own removal switched off (`EstimationOptions.MaxBadDataRemovals` = 0), so the chi-square test still runs and its verdict is honest, but nothing is removed by LNR. If the estimate is not converged, or the chi-square test did not run, or it passed: stop. This is the same detection gate LNR uses (identification only follows a failed detection test). Otherwise run HTI on the biased estimate: every measurement whose normalised residual exceeds the suspect threshold is a suspect, the gross errors of all suspects are estimated JOINTLY, and each suspect whose test statistic exceeds the test threshold is identified as bad. Interacting errors are therefore separated in one step instead of being peeled off one at a time (where LNR can point at a good measurement). Remove every identified measurement (up to the removal cap, largest test statistic first) and go round again. If HTI identifies nothing while chi-square still fails, stop and report the failure. HTI is dense (it forms the gain inverse and an m x s Jacobian, and costs O(m s^2) for the suspect screen), so it is refused above `DenseEstimationLimits.StateCovarianceMaxState` states (the same dense "form and invert G" limit the opt-in state covariance uses). The robust methods (Huber, LAV, Schweppe-GM) down-weight outliers instead of removing them and run no removal loop, so HTI does not apply to them and is refused; prior backfill (`EstimationOptions.BackfillRemovedFromPrior`) belongs to the LNR loop and is refused too. Every refusal throws `NotSupportedException` or `ArgumentException`; nothing silently falls back to LNR.

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Estimation`. 176 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Estimation/HypothesisTestingBadData.cs).

- [`HtiIdentified`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Estimation/HypothesisTestingBadData.cs#L18) (record): A measurement identified as bad by the hypothesis test, with its estimated error and test statistic.
- [`HypothesisTestingBadData`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Estimation/HypothesisTestingBadData.cs#L28) (class): Hypothesis-Testing Identification of bad data. The sequential largest-normalized-residual loop removes one measurement at a time and can mis-identify when several errors interact (their residuals smear so the largest normalized residual points at a good measurement). HTI instead forms a joint estimate of the errors over a suspect set and applies a per-suspect hypothesis test: e^ = S_SS^-1 r_SS with S = I - H G^-1 H^T W, then t_i = |e^_i| / sqrt(Cov_ii). A suspect with t_i above the threshold is bad; one below is exonerated even if its raw normalized residual crossed the suspect threshold. Dense; runs on a converged estimate.

### src/GridSim.Core/Estimation/LavLinearProgram.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Estimation`. 553 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Estimation/LavLinearProgram.cs).

- [`LavLpStatus`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Estimation/LavLinearProgram.cs#L4) (enum): How a `LavLinearProgram.Solve` call ended.
- [`LavLpSolution`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Estimation/LavLinearProgram.cs#L32) (record): The outcome of one `LavLinearProgram.Solve` call.
- [`LavLinearProgram`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Estimation/LavLinearProgram.cs#L73) (class): N331 (CF5): the weighted least-absolute-values correction as a linear program, solved exactly by a vertex-descent (simplex) method specialised to L1 fitting, in the form Abur and Celik use for LAV state estimation ("A fast algorithm for the weighted least absolute value state estimation", IEEE Trans. Power Systems 6(1), 1991; Abur and Exposito, "Power System State Estimation", 2004, ch. 6) and Barrodale and Roberts' L1 simplex uses for the line search. The problem, at one Gauss-Newton iterate: given the measurement Jacobian H (m x s, full column rank), the residual r = z - h(x) and weights w_i = 1 / sigma_i, find dx minimising f(dx) = sum_i w_i |r_i - H_i dx|. As a linear program (dx free, e+ and e- at or above 0, H dx + e+ - e- = r, minimise w.(e+ + e-)) its optimal vertices interpolate s linearly independent rows exactly. This class walks those vertices directly instead of building the 2s + 2m column tableau: 1. Vertex: a basis B of s independent rows; dx = H_B^-1 r_B (those rows' residuals are 0). 2. Optimality (the dual test): with g = sum over i not in B of w_i sign(res_i) H_i and v = H_B^-T g, the vertex is optimal when |v_k| <= w_(B_k) for every basis position k (v is the dual y_B; the nonbasic duals are w_i sign(res_i)). 3. Otherwise release the position k with the largest excess |v_k| - w_(B_k): moving along d = sign(v_k) H_B^-1 e_k keeps the other basis rows at residual 0 and lifts row k off zero, at initial slope w_(B_k) - |v_k| < 0. 4. Line search (Barrodale-Roberts): f along d is convex and piecewise linear; each nonbasic row i with a_i = H_i d != 0 is a breakpoint at t_i = res_i / a_i > 0 where the slope rises by 2 w_i |a_i| (a row already at residual 0 is a breakpoint at t = 0 rising by w_i |a_i|). Walk the breakpoints in increasing t until the slope reaches 0; that row enters the basis at position k. Each move is a strict decrease of f unless it is a degenerate (t = 0) move, and f is bounded below, so the walk ends; a pivot cap guards degenerate cycling (fail loud). 5. Degenerate vertices (end pass E, 2026-10-11): a nonbasic row whose residual is exactly 0 (after the round-off snap `ZeroResidualTolerance`) keeps a side, +1 or -1, which says whether e+ or e- of that row is the basic variable at value 0. It enters g on that side, and it is a breakpoint at t = 0 only when the move drives it against its side. This makes step 2 the exact reduced-cost test of one LP basis. The first version gave such a row the dual 0, which is no basis's dual: on four collinear points it released and re-entered the same two rows until the pivot cap, and on an exact measurement set (every good residual 0 at the truth) the estimator failed. After a move that does not lower f (beyond `DegenerateDecreaseTolerance`) the next move uses Bland's rule (release the lowest row index, enter the first breakpoint), which cannot cycle. An optimum is reported only from a fresh factorisation of its basis, so the result depends on the basis alone, not on the path to it. Numerics: the basis inverse is held dense (s x s) and updated by the rank-one row-replacement formula, refactorised from scratch every `RefactorInterval` moves; dx and every residual are recomputed from the current inverse after each move (no drift carried in the residuals), and the basis rows' residuals are set to exactly 0. Every loop runs serially in a fixed order with plain IEEE operations (no fused multiply-add, no transcendental), every choice breaks ties by the lowest index after a relative margin, so the result is bit-identical on every CPU tier and OS and on every run. Cost per move O(s^2 + nnz(H)); the starting basis costs O(m s^2) when no warm basis is given.

- [`PmuCurrentMeasurement`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Estimation/LinearPmuStateEstimator.cs#L27) (record): A synchronized branch current-phasor measurement (per-unit, rectangular), from a PMU.
- [`LinearPmuResult`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Estimation/LinearPmuStateEstimator.cs#L35) (record): The single-shot linear PMU estimate: rectangular voltages resolved in one non-iterative solve.
- [`LinearPmuStateEstimator`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Estimation/LinearPmuStateEstimator.cs#L59) (class): A linear PMU state estimator: with the state in rectangular voltages x = [Vre; Vim], both the synchronized voltage phasors (h = x) and the branch current phasors (I = Yff V_from + Yft V_to) are linear in x, so the whole estimate is a single non-iterative weighted-least-squares solve x = (H^T W H)^-1 H^T W z - unlike the iterative nonlinear WLS. It is the fast inner estimator of the hybrid multi-rate scheme (run at PMU rate). A static, measurement-only filter (no review-gate entry); inputs arrive guard-checked from the PMU mapper. Experimental (R062, October 2026): one non-iterative solve with no bad-data test. Production caller (1.95.245): the CLI verb `pmu-estimate` runs it over a gridsim-measurements/1 set (for example one `pmu-ingest --measurements-dir` wrote), through `PmuMeasurementSetAdapter`, which pairs the mapper's polar VmPu / VaDeg / IMagPu / IAngDeg rows into these rectangular records with their exact first-order error covariance (`SigmaIm` and `CovOffDiag`). Until then it was Core API and tests only (R062; D-DOC-219 corrected the earlier note). Still outstanding: a live or replay surface at PMU rate (the hybrid multi-rate scheduler is test-only), and to-end current phasors. Inputs are checked (D-DOC-109, October 2026). Every measurement is checked before any row is built and every problem is named in one `InvalidDataException`: a voltage phasor at a bus the model does not have, a sigma that is not a finite number above 0, a covariance that is not finite or does not give a positive-definite 2x2 error matrix, and a non-finite phasor value. A current on a branch that is not an in-service model branch (or that matches parallel circuits without a circuit name) is refused by name, as before.

### src/GridSim.Core/Estimation/MeasuredInjectionPrior.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Estimation`. 156 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Estimation/MeasuredInjectionPrior.cs).

- [`MeasuredInjectionPrior`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Estimation/MeasuredInjectionPrior.cs#L23) (class): The triad's solve stage: turn a measurement set into a MEASURED-INJECTION POWER FLOW and solve it with the validated Newton engine. GDA provides the warm-start data (the measured per-bus injections inside the set), GridSim solves it into a physically exact operating point, and the estimator then fuses that solved prior with the same telemetry - the prior replaces the flat voltage-schedule guess with solved physics, and the solution doubles as the Gauss-Newton warm start. Model construction: every bus's net injection is read off the set's PInjMw/QInjMvar rows (several rows at one bus are redundant meters of the same injection and are combined by their inverse-variance weighted mean, bug hunt 2026-11-01 #183; unmeasured buses default to zero injection). Buses injecting more than `PvThresholdMw` become PV at `PvSetpointPu` (a generating site holds its voltage - without var support a pure-PQ conversion sags unrealistically); everything else is PQ with the measured injection as (negative) load. The slack keeps its reference role and absorbs the residual imbalance, exactly as it does in the estimator.

The estimator's measurement equation is z = h(x) + e: each kind has a closed-form h over the state x = (Va, Vm) evaluated through the same admittance stamps the power-flow solvers use.
- [`BranchEnd`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Estimation/Measurement.cs#L39) (enum): Which end of a branch a flow measurement meters.

Bus measurements address the bus by id (not solver index) and branch measurements by the branch's (`From`, `To`) endpoints - plus `Circuit` (the `Model.Branch.Name`) to disambiguate parallel circuits - so an external crosswalk (GDA GSP/BMU mapping) can author sets without knowing solver internals. Values travel in engineering units (pu for voltage, MW/MVAr for power) and are converted to per-unit once, at ingestion, against the model's BaseMva. `Source` is the row's CLASS (the noise-floor grouping, the distrust key, the hard-constraint tag); `Provenance` (GR-529, November 2026) is optional per-row detail that must not split the class, such as a phase-angle row's frequency and instant. Null when there is none; a JSON file without it reads as null and a set without it is written exactly as before.

The state is x = [Va at every non-slack bus (radians); Vm at every bus (pu)], in model bus order - the same conventions as `NewtonShell.BusSpec`, so estimates are directly comparable to power-flow results. Injection rows evaluate through `ComputeInjectionsSparse`: the solver's injection sum (`NewtonRaphsonPowerFlow.ComputeInjections`) restricted to each bus's electrical neighbours, bit-identical to it because the terms skipped are exact structural zeros (`SparseEstimatorTests` pins the agreement bitwise). D-DOC-204 (October 2026): this summary used to say the rows call the solver's own method, which they have not since the neighbourhood path was added for large networks. Branch-flow rows use the same pi-model admittance stamps as `NewtonShell.ComputeLineFlows`. Everything here is in per-unit: measured values and sigmas are converted once, at construction.

- [`NoiseFloorReport`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Estimation/NoiseFloorAnalysis.cs#L27) (record): A noise-floor study over a corpus of estimation residuals.
- [`NoiseFloorAnalysis`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Estimation/NoiseFloorAnalysis.cs#L50) (class): Characterises the measurement-noise floor per class (source tag x kind) from estimation residuals - the study that decides whether the declared sigmas match the noise the feeds actually carry, and by how much each sigma class should be rescaled. It reads the LEVERAGE-CORRECTED normalized residuals the estimator already produces (`MeasurementResidual.NormalizedResidual`). Those are the ABSOLUTE values |r|/sqrt(omega), so a correctly-declared class is HALF-normal (|N(0,1)|); the tool recovers a per-class scale factor of k (true noise ~ k x declared sigma) from the half-normal statistics. This is the automated form of the "broad shelf slightly above 1 across one source tag = miscalibrated sigma class" reading. Run it over a CORPUS spanning many timestamps (aggregate residuals from many estimations) so each class has enough samples; a single snapshot rarely does. The tool is data-agnostic - point it at synthetic or real GB residuals; the GB sigma-class re-fit is then just its output on a real residual corpus.

This is the estimator-improving path: a genuine per-bus angle (one that carries real inter-bus spread) becomes a direct `1.0`-pivot row on that bus's angle column, converting a weakly/indirectly-observed angle direction into a directly-observed one. It does NOT and cannot manufacture spatial detail from a system common-mode angle: the estimator solves angles relative to a fixed slack, so a common offset applied to every bus cancels on re-referencing. Feed this real per-bus differences; use a system COI angle (GDA `PHASEANGLE_INFERED`) only as the absolute reference frame / projection frequency, never as a per-bus row.

### src/GridSim.Core/Estimation/PmuMeasurementSetAdapter.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Estimation`. 144 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Estimation/PmuMeasurementSetAdapter.cs).

- [`PmuPhasorSet`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Estimation/PmuMeasurementSetAdapter.cs#L13) (record): The phasors `PmuMeasurementSetAdapter.FromSet` built, and what it did not use.
- [`PmuMeasurementSetAdapter`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Estimation/PmuMeasurementSetAdapter.cs#L38) (class): The adapter from a polar `MeasurementSet` (gridsim-measurements/1, as `pmu-ingest` writes it through `Synchrophasor.PmuMeasurementSetMapper`) to the rectangular phasors `LinearPmuStateEstimator` takes (1.95.245; the outstanding item in that class's notes and in FEATURE-GAPS-RELEASE section 7). Pairing. A bus's `MeasurementKind.VmPu` and `MeasurementKind.VaDeg` rows form its voltage phasor; a branch end's `MeasurementKind.IMagPu` and `MeasurementKind.IAngDeg` rows (same From, To, End and Circuit) form its current phasor. Angles are slack-referenced degrees, the set's convention. Rows of any other kind, and a magnitude or angle without its partner, are listed in `PmuPhasorSet.NotUsed`. Refused (`InvalidDataException`, every problem named): two rows of one kind at one place (which to pair is ambiguous), and a current metered at the To end (the linear model holds the from-end current only). Error model. A polar reading z = m e^(j theta) with independent sigmas s_m (pu) and s_theta (degrees, converted to radians) maps to the rectangular error covariance by the first-order (linearised) transform at the measured value, R = J diag(s_m^2, s_theta^2) J^T with J = [[cos theta, -m sin theta], [sin theta, m cos theta]]: var_re = c^2 s_m^2 + m^2 s^2 s_theta^2, var_im = s^2 s_m^2 + m^2 c^2 s_theta^2, cov = c s (s_m^2 - m^2 s_theta^2). Its determinant is m^2 s_m^2 s_theta^2, positive for m above 0, so the pair is weighted exactly by its full 2x2 inverse (`PmuVoltageMeasurement.SigmaIm`). A phasor of magnitude 0 has no direction to linearise about and is refused. Sines and cosines are GridSim's own (`DetMath`, D1), so the result is the same on every CPU.

### src/GridSim.Core/Estimation/ProjectionStatistics.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Estimation`. 213 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Estimation/ProjectionStatistics.cs).

- [`ProjectionStatistics`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Estimation/ProjectionStatistics.cs#L39) (class): Projection statistics (Mili-Cheniae-Rousseeuw): a masking-immune measure of how outlying each measurement Jacobian row is among all rows, using a high-breakdown location/scale. Unlike the hat-matrix leverage (which is computed against the possibly-contaminated fit and can itself be masked by multiple interacting errors), PS looks only at the geometry of the rows in state space, so it cannot be masked. NOT YET WIRED (R259, October 2026 review): this doc used to call PS "the leverage source for the Schweppe-Huber GM estimator", but `EstimationMethod.SchweppeGm` uses the hat-matrix normalised residual from `IWlsStep.NormalizedResiduals` (with the declared weights since 1.95.038), not PS. PS is a tested building block kept for that wiring (the Mili weight a_i = min(1, (d / PS_i)^2) multiplying the Huber threshold); note `Compute` is O(m^2 s) and needs a sparse projection before it can run at gb-full scale. NOT READY FOR WIRING (N330, 1.95.247): this is the dense Gasko-Donoho form (median and MAD over every row's projection). On a power-system Jacobian most rows share no column with a given direction, so most projections are 0 and the MAD is tiny: on case14 with the synthetic set every row's PS came out large (median 437 for P injections, 10.5 for voltage magnitudes, maximum 5,960), so a_i = min(1, (d / PS_i)^2) down-weights almost every row by four orders of magnitude. Wired into SchweppeGm as a trial it turned a clean case14 estimate from J = 86.33 (PASS) into J = 365.50 (FAIL). Mili, Cheniae and Rousseeuw's sparse-matrix form (median and MAD over the nonzero projections only) is the published remedy; it should be built and checked against a reference before PS is wired. CF5 (N330): `ComputeSparse` is that sparse form (location and scale over the overlapping rows only), validated against a hand-computed reference in Cf5ProjectionStatisticsTests. `Compute` is kept unchanged (its existing tests pin it). STILL NOT WIRED (CF5, measured 2026-10-11): the trial wiring (Mili's r_Si = r_i / (sigma_i a_i) with a_i = min(1, (d_i / PS_i)^2), d_i = sqrt of the chi-square 0.975 quantile at the row's nonzero count) was re-run with the sparse form on the same clean set (estimate case14 --synth --seed 3 --method schweppe-gm): hat leverage J = 86.34 vs chi2(95 %) 118.75 PASS (35 iterations, max |dVa| 0.1150 deg); sparse PS J = 509.80 FAIL (115 iterations, max |dVa| 0.1295 deg). The sparse form cut the PS by an order of magnitude (P injection median 437 -> 30.31) but the overlap sets still mix rows of very different scale (|V| rows with entries near 1 against injection rows near the bus self-susceptance, tens of pu), so every injection row is a leverage point: median a_i 0.0217 for P injections (14 rows, d 4.187), 0.0669 for Q injections, 0.181 / 0.278 for P / Q flows, 1 for |V|. A robust estimator must not reject clean data, so SchweppeGm keeps the hat-matrix leverage (bit for bit unchanged). The next step would be the [VERIFY] above (the published estimator may scale each direction differently) and a row normalisation decision; Cf5ProjectionStatisticsTests records the per-kind weights so the reason stays visible.

### src/GridSim.Core/Estimation/Security/FdiaScreen.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Estimation.Security`. 334 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Estimation/Security/FdiaScreen.cs).

- [`ProtectedAnchorViolation`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Estimation/Security/FdiaScreen.cs#L12) (record): A protected (PMU-anchored) measurement that the estimated state disagrees with by more than its own noise - the signature of a feasible-landing FDIA attack the envelope check cannot see.
- [`FdiaScreenReport`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Estimation/Security/FdiaScreen.cs#L28) (record): The outcome of screening an estimate for a residual-cloaked False Data Injection attack.
- [`FdiaScreen`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Estimation/Security/FdiaScreen.cs#L59) (class): A second-layer detector for residual-cloaked False Data Injection (FDIA) attacks. Model-based bad-data detection (chi-square + largest-normalized-residual) is provably bypassable: an attack a = H c lies in the range of the measurement Jacobian, leaves every residual unchanged, and shifts the estimated state by c completely undetected (Liu-Ning-Reiter). This screen catches the sub-class of such attacks that pushes the state into a physically-implausible region - a measurement-consistent (chi-square PASS) estimate whose state nevertheless violates a hard physical law or the operational envelope (voltage band, thermal rating, generator reactive capability). It reuses GridSim's physics-conformance audit as an independent validator the attacker must also satisfy. Feasible-landing attacks and protected anchors. A perfectly crafted attack that lands on another feasible, in-limit operating point is invisible to the envelope and physics checks, because its state is self-consistent. This is caught by a second, independent handle the attacker does not control: a set of protected (PMU-anchored) measurements the attacker cannot forge. If the estimated state disagrees with a protected anchor by more than that anchor's own noise, the state was shifted and the screen flags it (`FdiaScreenReport.AnchorInconsistent`). Supply the trusted PMU rows as `protectedAnchors`; they must be sources the deployment trusts (not ones a distrusted-source control has down-weighted). Without anchors the screen behaves exactly as before. The screen reports, it never silently rejects - an operator sees "consistent but implausible, or inconsistent with a trusted anchor" and investigates.
- [`TelemetrySigmas`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Estimation/Security/FdiaScreen.cs#L246) (class): The declared sigmas of the telemetry the estimate used, indexed by location, and the per-limit uncertainty bound built from them (see `Screen`). Removed bad data is not in the residual table, so it does not count. Several rows at one BUS (same kind) measure the same quantity, and H G^-1 H^T = R - Omega with Omega positive semi-definite gives Var(h_i(x^)) <= sigma_i^2 for every one of them, so the SMALLEST sigma is the tightest valid bound (GR-077; the largest used to be taken, so a loose pseudo row or a distrusted row at the bus widened the margin enough to hide an envelope breach). Bug #189 (2026-11-01): branch rows now follow the same rule wherever the rows are known to measure the same quantity. They used to keep the LARGEST sigma per (From, To, end) always, widening the margin and hiding some rating breaches, against GR-077. Now the rows are grouped by their circuit label within (kind, From, To, end) and each group keeps its SMALLEST sigma (one circuit, one quantity). At the lookup, when the projected flow has ONE line between those buses, every row measures it, so the smallest sigma of all groups is the bound; only when there are parallel circuits (the violation names its buses, not its circuit) is the widest group bound kept, as before, because only it bounds whichever circuit is the one. Rows with no circuit label form one group of their own.

The project convention: alternatives live behind a seam and cross-validate each other (see `IWlsStep`). Further members (Hachtel-constrained, Huber/LAV robust, QR-orthogonal) land here as they are built.
- [`EstimationOptions`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Estimation/WlsStateEstimator.cs#L103) (record): Knobs for a `WlsStateEstimator` run.
- [`WlsStateEstimator`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Estimation/WlsStateEstimator.cs#L264) (class): The classical weighted-least-squares state estimator: given redundant, noisy measurements z = h(x) + e over a network, find the state x^ = (Va, Vm) minimising J(x) = sum (z_i-h_i(x))^2/sigma_i^2. The estimator owns the LOOP - start point, trust-capped damping, convergence, chi-square consistency, largest-normalized-residual bad-data removal - while everything representation-dependent (how H is held, how the gain is formed/solved, observability gating, residual covariance) lives behind the `IWlsStep` seam, with dense-LU and sparse Gilbert-Peierls backends today and alternative methods (constrained, robust, orthogonal) to follow. Unlike a power flow - which needs a complete, exactly-determined P/Q spec at every bus - the estimator takes whatever measurements exist, wherever they are, and lets redundancy fight noise. A singular gain matrix means the measurements cannot determine the state (unobservable) and is reported honestly, never as NaN. Critical measurements - the sole observers of a state direction - are flagged and protected from removal.
