### src/GridSim.Core/Estimation/WlsStep.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Estimation`. 742 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Estimation/WlsStep.cs).

- [`IWlsStep`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Estimation/WlsStep.cs#L18) (interface): One estimation-step backend: everything a Gauss-Newton pass needs that depends on how the normal equations are represented - the estimator-side sibling of `ILinearSolver` / `IPowerFlowSolver`. The estimator owns the loop (start point, damping, convergence, chi-square, bad-data removal); the step backend owns representation: how H is held, how the gain is formed and solved, how observability is gated, and how the residual covariance is computed. Today's implementations are dense LU (<= threshold) and sparse Gilbert-Peierls (above it); alternative METHODS (Hachtel-constrained, QR-orthogonal, robust reweighting) drop in behind this same seam without touching the loop.
- [`DenseWlsStep`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Estimation/WlsStep.cs#L53) (class): Dense normal equations on `ILinearSolver` - the <= threshold backend.
- [`SparseWlsStep`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Estimation/WlsStep.cs#L172) (class): Sparse normal equations on the Gilbert-Peierls LU - the gb-full-scale backend. H is held as per-measurement sparse rows from the shared evaluation path. The gain matrix's SPARSITY PATTERN is fixed for a whole pass (it is structural - the measurement topology), so `Begin` builds the CSC structure, per-row value slots and the RCM ordering exactly once; each iteration only refills values and refactors numerically. That removes the per-iteration CSR rebuild + re-sort + re-ordering the first implementation paid.
- [`ConstrainedDenseWlsStep`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Estimation/WlsStep.cs#L364) (class): Equality-constrained WLS (--method constrained): rows tagged `Source == "virtual-zero-injection"` are promoted from soft large-ish-sigma pseudo-measurements to HARD equalities via the KKT (Hachtel-style augmented) system [ G_f C^T ] [deltax] [ g_f ] [ C 0 ] [lambda ] = [ r_c ] where G_f/g_f are the free rows' normal equations and C the constraint Jacobian. A pure switching node's zero net injection is a network FACT, not telemetry - the constrained method honours it exactly instead of "within 10 MVAr", and conditions better than the huge-weight trick. Dense backend (<= SolverSelector threshold); the sparse constrained backend is future work and selection above the threshold fails loud rather than silently degrading.
- [`QrWlsStep`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Estimation/WlsStep.cs#L617) (class): Orthogonal (Householder QR) least-squares step - solves the Gauss-Newton correction from the weighted Jacobian directly, WITHOUT forming the ill-conditioned normal equations G = H^TWH (which square the condition number). Numerically the robust path for stressed cases; dense (forms the full weighted Jacobian). Observability and residual covariance still use the gain, formed only for those.
- [`CanonicalWlsStep`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Estimation/WlsStep.cs#L710) (class): The CANONICAL WLS step (Ruling, 2026-10-15): every plain WLS (and robust IRLS) estimate on the CPU, whatever its size, solves the gain through ONE factorisation, the sparse Gilbert-Peierls LU under the frozen RCM ordering (`SparseWlsStep`), exactly as every Newton step is solved through one canonical sparse routine. Before, a case at or below 200 buses was solved by a dense partial-pivot LU and a larger one by the sparse LU, so the same network estimated as 200 and as 201 buses went through different arithmetic and differed in the last bits, against the bit-identity rule; now the estimate does not depend on which side of any size threshold the case falls. Only the observability REPORT keeps its size rule: at or below the old threshold the start-point gate is the dense gain-rank proof (`DenseWlsStep.GateObservability`, the report those cases always had), above it the sparse diagnosis. The gate decides only whether the estimate runs and what the report names; it does no arithmetic of the estimate, so the numbers are canonical either way.

### src/GridSim.Core/Events/EventCatalog.cs

- [`EventCatalog`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Events/EventCatalog.cs#L16) (class): Loads/saves a catalog of `GridEvent`s (schema `gridsim-event-catalog/1`) under `data/events/`. ### src/GridSim.Core/Events/GridEvent.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Events`. 300 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Events/GridEvent.cs).

- [`PowerStep`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Events/GridEvent.cs#L7) (record): A power step within an event: negative MW = a generation loss/deficit; positive = restoration.
- [`RecordedActionKind`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Events/GridEvent.cs#L14) (enum): D-DOC-034 (October 2026, docs-session finding): what a recorded action IS, which decides whether a counterfactual replays it. `Unspecified` is the value a catalog entry gets when it does not say; the catalog loader refuses it (fail loud), because guessing either way changes every counterfactual of the event.
- [`RecordedAction`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Events/GridEvent.cs#L45) (record): A protective/operator action the record shows during the event - most importantly low-frequency demand disconnection (LFDD). It enters the swing model as a positive deltaP (load removed = deficit reduced), so feeding the RECORDED action in is replay, not prediction: we are told what happened and reproduce it. `Kind` (D-DOC-034) says whether a counterfactual replays it too (see `RecordedActionKind`).
- [`ResponseService`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Events/GridEvent.cs#L60) (record): A frequency-response service the system HELD at the event - volumes from the procurement record (e.g. EAC auction cleared quantities for the delivery block), delivery shape from the published service terms: DC ramps to 5% at 0.2 Hz deviation then to full at 0.5 Hz, within ~1 s; DM ramps 0.1->0.2 Hz within ~1 s; DR ramps 0.015->0.2 Hz over ~10 s. The knee pair carries the low-gain segment (DC: 0.2 Hz / 0.05); knee at the deadband with fraction 0 is a plain ramp-from-deadband (DM/DR); knee <= 0 is a droop line through zero. It enters the swing model as a proportional responder - replay of what the real system had, not prediction. Kept in BOTH the baseline replay and counterfactuals: stripping it from a counterfactual would credit the device with response the system already owned.
- [`RecordedDemandEffect`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Events/GridEvent.cs#L83) (record): N317 (October 2026, stream LF6; Ruling R1, Mark delegated EE calls 2026-10-04): the demand effect the record gives for the event, as MW of demand reduction per Hz of frequency fall. Demand varies with frequency (synchronous motors draw slightly less when the frequency is low), and a system operator can state how much for the system as it was: National Grid ESO's 9 August 2019 report (docs/reference S192, Tables 3 and 4 footnote) gives "approximately 350MW at 49.5 Hz" for the event's 29 GW demand, 700 MW/Hz. It is load damping (physics), so it is not a response service: it acts instantly, on both sides of nominal, and is kept in counterfactuals like the losses are. When an event carries one, `GridEvent.ApplyRecordedServices` sets `DynamicsConfig.DampingPctPerHz` so that the swing model's damping, DampingPctPerHz / 100 x `GridEvent.PreEventDemandMw`, is this figure (MW per Hz). The record's MW per Hz is kept as MW per Hz rather than as a percentage, because the percentage depends on which demand it is a percentage OF: the ESO figure is for the gross national demand (29 GW), the event's PreEventDemandMw is transmission-net (21.1 GW). Every other consumer of the damping (the declared-uncertainty corners, the exports the crossval sidecars read) sees the ordinary DampingPctPerHz field, so they need no change.
- [`RecordedOutcome`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Events/GridEvent.cs#L86) (record): What the record says actually happened - the headline metrics a replay must reproduce.
- [`GridEvent`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Events/GridEvent.cs#L114) (record): A real GB frequency event, described from the record: its pre-event system state, the loss(es) that occurred, the protective actions the record shows, and the `RecordedOutcome` the engine must reproduce before any counterfactual is allowed (the credibility gate). Every number not taken from a primary source is tagged `ProvenanceTag.CuratedPlaceholder` and flagged `[VERIFY]` in Notes.

### src/GridSim.Core/Evidence/AvoidedCost.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Evidence`. 149 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Evidence/AvoidedCost.cs).

- [`AvoidedCostInputs`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Evidence/AvoidedCost.cs#L13) (record): Inputs to an avoided-cost calculation. The Value of Lost Load (VoLL) and the outage duration are POLICY numbers, not physics - both default to `ProvenanceTag.CuratedPlaceholder` and must be replaced with a cited figure ([VERIFY]) before the result is quoted. GB VoLL estimates span roughly GBP6k-GBP17k/MWh. D-DOC-033 (October 2026): each input carries its OWN provenance, and the result takes the weaker of the two (`AvoidedCost.Weakest`). `VollSourceId` names the reference the VoLL figure was checked against (`VollSources`), null when none was given.
- [`AvoidedCostResult`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Evidence/AvoidedCost.cs#L24) (record): The avoided cost of an averted LFDD event, with its full arithmetic exposed for checking.
- [`AvoidedCost`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Evidence/AvoidedCost.cs#L41) (class): Avoided cost from a replayed event: the recorded demand actually disconnected by LFDD, valued at VoLL over the outage duration. This is grounded in the record (MW shed comes from `RecordedOutcome.LfddMwShed`), not a marketing figure. The result is only meaningful when the counterfactual device actually keeps the nadir above the LFDD threshold - otherwise the shed would still have happened and nothing is avoided.
- [`VollSource`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Evidence/AvoidedCost.cs#L103) (record): One published GB Value of Lost Load figure: the reference that states it and the figure itself.

### src/GridSim.Core/Fleet/FleetDynamics.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Fleet`. 139 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Fleet/FleetDynamics.cs).

- [`FleetResult`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Fleet/FleetDynamics.cs#L14) (record): A fleet frequency solve: the excursion, the peak fast-response the fleet ever delivered, and - the decision-relevant figure - the fast-response online at the nadir instant, when the fall must be arrested. Identical units that stay engaged all reach full output during a sustained excursion (so peak is additive), but a staggered fleet has fewer units online at the early nadir - that gap is the emergent non-additivity, and it shows up as a deeper nadir than an aggregate device of the same total budget.
- [`FleetDynamics`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Fleet/FleetDynamics.cs#L27) (class): The batch (pre-computed-trace) analogue of `FrequencyDynamics.Simulate` for a fleet of devices. Identical governor/damping/swing physics, but the device term is the sum of N independently deadbanded, lagged and onset-staggered unit outputs. With a single unit at zero stagger it is byte-identical to `Simulate` with that device - the fleet generalises, it doesn't fork, the physics.

Each unit has its own deadband, first-order lag and onset stagger, and all of them see one system frequency; the fleet's fast response is the sum of the independently clamped, independently staggered unit outputs, which is why fleet FFR is non-additive. Arming: a unit's `FleetUnit.StaggerSeconds` is a RESPONSE LATENCY measured from the moment the frequency leaves that unit's deadband, not from absolute t = 0 (anchoring it to t = 0 made stagger a no-op whenever units armed before the loss landed).

### src/GridSim.Core/Frequency/NesoFrequencyCsv.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Frequency`. 97 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Frequency/NesoFrequencyCsv.cs).

- [`NesoFrequencyCsv`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Frequency/NesoFrequencyCsv.cs#L20) (class): Streams NESO system-frequency CSV (`dtm,f` - timestamp, Hz) one row at a time, so a month of 1-second data (~2.7 M rows) reads without loading it all into memory. Every row's timestamp is passed through `ForwardInferenceGuard` - a recording newer than the historical horizon is rejected, so this ingester can only ever read the past. D-DOC-027 (October 2026, docs-session finding): what is skipped and what is refused. Blank lines are skipped. The FIRST non-blank line is skipped as the column header when it is not a data row and its first field holds no digit (NESO writes `dtm,f`; `timestamp,frequency` is skipped the same way). Every other line must be a data row - a timestamp, a comma, and a finite frequency above 0 Hz - or the read stops with an `InvalidDataException` that names the file, the line number and the line. The reader used to skip every line it could not parse without a word, so a file with no parsable rows at all gave `freq` zero statistics and exit 0, and a damaged row inside a trace silently shortened the comparison window.

### src/GridSim.Core/Frequency/RocofUpsampler.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Frequency`. 111 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Frequency/RocofUpsampler.cs).

- [`RocofUpsampler`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Frequency/RocofUpsampler.cs#L11) (class): Refines a coarse frequency trace to a fine timeline. Between two consecutive samples it computes the rate of change of frequency, `RoCoF = (f2 - f1) / deltat`, and fills the gap by linear interpolation - turning NESO's 1-second data into 50 sub-samples at 20 ms each (`f(t) = f1 + RoCoFt`). That 20 ms cadence is the resolution the frequency-dynamics model and a fast frequency-response controller want to see.

### src/GridSim.Core/Harmonics/ConverterHarmonicSources.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Harmonics`. 226 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Harmonics/ConverterHarmonicSources.cs).

- [`ConverterHarmonicLevel`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Harmonics/ConverterHarmonicSources.cs#L11) (enum): The fundamental current a converter source's G5 profile is scaled by (N036): the profile gives each harmonic as a fraction of the converter's fundamental current I1, and this says which I1.
- [`ConverterHarmonicSourceSet`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Harmonics/ConverterHarmonicSources.cs#L43) (record): The per-converter harmonic sources of a model (N036): one `HarmonicSource` per in-service converter-interfaced generator, plus what the rule left out and why. Nothing is dropped without a line here.
- [`ConverterHarmonicSources`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Harmonics/ConverterHarmonicSources.cs#L103) (class): N036 (October 2026): the Core rule that turns every converter-interfaced generator of a model into a harmonic current source, so a study need not rely on one synthetic six-pulse source at the largest-demand bus (the CLI and web default, which is unchanged and stays the default; this rule is opt-in and additive). Which units. Every in-service generator with `Generator.IsConverterInterfaced` true (battery, PV, type-4 wind, tidal, HVDC / interconnector: `ConverterPlant`, or an explicit `converterInterfaced`), except power-flow-only devices (`Generator.PowerFlowOnly`: a slack balancer or control unit is not physical plant). Synchronous machines inject no characteristic harmonic current in this engine; they are the harmonic SINKS (`HarmonicModelOptions.IncludeGeneratorSources`). Which spectrum. The technology profiles of ENA EREC G5 Issue 5 (2020), docs/reference S139, Annex B Table B.3 "Harmonic current emission assumptions for three-phase equipment types" pp.99-100 (listed as Table B.1 in the document's list of tables), already in `HarmonicSourceLibrary`: Self-commutated converters -> `afe-g5` (active front end). S139 Annex B pp.96-97: an active-front-end converter replaces the diode bridge with self-commutated IGBT modules, can transfer power both ways and produce reactive power. That is the topology of grid-connected battery, PV, full-converter wind and VSC HVDC plant, which is why the fault studies already treat these units as current sources. G5 Stage 1C / 2A list exactly three three-phase technologies (six-pulse, active front end, twelve-pulse: s.7.4 p.47, s.8.2 p.59); a converter-interfaced generator is none of the rectifier types, so active front end is the only one that fits. Line-commutated converters -> `12-pulse-g5`. A unit marked as feeding no fault current (`Generator.ConverterFaultCurrentPu` exactly 0, the model's own encoding of a line-commutated HVDC link) is a thyristor converter (S139 Annex B Figure B.2 p.96). That a line-commutated HVDC station is twelve-pulse is [VERIFY]: G5 does not say so (it is the usual HVDC arrangement), and a real station's AC filters remove most of the 11th / 13th, so this profile overstates such a station. The profiles are typical, not measured, so every source keeps the library's `Diagnostics.ProvenanceTag.CuratedPlaceholder` tag. At what level. I1 per `ConverterHarmonicLevel` (rated by default, the G5 assessment basis). Each component is the profile's Ih/I1 times I1, at phase 0. How several units add. All sources are at phase 0, so units at one bus, and their effects at every other bus, add linearly. G5 Issue 5 s.6.3.3 p.36: the summation exponents of Table 16 may be used only on a declared operational and locational diversity, "without which linear addition shall be employed" (exponent 1.0 means the sources are in phase). No diversity is declared in a model, so linear addition is the G5 rule. Orders. Table B.3 runs from order 2 to 50 and the active-front-end profile has even orders, which the default odd 3-49 study would not analyse (N075: they would be dropped). `StudyOptions` is `HarmonicModelOptions.Study` with orders 2 to 50 (`StudyOrders`). The study is balanced, so the triplen orders (3, 6, 9, ...: zero sequence) of the active-front-end profile cannot be carried by the positive-sequence network (R029); with `balanced: true` they are left out of the sources and each is listed in `ConverterHarmonicSourceSet.OmittedComponents`. A balanced three-phase converter with a delta or unearthed-star converter-transformer winding passes no zero-sequence current anyway, but nothing on disk states the winding of a given unit ([VERIFY]); use the three-phase study for triplens. Internal impedance (N149). S139 s.3.29 p.17 notes that active-front-end converters "may be classified as resonant plant due to their internal impedance". By default this engine stamps no converter impedance in Y(h) (a converter is an ideal current source, as in the fault studies). With `HarmonicModelOptions.ActiveFrontEndReactancePu` set, every unit of the active-front-end class (the `SelfCommutatedProfile` units, `FrequencyDependentYBus.IsActiveFrontEndPlant`) becomes a Norton equivalent: its source in parallel with that impedance to ground; line-commutated units are unchanged. No document on disk gives the value, so it has no default [VERIFY].

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Harmonics`. 186 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Harmonics/CoupledHarmonicPowerFlow.cs).

- [`IHarmonicCouplingModel`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Harmonics/CoupledHarmonicPowerFlow.cs#L18) (interface): A voltage-dependent harmonic-source coupling model: how a converter presents to the harmonic network. It has two parts - a LINEAR harmonic admittance `ShuntAdmittance` (the converter's Norton admittance, folded into Y so the solve stays stable and damps the resonance it would otherwise excite) and a current-source `Injection` that may depend nonlinearly on the terminal harmonic voltage. This is the ONE assumed part of the coupled solve - a converter's true behaviour is (vendor-proprietary) control-dependent - so it carries a `ProvenanceTag`, honestly `ProvenanceTag.CuratedPlaceholder`.
- [`NortonCouplingModel`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Harmonics/CoupledHarmonicPowerFlow.cs#L37) (class): A Norton coupling: the converter is a current source `Is(h)` in parallel with a harmonic admittance `Yc(h)`. The conductance damps the network resonance. A simple, honestly-assumed placeholder for a real, control-dependent characteristic.
- [`CoupledHarmonicResult`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Harmonics/CoupledHarmonicPowerFlow.cs#L56) (record): The outcome of a coupled harmonic power flow.
- [`CoupledHarmonicPowerFlow`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Harmonics/CoupledHarmonicPowerFlow.cs#L73) (class): Coupled iterative harmonic power flow. The converter's LINEAR harmonic admittance is folded into Y(h) (so the system is always stable and the converter damps, rather than only excites, the resonance), and any NONLINEAR voltage dependence of the injection is resolved by fixed-point iteration on that stable system: solve, update the injection from the coupling model, re-solve, until the voltage settles. The network physics stays grounded; only the coupling model is assumed, and it is provenance-tagged. Experimental (R062, October 2026): Core API and tests only; no CLI verb or production caller. Still needs: a measured or vendor converter coupling model (the only model, NortonCouplingModel, is a CuratedPlaceholder), a CLI surface, and validation against an independent coupled harmonic solver.

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Harmonics`. 288 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Harmonics/FrequencyDependentYBus.cs).

It is built from the SAME `AdmittanceStamp` as the fundamental `YBus`, with the frequency dependence applied per element: series reactance and line charging scale with h (`X -> hX`, `B -> hB`), series resistance by an optional skin-effect factor, and bus shunts by their nature (a capacitor's susceptance scales with h, a reactor's inversely). Loads are optionally added as frequency-dependent damping shunts. Grounded, and reduces exactly: at h=1 with the default options (no skin, no load shunts) this is bit-for-bit the fundamental `YBus.BuildSparse`. It emits a `ComplexCsr` for the `Abstractions.IComplexLinearSolver` seam. It degrades gracefully on today's data (lumped pi-model per order); once GDA hands over line length + OHL/cable + zero-sequence fields (Phase 6) the skin and long-line refinements attach here.

IEEE 519-2014 sets bus voltage-distortion limits (THD and each individual order) that tighten with voltage level; the UK G5/5 planning levels are broadly comparable at the distribution/HV tiers. ### src/GridSim.Core/Harmonics/HarmonicFrequencySweep.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Harmonics`. 205 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Harmonics/HarmonicFrequencySweep.cs).

- [`FrequencySweepOptions`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Harmonics/HarmonicFrequencySweep.cs#L11) (record): The grid and refinement settings for a `HarmonicFrequencySweep`.
- [`FrequencySweepResult`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Harmonics/HarmonicFrequencySweep.cs#L38) (record): The result of a fine driving-point frequency sweep. `Orders` is the sweep grid; `PositiveZ` is the positive-sequence driving-point impedance on it and `NegativeZ` the negative-sequence one (swept only when the network has a phase-shifting transformer - otherwise the two networks are identical and it is null). `PeakOrder` / `PeakMagnitude` are the REFINED resonance: the largest |Z| found, located between grid points by golden-section search.
- [`HarmonicFrequencySweep`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Harmonics/HarmonicFrequencySweep.cs#L65) (class): A fine driving-point impedance sweep (R063, October 2026). The order-by-order `HarmonicImpedanceScan` samples |Z| only at the analysed integer orders, so a sharp, lightly damped parallel resonance BETWEEN orders - at h = 6.2, say, the very signature the sharpness metric is meant to catch - was never sampled and was reported at the nearest order with a much smaller peak. This sweeps a fine grid of frequency multiples on the positive-sequence network (and the negative-sequence one when a phase shifter makes them differ), then refines the largest peak by golden-section search. Deterministic: grid points are `MinOrder + k*Step` (never accumulated), every point is solved independently and written by index, the peak tie-break is the first (lowest) grid point, and the refinement runs a fixed number of steps. A singular point fails loud (`SingularHarmonicNetworkException`, lowest frequency first).

### src/GridSim.Core/Harmonics/HarmonicImpedanceScan.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Harmonics`. 116 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Harmonics/HarmonicImpedanceScan.cs).

- [`ImpedanceScanResult`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Harmonics/HarmonicImpedanceScan.cs#L18) (record): A frequency scan of the driving-point harmonic impedance seen at one bus, plus the resonance it reveals. `Z`[oi] is the driving-point impedance Z_kk at `BusId` at `Orders`[oi]; a large |Z| is a parallel resonance (a small injected harmonic current there produces a large voltage). `ResonanceOrder` / `PeakMagnitude` name the worst peak, and `Participation` gives, at that order, the transfer impedance to every bus - the buses that "participate" in the resonance (a proxy for the modal participation factor without a complex eigensolve).
- [`HarmonicImpedanceScan`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Harmonics/HarmonicImpedanceScan.cs#L34) (class): The harmonic impedance / frequency scan and resonance identification. The driving-point impedance at a bus is the k-th entry of the solution of `Y(h) x = e_k` (a unit current injected at bus k), i.e. the k-th column of `Y(h)^-1`; scanning it across orders reveals where the network resonates. This is the tool that turns "harmonic-damping loss" from a claim into a measurement: as synchronous machines retire, the resonance peaks sharpen and move into the ordered-harmonic range.

This is the grounded core of the harmonic engine - the physics (Y(h), the solve, KCL) never guesses; the only assumed input is the source spectra, which arrive provenance-tagged. The default backend is the scalable real 2n-expansion solver, so this runs at gb-full scale.

Its `Spectrum` gives the per-order injection as a percent of `FundamentalCurrentPu` (the reference current); the physics (Y(h), the penetration solve) is fully grounded and does not depend on where the spectrum came from. A default library spectrum is `ProvenanceTag.CuratedPlaceholder` (assumed-typical, [VERIFY]); a measured spectrum loads identically tagged `ProvenanceTag.Recorded` - the same solver, the tag the only difference.
- [`HarmonicSourceLibrary`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Harmonics/HarmonicSource.cs#L74) (class): Typed default harmonic-source spectra - the library that lets a study run before any measured data exists. Every spectrum here is assumed-typical, literature-idealised, so it is tagged `ProvenanceTag.CuratedPlaceholder` and carries a `[VERIFY]` in its type name: a real converter's spectrum depends on its control, loading and the local voltage, none of which these encode. They exist so the grounded engine has an input to run on; a measured spectrum replaces one by swapping the tag, not the code path.

### src/GridSim.Core/Harmonics/HarmonicStateEstimator.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Harmonics`. 133 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Harmonics/HarmonicStateEstimator.cs).

- [`HarmonicVoltageMeasurement`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Harmonics/HarmonicStateEstimator.cs#L10) (record): One harmonic voltage measurement: the measured complex voltage at a bus at a given order, and its standard deviation (for weighting).
- [`HarmonicStateEstimate`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Harmonics/HarmonicStateEstimator.cs#L17) (record): The result of estimating the harmonic sources at one order.
- [`HarmonicStateEstimator`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Harmonics/HarmonicStateEstimator.cs#L36) (class): Harmonic state estimation: recover the harmonic SOURCE injections (and hence the whole harmonic state) from a handful of harmonic voltage measurements. It is the natural inverse of penetration, and the on-brand extension of GridSim's estimator identity to the harmonic domain. At a single order the problem is LINEAR - the measurements are `z = H x + noise` with `H = Z(h)[measured, source]` (columns of the harmonic impedance matrix) and `x` the unknown injections - so it is a complex weighted least-squares solve, reusing the complex-solver seam for both the impedance columns and the small normal equations. It never nowcasts: harmonic measurements are dated inputs guarded upstream like any other. Experimental (R062, October 2026): Core API and tests only; no CLI verb or production caller. Still needs: an input format for dated harmonic voltage measurements (guarded like every other dated input), a CLI surface (for example under the harmonics verb), and validation against an independent reference.

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Harmonics`. 33 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Harmonics/SingularHarmonicNetworkException.cs).

- [`SingularHarmonicNetworkException`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Harmonics/SingularHarmonicNetworkException.cs#L15) (class): Thrown when the harmonic network admittance `Y(h)` at some order cannot be solved: it is singular, so there is no unique harmonic voltage for the injected current. Physically this means part of the network has no path to ground at that frequency - typically a radial feeder or island with no line charging, no shunt and no modelled source impedance (synchronous machines are the main harmonic path to ground; see `HarmonicModelOptions.IncludeGeneratorSources` and `HarmonicModelOptions.Study`). Fail loud (October 2026 review, R001): every harmonic solver used to substitute a ZERO voltage vector for a singular solve, which the indices then reported as 0% THD and the IEEE-519 check as "Compliant" - a wrong answer that looked like a clean pass. A singular order is now an error that names the order, never a result.

### src/GridSim.Core/Harmonics/ThreePhaseHarmonics.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Harmonics`. 354 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Harmonics/ThreePhaseHarmonics.cs).

- [`ThreePhaseHarmonicSource`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Harmonics/ThreePhaseHarmonics.cs#L15) (class): A three-phase harmonic current source: the per-phase injection at each order. Harmonics are inherently unbalanced, so this carries a full per-phase spectrum. The `Balanced` factory generates the classic balanced rotation - phase B lags A by `h*120 deg`, phase C leads by the same - which reproduces the sequence pattern automatically (triplens collapse to zero sequence, the 5th is negative, etc.).
- [`ThreePhasePenetrationResult`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Harmonics/ThreePhaseHarmonics.cs#L58) (record): Per-bus, per-phase harmonic voltages from a three-phase penetration study, plus the sequence view.
- [`ThreePhaseActiveFrontEnd`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Harmonics/ThreePhaseHarmonics.cs#L81) (record): N348 / N149 rest (CF4, October 2026; Ruling R1): an active-front-end converter on a three-phase feeder, as resonant plant through its internal impedance (ENA EREC G5 Issue 5 s.3.29 p.17, docs/reference S139; the positive-sequence study's `HarmonicModelOptions.ActiveFrontEndReactancePu`). `ReactancePu` (at the fundamental) and `ResistancePu` are per-unit on the unit's own three-phase rating `RatingMva`; the study converts them to the feeder's base (`MultiPhaseModel.BaseMva`) by `BaseMva / RatingMva`, as the positive-sequence study converts from MBase. No default value exists on disk [VERIFY]: the caller states it (the converter's coupling reactor or filter, from the manufacturer).
- [`ThreePhaseHarmonicPenetration`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Harmonics/ThreePhaseHarmonics.cs#L98) (class): Three-phase / unbalanced harmonic penetration. It assembles the reduced 3n complex admittance Y(h) of the unbalanced feeder (each line branch's 3x3 series impedance with reactance scaled to order h, inverted to a 3x3 admittance and stamped block-wise), with the source substation as the harmonic ground, and solves `Y(h) V(h) = I(h)` for the per-phase bus voltages via the complex-solver seam. A balanced feeder with balanced injection reduces to the single-phase penetration (the non-regression bridge); an unbalanced one produces the negative/zero-sequence content the positive-sequence engine cannot see. Experimental (R062, October 2026). On the CLI since N062 as `dist3ph <feeder> harmonics` (one balanced library source on a gridsim-dist3ph/1 feeder). Still needs validation of the sequence content against an independent three-phase reference [VERIFY]. N167 (October 2026): shunt capacitors (j h B per phase), line charging (half the pi shunt at each end, G + j h B) and closed switches (their buses merged into one node) are modelled; loads of every kind stay outside Y(h); a single- or two-phase branch or a step-voltage regulator is refused by name (`MultiPhaseModel.RequireSupportedElements`). It used to refuse every N062 element.

- [`RtuQuality`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Interpose/IRtuProtocol.cs#L35) (enum): Normalised telemetry-quality flags, folded from each protocol's own descriptor (IEC-104 QDS, DNP3 object flags, GOOSE validity, C37.118 STAT). There is no quality field on `Estimation.Measurement` - `QualityFold` turns these into a sigma multiplier or an outright drop, because in the estimator sigma is the weight.
- [`RtuPoint`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Interpose/IRtuProtocol.cs#L71) (record): One decoded, corrected telemetry point in protocol-native address space: a value plus quality and an optional device timestamp, keyed by an address string the `RtuPointMap` crosswalk resolves to a bus or branch. Address forms are per-protocol, e.g. `"IOA:1001"` (IEC-104/101), `"DNP:AI:12"` (DNP3), `"MB:HR:40001"` (Modbus), a GOOSE dataset-member path, or `"PMU:3:V0"` (C37.118).
- [`RtuTransportKind`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Interpose/IRtuProtocol.cs#L88) (enum): How a protocol's frames arrive off the wire.

The transport framing is already handled by the codecs in `GridSim.Core.IO.Telemetry`; an implementation adds the application / object-model layer, turning a validated frame into zero-or-more `RtuPoint`s. Control frames that carry no measurement (IEC-104 U-frames, DNP3 link ACKs) decode to an empty list, not an error.
- [`IRtuSessionState`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Interpose/IRtuProtocol.cs#L130) (interface): GR-329: a protocol whose decoder keeps per-connection state (the Modbus stack remembers outstanding requests by transaction id). The interposer calls `ResetSession` whenever its client goes away, so nothing one client sent can pair with, or be refused because of, what the next client sends. A stateless protocol need not implement it.

### src/GridSim.Core/Interpose/Protocols/Iec104ControllingStation.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Interpose.Protocols`. 336 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Interpose/Protocols/Iec104ControllingStation.cs).

- [`Iec104ControllingStation`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Interpose/Protocols/Iec104ControllingStation.cs#L46) (class): N230 (October 2026, main's ruling R1 on question 3): the IEC 60870-5-104 CONTROLLING STATION link behaviour of the interposer. `interpose` listens and the outstation (the RTU) connects to it, but in IEC 104 terms the interposer is the controlling station, so it must drive the session: an outstation does not send monitor data until the controlling station has started data transfer, and it stops sending when its window of unacknowledged I-frames is full. Before this, interpose never sent a byte, so a real outstation would wait for STARTDT act for ever (or stall after k frames waiting for an acknowledgement). What it does, and nothing more (minimal and deterministic; the received-data path is unchanged, every frame still goes to the pipeline exactly as before): On connect: send STARTDT act. A STARTDT con from the outstation is recorded (`DataTransferStarted`). TESTFR act received: answer TESTFR con at once. I-frames received: count them in V(R) (mod 32768) and acknowledge with an S-frame carrying N(R) = V(R) at the latest after `W` unacknowledged I-frames, or `T2Ms` after the first unacknowledged one. No frame received for `T3Ms`: send TESTFR act (once per idle period of t3; the idle clock restarts when it is sent and whenever a frame arrives). GR-803 and GR-823: the station now also asks for the connection to be CLOSED (`CloseRequested`, with `CloseReason`; the transport drops the client, counted as a reset) when a STARTDT act or a TESTFR act it sent is not confirmed within `T1Ms` (t1), and when an I-frame's send sequence number N(S) is not the receive sequence V(R) it expects (an I-frame lost or repeated). Before, an unanswered STARTDT act or TESTFR act stalled the link silently and a sequence gap went unnoticed. A frame with the wrong N(S) is not counted in V(R) and not acknowledged; the transport still hands it up (it was received), and nothing more is answered on that connection. N366, the k window: this station sends no I-frames, so its send sequence V(S) is always 0 and it never has an I-frame outstanding (0 is within any k). The window is therefore enforced from the other side: every N(R) the outstation sends (in an S-frame or an I-frame) acknowledges this station's I-frames and must equal V(S) = 0. Any other N(R) acknowledges frames that were never sent, a protocol error, and the station asks for the connection to be closed (as for an N(S) gap). The receive side keeps the outstation inside ITS k window by acknowledging after w = 8 < k = 12 I-frames (the standard's recommendation is w no more than two thirds of k). N366, STOPDT: `StopDataTransfer` acknowledges any unacknowledged I-frames and sends STOPDT act, supervised by t1 like STARTDT act. STOPDT con ends data transfer (`DataTransferStarted` false, `DataTransferStopped` true). An I-frame that arrives after STOPDT con is a protocol error and closes the connection; I-frames between STOPDT act and its con are still counted and acknowledged (the outstation may finish sending what it had queued). `StartDataTransfer` restarts transfer on the same connection. All times come in as a monotonic millisecond clock value from the caller, so the behaviour is a pure function of the frames and the times (unit-testable without a socket). [VERIFY] The parameter values are the defaults of IEC 60870-5-104 clause 5 as commonly cited (k = 12, w = 8, t1 = 15 s, t2 = 10 s, t3 = 20 s). The standard's text is not on disk.

S/U-format frames (acknowledgements, STARTDT/STOPDT/TESTFR) carry no measurement and decode to an empty list. GR-306 (November 2026): with the opt-in `Iec104PointKey.CasduIoa` (crosswalk `"iec104Key": "casdu-ioa"`) points are named `CA:<casdu>/IOA:<n>`, so stations sharing a link never collide. With the default `Iec104PointKey.Ioa` the names are unchanged, but an IOA that arrives with a second common address on one link is a collision: from then on its points are marked `RtuQuality.Invalid` (the crosswalk cannot say which station it means), counted, and the first one is named.

### src/GridSim.Core/Interpose/Protocols/ModbusProtocol.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Interpose.Protocols`. 149 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Interpose/Protocols/ModbusProtocol.cs).

- [`ModbusProtocol`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Interpose/Protocols/ModbusProtocol.cs#L37) (class): Modbus TCP. Decodes a read-holding/input-registers response (`ModbusFrame`) into one point per register. Modbus has no native quality or timestamp: points are `RtuQuality.Good` with no device time (the window's receive clock stamps them), and the raw register is turned into engineering units by the crosswalk binding (`RtuPointBinding.DataType`, then `RtuPointBinding.Scale`). Addressing (R271). A Modbus response carries no start address; only the request that asked for it does. So this decoder remembers every read request it sees (keyed by MBAP transaction id) and pairs each response with its request: Paired (the tap sees both directions): each register gets its ABSOLUTE address `MB:U<unit>:<fc>:@<register>`, e.g. `MB:U1:3:@100`. Two different polled blocks can never collide. Unpaired (only responses are seen): the register is addressed by its POSITION in the response, `MB:U<unit>:<fc>:<index>`, as before. Positional addresses from two different blocks on the same unit and function code would collide in the crosswalk and silently bind one block's register to the other's measurement. That is refused: once a positional block of N registers has been seen for a unit/fc, a positional response with a different register count throws `InvalidDataException` (counted by `InterposePipeline.DecodeErrors`, never mapped). Two blocks of the SAME size cannot be told apart without their requests; a deployment that polls more than one block per unit/fc must let the interposer see the requests. The decoder is stateful (it holds the outstanding requests), so it is thread-safe but one instance should serve one stream. GR-329: `ResetSession` forgets that state; the interposer calls it when its client goes away, so a new connection starts clean. Transaction ids (GR-801). A response is paired with the outstanding request of its transaction id. When a second, DIFFERENT read request arrives with an id that is still outstanding (a gateway that reuses or pipelines ids), which request the next response with that id answers cannot be known: that id is marked ambiguous, and its response is refused (InvalidDataException, counted as a decode error, never mapped) rather than paired with the later request. The same request sent again (a retry) is not ambiguous. An exception response (function code with bit 7 set) ends its transaction: the outstanding request is forgotten and no point is produced.

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Interpose`. 79 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Interpose/QualityFold.cs).

The multipliers are deliberately conservative: a stale or substituted value is admitted but down-weighted; an invalid/blocked/comm-lost value never enters the solve.

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Interpose`. 296 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Interpose/RtuPointMap.cs).

Bus kinds address a bus by `Bus` id; branch kinds by (`From`, `To`, `Circuit`, `End`), exactly as `Measurement` does. The value is converted to engineering units by dividing by `BaseKv` (voltage) or `BaseAmps` (current); power kinds pass through as MW/MVAr. Angle kinds are re-referenced by subtracting `DatumAngleDeg` so an external feed's arbitrary reference aligns with the estimator's slack (see `MeasurementKind.VaDeg`).
- [`RtuRegisterType`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Interpose/RtuPointMap.cs#L61) (enum): How a binding's raw register value(s) are interpreted (see `RtuPointBinding.DataType`).
- [`RtuWordOrder`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Interpose/RtuPointMap.cs#L78) (enum): The 16-bit word order of a 32-bit value spread over two consecutive registers.

Wire format `gridsim-rtu-pointmap/1` (camelCase JSON, enums by name) - the same serializer contract as `MeasurementSet`. Addresses have no intrinsic bus meaning, so this map is authored per RTU; a skeleton can be pre-filled from the GDA `asset_crosswalk.json` (bus ids) with the native addresses added by hand.
- [`RtuPointMapJsonContext`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Interpose/RtuPointMap.cs#L296) (class): Phase 0.1: the source-generated JSON metadata for an RTU point map and every type it reaches, so it is read and written without runtime reflection (NativeAOT). Metadata mode only: the bytes come from the same converters the reflection path used, never from a separately generated fast path. Enums by name, as before. The runtime options (naming, key case, null and number handling, indentation) are passed in by the call site.

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.IO`. 1279 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/IO/BridgeProtocol.cs).

A single socket carries three message kinds, each tagged by a `type` discriminator: `topology` - sent once at the start of a stream: `{type,model:{...}}`, where `model` is exactly the `model` block of a `gridsim-solve-export/1` document (so it reuses `SolveImport`'s bus/generator/branch shapes). Cached by the client and reused for every frame. `state` - one per tick, a slim solved snapshot: `{type,t,result:{buses,lineFlows}, scalars:{...},overlays:{...}}`. The `result` block reuses the solve-export `result` shape; `StateMessage.ToPowerFlowResult` rebuilds a `PowerFlowResult` from it against the cached topology, and `StateMessage.ToSimFrame` assembles the `SimFrame` the views bind to. `result` - the response to an on-demand `query`: `{type,op,at,payload:{solveExport,verdict, bindingConstraint,violations}}`. `payload.solveExport` is a full `gridsim-solve-export/1` document that goes straight through `SolveImport.Read(string)`. Deserialisation mirrors `SolveImport`: case-insensitive (PascalCase and camelCase both bind) and tolerant of named float literals (Infinity limits).
- [`NoteMessage`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/IO/BridgeProtocol.cs#L148) (class): `{type, message}` - an `info` or `error` envelope carrying a human-readable note.
- [`TopologyMessage`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/IO/BridgeProtocol.cs#L372) (class): `{type:"topology", model:{...}}` - the network, sent once per stream.

- [`AssetEntry`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/IO/BridgeProtocol.cs#L1139) (record): One row of a per-asset block (e.g. one BM unit envelope, one tap changer, one consumer).
- [`AssetData`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/IO/BridgeProtocol.cs#L1146) (record): The projected `op="asset"` payload: the resolved unit ids and the four per-asset blocks (generator envelope MSG/Pmax, BESS SoC ratings, tap-changer wear, consumer/demand placement), each a list of raw Derived-dataset rows. Blocks the unit doesn't have arrive empty.
- [`PropagationData`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/IO/BridgeProtocol.cs#L1207) (record): The projected `op="propagation"` payload: GDA's per-corridor electromechanical delays as a `(fromBus, toBus) -> tau seconds` map ready to drop into `DistributedConfig.ProvidedTauSeconds`, plus the honest provenance note (distances/inertia real; wave speed + tau modelled, unvalidated at scale). Metadata mode only: the bytes come from the same converters the reflection path used. The runtime options are the bridge settings, passed in by `BridgeProtocol.Json`.

- [`CimControlOptions`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/IO/Cim/CimControlledPowerFlow.cs#L15) (record): N295 / N296 (CIM3, 2026-10): the knobs of `CimControlledPowerFlow`.
- [`CimShuntControlMode`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/IO/Cim/CimControlledPowerFlow.cs#L20) (enum): N296 (CIM3, 2026-10): how `CimControlledPowerFlow` solves the voltage-regulating shunts (`CimBridgeResult.ShuntRegulations`).
- [`CimControlledSolveRecord`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/IO/Cim/CimControlledPowerFlow.cs#L47) (record): N306 (LF3, October 2026): what a settled `CimControlledPowerFlow` solve set the regulated devices to, kept against the result object it returned so `CimBridgeResult.SwitchFlows` can balance a switch with the regulated values instead of the plain model's fixed ones.
- [`CimControlState`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/IO/Cim/CimControlledPowerFlow.cs#L59) (record): N295: where one control ended after `CimControlledPowerFlow.Solve`.
- [`CimControlledPowerFlow`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/IO/Cim/CimControlledPowerFlow.cs#L92) (class): N295 / N296 (CIM3, 2026-10): the power flow of a bridged CIM network WITH the CIM voltage controls GridSim's PV / PQ bus cannot express, as an outer loop around an unchanged engine (the way GridSim's tap-changer loop and switched-shunt loop work, and the way PSS/E and PowerFactory solve remote control and SVC droop in outer loops): Remote voltage control (`CimBridgeResult.RemoteVoltageControls`): the machines' buses are made PV and their set-points are chosen so the REMOTE bus is at its target. The machines' reactive limits are enforced by the engine as usual: when they bind (the engine ends their bus PQ), the remote bus cannot be held and the control is reported at its limit (PSS/E's behaviour). N307 (LF3, October 2026; Ruling R1): a SHARED control (machines at several buses) has one set-point per machine bus; the first free one carries the voltage law and each other free one the sharing law Q_k / key_k = Q_lead / key_lead (keys: the reactive ranges, `CimRemoteVoltageControl.ReactiveShareKeys`), so the reactive output is shared in proportion to the machines' reactive ranges (powsybl; the PSS/E RMPCT default). A machine bus the engine pins at a reactive limit leaves the sharing and the others carry on. A control with one machine bus is solved exactly as before (one set-point, the voltage law), bit for bit. Susceptance controls (`CimBridgeResult.SusceptanceControls`: StaticVarCompensators, and shunt compensators under continuous control, N296): a susceptance B between its limits at its bus, with V_regulated + slope x B x V_bus^2 / baseMVA = target. At a limit it stays a fixed susceptance (exact: its output follows V^2, unlike a PV bus pinned at a fixed Q). The control variables are found by a damped Newton iteration whose sensitivities are taken by finite differences of whole engine solves (one probe per variable), then updated by Broyden's rank-one rule; a variable at a limit that wants to go further is held there. Every solve is an ordinary solve of the engine on a copy of the model, so the dense and sparse engines give the same bits, and the iteration is fully deterministic (fixed order, no randomness). It ends when every free control is within `CimControlOptions.TolerancePu`. Fail loud: when it cannot (the cap is reached, the sensitivities are singular, the engine does not converge, or a machine is held at a limit on the wrong side), the result is returned with `PowerFlowResult.Converged` false and `LastNote` says why; such a state must never be reported as regulated. A plain engine solve of `CimBridgeResult.Model` holds remote-regulating machines and SVCs at their SSH q; this solver is the opt-in that regulates them. With no control at all it is one engine solve of the model as given (the same result object).
- [`Var`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/IO/Cim/CimControlledPowerFlow.cs#L250) (class): One control variable.

### src/GridSim.Core/IO/Cim/CimExporter.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.IO.Cim`. 604 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/IO/Cim/CimExporter.cs).

- [`CimExporter`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/IO/Cim/CimExporter.cs#L24) (class): Exports a `CimNetwork` to striped CIM / CGMES RDF/XML - the inverse of `CimImporter`. Emits TopologicalNode buses (with their BaseVoltage), ACLineSegment branches, EnergyConsumer loads, SynchronousMachine generators and two- and three-winding PowerTransformers (ends + tap/phase changers; a three-winding unit gets one changer per tapped winding), each with the Terminals linking equipment to nodes - so an import-export round-trip preserves buses, base voltages, branches, loads, generators and transformers. D-DOC-099 / 101 / 104 (2026-10): a load keeps its class, a line its own base voltage, and a generator its machine data (ratedS, minQ / maxQ, referencePriority, controlEnabled, a local voltage RegulatingControl, a GeneratingUnit with its operating limits, and its inertia as a SynchronousMachineSimplified dynamics model); each is written only when present. N253 / N254 (CIM1, 2026-10): a closed switch joining two buses (CimNetwork.ClosedSwitches) is written as a closed switch of its class with its retained flag, and a generator's type as the GeneratingUnit subclass it came from (with its FossilFuel for a fuel type); both only when present, so a network without them exports exactly as before. N286 (CIM2, 2026-10): shunts (as one section holding their whole admittance), ExternalNetworkInjection / EquivalentInjection / PowerElectronicsConnection generators (under their own class, with a PV / wind / battery unit for a typed connection) and AsynchronousMachine loads are written back under their own class; again only when present.

The device is a susceptance B at bus `BusId` between `BMinMvar` and `BMaxMvar`, chosen so that the regulated bus's voltage V (pu) satisfies V = `TargetPu` - `SlopePu` x Q / baseMVA, with Q = B x Vbus^2 its capacitive output (MVAr); at a limit it stays a fixed susceptance (its output then follows V^2, which is what an SVC at its limit does, and what the CGMES 3.0 MicroGrid BE's published SV shows: q = -9.88107 MVAr = 223.658^2 / 5062.5).

A form that cannot be built is null and `Basis` says why.

### src/GridSim.Core/IO/Cim/CimGridModelBridge.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.IO.Cim`. 731 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/IO/Cim/CimGridModelBridge.cs).

- [`CimGridModelBridge`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/IO/Cim/CimGridModelBridge.cs#L69) (class): Bridges a parsed `CimNetwork` into a solvable `GridModel`: CIM nodes become buses (energy consumers add their load, synchronous machines add generators), AC line segments become branches. Generators (D-DOC-104). Each machine keeps its P and Q, its voltage set-point (the local RegulatingControl target in kV, per-unitised on its bus's base voltage), its reactive limits (minQ / maxQ), its active limits (the GeneratingUnit's min / maxOperatingP), its base (ratedS) and its inertia H (from the dynamics profile). A bus with a voltage-controlling machine is PV; a bus whose machines all have voltage control off (controlEnabled false, a disabled or non-voltage control, remote regulation) is PQ with their Q injected. Slack rule (D-DOC-104). The angle reference is chosen from the voltage-controlling machines (all machines when none controls), by, in order: (1) the lowest positive `SynchronousMachine.referencePriority` (IEC 61970-301 / CGMES: 1 = the highest priority as the power-flow reference, 0 = no preference); (2) the largest unit, by `GeneratingUnit.maxOperatingP`, else `ratedS`; (3) the lowest bus number (the CIM node order). The choice and the rule that decided it are written to the notes. It used to be the first generator in document order, always, with no word. Per-unit (D-DOC-101). Impedances are per-unitised on the way in: a line's ohms against the base voltage of its end nodes (Zbase = kV^2 / MVA); the from node's base, else the to node's, else the line's own ConductingEquipment.BaseVoltage. Two end nodes of different base voltage (N294, CIM3 2026-10) are each per-unit on their own base with the ratio as an off-nominal tap on the line (exact), up to `LineBaseRatioBound` apart; further apart they are refused (two voltage levels, not two names for one). Each transformer winding's ohms are per-unitised against that winding's own ratedU, else the base voltage of the node it connects to. With no base voltage at all, a non-zero impedance is REFUSED: it used to be taken as already per-unit without a word, which for ohm data is wrong by a factor of Zbase. A caller whose CIM network really carries per-unit values says so with `unbasedImpedancesArePerUnit: true`. A two-winding transformer becomes one tapped branch; a three-winding transformer becomes a star-point bus with one branch per winding, each carrying its own tap. Closed switches (N253). The buses each `CimNetwork.ClosedSwitches` entry joins (a closed retained switch) are solved as one bus: a closed switch has zero impedance. The joined bus keeps the name and place of the first of them; each join is written to the notes. A line left with both ends on one joined bus is left out (it carries no current) and noted. Generator type (N254): `CimGenerator.Type` becomes `Generator.Type`. Transformer ratings and magnetising admittance (CIM2 2026-10). When a winding's rated voltage differs from its bus's base voltage, the nominal turns ratio is off-nominal on the bus bases: a two-winding unit gets tap x n1 / n2 (n = ratedU / bus base) with its impedance referred to the to-bus base (x n2^2); a three-winding winding k gets tap x n_k (the star point's base is winding 1's rating) and the star point starts at 1 / tap of winding 1. The magnetising susceptance `PowerTransformerEnd.b` is the branch's shunt susceptance (b x ratedU^2 / baseMVA, half at each end); N307 (LF3 2026-10, Ruling R1): the magnetising conductance g is represented the same way, as end-bus shunt conductance placed where the branch puts each half of b (it used to be listed as not represented). Call (Ruling R1), from the ENTSO-E conformity models' published SV: without the rated ratio the MiniGrid solves 4 to 5 % off its SV voltages and with it to 1e-5 pu; the SmallGrid's one transformer with b reproduces its SV only with b split half to each end (the IEEE-118 origin of that model is a pi branch). A transformer whose ratings equal its bus bases and whose b is zero (every transformer in every test before this) bridges bit for bit as before. Shunts and injections (N286, CIM2 2026-10). Each `CimNetwork.Shunts` entry adds G kV^2 MW and B kV^2 MVAr (at 1.0 pu of its bus's base voltage) to the bus's Gs / Bs. ExternalNetworkInjection, EquivalentInjection and PowerElectronicsConnection generators are generators like any other (the same slack rule); a PowerElectronicsConnection sets `Generator.ConverterInterfaced`. De-energised islands (N287, CIM2 2026-10). An island that holds neither the slack nor a voltage-controlling machine (cut off by open switches or disconnected terminals) is left out of the GridModel, its buses named in one note (PSS/E's isolated buses, type 4); it used to make GridModel.Validate refuse the whole model. N296 (CIM3 2026-10): an energised island that does not hold the slack gets its own slack, elected by the same rule within the island (PSS/E's swing bus per island); it used to be kept with none and refused by GridModel.Validate. `Bridge` also returns where each CIM bus went and, after a solve, the flow through each closed retained switch (`CimBridgeResult.SwitchFlows`). Fail loud: a load, generator, line or transformer that names a node which is not one of the network's buses throws `InvalidDataException`; it used to be skipped without a word. Topology carries no timestamp, so no horizon guard applies to the model bridge.

- [`CimImporter`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/IO/Cim/CimImporter.cs#L391) (class): A CIM / IEC 61970 (CGMES) network importer. It reads striped RDF/XML equipment + topology and extracts the buses, line branches (ACLineSegment), two- and three-winding transformers, loads (EnergyConsumer and its subclasses ConformLoad, NonConformLoad and StationSupply) and generators (SynchronousMachine) with their terminal connectivity. It matches elements and attributes by local name, so it is robust across CIM schema versions (cim14/16/100). Multi-profile CGMES (R064). CGMES splits each object across profiles: the EQ description uses `rdf:ID`, and the TP / SSH / SV descriptions of the same object use `rdf:about` with the same mRID. All descriptions of one mRID are merged into one object first (the first value of each property wins), so a merged EQ+TP(+SSH) document resolves an EQ Terminal's equipment and its TP node together, and an EnergyConsumer's SSH p/q join its EQ description. `urn:uuid:` identifiers (CGMES 3) are normalised. Identifiers (D-DOC-105). An identifier is reduced to its mRID by removing ONE leading `#` (a reference) and then ONE leading `_` (the CGMES 2.4 XML-ID prefix), or a `urn:uuid:` prefix. Two different XML IDs that reduce to the same mRID (`a` and `_a`) are refused, never merged. One node view. When the document has TopologicalNodes (bus-branch view) they are the buses, and a terminal that only names a ConnectivityNode is mapped through `ConnectivityNode.TopologicalNode`; the ConnectivityNodes are not also turned into buses (they used to be, leaving orphan buses). With no TopologicalNodes the buses come from the ConnectivityNodes through the topology processor (node-breaker view). `CimImportOptions.Topology` can force either view. Topology processor (N253, CIM1 2026-10). In the node-breaker view the ConnectivityNodes joined by CLOSED switches (Switch and every subclass: Breaker, Disconnector, LoadBreakSwitch, Fuse, Jumper, ...) are one bus; an open switch keeps them apart. This is the CGMES definition of a TopologicalNode ("a set of connectivity nodes that, in the current network state, are connected together through any type of closed switches, including jumpers", IEC 61970-301 / CGMES 2.4.15 TP) and what PowerFactory, PSS/E and powsybl do on import. The rules: (1) the state is the SSH `Switch.open`, else the EQ `Switch.normalOpen`; a switch with neither is refused; (2) a switch whose terminal is disconnected (`connected` = false) or which is out of service conducts nothing (treated as open); (3) a closed retained switch does not merge: by the CGMES definition it is kept in the bus-branch model, its sides are two TopologicalNodes, so here they are two buses and the switch is listed in `CimNetwork.ClosedSwitches` (the bridge solves them as one bus: a closed switch has zero impedance); (4) a GroundDisconnector never joins two nodes (it earths one), and a closed one is listed. The result is deterministic: the joining is a union-find whose outcome does not depend on the order of the switches; each bus takes the smallest (ordinal) ConnectivityNode mRID of its set as its mRID, the name of the smallest-mRID BusbarSection on it (else that ConnectivityNode's name), and the buses are ordered by mRID, so neither the file order nor any dictionary order shows in the result. Its base voltage is the one its ConnectivityNodes share through their VoltageLevel (directly or through a Bay); two different ones joined by a closed switch are refused. When the document ALSO has TopologicalNodes, the two views are compared and every disagreement is listed by name (a bus spanning two TopologicalNodes, a TopologicalNode split over two buses). Benchmarked on the ENTSO-E CGMES 2.4.15 conformity models (see the CIM1 notes): MiniGrid node-breaker, 103 ConnectivityNodes and 90 switches give 13 buses, one to one with its 13 TopologicalNodes; SmallGrid node-breaker, 1225 and 1107 give 118, one to one with its 118. Generator type (N254). The class of a machine's GeneratingUnit sets `CimGenerator.Type` (it used to be ignored, so every CIM machine was synchronous plant to the fault studies). The SV profile's `SvTapStep.position` is read (used when there is no SSH step, or always with `CimTapPositions.StateVariables`; a difference from the SSH step is listed), and a phase tap changer's `xMin` / `xMax` reactance curve is checked and, where it matters, listed as not represented. Equipment (N286, CIM2 2026-10). Shunt compensators (LinearShuntCompensator, NonlinearShuntCompensator) and EquivalentShunt are read with their sections in service (`CimNetwork.Shunts`); ExternalNetworkInjection, EquivalentInjection and the CGMES 3.0 PowerElectronicsConnection are generators (`CimGenerator.Class`); an AsynchronousMachine is a fixed P / Q load. See CimImporter.Equipment.cs for each mapping and its sources. Each used to be listed as equipment the importer does not represent. Fail loud (D-DOC-100). A present attribute that does not parse (a decimal comma, a unit suffix, an empty element, NaN) is refused naming the element, its mRID and the attribute; it used to become 0.0. Anything left out is listed in `CimNetwork.Diagnostics`. Network topology carries no timestamp, so no horizon guard applies here; a CIM state (SV profile) or measurement import - which is dated - would go through `Diagnostics.ForwardInferenceGuard` like every other dated ingester.
- [`IdTable`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/IO/Cim/CimImporter.cs#L440) (class): D-DOC-105 (NUM, 2026-10): the identifier table of one document. Every rdf:ID / rdf:about spelling that defines an object is recorded against the mRID it reduces to, so two DIFFERENT spellings that reduce to the same mRID (rdf:ID="a" and rdf:ID="_a") are refused instead of being merged into one object, and a reference (rdf:resource) whose spelling differs from the object it would land on is refused the same way.
- [`CimObject`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/IO/Cim/CimImporter.cs#L484) (class): One CIM object: its class (element local name), mRID and merged properties.
- [`EndRow`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/IO/Cim/CimImporter.cs#L1803) (record): One PowerTransformerEnd while the transformer's windings are gathered: its endNumber (null when the document gives none), document order, mRID, node (null when its terminal is not connected) and impedance.

See the `CimImporter` class summary for the rules; this file holds the code. Before N253 the node-breaker view made every ConnectivityNode its own bus and ignored the switches, so a substation drawn with breakers and disconnectors imported as a heap of separate islands (each switch was only listed). That was the largest gap in the CIM import.
- [`SwitchState`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/IO/Cim/CimImporter.Topology.cs#L26) (record): One switch as the topology processor sees it.

### src/GridSim.Core/IO/EstimateExportResiduals.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.IO`. 155 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/IO/EstimateExportResiduals.cs).

- [`EstimateExportResidualTable`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/IO/EstimateExportResiduals.cs#L14) (record): The residual table of one `gridsim-estimate-export/1` document, as read back for a corpus study.
- [`EstimateExportResiduals`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/IO/EstimateExportResiduals.cs#L30) (class): Reads the residual table back out of a `gridsim-estimate-export/1` document (written by `EstimateExport`, i.e. by `gridsim estimate`). This is the input of the `estimate-noise-floor` verb (R062): `NoiseFloorAnalysis` needs residuals from MANY estimates, grouped by measurement source tag and kind, and the export is the one place that carries the source tag next to each normalised residual (residuals.csv does not). Fail loud: a file that is not JSON, carries a different schema, lacks the residual table, or has a row with an unknown measurement kind throws `InvalidDataException` naming the file. Nothing is skipped silently. D-DOC-069 (October 2026, docs-session finding): a row's location is required too. A bus measurement must carry an integer `bus`, a branch measurement integer `from` and `to` and an `end` of "From" or "To" (the export always writes them). A missing one used to read as bus 0 (or the From end), so a damaged row was grouped and reported as a measurement at a bus that does not exist.

- [`FrequencyExport`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/IO/FrequencyExport.cs#L21) (class): The swing-solve analogue of `SolveExport`: serialises everything a frequency solve used and produced so a reviewer can hand-check `RoCoF = f0*deltaP/(2E)` the way they hand-check the Jacobian today. It records the run metadata, the split inertia budget (system (1/2)J*omega^2 + device (1/2)J*omega^2 -> the E that enters the swing equation), the fast-response power as a separate injection (never folded into E), every event, the full `DynamicsConfig`, the discrete recurrence in plain text, the headline metrics, and the whole trajectory. Deterministic given a deterministic solve.

### src/GridSim.Core/IO/H0StudyExport.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.IO`. 355 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/IO/H0StudyExport.cs).

- [`H0StudyMeta`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/IO/H0StudyExport.cs#L9) (record): Provenance for an H=0 counterfactual study export.
- [`H0StudyExport`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/IO/H0StudyExport.cs#L23) (class): Serialises an `H0StudyResult` to schema `gridsim-h0-study/1`: the passed baseline gate, the untransformed per-generator inertia table (so a sidecar can recompute E for any scale), the sweep axes, and every cell. The real-vs-synthetic separation is visible in the wire format and testable: `systemInertiaGvaS` / `deviceRotationalInertiaMwS` are REAL (1/2)Jw^2 that enter E; the grid-forming fleet's virtual inertia `virtualInertiaMwS` (Ev) is a SEPARATE column that enters only `effectiveFormingInertiaMwS` (E_real + Ev, NO floor), never the real budget. RoCoF and nadir fields are JSON `null` (an explicit "undefined" sentinel) on a forming-dependent cell rather than a huge finite E-floor artifact.
- [`H0Doc`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/IO/H0StudyExport.cs#L199) (class): The whole `gridsim-h0-study/1` document.

Wire format `gridsim-harmonics/1` (camelCase JSON, enums by name), the authoritative contract for which lives in GDA (`NetworkModel/HarmonicDataSchema.json`) so GDA or a third party can feed spectra the same way. Like every dated input, an optional `TakenUtc` stamp is checked against the historical horizon on load - measured harmonic data is a historical replay, never a nowcast (see `ForwardInferenceGuard`). Assumed-typical library spectra load tagged `ProvenanceTag.CuratedPlaceholder`; measured spectra load tagged `ProvenanceTag.Recorded` - the same solver either way.
- [`HarmonicSourceSetJsonContext`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/IO/HarmonicSourceSet.cs#L171) (class): Phase 0.1: the source-generated JSON metadata for a harmonic source set and every type it reaches, so it is read and written without runtime reflection (NativeAOT). ### src/GridSim.Core/IO/Json/CaseEditing/CaseCommitter.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.IO.Json.CaseEditing`. 139 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/IO/Json/CaseEditing/CaseCommitter.cs).

- [`CaseCommitter`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/IO/Json/CaseEditing/CaseCommitter.cs#L14) (class): Writes a session's dirty documents to disk as safely as plain files allow (SCHEMA-EDITOR-PLAN.md section 7, step 5; risk R5): first every new file is written beside its target as `<file>.gridsim-new`, flushed and read back to verify its bytes; only when ALL are verified is each renamed over its target. A failure while writing the new files leaves every target untouched; a failure while renaming rewrites the targets already replaced from the in-memory baselines and reports loudly. A multi-file save is still not atomic if the process dies mid-rename; the leftover `.gridsim-new` files are then reported the next time the case is opened. Files the case does not read are never opened.
- [`Target`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/IO/Json/CaseEditing/CaseCommitter.cs#L17) (record): One file to commit: the document and what its file must become (null = the file must not exist).

- [`CaseOps`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/IO/Json/CaseEditing/CaseOps.cs#L30) (class): The editing operations of the case editor at FILE level (the built GridModel is not the file: outputs are derived, lines divided by circuits, demand aggregated per bus; SCHEMA-EDITOR-PLAN.md section 2, fact 12). Every operation: parses typed input strictly, refuses anything that would introduce a schema error into the record or a dangling reference, then applies byte patches in ONE transaction (one undo step, possibly spanning files). Existing problems in a case are reported by Check and never block an unrelated edit: a record is refused only for errors the edit would ADD.

- [`CaseSession`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/IO/Json/CaseEditing/CaseSession.cs#L58) (class): An open case: its documents (the bytes are the model, SCHEMA-EDITOR-PLAN.md section 4), the files it does not read, what pre-flight found, and the undo / redo history. Every change goes through a `CaseTransaction`, which is atomic (a failure part-way puts every document back) and becomes ONE undo step even when it spans files (a cascading rename). Nothing here touches the disk after open; saving is `SaveGate` and `CaseCommitter`.
- [`CaseTransaction`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/IO/Json/CaseEditing/CaseSession.cs#L618) (class): An open, atomic change to a `CaseSession`. Each step applies at once (later steps see earlier ones); `Commit` turns them into one undo step; disposing an uncommitted transaction (an operation that failed part-way, or was refused after a first step) reverses every step, so the documents are exactly as before.

The `DynamicallyAccessedMembersAttribute` on `Type` tells the trimmer to keep exactly those members of every type stored here, so the reflection still finds them in a trimmed or AOT build, and the trim analyser can prove it (no warning is suppressed). A plain Type in a dictionary carries no such promise.
