A check runs the same stages over ALL files (not only dirty ones) and writes nothing.

### src/GridSim.Core/IO/Json/GeneratorCostFile.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.IO.Json`. 252 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/IO/Json/GeneratorCostFile.cs).

- [`GeneratorCostFile`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/IO/Json/GeneratorCostFile.cs#L36) (class): The JSON generator cost file (F19, October 2026): the JSON equivalent of MATPOWER's `mpc.gencost`, read by `dcopf --costs <file.json>` and laid onto a loaded case's generators (`Generator.Cost`). Layout (every key is checked; an unknown key is refused, so a misspelling cannot silently drop a cost): { "format": "gridsim-costs/1", "generators": [ { "index": 1, "model": "polynomial", "coefficients": [0.11, 5, 150] }, { "name": "G2", "model": "piecewiseLinear", "points": [[0, 0], [100, 2500], [200, 6000]], "startup": 0, "shutdown": 0 } ] } `index` is 1-based in the case's generator list in FILE order, out-of-service units included (the order of MATPOWER's mpc.gen rows, or of generation.json); `name` matches `Generator.Name` exactly and must name one unit. Give exactly one of them. A unit may be named once only. `polynomial`: `coefficients` highest order first, as MATPOWER writes them (c2 c1 c0 for a quadratic); `piecewiseLinear`: `points`, each [MW, cost per hour]. `startup` / `shutdown` are optional (default 0) and carried only (the single-period DC-OPF has no commitment decision). The file OVERLAYS the case: a unit it names takes the file's curve; a unit it does not name keeps the case's own curve (MATPOWER gencost), if any. Whether every in-service unit then has a curve is checked by the solve. Each curve is checked for what the DC-OPF can optimise (`GeneratorCostCurve.From`) when it is read, so a bad curve is refused here, naming the entry.

### src/GridSim.Core/IO/Json/InitMemberDefaults.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.IO.Json`. 211 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/IO/Json/InitMemberDefaults.cs).

- [`InitMemberDefaults`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/IO/Json/InitMemberDefaults.cs#L33) (class): UI programme Phase 0.1 (source-generated JSON): hand-written JSON metadata for the four types whose init-only properties have initialisers that a file may leave out: `MeasurementSet`, `HarmonicSourceSet`, `RtuPointMap` and `RtuPointBinding`. Why it exists. The System.Text.Json source generator cannot call an init accessor after construction, so it builds such a type in one object initializer that sets EVERY init-only property, and a member absent from the file is given default(T) there, overwriting the initialiser. A measurement set with no `baseMva` then loaded as 0 MVA instead of 100 MVA, an RTU binding with no `sigma` as 0 instead of 0.01, and so on (found by JsonSourceGenEquivalenceTests on docs/_captures/interpose/bad-datatype.json). It also changes the wording of some errors, because a member then fails as a constructor argument rather than as a property. What this does. Exactly what the reflection serializer (up to 2.0.48) did: make the object with its parameterless constructor, so every initialiser runs, then call the setter of each member the file holds, in file order, and no other. The setters are the properties' own init accessors, reached through `UnsafeAccessorAttribute` (resolved at compile time, supported by NativeAOT and trimming, no reflection); the reflection serializer called the same accessors. So an absent member keeps its initialiser, a member written as null is null, a wrong value fails with the property-path message, and a present member is the value read. Every property's JSON name, order, getter and type are as the generator describes them (CLR name, the options' naming policy applied), so the written bytes are unchanged too. Every other type still comes from the call site's generated context, which this resolver is chained in front of. JsonSourceGenEquivalenceTests pins all of this against the reflection path: the fixtures, a member-by-member absent and null test for each of these four types, and a scan that fails if any other loaded type gains an init-only property with an initialiser (it would then need describing here).
- [`Ms`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/IO/Json/InitMemberDefaults.cs#L103) (class): Declared class; see the source and member declarations for its role.

### src/GridSim.Core/IO/Json/JsonCaseWriter.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.IO.Json`. 291 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/IO/Json/JsonCaseWriter.cs).

- [`JsonCaseWriter`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/IO/Json/JsonCaseWriter.cs#L24) (class): Writes a `GridModel` as a JSON case folder that `JsonGridLoader.LoadDirectory` reads back to the same network (F24, October 2026: the `convert` verb's JSON side). What "the same" means here. Every number any power flow reads is written exactly (System.Text.Json writes the shortest form that reads back to the same double) and in the same ORDER: buses, generators (the whole fleet, out-of-service units included, F16) and branches stay in model order, because the solvers sum per-bus admittances and injections in that order and a different order can change the last bit. So the loaded model solves bit-identically to the model written. To make that possible the folder uses the F24 keys: `system.json "dispatch": false` (no capacity-based balance: the written outputs are the operating point), `generation.json` pMinMw / pMaxMw / qOutputMvar and the strings "Infinity" / "-Infinity" for unlimited limits, and every branch in `transmission.json` (a transformer carries tapRatio / phaseShiftDeg / isTransformer there, in place), never in transformer.json. What JSON v1 cannot carry is reported in the returned notes, never silently dropped: generator subtransient / negative-sequence reactances and gencost curves, transformer winding connections and neutral reactances, out-of-service branches, and the asset-dynamics and protection bundles.

The runtime options (naming, key case, null and number handling, indentation) are passed in by the call site.

The schema accepts `1.0` as an integer (JSON Schema does), but `JsonElement.GetInt32` throws a bare `FormatException` on it, which named no member and was not an `InvalidDataException`, so a file written by a tool that prints whole numbers as `1.0` validated and then failed to load. A fraction or a value beyond the int range (`3e9` also passes the schema) is refused with `InvalidDataException` naming the member.

### src/GridSim.Core/IO/Json/Lossless/JsonLiteral.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.IO.Json.Lossless`. 166 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/IO/Json/Lossless/JsonLiteral.cs).

- [`JsonLiteral`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/IO/Json/Lossless/JsonLiteral.cs#L19) (class): The JSON literals the case editor writes, and the strict input rules for what a user may type. Numbers (Q2, resolved to the plan's recommendation): a typed number is written as the SHORTEST literal that round-trips to the same double ("R" format, invariant culture), never the characters the user typed. So "1300.0", "1300" and "1.3e3" all become 1300, and reading the literal back (by System.Text.Json, as the loader does) gives exactly the same bits. Only finite numbers exist in JSON; NaN and infinities are refused. Strings: only '"', '\' and control characters (below U+0020) are escaped; every other character, including non-ASCII letters and '&', is written raw as UTF-8, so a name typed into an intl or uk file looks like its neighbours. An unpaired surrogate cannot be encoded as UTF-8 and is refused.

The span is half-open: `Start` is the first byte of the token (the quote of a string, the first digit or minus sign of a number, the opening brace or bracket of a container) and `End` is one past its last byte. Nothing here ever re-serialises: the bytes of the file are the model, and every edit is a patch of those bytes (see `JsonTextOps`).

### src/GridSim.Core/IO/Json/Lossless/JsonSourceText.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.IO.Json.Lossless`. 317 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/IO/Json/Lossless/JsonSourceText.cs).

- [`JsonSourceText`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/IO/Json/Lossless/JsonSourceText.cs#L27) (class): One JSON file held as its ORIGINAL bytes plus a span tree over them (the lossless text layer of the case editor, SCHEMA-EDITOR-PLAN.md section 4, "the bytes are the model"). Why not JsonNode or a DTO round trip: re-serialising loses what a hand-maintained case file is made of. Strings are re-escaped (the uk files' raw '&' becomes "&"; intl names with raw UTF-8 letters become "?" escapes), alignment and blank lines vanish, comments cannot be kept, and the bundled cases use at least four different layouts (hand-aligned uk, Python indent=2 gb-full, STJ-written gb-synthetic, Python intl with raw non-ASCII). So this class never writes JSON: it parses the bytes once with `Utf8JsonReader` (comments allowed and left in the bytes, trailing commas allowed), records where every value sits, and every change is a byte patch (`JsonTextEdit`, built by `JsonTextOps`) after which the file is parsed again. What is detected and kept: a UTF-8 byte-order mark, the newline style (the first newline in the file decides, "\r\n" or "\n"), and whether the file ends with a newline. None of them is ever changed by an edit; new text a patch inserts uses the detected newline. Duplicate member names are refused at parse time under `KeyComparer`: OrdinalIgnoreCase for a v1 case file (the loader matches keys case-insensitively, so "bus" and "Bus" in one record are the same member and the later would silently win) and Ordinal for a v2 document. Instances are immutable; a patch produces a new one.

### src/GridSim.Core/IO/Json/Lossless/JsonTextOps.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.IO.Json.Lossless`. 167 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/IO/Json/Lossless/JsonTextOps.cs).

- [`JsonTextOps`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/IO/Json/Lossless/JsonTextOps.cs#L17) (class): The structural edits of the lossless text layer. Each one looks at a `JsonSourceText` and returns the byte patches (`JsonTextEdit`) that make the change; nothing is applied here, so a caller can combine several, apply them in one go and keep the inverse for undo. Every edit touches only the bytes it must, and new text takes the layout of its neighbours (`JsonLayout`): a scalar edit replaces exactly the value token; a member or element insert goes after its predecessor (or before the first child) with the container's own separator: `, "k": v` on a one-line record, `,<newline><indent>"k": v` on a multi-line one; a removal takes the separator BEFORE the child (comma, whitespace and any comment), or the one after it for the first child, and an only child leaves an empty container; a copy duplicates the source's own bytes, so alignment inside the copied record survives.

- [`MachineDynamicsEntry`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/IO/Json/MachineDynamicsLoader.cs#L58) (record): One bound machine of a `gridsim-dynamics/2` file.
- [`MachineDynamicsSet`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/IO/Json/MachineDynamicsLoader.cs#L62) (class): A loaded `gridsim-dynamics/2` file, bound to one case's generators.
- [`MachineDynamicsLoader`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/IO/Json/MachineDynamicsLoader.cs#L142) (class): F23 (October 2026 review, stream B3; Ruling R1: Mark delegated EE calls 2026-10-04): reads a machine dynamic data file, `gridsim-dynamics/2` (`schemas/v2/dynamics.schema.json`), and turns it into the RMS study's per-machine `SubtransientInit.MachineData` (reactances, time constants, inertia, damping, saturation, leakage, governor) and exciters, replacing the CLI's synthetic GENROU defaults for every machine the file covers. JSON first; a PSS/E `.dyr` reader is a later step and would produce the same objects. Fit with the v2 family. The file carries its own templates in exactly the library template shape, so the same kind specs, closed unit vocabulary, value forms and provenance tags apply: `synchronousMachine` for the machine (whose `controllers` slots name its `exciter`, `pss` and `governor` templates), `exciter` (SEXS, IEEET1, EXAC1, ESAC1A or ESST4B), `pss` (PSS1A) and `governor` (TGOV1, IEEEG1, HYGOV, GAST). A `machines` list binds machine templates to the case's generators. Validation is fail loud and collects every problem: the document against `dynamics.schema.json`, then its templates as one library (`V2DocumentValidator`: kind specs, units, ranges, unique id@rev, controller targets); here: each binding names exactly one generator of the case; no generator is bound twice; a bound unit must be a synchronous machine (not converter plant, not power-flow-only); a bound machine template must be active; here: each model's REQUIRED parameters are present (a GENROU machine needs all six reactances and four time constants; SEXS, IEEET1, EXAC1, ESAC1A, ESST4B, PSS1A, TGOV1, IEEEG1, HYGOV and GAST need theirs, listed in `RequiredFor`) and no parameter is given that the model would ignore (another model's parameters, the lumped governor's, or machine parameters that belong to the case such as `unitTransformerXPu`): a silently ignored number is refused. Absent optional values take the documented defaults: damping 0, Xl 0 (the leakage-free saturation scale), no saturation, unlimited exciter / governor limits except the valve floor of 0, IEEEG1 fractions K1 = 1 and the rest 0, unlimited valve rates. An absent `inertiaH` takes the CASE's own H for that unit (case data, not a synthetic default), and the entry's notes say so.

- [`TopologyGroup`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/IO/Json/Overlay/SubstationTopology.cs#L112) (record): A set of sections that are electrically one node under the normal switch states.

- [`SubstationTopology`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/IO/Json/Overlay/SubstationTopology.cs#L143) (class): The topology of one substation record of the asset overlay (Phase 5c): its busbar sections, its switching devices, its bays, the nodes the sections form under the normal switch states, and the implied split / coupling warnings. Rules, in plain words: The substation's sections and devices are its DIRECT children (kinds busbarSection and switchingDevice), in overlay order. A device is an earth switch (joins nothing); else a coupler when its "to" is another section of this substation; else a feeder device when it names a line, transformer, generator or demand (the first such role written); else a spare. A device whose "from" is not a section of this substation is unplaced. Feeder devices on the same section naming the same circuit are one bay, in series. A circuit reached from two sections through closed bays joins those sections (a double busbar selector arrangement). Two sections are one node when a chain of closed couplers and closed bays joins them (union-find).
- [`UnionFind`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/IO/Json/Overlay/SubstationTopology.cs#L440) (class): Declared class; see the source and member declarations for its role.

### src/GridSim.Core/IO/Json/Overlay/V2AssetChecker.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.IO.Json.Overlay`. 260 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/IO/Json/Overlay/V2AssetChecker.cs).

- [`V2AssetChecker`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/IO/Json/Overlay/V2AssetChecker.cs#L34) (class): Phase 5a (2026-10-20): checks the asset overlay files of one case (`gridsim-assets/2`, schema `assets.schema.json`) as one set. Fail loud, and EVERY problem is listed, each naming the record id (in the message) and the field (in the JSON pointer); nothing stops at the first. Two layers, as `V2LibraryChecker` has: Each file against `assets.schema.json` (shape, scalar params, the one-member reference objects). When every file is schema-valid, the rules the schema subset cannot express, across all the files together: the kind is an asset overlay kind (`OverlayKindSet`; a template kind such as oltc is not); params against the kind spec (`KindSpecRegistry.CheckParams`, unchanged: unknown or missing parameter, type, unit, range), and no parameter or role written twice; ids unique across every file of the case; parent: it exists, the kind may have one and the parent is of one of the kind's parentKinds, a kind that requires a parent has one, and no parent chain loops; refs: every role is declared by the kind, with the target type the kind gives it, every required role is given, and every reference resolves: another record by id (of one of the role's recordKinds, never itself), and when the case is known (`targets` given) a bus by id and a line, transformer, generator or demand by a name exactly one element of that type carries. The second layer is skipped when the first finds anything: its checks assume the shape the schema guarantees. Without `targets` (a lone overlay file given to the `validate` verb), references to the case's elements are not resolved; the loader always resolves them.
- [`Indexed`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/IO/Json/Overlay/V2AssetChecker.cs#L42) (record): Declared record; see the source and member declarations for its role.

### src/GridSim.Core/IO/Json/Schema/JsonSchemaSubset.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.IO.Json.Schema`. 545 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/IO/Json/Schema/JsonSchemaSubset.cs).

- [`SchemaNode`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/IO/Json/Schema/JsonSchemaSubset.cs#L14) (record): One schema object inside a loaded schema set: the file it lives in, its JSON pointer inside that file, and the JSON object itself. Every place a schema may legally appear (a file root, a `$defs` entry, a `properties` entry, `items`, an object-valued `additionalProperties`, each `oneOf`/`anyOf` branch, and `if`/`then`/`else`) is registered as a node when the set loads, so a `$ref` may only ever land on a real schema, never on (say) an `enum` value.
- [`JsonSchemaSubset`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/IO/Json/Schema/JsonSchemaSubset.cs#L43) (class): A set of JSON Schema files (the GridSim v2 `schemas/v2/*.schema.json`) loaded under a deliberately small, hand-rolled subset of JSON Schema 2020-12. Zero dependencies: System.Text.Json only. Why a subset, and why so strict: the `.schema.json` files are the single source of truth for the v2 file formats and are actually enforced by `SchemaValidator`. A full JSON Schema implementation would be a large dependency; a partial one that silently ignored keywords it did not understand would be worse than none, because a schema author could write `"minLength": 1` and believe it was enforced. So loading REJECTS, loudly, any keyword outside `SupportedKeywords`, and checks the shape of every supported keyword too. What loading checks (every problem is collected, then one `InvalidDataException` lists them all, each naming the file and the JSON pointer): every file parses (comments and trailing commas allowed, duplicate member names refused); every schema object uses only supported keywords, each with a value of the right shape; `$schema` and `$id` appear only at a file root; `$schema` is the 2020-12 URI and `$id` equals the file name, so a cross-file `$ref` by file name is unambiguous; every `$ref` resolves, local (`#/$defs/x`) or cross-file (`common.schema.json#/$defs/quantity`), to a registered schema node; no `$ref` cycle exists that never consumes input (for example `a` refers to `b` which refers back to `a` at the same instance location): validation would recurse forever.

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.IO.Json.Schema`. 311 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/IO/Json/Schema/SchemaValidator.cs).

- [`SchemaError`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/IO/Json/Schema/SchemaValidator.cs#L11) (record): One validation problem: the JSON pointer (RFC 6901) of the offending value inside the document, and a plain-English message. `File` is set when the error came from a check that spans several documents (for example a controller reference into another library file), and left null otherwise.
- [`SchemaValidator`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/IO/Json/Schema/SchemaValidator.cs#L36) (class): Validates a JSON value against a schema in a loaded `JsonSchemaSubset`. It never stops at the first problem: every error is collected with the JSON pointer of the value it concerns, so an author fixing a file sees the whole list in one go. The caller fails loud on any error; `ValidateOrThrow` does that for you. Semantics follow JSON Schema 2020-12 for the supported keywords, with these points worth stating plainly: `integer` accepts any number with no fractional part (so `1.0` is an integer), as the spec says; `additionalProperties` sees only the `properties` written in the same schema object, never those of a sibling `$ref` or `if`/`then` (again as the spec says); `minimum`, `maximum`, `exclusiveMinimum` apply only to numbers, `minItems` only to arrays, `pattern` only to strings, and `properties`/`required`/`additionalProperties` only to objects: a value of another type is left to the `type` keyword to judge; `enum` and `const` compare with `JsonElement.DeepEquals` (numbers by value). Termination is guaranteed by the load-time cycle check in `JsonSchemaSubset`: any recursion that does not step into a child value is acyclic, and stepping into children is bounded by the document's depth.

What the load does, in order, failing loud with EVERY problem it finds (never only the first): The manifest and each network file are validated by `V2DocumentValidator` (case.schema.json and network.schema.json): the same checks the `validate` verb runs. A network file must lie inside the manifest's folder and may be listed once. Each import names a library file relative to the data root (the shipped `data` folder). The library files are validated together by `V2DocumentValidator` (library schema, kind specs, unique `id@rev`, controller references). Each import pattern must match at least one template: a pinned `id@rev`, an unpinned id (resolved to its highest revision in that file, and reported in the notes), an id prefix ending `.*`, or `gridsim.*`. Kind-spec enforcement: every local template's parameters are checked against its kind (`KindSpecRegistry.CheckParams`: unknown key, type, unit, range, null rules), as library templates are. A local template id may not shadow an imported id (any revision). Overrides: each names a template the case can see, sets at least one parameter, says why (schema) and acknowledges the shadowing (schema); a parameter may be overridden once. The merged parameters are checked against the kind again. An overridden value takes the override's provenance, or, when it gives none, CuratedPlaceholder with a [VERIFY] note quoting the reason (its source is not stated). Every template an element or binding names must resolve, be active (a placeholder is never bound) and be of a kind GridSim's asset classes model today (grid-following / grid-forming inverter, synchronous machine, oltc, line type, protection). The elements become the v1 DTOs and the model is built by `JsonGridLoader.Build`. Every active template of a modelled kind becomes an asset class (local templates first, in manifest order, then imported ones in import order). The class name of a local template `gridsim.local.NAME@1` is `NAME` (the v1 projection's rule, so a projected v1 case keeps its class names); every other template's class name is its `id@rev`. N234 (October 2026, LF2; JSON v2 phase P5 opened for fault sequence data ONLY, ruled by main under Mark's delegation): the fault sequence data reaches the model. A generator's `subtransientXdPu` and `negativeSeqXPu` become `Generator.SubtransientXdPu` / `Generator.NegativeSeqXPu`; a transformer's `windings`, `r0Pu` / `x0Pu` and `neutralXPu` become `Branch.FromWinding` / `Branch.ToWinding`, `Branch.R0` / `Branch.X0` and `Branch.FromNeutralXPu` / `Branch.ToNeutralXPu`. They are checked for consistency (see `CheckGeneratorSequence` / `CheckTransformerSequence`) and applied to the built model before dispatch; a case that gives none of them builds exactly as before (the same object), so every existing number is unchanged. v1 is unchanged: it has no keys for them, and the v1 writer reports them as content v1 cannot carry. Phase 5a (2026-10-20): the asset overlay. A manifest may list `assets` files (gridsim-assets/2). Step 1 checks them as one set (`V2AssetChecker`, run by `V2DocumentValidator`: schema, overlay kind specs, unique ids, parents, every reference resolving against the network files), so a bad overlay refuses the case with every problem listed. The overlay is read only AFTER the model is complete, into `V2CaseLoadResult.Overlay`, with the note "overlay: N records carried, not used by the solver". It never reaches `JsonGridLoader.Build`: a case with an overlay gives exactly the model it gives without one. A case without `assets` loads exactly as before (same model, same notes, Overlay null). v2 content the model cannot carry yet is REFUSED, naming it, never dropped: line and transformer `type`, an out-of-service line or transformer (later phases of the JSON v2 plan, held for Mark), a grid-code or solver profile (likewise), controller references and non-numeric parameters on a template that becomes an asset class (asset classes hold numbers only until templates are wired into their consumers). Descriptions are text and are accepted.

- [`V2CaseWriter`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/IO/Json/V2CaseWriter.cs#L67) (class): N299 (October 2026, LF5; Ruling R1: Mark delegated the EE / product calls 2026-10-04): writes a `GridModel` as a JSON v2 case, a `gridsim-case/2` manifest plus one `gridsim-network/2` file beside it, that `V2CaseLoader` reads back to the same network. It is the v2 twin of `JsonCaseWriter` (the v1 folder writer, F24) and exists so `gridsim convert` can round-trip a v2 case WITH its fault sequence data (N234: generator X''d / X2, transformer windings, zero-sequence impedance and neutral reactances), which JSON v1 cannot hold. What "the same" means. Every number a power flow reads is written exactly (System.Text.Json writes the shortest form that reads back to the same double) and in the same ORDER as the model: buses, generators (the whole fleet, out-of-service units included, F16), branches. The solvers sum per-bus admittances and injections in that order, so the loaded model solves bit-identically. As in the v1 writer, the manifest's system block says `"dispatch": false` (the written outputs are the operating point), generators carry pMinMw / pMaxMw / qOutputMvar and the strings "Infinity" / "-Infinity" for unlimited limits, and a bus's demand is one row holding its exact Pd / Qd. Branch order and the transformer array. The v2 loader builds every `lines` element first and every `transformers` element after them (across all network files), and only a `transformers` element can carry windings and neutral reactances. So a branch is written in place as a line (a transformer as a line with `isTransformer`, tapRatio and phaseShiftDeg, exactly as the v1 writer keeps transformers in transmission.json), except for the trailing run of branches from the first one carrying winding data: those are written as `transformers` elements, which keeps the model order. That covers every case the v2 loader itself builds (its transformers already come last). A branch whose winding data cannot be placed so without reordering the branches (it lies before a branch a transformer element cannot represent: a line, or a transformer with charging, a length, an equipment class, or zero-sequence data the v2 rules refuse) keeps its place as a line and its winding data is reported in the notes as not written; the power flow is unaffected either way. Byte-stable output. The files are a pure function of the model: members in a fixed order, numbers in their shortest round-trip form, two-space indentation, "\n" line ends on every OS and a final newline. Writing the loaded-back model again gives the same bytes (pinned by tests). The asset-dynamics and protection bundles (N321, LF7, October 2026; Ruling R1: Mark delegated the EE / product calls 2026-10-04). Every asset class of the model's bundles is written as a case-local template `gridsim.local.<class name>@1` (the v1 projection's convention, which the loader reads back to the class name itself), in library order; the binding rules as the manifest's `bindings`, in rule order; each element's class (generator, line or transformer `DynamicsClass`) as its `template`; and the placed protective devices as the network file's `protections`. The loader turns them back into the same library (same order, same kinds, modes, parameters and provenance), the same rules and the same devices, so asset-dynamics and protection runs on the written case are the runs on the model. The template kind is the loader's own table read backwards (`V2KindOf`: gridFollowingInverter, gridFormingInverter, oltc for a transformer class, lineType for a line class, protection). A class with no `_default` provenance gets the provenance v1 falls back to (`V2CaseLoader.V1Fallback`), because a v2 template requires one; the loader drops exactly that entry again. A bundle this writer cannot represent exactly is NOT written in part: when a class name cannot be a local template id (it must be dot-separated segments of letters, digits, '_' and '-'; a name that came from an imported template, `id@rev`, cannot), a class has a kind no template kind models, or a binding rule's match type is not a v2 match type even in lower case, nothing of the bundles is written and the notes say why, as before N321. What is not written is reported in the returned notes, never dropped silently, as the v1 writer does: a bundle that cannot be written (above) and the element template references that point into it, an element class that names no class of the bundle, MATPOWER cost curves, out-of-service branches (the v2 loader refuses them for now; D-DOC-162), names synthesised for unnamed elements (v2 requires names). A value v2 cannot hold (a non-finite number where a finite one is needed, a blank case name, a bus with no positive base voltage) is refused with `InvalidDataException`, naming it, and so is a model whose bundles contradict themselves (two different classes under one name, a binding rule or a placed device naming no class).
- [`Bundles`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/IO/Json/V2CaseWriter.cs#L568) (class): What one write carries of the bundles: the classes (library order), the binding rules (rule order, each with the class's own spelling) and the placed devices, plus the class lookup element references go through.

### src/GridSim.Core/IO/Matpower/MatpowerWriter.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.IO.Matpower`. 235 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/IO/Matpower/MatpowerWriter.cs).

- [`MatpowerWriteResult`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/IO/Matpower/MatpowerWriter.cs#L9) (record): The text of a written MATPOWER case and the notes on what MATPOWER's format could not carry.
- [`MatpowerWriter`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/IO/Matpower/MatpowerWriter.cs#L31) (class): Writes a `GridModel` as a MATPOWER `.m` case (version 2) that `MatpowerParser` reads back to the same network (F24, October 2026: the `convert` verb's MATPOWER side). Exactness. Every number is written in round-trip form ("R", invariant culture; unlimited limits as `Inf` / `-Inf`), and buses, generators and branches keep model order, so the parsed model solves bit-identically to the model written. Generators are the whole fleet (`GridModel.AllGenerators`), an out-of-service unit with status 0 (F16). A branch's ratio column is its tap when it is a transformer, else 0 (a plain line), so the parser reproduces `Branch.IsTransformer` and `Branch.TapRatio`. What MATPOWER cannot carry is listed in the notes and as comments in the file, never dropped silently: names, layout coordinates, ZIP loads, generator dynamics and fault data, the nominal frequency (a MATPOWER file has none; the parser assumes 50 Hz unless told), OLTCs, boundaries and the asset bundles. A bus with no per-bus voltage limits gets the operational band (0.94 / 1.06 pu) in VMAX / VMIN, the band GridSim's checks fall back to. The parsed case then CARRIES those per-bus limits, so it is judged exactly as before only while the caller's global band is the operational band; a check run with a different global band judges the reloaded case against 0.94 / 1.06 at those buses (the note says how many buses this affects). gencost is written when every generator carries a cost curve (and the reactive rows when every one carries a reactive curve); DC lines are written when given (they come from the parse result, not the model).

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.IO`. 57 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/IO/NeverOverwrite.cs).

Used by the interposer's window sinks: two windows can carry the same instant and sequence number (a replayed stream, a restarted listener writing into the same folder, a device clock that stands still), and before October 2026 the second silently overwrote the first, losing evidence. Here the requested name is tried first; if it is taken, "-dup1", "-dup2", ... is inserted before the extension until a free name is found. The file is opened with `FileMode.CreateNew`, so the check and the creation are one atomic step: a file appearing between them cannot be overwritten either.

### src/GridSim.Core/IO/Psse/PsseDyrRenewables.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.IO.Psse`. 341 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/IO/Psse/PsseDyrRenewables.cs).

- [`PsseDyrRenewables`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/IO/Psse/PsseDyrRenewables.cs#L26) (class): The PSS/E DYR records of the WECC second-generation renewable models that GridSim maps (WECC expansion), and their mapping onto `WeccPlant` parameter sets. Each model has a fixed record: its integer parameters (ICONs) then its real parameters (CONs), in the PSS/E order listed with it below. Names. The PSS/E library names (REGCA1, REECA1, ...; V34 and later), the PSS/E V33 user-model names (REGCAU1, REECAU1, ...) and the WECC / PowerWorld names (REGC_A, REEC_A, ...) all name the same model. A V33 user model may also be written as a `USRMDL` record (`IBUS 'USRMDL' ID 'REECCU1' IC IT NI NC NS NV ICONs CONs`); the six header integers are checked (NI and NC must match the model's counts) and dropped. Record order sources (WECC expansion, DECISIONS in the branch notes): REGCA1, REECA1 and REECB1 as the open-source ANDES PSS/E DYR map lists them, which agrees with the EPRI 3002006525 parameter lists and the reader's historical REGC_A value count (15); REECCU1 as the open-source OpenIPSL REECCU1 model declares its parameters (the one public source found; its order is flagged as single-source). Nothing is dropped silently. A value out of its range (a flag not in its set, a negative time constant, unordered breakpoints, ...) is listed by the parameter set's own check and the file is refused with every problem. REGC_A's Accel (a PSS/E network-solution acceleration factor, not a model dynamic) is range-checked and named in the notes: GridSim solves the converter / network fixed point to 1e-10 pu, so its answer does not depend on it.

### src/GridSim.Core/IO/RmsEventsExport.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.IO`. 305 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/IO/RmsEventsExport.cs).

- [`RmsEventsExport`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/IO/RmsEventsExport.cs#L31) (class): N363 (CF6): the export of one RMS scheduled-event study (`gridsim stability --rms --events ... --events-out <dir>`, `RmsTransientStability.StudyEvents`). Until N363 that run printed its verdict and nothing else: no result file and no trajectory. The export follows the stability / RMS conventions of the other exports: `rms-events-machines.csv`: every integrated machine's trajectory at every integration step, one row per (sample, machine): time, trace index, bus, rotor angle (rad, as integrated: no conversion), speed and the four flux states (pu), each double in its shortest round-trip form ("R", invariant culture), so the file holds exactly the bits the integrator produced. `rms-events-converters.csv` (only when the fleet has converter plant): each converter's terminal voltage, active and reactive power and current, and its dip-mode flag, at every step. `rms-events.json` (schema `Schema`): the summary a reader needs to interpret the CSVs: the case, step, duration, nominal frequency, every event in time order, the verdict, the converter-iteration count, the machine list (trace index, bus, island reference or not) and the provenance. Both CSVs start with the caller's header lines, each prefixed "# " (the CLI passes its run header: code version, machine, run description), followed by a "# provenance:" line. Provenance: a model trajectory, not a record, so `ProvenanceTag.Synthetic` (the tag every model-output export carries, as the frequency export does); `indicativeNote` says in words whether the machine data was synthesised (INDICATIVE) or came from a dynamics file. Pure formatting: nothing here changes or recomputes a number of the run.
- [`RmsSummaryDoc`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/IO/RmsEventsExport.cs#L226) (class): The whole RMS event-study summary document.

- [`VerdictRow`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/IO/RmsEventsExport.cs#L260) (class): { stayedInSynchronism, text }.
- [`MachineRow`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/IO/RmsEventsExport.cs#L267) (class): One machine trace: { trace, bus, islandReference }.

### src/GridSim.Core/IO/SchemaMember.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.IO`. 39 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/IO/SchemaMember.cs).

- [`SchemaMember`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/IO/SchemaMember.cs#L16) (class): D-DOC-070 (October 2026, docs-session finding): a versioned GridSim input file must SAY what it is. The readers of `gridsim-measurements/1` (`Estimation.MeasurementSet`), `gridsim-harmonics/1` (`HarmonicSourceSet`) and `gridsim-rtu-pointmap/1` (`Interpose.RtuPointMap`) bind the file onto a record whose `Schema` property DEFAULTS to the expected id, so a file with no `schema` member at all (an unrelated JSON file, a hand-written file that forgot it, another tool's output) passed the schema check and loaded as a set: an empty measurement set, harmonic set or point map, or worse, a half-understood one. The check below reads the raw document first and refuses a file without the member, naming the file and the id it must declare. A file WITH the member is checked by the reader as before (the exact id, ordinal). Every file GridSim writes carries the member, and so does every bundled fixture.

```csharp
// line 16

public static void Require(string json, string path, string expectedSchema, string what);
```

### src/GridSim.Core/IO/SmallSignalExport.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.IO`. 150 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/IO/SmallSignalExport.cs).

- [`SmallSignalExport`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/IO/SmallSignalExport.cs#L22) (class): Serialises a small-signal / modal analysis to the `gridsim-smallsignal/1` document: the real state matrix A (the eigen input), the kind-tagged states (so a downstream check can assert the real/synthetic separation survives the wire format), the synchronising matrix, and the computed eigenvalues, damping ratios, modal frequencies, participation factors and RHP count. The sidecar (`crossval_smallsignal.py`) recomputes the eigenvalues from `aMatrix` and diffs. N180 (October 2026, additive fields; every existing field and value is unchanged): the document now says whether the participation factors exist. `participationAvailable` is false when the modal decomposition found the state matrix defective (`ModalResult.ParticipationUnavailable`); the `participation` rows are then all-zero placeholders, NOT participation, and `participationUnavailableReason` carries the decomposition's own explanation. Before N180 the zeros were written with no flag, so a reader could not tell them from real participation. A caller that decides an exit code (the CLI) can also pass it, and it is written as `exitCode`, so the file carries the verdict its run ended with (omitted when not given).
- [`SmallSignalDoc`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/IO/SmallSignalExport.cs#L103) (class): The whole `gridsim-smallsignal/1` document.

- [`EigenvalueRow`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/IO/SmallSignalExport.cs#L135) (class): One eigenvalue: { re, im }.
- [`SmallSignalExportJsonContext`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/IO/SmallSignalExport.cs#L150) (class): Phase 0.1: the source-generated JSON metadata for the small-signal export document and every type it reaches, so it is read and written without runtime reflection (NativeAOT). Metadata mode only: the bytes come from the same converters the reflection path used, never from a separately generated fast path. The runtime options (naming, key case, null and number handling, indentation) are passed in by the call site.

### src/GridSim.Core/IO/SolveExport.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.IO`. 589 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/IO/SolveExport.cs).

- [`SolveExportMeta`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/IO/SolveExport.cs#L13) (record): Provenance for a solve export (filled by the caller - commit, timing, host).
- [`SolveExportEstimate`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/IO/SolveExport.cs#L27) (record): D-DOC-071 (October 2026, docs-session finding): what a solve-shaped document holds when it is an ESTIMATE projected into the solve-export shape (`estimate --export-solve`, `estimated-solve-export.json`), not a power-flow solve. The projection (`Estimation.EstimationResult.ToPowerFlowResult`) has no power-flow mismatch: it carries the estimator's last state update in the mismatch slot. With this passed, `SolveExport` writes that number under its own name, `maxStateUpdate`, writes no `maxMismatch`, and names the estimator's status.
- [`SolveExport`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/IO/SolveExport.cs#L53) (class): Serialises everything a solve computed to a single JSON document: the run metadata, the full network inputs, the solver's internal trace (admittance matrix, per-unit bus spec, per-iteration mismatch/correction/Jacobian, Q-limit switching) and the converged result with all line flows. Driven by `--enableExport`. Deterministic given a deterministic solve. "The full network inputs" means every field of the model's buses, generators and branches, plus the OLTCs, boundaries, base and nominal frequency (D-DOC-067, October 2026: the export used to write only the in-service generators and to drop the bus angles, layout coordinates and voltage limits, the generators' fault, converter, cost and dynamics-class fields, and the branches' length, equipment, short-term and emergency ratings and dynamics class, against this comment's claim). Buses carry their ZIP load model and their own voltage limits; generators the WHOLE fleet (`GridModel.AllGenerators`) with `inService` on each, so an out-of-service unit re-imports out of service; branches their service state, zero-sequence and winding data. Every one of these is read back by `SolveImport` (through `BridgeProtocol.BuildModel`), so an exported state re-imports as the same network: the same buses, generators and branches, field for field (R031; pinned by Doc8SolveExportRoundTripTests). What is NOT carried: the per-asset dynamics model and the protection bundle (the asset-classes.json / protections.json content; a generator or branch keeps the NAME of its dynamics class). The schema stays `gridsim-solve-export/1`: the fields are additive and optional, and a reader of an older document gets the model defaults (in service, constant power, no limits, no OLTCs). Units of `solve.busSpec` (D-DOC-068): `Pspec` and `Qspec` are per unit on the system base, `Qd`, `Qmin` and `Qmax` are MVAr, `Vg` and `VmInit` per unit, `VaInitDeg` degrees, on every engine (the backward/forward sweep used to write `Qd` in per unit while the Newton engines wrote MVAr).
- [`SolveDoc`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/IO/SolveExport.cs#L311) (class): The whole `gridsim-solve-export/1` document.
- [`ModelRow`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/IO/SolveExport.cs#L322) (class): The network the solve ran on.

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.IO`. 177 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/IO/SolveImport.cs).

- [`SolveSnapshot`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/IO/SolveImport.cs#L9) (record): A grid state reconstructed from a solve-export: the network and its solved result.
- [`SolveImport`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/IO/SolveImport.cs#L29) (class): The inverse of `SolveExport`: rebuilds a `GridModel` + `PowerFlowResult` from a `gridsim-solve-export/1` JSON document, so a pre-solved run can be loaded and rendered by the same views that drive the live solve. Deserialisation is case-insensitive (the export writes `meta` in PascalCase but `model`/`result` in camelCase) and tolerant of named float literals (Infinity limits). The model block is read by `BridgeProtocol.BuildModel`, the same reader the bridge topology uses, so every bus, generator (in service or not) and branch field the export writes round-trips, with the OLTCs and boundaries (R031, D-DOC-067). What the export does not carry (the asset dynamics model and the protection bundle) is absent from the re-imported model. The `solve` block (D-DOC-180, D-DOC-071): `status`, when present, is the solve's `PowerFlowStatus` and is restored (an older document without it reads Converged when it converged and MaxIterations when not). The block itself and its `converged` flag are required (GR-180): a document without them is refused rather than read as a converged solve. A document written for an ESTIMATE (`estimated-solve-export.json`) carries `maxStateUpdate` and no `maxMismatch`; the imported result then holds that state update in `PowerFlowResult.MaxMismatch`, exactly as the in-memory projection `EstimationResult.ToPowerFlowResult` does, so the round trip is exact.
- [`RootDto`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/IO/SolveImport.cs#L116) (class): Declared class; see the source and member declarations for its role.

### src/GridSim.Core/IO/Telemetry/Iec104Asdu.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.IO.Telemetry`. 197 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/IO/Telemetry/Iec104Asdu.cs).

- [`Iec104InfoObject`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/IO/Telemetry/Iec104Asdu.cs#L17) (record): One decoded IEC 60870-5 information object: its address (IOA), the measured value in the type's native scale, the quality descriptor octet (QDS/SIQ/BCR high nibble), and an optional CP56Time2a timestamp. Normalised values arrive as the raw fraction in [-1, +1); scaled/counter values as their integer magnitude; short-float values as the IEEE-754 quantity; single-point values as 0 or 1.
- [`Iec104Asdu`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/IO/Telemetry/Iec104Asdu.cs#L51) (record): The IEC 60870-5 ASDU object model - the application layer that sits inside the raw ASDU bytes the `Iec104Frame` (104/TCP) and IEC-101 (serial) framers hand up. It decodes the Data Unit Identifier (type id, variable structure qualifier, cause of transmission, common address) and the information objects for the common monitor-direction types. This is the piece the codec docstrings deferred as "a follow-up": with it, dated ASDUs become `Interpose.RtuPoint`s and, via the crosswalk, a horizon-guarded `Estimation.MeasurementSet`. Supported type ids: 1 M_SP_NA_1, 3 M_DP_NA_1, 9 M_ME_NA_1 (normalised), 11 M_ME_NB_1 (scaled), 13 M_ME_NC_1 (short float), 15 M_IT_NA_1 (counter), and their time-tagged CP56Time2a siblings 30 M_SP_TB_1, 31 M_DP_TB_1 (double point + CP56Time2a, the common timed breaker status; R089), 34 M_ME_TD_1, 35 M_ME_TE_1, 36 M_ME_TF_1, 37 M_IT_TB_1, and (N337) 5 M_ST_NA_1 / 32 M_ST_TB_1 step position and 7 M_BO_NA_1 / 33 M_BO_TB_1 bitstring of 32 bits. Unsupported / control types (commands, ...) decode to an empty object list; `IsSupportedType` lets a pipeline count them rather than drop them unseen (the interposer's `Iec104Protocol.UnsupportedTypeIds`). N337 (October 2026, ruled by main; this reverses R089's "5 / 32 and 7 / 33 stay unsupported"): the four status types are now decoded here, with exactly the element layouts of the explicit fail-loud codec `Iec104StatusTypes` (VTI + QDS, BSI + QDS; the layout [VERIFY] items are listed there, the IEC 60870-5-101 text is not on disk). A step position becomes a `RtuPointType.StepPosition` object whose value is the signed step (-64..+63) and whose `Iec104InfoObject.Transient` carries the VTI T bit; a bitstring becomes a `RtuPointType.Bitstring` object whose value is the 32-bit word as an unsigned integer (exact in a double). Both carry the full QDS octet as their quality, as the other QDS types do. The R089 pins that counted them unsupported move at the end pass.

- [`Iec104StepPosition`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/IO/Telemetry/Iec104StatusTypes.cs#L17) (record): One step position information object (IEC 60870-5-101 / -104 type 5 M_ST_NA_1 or 32 M_ST_TB_1).
- [`Iec104Bitstring`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/IO/Telemetry/Iec104StatusTypes.cs#L25) (record): One bitstring-of-32-bits information object (IEC 60870-5-101 / -104 type 7 M_BO_NA_1 or 33 M_BO_TB_1).
- [`Iec104StatusTypes`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/IO/Telemetry/Iec104StatusTypes.cs#L59) (class): N337 (October 2026): the IEC 60870-5-101 / -104 monitor-direction types that `Iec104Asdu` deliberately leaves undecoded, as a SEPARATE, explicit codec: type 5 M_ST_NA_1, step position information: element = VTI (1 octet) + QDS (1 octet); type 32 M_ST_TB_1, step position with CP56Time2a: VTI + QDS + 7-octet time tag; type 7 M_BO_NA_1, bitstring of 32 bits: element = BSI (4 octets) + QDS (1 octet); type 33 M_BO_TB_1, bitstring of 32 bits with CP56Time2a: BSI + QDS + 7-octet time tag. Relation to `Iec104Asdu.Parse`. This codec came first (CF1), behind R089's "counted unsupported" rule. Main then ruled (N337, CF2) that the four types are supported: `Iec104Asdu.Parse` now decodes them too, with the same element layouts, into `RtuPointType.StepPosition` and `RtuPointType.Bitstring` objects that the interposer turns into points. The difference that remains is strictness: the pipeline decoder is lenient like every other type (it ignores trailing octets and never throws on a field value), this codec refuses. A caller that wants the fail-loud reading, or needs to encode, uses this class. Source of the layouts and what is [VERIFY]. The IEC 60870-5-101 text is not on disk (docs/reference). The layouts are the published ones (IEC 60870-5-101 clause 7.3.1 type definitions, information elements VTI 7.2.6.5, BSI 7.2.6.13 and QDS 7.2.6.3; clause numbers from the 2003 edition as widely quoted, [VERIFY] against the text): VTI = value I7 in bits 0 to 6 (two's complement, -64..+63) and the transient bit T in bit 7; BSI = 32 bits sent as four octets, least significant octet first [VERIFY the bit numbering convention: this codec treats the first octet's bit 0 as bit 0 of `Iec104Bitstring.Bits`, the IEC 60870-5-4 convention for multi-octet fields]; QDS = OV bit 0, BL bit 4, SB bit 5, NT bit 6, IV bit 7, bits 1 to 3 reserved. The DUI is the 6-octet profile the rest of this build targets (type, VSQ, two-octet COT, two-octet common address), the IOA three octets. Fail loud. Unlike the lenient pipeline decoder, this codec refuses (ArgumentException) a wrong type id, an ASDU with no objects, a truncated element, trailing octets after the last element, and on encode any value out of its field's range, reserved quality bits, a time that is not UTC or not whole milliseconds, or an SQ = 1 run whose addresses are not consecutive. It never guesses.

- [`ModbusResponse`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/IO/Telemetry/ModbusFrame.cs#L13) (record): A decoded Modbus read-registers response.

A response carries no start address of its own, so pairing it with its request (by MBAP transaction id) is the only way to know the absolute register numbers.
- [`ModbusFrame`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/IO/Telemetry/ModbusFrame.cs#L33) (class): A codec for the Modbus TCP (MBAP) framing and the read-holding/input-registers response PDU - the application layer for the register-oriented half of the interposer. It decodes the 7-octet MBAP header (transaction id, protocol id, length, unit id) and, for a function-3/4 response, the byte-count + big-endian 16-bit register block. Modbus carries no native quality or time tag; the register scale to engineering units and the bus/branch binding are supplied by the crosswalk. Responses are address-less on the wire, so registers are keyed by their position in the response (the poll layout the crosswalk author configured).

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Layout`. 531 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Layout/GraphLayout.cs).

Power-system cases imported from IEEE / MATPOWER carry no geographic coordinates, so every `Bus` lands at the origin (X = Y = 0) and the WPF map draws them all stacked on one point. This class synthesises a readable, London-Underground-style planar layout from the pure graph topology (buses = nodes, in-service branches = edges) using a Fruchterman-Reingold force-directed algorithm, normalised into the 0..1 coordinate box the renderer expects. Everything here is deterministic: given the same model and seed it always produces byte-identical coordinates. No `System.Random` without a seed, no `System.DateTime`, no hashing of unordered collections. Pure Core - no UI dependencies.

### src/GridSim.Core/Layout/TopologyTiers.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Layout`. 160 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Layout/TopologyTiers.cs).

- [`TopologyTiers`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Layout/TopologyTiers.cs#L25) (class): Synthesises a voltage hierarchy from pure graph topology for coordinate-/voltage-less imported cases (IEEE / MATPOWER). A real grid layers 400/275 kV transmission -> 132 kV sub-transmission -> 33/11 kV distribution; a bare test case has no such tiers, so the map draws every bus identically and reads flat. This assigns each bus a display tier (0 = backbone, higher = deeper into distribution) from its structural role, so the renderer can size roundels, weight rings and reveal detail exactly as it does for the real GB network. This is a visualisation aid, not electrical data. The power-flow solve is untouched and tooltips keep each bus's true nominal kV. The tier only drives how the topology is drawn. Two structural signals, both deterministic: Radial feeders (a tree): the downstream subtree size rooted at the source. The trunk carries everything (large subtree) -> backbone; twigs carry little -> distribution. This is monotonic from source to leaf, i.e. a clean feeder hierarchy. Meshed networks: betweenness centrality (Brandes). The backbone that most shortest paths traverse scores highest -> transmission; the periphery -> distribution. Scores are ranked and bucketed into a pyramid (few backbone buses, many distribution buses), and the source bus is always pinned to the top tier.

### src/GridSim.Core/Licensing/BundledNetworks.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Licensing`. 371 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Licensing/BundledNetworks.cs).

- [`BundledNetworks`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Licensing/BundledNetworks.cs#L51) (class): The one list of Bundled Networks (LICENSE.md section 1): network models shipped with the Software that never count toward a tier's bus limit. The CLI (`Gated`), the WPF shell and the Web case catalogue all ask this class, so the three front-ends cannot disagree about the same shipped case. R002 (October 2026 review): the CLI kept its own list, which lacked `data/gb-full`, so on the free tier every CLI verb refused the shipped 3,539-bus GB case with exit 2 while the Web and WPF apps loaded it. What is bundled: the committed MATPOWER test library (IEEE / CIGRE / PEGASE cases under `data/matpower`), the UK boundary data (`data/uk`) and the shipped GB cases (`data/gb-synthetic`, `data/gb-reduced`, `data/gb-full`). Anything else, including a materialised `gda-*` model or a `gda-out/` tree, is a licensed user network. Built-in cases (`case9` and friends) never touch a file loader and are exempt by construction. N216 (October 2026): anchored to the shipped data root. A path is bundled only when it sits under one of `DataRoots`: the install's own `data/` folder (next to the running program, where every front-end's project file copies the shipped cases), plus, for a program run from a GridSim source checkout's build output, that checkout's `data/` folder. Before, ANY path with a `data/<bundled folder>` segment counted, wherever it sat (`C:\anything\data\uk\mycase.m`), so a user network escaped the tier's bus limit just by being copied under a folder of the right name. The shipped GB reduced model lives in `data/uk` (the case name `gb-reduced` is an alias of `uk`); the folder list used to name a `data/gb-reduced` folder that does not exist, and no longer does. N229 (October 2026, LF5; ruled: adopt with the F-release work): bundled by CONTENT, not location. N216's anchoring left one way round the tier limit: anyone who can write into the install's own `data/` folder (an administrator on a Program Files install, anyone on a portable unzip) could drop a large user network there, or edit a shipped case into one, and it counted as bundled. Now a path is bundled only when it is in place (the N216 rule) AND its content is what shipped: every data root carries a manifest, `ManifestFileName`, listing the line-ending-normalised SHA-256 (`ContentHash`) of every file under the `DataFolders` (generated by `tools/gen_bundled_manifest.py` from the source data, checked against it by a test, and copied next to the program with the data by every front end's project file). A FILE is bundled when the manifest lists its path under the root and its hash matches. A FOLDER (a JSON case folder, a whole data folder) is bundled when it holds at least one file and EVERY file in it, at any depth, is listed with a matching hash: a file added to a shipped folder or a shipped file edited makes the folder a user network. A root with no manifest (or a manifest that cannot be read) has nothing bundled under it: the licence check then runs, which is the safe direction. Line ends are normalised (CR LF read as LF) before hashing because a git checkout on Windows writes text files with CR LF and one on Linux with LF; the shipped bytes are otherwise compared exactly. Bug #178 (2026-11-01): every check hashes the files afresh. Hashes used to be cached for the life of the process by (path, size, last write time), so on a long-running web host a same-length swap with the write time put back reused the old "bundled" verdict; the shipped data is a few megabytes, so hashing it each time costs milliseconds. The callers also check BEFORE and AFTER they load a case and treat it as bundled only when both checks pass (see `BundledAcrossLoad{T}`), so a file swapped while it was being parsed is not exempt either. The explicit-roots overload `IsBundledPath(string?, IReadOnlyList{string})` keeps the location rule alone (its contract and tests are about the anchoring).

Signing now always writes the low-S form, so each key or anchor GridSim issues from here on has one canonical signature. Verification still accepts both forms (decision: keys already issued in the high-S form stay valid; refusing high-S waits for a revocation list and a reissue). Only P-256 signatures in the fixed-field (IEEE P1363, r || s) layout are normalised; anything else is returned unchanged.

Legacy keys with no major version read as 1.x, so they keep working on 1.x.

### src/GridSim.Core/Licensing/LicenceKey.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Licensing`. 244 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Licensing/LicenceKey.cs).

- [`LicenceKey`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Licensing/LicenceKey.cs#L29) (class): Encode and verify GridSim licence keys. A key is a single SSH-authorized-keys-style line: GSK1 <base64url-blob> The blob is `magic "GSK1" (4) | version (1) | payloadLen u16-BE (2) | payload | signature (64)`. The payload is canonical pipe-delimited UTF-8: `v2|email|org|type|buslimit|issuedDays|expiresDays|licenseId|majorVersion` (dates = days since 1970-01-01 UTC). F27 (Ruling R1, 2026-10-04): `majorVersion` is the GridSim major version the key was issued for (LICENSE.md section 1 sells a licence per major version). It sits inside the signed bytes, so it cannot be edited without breaking the signature. Every key this class encodes is a `v2` key. Keys issued before the binding are `v1` keys (the same fields without `majorVersion`); they are still read, as keys for `LegacyMajorVersion` (1), the line they were issued on, so existing keys keep working on 1.x. Whether a key's major version fits the running build is decided by `LicenceGate`, not here (as with expiry, parsing reports what the key says; the gate applies the policy). GridSim builds from before F27 read only `v1`: they refuse a `v2` key ("unsupported licence schema"), failing safe to the free tier. The signature is ECDSA P-256 / SHA-256 (IEEE-P1363, fixed 64 bytes) over every byte before it. The key is signed, not encrypted: the fields are inspectable, but cannot be altered or forged without the out-of-repo private key. That is the correct trust model for offline licensing of source-available software - you cannot hide fields in a binary the customer can read anyway.

This is safe to commit and ship: a public key can only verify a signature, never mint one. The matching private key is held offline by the maintainer (rotated 2026-10-25) and is never committed. To rotate keys: run the forge's `keygen` and paste the new public SPKI here. Keys signed by the old private key stop verifying, so rotate deliberately.

### src/GridSim.Core/Model/FuelTypes.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Model`. 302 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Model/FuelTypes.cs).

- [`FuelKind`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Model/FuelTypes.cs#L8) (enum): The fuel / technology kinds GridSim distinguishes. Every reader of a generator's free-text fuel or type string (the GDA importer, the presentation layers, the DC-OPF merit order, carbon tracing) classifies it into one of these through `FuelTypes.Classify`, and then looks its own values up by kind.
- [`FuelReader`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Model/FuelTypes.cs#L45) (enum): Which reader is classifying a string (see `FuelTypes`, "deferred keywords").
- [`FuelKeyword`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Model/FuelTypes.cs#L64) (record): One keyword (or phrase) of the taxonomy: the kind it selects and which readers read it.
- [`FuelTypes`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Model/FuelTypes.cs#L100) (class): THE fuel taxonomy (R305 rest, N020; October 2026). One ordered keyword list turns a generator's free-text fuel or type string into a `FuelKind`; each reader then looks up its own value by kind (the GDA importer its canonical type and inertia constant, the shells their name and colour, the DC-OPF its merit-order cost, carbon tracing its intensity). It replaces four separate keyword lists (GDA `FuelMap`, presentation `FuelTaxonomy`, `FuelCostPerMwh`, `FuelCarbon`) that disagreed with each other: the same plant could be OCGT to the importer and Gas to the shells ("gas turbine"), wind to the converter test and mid-merit "unknown" to the DC-OPF ("onshore", which data/uk and data/gb-synthetic use), hydro to the cost table ("hydrogen"). Matching (N020). The string is lower-cased and split into words at every character that is not a letter or digit (so "Pump-Storage", "pump_storage" and "Pump Storage" read alike). A keyword matches when each of its words is the START of consecutive words in the string: "hydro" matches "Hydroelectric" and "Run of river hydro"; "recip" matches "Reciprocating". It no longer matches inside a word, which the old substring test did: "Charcoal" was coal (H = 4 s), "Boiler" an oil engine (H = 1 s), "Microwave" wave power. The first keyword in list order that matches decides. On every type string in the bundled data and every fuel / plant-type string in the GDA lake the word rule gives the same kind as the old substring rule did (pinned by tests). Source. The kinds follow the GB fuel-type categories Elexon publishes for BM units and the BMRS generation-by-fuel-type data (`ElexonFuelType`: NUCLEAR, COAL, CCGT, OCGT, OIL, BIOMASS, NPSHYD, PS, WIND, INT*, OTHER), refined where the GB datasets GridSim imports are finer: the NESO TEC and Embedded Capacity registers' "Plant Type" (CCGT, CHP, Energy Storage System, PV Array, Wind Onshore, Tidal, Wave, Hydro, Biomass, Waste, Gas Reciprocating, Thermal), the NESO "Fuel Type" (Bioenergy, Hydrogen, Natural Gas, Oil) and the DNO LTDS "Fuel Type" columns (Photovoltaic, Onshore Wind, Offshore Wind, Small CHP, Waste incineration, Biomass & energy crops). Evidence on disk: the Elexon BM unit reference (Insights API `/reference/bmunits/all`, GDA lake copy `DataSources\Elexon\Reference\bmunits_all.json`, 3,025 units, 2026-10-02) carries exactly the fuel types listed on `ElexonFuelType`. [VERIFY]: Elexon's own fuel-type definitions document is not yet in docs/reference (recorded for S3 / N136). Deferred keywords. Where the old lists disagreed in a way that changes whether a plant is synchronous (or its inertia constant), the reader keeps its old reading until the frequency / inertia pass with Mark: the keyword lists only the readers that already read it that way (`FuelKeyword.Deferred` says why). For example the shells never knew "oil" (they showed oil plant as non-synchronous Other while the importer gave it H = 1 s as a reciprocating engine), so "oil" is skipped by the presentation reader for now.
