### src/GridSim.Core/Model/Model.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Model`. 1181 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Model/Model.cs).

- [`BusType`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Model/Model.cs#L4) (enum): How a bus behaves in the power-flow solve.
- [`Bus`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Model/Model.cs#L20) (record): A node in the network. Loads are folded onto the bus (MATPOWER convention): `Pd`/`Qd` are the demand here, in MW / MVAr. A shunt admittance (e.g. a capacitor bank) is given as `Gs`/`Bs`, the MW / MVAr it would draw at 1.0 p.u. voltage.
- [`ZipLoad`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Model/Model.cs#L45) (record): A ZIP (polynomial) load model: the bus load varies with voltage as a constant-impedance (Z), constant-current (I) and constant-power (P) blend. The drawn power is `P(V) = Pd * (Ap*V^2 + Bp*V + Cp)` and `Q(V) = Qd * (Aq*V^2 + Bq*V + Cq)` with V in p.u.; the coefficient triple in each row should sum to 1 so the model draws exactly `Bus.Pd` / `Bus.Qd` at nominal voltage. The default (0,0,1) is pure constant power - i.e. the historical behaviour - so a bus with no `Bus.Zip` solves bit-for-bit as before.
- [`Generator`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Model/Model.cs#L91) (record): A generator attached to a bus. `Vg` is its voltage setpoint (used at Slack and PV buses). `H` (inertia constant, MWs/MVA on `MBase`) is not used by the load flow; the frequency and dynamics studies read it, with system inertia = sum of H x MBase (`GridModel.SystemInertiaGvaS`). (D-DOC-207: this used to say it was "ready for the frequency-dynamics phase", which has long since been built.)
- [`GeneratorCostModel`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Model/Model.cs#L175) (enum): The two cost-curve forms of a MATPOWER `mpc.gencost` row (its MODEL column).
- [`GeneratorCost`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Model/Model.cs#L195) (record): A generator's cost curve, exactly as a MATPOWER `mpc.gencost` row gives it (F24, October 2026). It is parsed, kept on the `Generator` and written back out by the MATPOWER writer. Since F19 the costed DC-OPF reads the active-power curve (`Generator.Cost`) when asked to (`dcopf --costs`, `acopf --costs`, `DcOpfCosted`); without that option the DC-OPF and its loss loop use the fuel-type merit order as before. The reactive-power curve is carried only. D-DOC-207 (October 2026): this summary used to say no solver reads it.
- [`ConverterPlant`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Model/Model.cs#L207) (class): Classifies generator `Generator.Type` strings as converter-interfaced plant. Covers the type vocabularies used by the GDA builder (`wind-offshore`, `storage`...), the JSON cases (`wind_offshore`, `battery`...) and the synthetic GB. Pumped storage is a synchronous machine and is deliberately not a converter type.
- [`WindingConnection`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Model/Model.cs#L237) (enum): A transformer winding's connection, for building the zero-sequence network of a short-circuit study. Zero-sequence current can flow through a winding only if it has a path for the zero-sequence ampere-turns: a `Delta` winding blocks the external zero-sequence current (it circulates internally, providing the return for a grounded wye on the other side); a `WyeGrounded` winding passes it (through its earthed neutral); an `WyeUngrounded` winding blocks it (no neutral path). See `Iec60909.ZeroSequenceThevenin` for how the pair of windings maps to the terminal equivalent.
- [`Branch`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Model/Model.cs#L253) (record): A transmission line or transformer between two buses, as a standard pi-model: series impedance `R`+j`X` (p.u.) and total line charging susceptance `B` (p.u., split half to each end). `TapRatio` and `PhaseShiftDeg` model an off-nominal transformer (1.0 / 0 = a plain line).
- [`Oltc`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Model/Model.cs#L283) (record): An on-load tap changer: it nudges a transformer's tap up or down to hold a controlled bus near `TargetVpu`, the way a Grid Supply Point keeps the distribution-side voltage steady as demand swings. Referenced by the transformer's `Branch.Name`.
- [`MachineZeroSequence`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Model/Model.cs#L303) (record struct): A machine's zero-sequence impedance R0 + j X0 (pu on its MBase).
- [`ZeroSequenceMutual`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Model/Model.cs#L312) (record): Zero-sequence mutual coupling between two lines over their whole length (PSS/E sequence data): the model branches `BranchA` and `BranchB` (indices into `GridModel.Branches`, with their end buses as a check) and the mutual impedance R + jX (pu on the system base), signed for each branch's From-to-To direction. The zero-sequence network stamps each group of mutually coupled lines from the inverse of its impedance matrix.
- [`TransformerFlowKind`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Model/Model.cs#L315) (enum): What a transformer flow control regulates (PSS/E COD 2 and 3).
- [`TransformerFlowControl`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Model/Model.cs#L330) (record): A transformer that regulates the power flowing through it (PSS/E automatic control COD 2 and 3): the transformer (branch name and From bus), what it regulates, the band FlowMin..FlowMax (Mvar for reactive power, MW for active power, flowing into the transformer at its From end), and the range and step of what it moves: the tap ratio (pu of the branch tap) for reactive power, the phase shift angle (degrees) for active power. The steady-state solve's tap loop steps it one position per pass until the flow is in its band. Read with PSS/E tap control.
- [`LccMode`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Model/Model.cs#L339) (enum): How a two-terminal LCC link is ordered (PSS/E MDC): blocked, a power order or a current order.
- [`LccConverter`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Model/Model.cs#L352) (record): One converter of a two-terminal LCC link: its AC bus, bridges in series, angle limits (firing angle alpha for the rectifier, extinction angle gamma for the inverter, degrees), commutating resistance and reactance per bridge (ohms), the converter transformer's AC base voltage (kV), ratio and tap with its limits and step.
- [`LccDcLink`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Model/Model.cs#L359) (record): A two-terminal line-commutated HVDC link (PSS/E two-terminal DC record): its order, the DC line resistance (ohms), the scheduled compounded DC voltage (kV) the inverter holds, the voltage below which a power order becomes a current order (kV), the compounding resistance (ohms), the current margin (pu) and the two converters. Solved by `PowerFlow.LccDcLinks`.
- [`MtdcConverter`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Model/Model.cs#L365) (record): A converter of a multi-terminal DC link (PSS/E multi-terminal DC converter line): AC bus, bridges, angle limits (degrees), commutating resistance and reactance per bridge (ohms), transformer base kV, ratio, tap with limits and step, its set-point (kV for the voltage converter; otherwise MW or A, positive for a rectifier) and the DC bus it is on.
- [`MtdcDcBus`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Model/Model.cs#L370) (record): A DC bus of a multi-terminal DC link: its number, the AC bus of the converter on it (0 when none), its grounding resistance (ohms; 0 = not grounded) and name.
- [`MtdcDcLine`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Model/Model.cs#L373) (record): A DC line of a multi-terminal DC link between two of its DC buses, with its resistance (ohms).
- [`MtdcLink`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Model/Model.cs#L378) (record): A multi-terminal line-commutated DC link (PSS/E multi-terminal DC record): its order kind (power or current), the AC bus of the converter that holds the DC voltage, its converters, DC buses and DC lines. Solved by `PowerFlow.MtdcLinks`.
- [`VscDcControl`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Model/Model.cs#L382) (enum): What a VSC converter holds on its DC side (PSS/E TYPE).
- [`VscAcControl`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Model/Model.cs#L391) (enum): What a VSC converter holds on its AC side (PSS/E MODE).
- [`VscConverter`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Model/Model.cs#L402) (record): One converter of a VSC link (PSS/E VSC DC converter line): AC bus, controls and set-points, losses max(MINLOSS, ALOSS + BLOSS x Idc) (kW, Idc in A), MVA and AC current ratings (0 = none), the power weighting fraction and the reactive limits (Mvar).
- [`VscDcLink`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Model/Model.cs#L407) (record): A two-terminal VSC HVDC link (PSS/E VSC DC record): one converter holding the DC voltage, one an active power order, joined by a DC line of `ResistanceOhms`. Solved by `PowerFlow.VscDcLinks`.
- [`FactsMode`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Model/Model.cs#L410) (enum): How a FACTS device operates (from PSS/E's FACTS MODE and its terminal end bus).
- [`FactsDevice`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Model/Model.cs#L433) (record): A FACTS device (PSS/E FACTS device record, modes 1 to 3): its name and mode, sending end bus I and terminal end bus J (0 when none), the series element's set-points (PDES MW and QDES Mvar arriving at J), the shunt element's voltage set-point VSET (pu) and current rating SHMX (MVA at unity voltage; 0 = no shunt element), the bridge active power rating TRMX (MW), the terminal end voltage band VTMN..VTMX (pu), the series voltage rating VSMX (pu), the series current rating IMX (MVA at unity voltage; 0 = none). A bypassed series element (`FactsMode.Statcom` with a terminal end bus) and a constant series impedance (`FactsMode.SeriesImpedance`) are ordinary branches of the model between I and J (the PSS/E reader adds them); this record then describes the shunt element only. Solved with the AC power flow by `PowerFlow.FactsDevices`.
- [`StaticVarCompensator`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Model/Model.cs#L450) (record): A static var compensator (a PSS/E switched shunt with continuous voltage control, MODSW 2): its bus, the susceptance range (Mvar at 1 pu: every reactor block in, negative, to every capacitor block in), the initial susceptance BINIT (already in the bus shunt), the voltage band VSWLO..VSWHI (pu; equal for a fixed set-point) and a name. Solved with the AC power flow by `PowerFlow.FactsDevices`.
- [`InductionPowerCode`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Model/Model.cs#L459) (enum): What an induction machine's schedule PSET is (PSS/E PCODE).
- [`InductionMachine`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Model/Model.cs#L473) (record): An induction machine (PSS/E induction machine record, custom design with a single rotor cage): its bus and name, what its schedule is and the schedule (MW, positive for a motor), the machine base (MVA) and rated voltage (kV; 0 = the bus base) its impedances are on, and the equivalent circuit (pu): stator RA + j XA, magnetising j XM, rotor R1 + j X1. Solved with the AC power flow by `PowerFlow.InductionMachines`.
- [`ImpedanceCorrectionPoint`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Model/Model.cs#L478) (record struct): One point of an impedance correction table: at ratio (or phase shift angle) `T`, the transformer's nominal series impedance is multiplied by the complex factor `ReF` + j `ImF`.
- [`TapImpedanceCorrection`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Model/Model.cs#L486) (record): A transformer's series impedance as a function of its tap (PSS/E impedance correction tables, TAB): R + jX = (BaseR + j BaseX) x F(tap x `RatioScale`), F interpolated in `Points`. `RatioScale` turns the branch tap into the table's variable (a two-winding unit's branch tap is w1 / w2 and its table runs on w1, so the scale is w2; 1 for a three-winding unit's winding branch).
- [`BoundaryBranch`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Model/Model.cs#L514) (record): One branch's contribution to a boundary cut, with the sign that counts as "positive" transfer.
- [`Boundary`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Model/Model.cs#L522) (record): A transmission boundary (a cut across the network, like NESO's ETYS B6 Scotland-England) with a maximum permitted power transfer. The flow across it is the signed sum of the named branches' flows; comparing that to `LimitMw` is exactly the constraint NESO manages to keep the system secure.
- [`GridModel`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Model/Model.cs#L567) (class): A complete grid: a system base (MVA) plus its buses, generators and branches. All per-unit conversions in the solver are taken against `BaseMva`.
- [`ValidationSeverity`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Model/Model.cs#L1167) (enum): Severity of a `GridDiagnostic` from `GridModel.Validate`.
- [`GridDiagnostic`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Model/Model.cs#L1178) (record): One human-readable validation finding. `ToString` renders as "error: ..." / "warning: ...".

### src/GridSim.Core/Net/BridgeReconnectSupervisor.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Net`. 440 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Net/BridgeReconnectSupervisor.cs).

- [`BridgeReconnectState`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Net/BridgeReconnectSupervisor.cs#L6) (enum): Where a `BridgeReconnectSupervisor` is in its cycle.
- [`BridgeReconnectSchedule`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Net/BridgeReconnectSupervisor.cs#L31) (record): One reconnect attempt about to be made: its 1-based number, the bound (0 means no bound), the backoff delay the supervisor waits first (exactly `ResilienceOptions.BackoffDelay` of the attempt number) and why the connection is being re-established (the fault that lost it, or the failure of the previous attempt).
- [`BridgeReconnectAttempt`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Net/BridgeReconnectSupervisor.cs#L35) (record): The outcome of one reconnect attempt. `Failure` is null when the attempt re-established the connection.
- [`BridgeReconnectGiveUp`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Net/BridgeReconnectSupervisor.cs#L43) (record): The supervisor's final failure report: how many attempts were made in this outage, the last failure, and a plain-English reason that says why it stopped.
- [`BridgeReconnectSupervisor`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Net/BridgeReconnectSupervisor.cs#L80) (class): Supervised reconnect for a GDA bridge connection (NCSC CAF B5, "resilient networks and systems"; NIS principle 4). `ResilienceOptions` carries a bounded backoff schedule; this class is the part that drives it. What it does. The host tells it when the connection is lost (`ConnectionLost`, from the client's `GridBridgeClient.Faulted` event). It then works through the schedule: for attempt n (1-based) it waits exactly `ResilienceOptions.BackoffDelay`(n) and calls the host's reconnect function, which builds, wires and connects a FRESH client (a `GridBridgeClient` wraps one socket and cannot be reused). A reconnect that throws is a failed attempt and the next one is scheduled. A reconnect that returns is a success: the attempt count goes back to 0 and the state to `BridgeReconnectState.Connected`. When `ResilienceOptions.MaxReconnectAttempts` attempts have failed (0 means no bound) it stops and raises `GaveUp` exactly once. It never spins silently: every attempt is announced before it is made (`ReconnectScheduled`) and reported after (`AttemptCompleted`). The restriction invariant is untouched. The supervisor carries no timestamps and no data. Each attempt goes through the host's own connect path, so every reconnected stream is a new client with the same exact 169 h forward-inference guard and no clock-skew allowance (R276), streaming from the host's own historical anchor. A horizon rejection (`ForwardInferenceException`) is an invariant breach, not a dropped connection: it is NEVER retried automatically. The supervisor gives up at once and reports why, so the operator decides. Testable without sleeping. The wait is an injected function (default `Task.Delay(TimeSpan, CancellationToken)`), and the reconnect is an injected function, so a test can record every requested delay and script every outcome with no socket and no real time passing. Threading. Every member is thread-safe. The events are raised on the supervisor's own background task (or, for a horizon rejection, on the thread that called `ConnectionLost`); a UI host moves them onto its UI thread itself. A handler must not await `DisposeAsync` of the supervisor that raised it (it would wait for itself). The injected delay must honour its cancellation token, so `Stop` and `DisposeAsync` end a pending wait at once. One outage at a time. A second loss reported while the supervisor is already reconnecting does not start a second schedule. If it arrives while an attempt is in progress, that attempt is counted as failed (the new client lost its connection before the attempt finished), so a reconnect that "succeeds" into an already-dead stream is not reported as a success.

### src/GridSim.Core/Net/GridBridgeClient.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Net`. 701 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Net/GridBridgeClient.cs).

- [`GridBridgeClient`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Net/GridBridgeClient.cs#L27) (class): The GridSim side of the GDAGridSim bridge. Wraps a `ClientWebSocket` over one socket that carries both the state stream and request/response (forked from the RoCoF app's `server.py` transport). On connect it runs a receive loop that deserialises each `BridgeProtocol` message by its `type`: `topology` -> build and cache the `GridModel` (`Topology`), raise `TopologyReceived`. `state` -> call `ForwardInferenceGuard.RejectFuture` on the tick timestamp BEFORE building anything (a frame newer than the 169 h horizon is a protocol violation and is refused), then assemble a `SimFrame` against the cached topology and raise `FrameReceived`. `result` -> complete the pending `Query` the reply's `id` correlates to. `error` -> a stream-level failure (unknown case, rejected start, no settled data, ...): fire `Faulted` with the server's message so the stream death is visible rather than silently dropped. Pure Core (no UI/OS deps beyond the BCL socket), so the message pipeline is unit-testable without a live server.
- [`PendingQuery`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Net/GridBridgeClient.cs#L87) (record): Declared record; see the source and member declarations for its role.
- [`BridgeStreamException`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Net/GridBridgeClient.cs#L651) (class): A stream-level failure surfaced by `GridBridgeClient.Faulted`: either a `type:"error"` message from the server (unknown case, rejected start, no settled data, an internal stream exception) or a clean remote close while queries were still pending. Distinct from a query's own `verdict:"ERROR"`, which rides a normal `result`. (GS-H2 / GS-H4)
- [`BridgeMessageException`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Net/GridBridgeClient.cs#L661) (class): One bridge message that could not be read and was skipped, surfaced by `GridBridgeClient.MessageRejected`. The stream itself carries on. The original parse or validation failure is the `Exception.InnerException`. (R275)
- [`BridgeSubscriberException`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Net/GridBridgeClient.cs#L668) (class): GR-228: a GridSim subscriber threw while handling a good bridge message (see `GridBridgeClient.SubscriberFailed`).
- [`BridgeRequests`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Net/GridBridgeClient.cs#L679) (class): Phase 0.1 (source-generated JSON, NativeAOT): the fixed requests the client sends, as named records instead of anonymous objects. Each record has exactly the members the anonymous object had, in the same order, so under the bridge options (camelCase) it writes the same JSON: { "action": ..., "case": ..., ... }. Written through `BridgeProtocol.Json`.
- [`StartRequest`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Net/GridBridgeClient.cs#L682) (record): {action:"start", case, start, fps, source}: start streaming from a dated instant.
- [`StartLoopingRequest`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Net/GridBridgeClient.cs#L685) (record): {action:"start", case, start, fps, source, loop}: start a stored lake from a literal start token.
- [`StopRequest`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Net/GridBridgeClient.cs#L688) (record): {action:"stop"}.
- [`SetSpeedRequest`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Net/GridBridgeClient.cs#L691) (record): {action:"set_speed", fps}.
- [`SeekRequest`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Net/GridBridgeClient.cs#L694) (record): {action:"seek", start, source}.
- [`QueryRequest`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Net/GridBridgeClient.cs#L697) (record): {action:"query", op, id, at, params}: an on-demand query with a typed params object.

### src/GridSim.Core/Net/ResilienceOptions.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Net`. 80 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Net/ResilienceOptions.cs).

- [`ResilienceOptions`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Net/ResilienceOptions.cs#L21) (record): How a resident service rides out an interruption of the bridge stream (NCSC CAF B5, "resilient networks and systems"): the bounded reconnect schedule, and the resource limits a `GridBridgeClient` applies. A record so a deployment can tune it; the defaults are conservative. Determinism is the recovery ally. A reconnect does not reconstruct anything new: because a replay is bit-reproducible, a service that drops and reconnects re-runs the same window and gets the identical state, so there is no divergent recovered state to reconcile - and a divergence would itself be an incident signal. The backoff here only bounds how hard the client retries; it never changes what the stream is allowed to carry (still permitted-age or replay data, behind the forward-inference guard).

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Numerics`. 522 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Numerics/BoundedSimplex.cs).

- [`LpStatus`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Numerics/BoundedSimplex.cs#L4) (enum): The terminal state of a linear program solved by `BoundedSimplex`.
- [`BoundedSimplex`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Numerics/BoundedSimplex.cs#L30) (class): A dense two-phase primal simplex for the bounded-variable linear program minimise c.x subject to A x = b, lo <= x <= hi (any hi may be +inf). Variable bounds are handled natively (nonbasic variables rest at a finite bound; the ratio test includes each entering variable's own opposite bound, so a step can be a bound flip with no basis change) rather than expanded into extra rows - the standard bounded-variable method. Phase I drives a set of artificial variables to zero to find a feasible basis (rows are pre-negated so every initial residual is non-negative and the artificials form an identity basis); Phase II then optimises the real objective. The basis inverse is carried by eta updates and refactorised periodically to bound round-off. Dense and self-contained (no third-party solver), sized for the moderate LPs the analysis layer builds - e.g. the security-constrained DC-OPF (one balance row plus a thermal row per rated line).
- [`CapturedLp`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Numerics/BoundedSimplex.cs#L102) (record): N262: a record of one LP solved inside a `CaptureScope` (tests only): copies of the inputs as given, the options, and what the solve returned, including how many pivots the tie margin decided.

- [`DenseComplexLuSolver`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Numerics/ComplexLinearSolvers.cs#L12) (class): Dense complex LU with partial pivoting (Gaussian elimination on a `Complex[,]`). Exact in one pass, O(n^3) - the small-case path and the cross-check oracle the scalable solvers are validated against. It was lifted out of the fault study; the fault study now uses the factor-based path (FaultNetworkSystem), and `SolveDense` has no production caller: it is kept as the test oracle (GR-452).
- [`DenseComplexLu`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Numerics/ComplexLinearSolvers.cs#L250) (class): A dense complex LU factorization from `DenseComplexLuSolver.FactorDense`: multipliers below the diagonal, U on and above it, and the per-step pivot rows. Immutable; thread-safe to solve.
- [`RealExpandedComplexSolver`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Numerics/ComplexLinearSolvers.cs#L313) (class): Solves the complex system by the real 2n-expansion: writing A = G + jB, x = xr + j xi, b = br + j bi, the complex equation `(G+jB)(xr+jxi) = br+jbi` is the real system `[G -B; B G][xr; xi] = [br; bi]`. That 2n x 2n real system is assembled into a `CsrMatrix` and solved by the existing tuned real sparse-direct `SparseLu` - so this reuses the whole real linear-algebra stack (fill-reducing ordering, Gilbert-Peierls LU) and scales to gb-full (~3,500 buses), unlike the dense O(n^3) path. It is the scalable default for harmonic penetration.
- [`RealExpandedFactorization`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Numerics/ComplexLinearSolvers.cs#L365) (class): Declared class; see the source and member declarations for its role.
- [`Scratch`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Numerics/ComplexLinearSolvers.cs#L396) (class): Declared class; see the source and member declarations for its role.
- [`SparseComplexBiCgStabSolver`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Numerics/ComplexLinearSolvers.cs#L448) (class): Native complex sparse solve: Jacobi-preconditioned complex BiCGSTAB operating directly on the `ComplexCsr` in complex arithmetic (no real expansion, no dense fill) - a third, independent path that cross-validates the other two. Returns `null` on breakdown/stagnation/non-finite iterates or a missing/zero diagonal, so a caller can fall back to the direct solvers. All inner products are the CONJUGATED (Hermitian) form `(a, b) = sum conj(a_i) b_i`, the standard complex BiCGSTAB (van der Vorst). Before October 2026 (R278) rho, alpha's denominator and omega used the bilinear sum `a_i b_i`: with rhat = r0 the very first rho = sum r0_i^2 is exactly zero for a valid non-zero complex residual such as [1, i] (1 + i^2 = 0), so the solver "broke down" on a perfectly good system, and omega was not the residual-minimising step.

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Numerics`. 30 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Numerics/DeterministicParallel.cs).

- [`DeterministicParallel`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Numerics/DeterministicParallel.cs#L13) (class): A parallel loop over independent items whose failure is reported exactly as the serial loop would report it. `Parallel.For` wraps whatever the workers throw in an `AggregateException`, holding one or several inner exceptions in the order the workers happened to fail, so a caller that catches the specific exception type (a refused input, a singular network) missed it, and which of several errors surfaced depended on scheduling. Here each item's exception is kept by its index, and after the loop the one for the LOWEST failing index is rethrown as itself (with its original stack trace): the same exception, of the same type, whether the items ran in parallel or not.

### src/GridSim.Core/Numerics/DetMath.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Numerics`. 161 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Numerics/DetMath.cs).

- [`DetMath`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Numerics/DetMath.cs#L34) (class): D1 (October 2026, Mark's determinism rule 2026-10-04: "a 1 bit change is enough to break machine epsilon"): GridSim's own deterministic transcendental functions. Every numerical path in Core calls these instead of `Math`'s Sin / Cos / Tan / SinCos / Asin / Acos / Atan / Atan2 / Exp / Log / Log10 / Pow / Sinh / Cosh and instead of `Complex.Phase`, `Complex.FromPolarCoordinates`, `Complex.Sinh` and `Complex.Tanh`. Why: .NET does not implement those System.Math functions itself. At run time they call the C runtime maths library of the host operating system (the Microsoft C runtime on Windows, glibc's libm on Linux, Apple's libm on macOS), and those libraries round some results differently in the last binary place. GridSim's iterative solvers carry such a difference forward, so the same case gave the same answer to a few units in the last place, but not the same bits, on Linux and Windows (N175: 33 exact-bit pins differed on ubuntu-latest). What: a C# port of Sun's FDLIBM 5.3 (`Fdlibm`), the library Java's `StrictMath` is defined by. It is plain IEEE 754 double arithmetic and integer bit work, no fused multiply-add, no platform call, so it gives the same bits on every CPU tier (AVX-512, AVX2, no hardware intrinsics), every instruction set and every operating system. Accuracy is fdlibm's: under 1 ulp for every function (not always correctly rounded, which is irrelevant to determinism: what matters is that the rounding is the same everywhere). Proved bit for bit against Java 21 `StrictMath` by `FdlibmStrictMathVectorTests`. `Math.Sqrt`, `Math.Abs`, `Math.Floor`, `Math.Round`, `Math.CopySign`, `Math.ScaleB` and `Math.IEEERemainder` stay on System.Math: IEEE 754 defines each of them exactly (the square root is correctly rounded; the rest are exact), so every conforming implementation gives the same bits. `Complex`'s arithmetic, `Complex.Magnitude` and `Complex.Sqrt(Complex)` are managed .NET code built only from those, so they also stay. `DeterministicMathGuardTests` fails the build's test run if a System.Math / System.Numerics.Complex transcendental call appears anywhere in GridSim.Core outside this module.

### src/GridSim.Core/Numerics/Fdlibm.Trig.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Numerics`. 748 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Numerics/Fdlibm.Trig.cs).

- [`Fdlibm`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Numerics/Fdlibm.Trig.cs#L48) (class): D1 (October 2026, Mark's determinism rule 2026-10-04): a line-by-line C# port of Sun's FDLIBM 5.3, the "freely distributable libm" that Java's `StrictMath` is defined by. Every routine is plain IEEE 754 double arithmetic (add, subtract, multiply, divide, the correctly rounded square root) plus integer work on the two 32-bit halves of a double, with no fused multiply-add and no lookup of the operating system's maths library. IEEE 754 fixes the result of each of those operations to the bit, and .NET's JIT never fuses or reorders floating-point operations, so the same input gives the same output bits on every CPU (AVX-512, AVX2, no SIMD; x64 or ARM64) and every operating system (Windows, Linux, macOS). That is the property System.Math lacks: its transcendental functions call the C runtime of the host operating system, which rounds some results differently in the last place (N175). Structure: each fdlibm C function becomes one C# method with the same name in PascalCase, the same constants (written exactly as the C source writes them, with the source's hexadecimal bit patterns in the comments), the same statement order and the same branch structure, so the port can be read side by side with the C file it cites. Where C relies on a feature C# lacks (writing one 32-bit half of a double in place, unsigned / signed mixing, the `goto recompute` loop), the comment at that line says what was done. The public front door is `DetMath`; callers never use this class directly. Proof: `FdlibmStrictMathVectorTests` checks every routine bit for bit against outputs of Java 21's `StrictMath` (Eclipse Temurin 21.0.12.1) over special values and tens of thousands of arguments.

### src/GridSim.Core/Numerics/FrozenIntroSort.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Numerics`. 165 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Numerics/FrozenIntroSort.cs).

- [`FrozenIntroSort`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Numerics/FrozenIntroSort.cs#L21) (class): GridSim's own copy of the comparison sort the .NET 10 base class library uses for `Array.Sort(T[], Comparison<T>)` and `Array.Sort(T[], int, int, IComparer<T>)` (the introspective sort in `ArraySortHelper<T>`: insertion sort up to 16 elements, median-of-three quicksort, heapsort past the depth limit), reproduced step for step. Why it exists. An introsort is not stable: when the comparer calls two elements equal (two nodes of the same degree in the reverse Cuthill-McKee ordering), which one comes first is decided by the algorithm's internals and the input order. Those internals belong to the runtime, not to GridSim, so a .NET servicing or major release that tuned them (a different insertion-sort threshold, a different pivot rule) would change the RCM permutation, hence the pivot order of every sparse LU, hence the last bits of every sparse result, with no GridSim change at all. Copying the algorithm freezes it: the order is now GridSim's, the same on every runtime and OS, and on .NET 10 it is exactly the order `Array.Sort` gives today, so no result moves (`FrozenIntroSortTests` checks it against the runtime's sort over many tie-heavy inputs, and pins fixed permutations against a future change of either). Use it wherever a sort with ties feeds numerics. Prefer a total-order key (no ties) for new code; this is for keeping an established order bit-for-bit.

### src/GridSim.Core/Numerics/GeneralEigen.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Numerics`. 758 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Numerics/GeneralEigen.cs).

- [`GeneralEigen`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Numerics/GeneralEigen.cs#L30) (class): Eigenvalues and biorthonormal left/right eigenvectors of a small dense REAL, generally NON-SYMMETRIC matrix - the state matrix A of a small-signal (modal) stability problem, whose asymmetric structure (the ws*I angle-speed block vs the -M^-1 K speed-angle block, and the transfer-conductance asymmetry of the synchronising matrix K itself) puts it outside `SymmetricEigen`'s reach and forces complex eigenpairs. Self-contained (no BLAS/LAPACK); intended for the tens-of-states systems modal analysis forms, exactly as `SymmetricEigen` is scoped. Algorithm. Eigenvalues: Parlett-Reinsch balancing (a diagonal similarity that trims the norm), an upper-Hessenberg reduction by our own Householder reflectors (a similarity, so eigenvalues are preserved), then the Francis double-shift implicit-QR iteration (the EISPACK/Numerical-Recipes `hqr` real-Schur eigenvalue kernel: 1x1 blocks = real eigenvalues, 2x2 blocks = complex-conjugate pairs). Eigenvectors: inverse iteration on the ORIGINAL A with the computed eigenvalue as the shift gives the right vectors (no back-transform through balancing/Hessenberg); the left vectors are the rows of W = V^-1, so psi^H phi = 1 by construction. (R090: this doc used to say the left vectors came from inverse iteration on A^T; that path was never called and is removed.) Honesty / conditioning. Participation factors need biorthonormal left/right vectors (psi^H phi = 1). We form that scaling explicitly and then assert |psi^H phi| is not tiny: a defective or near-defective A (e.g. the undamped swing system's rigid-body COI Jordan block) has a singular right-eigenvector matrix, so the biorthonormal scaling does not exist. Rather than fabricate a participation vector, `Decompose` throws `DefectiveEigenproblemException` - the caller (modal analysis) is expected to deflate the known null space first and re-call on the non-defective electromechanical subspace.
- [`Eigenpair`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Numerics/GeneralEigen.cs#L86) (record struct): One eigenpair: the eigenvalue s = sigma + j*omega, the right eigenvector phi (`A phi = s phi`) and the left eigenvector psi (`psi^H A = s psi^H`), scaled so the pair is biorthonormal (`psi^H phi = 1`) - the normalisation participation factors require.
- [`DefectiveEigenproblemException`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Numerics/GeneralEigen.cs#L97) (class): Thrown when the right-eigenvector matrix is (numerically) singular, so biorthonormal left/right vectors do not exist - the matrix is defective / near-defective. Fail loud, never fabricate participation.

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Numerics`. 389 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Numerics/MilpBranchAndBound.cs).

An integer column's bounds are rounded inwards (ceiling of the lower, floor of the upper) before the search.
- [`MilpStatus`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Numerics/MilpBranchAndBound.cs#L11) (enum): How `MilpBranchAndBound.Solve` ended.
- [`MilpNodeOrder`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Numerics/MilpBranchAndBound.cs#L31) (enum): The order `MilpBranchAndBound` takes open nodes in.
- [`MilpOptions`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Numerics/MilpBranchAndBound.cs#L41) (record): The settings of `MilpBranchAndBound.Solve`.
- [`MilpResult`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Numerics/MilpBranchAndBound.cs#L71) (record): The result of `MilpBranchAndBound.Solve`. `X` is the incumbent (integer columns exactly whole, continuous columns from a final relaxation with the integers fixed), or null when there is none; `Objective` is c'x at it (NaN with no incumbent). `Bound` is the best proven lower bound (the incumbent's objective when the search finished, +inf when infeasible).
- [`MilpBranchAndBound`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Numerics/MilpBranchAndBound.cs#L108) (class): A mixed-integer linear programming solver: LP-based branch-and-bound over the sparse bounded simplex (`SparseBoundedSimplex`), built in Core with no dependencies (roadmap decision Q2), for the unit commitment of the roadmap (P0-3). Method. Each node is the LP relaxation with some integer columns' bounds tightened. A node whose relaxation is infeasible (proven by the simplex's phase one) is dropped; one whose bound cannot beat the incumbent by more than the gap is pruned; one whose integer columns are all whole (within `MilpOptions.IntegralityTolerance`) gives a candidate incumbent: the integer columns are rounded to the whole numbers, fixed, and the relaxation is solved once more for the continuous columns, so the reported point has exactly whole integer columns and an objective computed at them. Otherwise the node branches on its most fractional integer column (distance to the nearest whole number; ties: the lowest column) into x <= floor and x >= ceiling, the child on the nearer side created first. Why a simplex and not the interior point method. The first version solved the nodes with `SparseInteriorPointLp` (2.0.140), because it scales with the nonzeros. On unit commitment relaxations it failed three ways that branch-and-bound cannot live with: it has no certificate of infeasibility (it diverges or stalls, and on one infeasible child its Newton matrix even held an infinite entry, bug #33); it does not converge when the relaxation has no strictly interior point (the optimal duals are then unbounded), which branching creates by fixing columns and which a period whose demand equals the committed capacity creates by itself; and an exact-penalty elastic reformulation, which has an interior point by construction, diverged too. A simplex has none of these problems: phase one proves infeasibility, fixed columns and empty interiors are ordinary, and the answer is a vertex, so whole values come out whole. The nodes are re-solved from a cold start (no dual simplex warm start yet), which is the price. A node whose relaxation ends without an answer (its iteration cap or a singular basis) is never pruned or branched on a guess: the search stops with `MilpStatus.LpFailure`, naming the node. Determinism. One thread; nodes are numbered as created, best-bound ties go to the lower number, branching ties to the lower column, and each relaxation is itself bit-identical from run to run, so the whole search (node count, incumbent, bound) is bit-identical from run to run and on every CPU the LP is.
- [`Node`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Numerics/MilpBranchAndBound.cs#L345) (record struct): One node: its parent, the column it branched (-1 at the root), the side (Up: x >= Value; else x <= Value) and the parent's relaxation bound.
- [`OpenSet`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Numerics/MilpBranchAndBound.cs#L348) (class): The open nodes: a stack for depth-first, a (bound, id) ordered set for best-bound.

### src/GridSim.Core/Numerics/MultiCaseSparseLu.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Numerics`. 381 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Numerics/MultiCaseSparseLu.cs).

- [`MultiCaseSparseLu`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Numerics/MultiCaseSparseLu.cs#L23) (class): The multi-case sparse LU: up to `Lanes` matrices with one sparsity pattern (Monte Carlo cases, scenario sets, a run of measurement frames) factored and solved together, one case per SIMD lane, on a `SparseLuPlan` recorded from a full factorisation. Bit-identity. Each lane does exactly the arithmetic `SparseLuFactorization.Refactor` does for that case alone, operation for operation and in the same order (lane-wise IEEE subtraction, multiplication and division, never a fused multiply-add), and `SparseLuFactorization.Refactor` does exactly what a fresh `SparseLuFactorization.Factor` does. So every lane's L, U and solution hold the bits the single-case path gives. The lane-wise operations are IEEE operations on each element whether the hardware runs them as AVX2 / AVX-512 instructions or the runtime runs them element by element (hardware intrinsics off), so the bits do not depend on the CPU either. Fallback. A lane whose CSC pattern differs from the plan's (a value-dependent dropped zero), or whose pivot search picks a different row from the plan's at any column, cannot share the plan: that lane is factored alone by `SparseLuFactorization.Factor`, exactly as a single case would be (and reported in `Batch.SharedLanes`). A lane whose matrix is singular gives null, as the single path does.
- [`Batch`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Numerics/MultiCaseSparseLu.cs#L30) (class): A factored batch: the shared-plan lanes' interleaved L and U values, and each lane's own factorisation when it fell back (or null when its matrix is singular).
- [`SparseLuFamily`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Numerics/MultiCaseSparseLu.cs#L304) (class): A family of sparse matrices that share one CSR structure (a DC susceptance matrix under sampled branch reactances, a time-domain network matrix under varied parameters), factored `MultiCaseSparseLu.Lanes` at a time in the SIMD lanes of `MultiCaseSparseLu`. What each lane equals. The single-case path for a matrix `a` of the family is `SparseLu.Factor(CsrMatrix)`: the reverse Cuthill-McKee ordering of `a`'s CSR structure, then `SparseLu.FactorWithOrdering`. The ordering depends on the CSR structure alone, so every member of the family has the same ordering, computed here once from the template. Each lane is then the full factorisation with that ordering, bit for bit (replayed on the template's plan, or factored alone when it cannot share it), so a lane's L, U and solution are exactly what `SparseLu.Factor(CsrMatrix)` gives for that matrix. Fail loud. A matrix whose CSR structure differs from the template's is not a member of the family and is refused with `ArgumentException` (naming its position): grouping matrices by structure is the caller's job, and silently factoring a stranger with the family's ordering would not be the single-case path. Immutable after construction, so one instance may serve many threads at once.

GridSim's other "simplex" is the linear-programming `BoundedSimplex`; this is the unrelated nonlinear-optimisation simplex, used where a handful of physical constants are fitted to a measured curve (e.g. the frequency nadir/recovery constants). Deterministic by construction: the initial simplex is the seed plus a fixed per-coordinate step, no randomness, so a fit is reproducible. Bounds are enforced by the caller inside the objective (return a large finite penalty outside the feasible box) - the classic Nelder-Mead has no native bound handling and reflecting through a hard wall is less robust than penalising.

### src/GridSim.Core/Numerics/NumericTolerances.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Numerics`. 324 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Numerics/NumericTolerances.cs).

- [`NumericTolerances`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Numerics/NumericTolerances.cs#L19) (class): The ONE table of numerical tolerances shared by GridSim's linear solvers, eigen-solvers and state estimator backends (October 2026, workstream WS5: R034, R049, R141-R144, R181, R183, R184, R280, R301). Why one table. Before this table the same question ("is this pivot numerically zero?") was answered differently at every site: a relative 1e-12 in the dense LU, an absolute 1e-300 in the sparse LU, exact zero in the Householder QR and the ROCm LU, an absolute 1e-14 clamp in the complex LU, a relative 1e-14 in the dynamic-estimator inverse, and so on. Absolute floors are scale dependent: a per-unit Y-bus with entries of 1e3, or an estimator gain matrix with entries of 1e8, never trips them, so a matrix that is singular to working precision "factorised successfully" and returned garbage as an answer. Each constant below names ONE concept, says what it is relative to, and is the only place that value lives. Bit-identity. A pivot floor only decides what is DECLARED singular. It never enters the arithmetic of a non-singular solve, so moving a site onto this table leaves every converged answer on a non-singular system bit-for-bit unchanged; it changes only which near-singular systems are rejected.

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Numerics`. 90 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Numerics/SimdCapabilities.cs).

The kernels are written widest-first (`SimdTier.Avx512` down to `SimdTier.Scalar`); this type reports what the CPU offers so the app can (a) pick the widest path at runtime and (b) record which tier ran a benchmark. Detection is by `System.Runtime.Intrinsics` hardware flags, NOT by the dev machine's capabilities - a build produced on an AVX2 box still lights up the full 512-bit path on an AVX-512 EPYC because the choice is made at run time. This deliberately does not rely on `System.Numerics.Vector<T>`'s width: that type does not reliably widen to 512 bits on AVX-512 hardware, so it can silently cap at 256. The kernels use explicit `Vector512{T}`/`Vector256{T}`/`Vector128{T}` paths keyed off `Tier` instead.
- [`SimdTier`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Numerics/SimdCapabilities.cs#L80) (enum): The vector width a numeric kernel will execute at, chosen once at startup by `SimdCapabilities`.

### src/GridSim.Core/Numerics/SimdKernels.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Numerics`. 535 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Numerics/SimdKernels.cs).

- [`SimdKernels`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Numerics/SimdKernels.cs#L35) (class): The shared vectorised double primitives every dense kernel in the solver and estimator builds on: scaled-row subtract/add (the LU trailing-update and normal-equations rank-1 axpy) and dot products. Written widest-first with explicit `Vector512{T}`/`Vector256{T}`/ `Vector128{T}` paths selected once by `SimdCapabilities.Tier`, so the same source runs 8-wide on an AVX-512 EPYC, 4-wide on an AVX2 desktop, and falls back to scalar where neither is present. The core kernels take a `ref double` origin plus an element offset, so they drive both flat `double[]` vectors AND the contiguous row-major storage of `double[,]` matrices (pass `ref m[0,0]`): loads/stores use the safe `LoadUnsafe`/`StoreUnsafe` ref APIs, no `unsafe` block, so the pedantic build stays clean. `double[]` convenience overloads resolve the array's data reference for callers that hold a vector. Rounding contracts (D1, October 2026, Mark's determinism rule 2026-10-04: identical bits on every CPU tier and operating system): Bit-exact at every width: `SubtractScaledRow(double[],int,int,int,double)`, `AddScaledRow` with `fastFma=false` and the complex column updates do a separate multiply then add/subtract per lane, matching the scalar `x -= f*y` to the bit. `Dot` sums in one DEFINED order (four partial sums, then the tail) that every width reproduces exactly, so it gives the same bits on every CPU (it is not the left-to-right order of `DotExact`, which stays available). `SinCos(double[],double[],double[],int)` is the deterministic fdlibm sin/cos per element. Not for numerical paths: `AddScaledRow` with `fastFma=true` fuses multiply and add where the CPU has FMA, so its last bit depends on the CPU. No GridSim numerical path passes it (`DeterministicMathGuardTests` fails if one does); it remains only as the tested R102 kernel arm.

### src/GridSim.Core/Numerics/Sparse.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Numerics`. 405 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Numerics/Sparse.cs).

- [`CsrMatrix`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Numerics/Sparse.cs#L10) (class): A real sparse matrix in compressed-sparse-row (CSR) form, with columns sorted within each row and a cached pointer to each diagonal. Built from triplets (duplicates summed left to right in the order they were added, D-DOC-026). This is the storage the large-network power flow assembles its Jacobian into - each row touches only a handful of neighbours, so the dense O(n^2) cost collapses to O(nnz).
- [`Builder`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Numerics/Sparse.cs#L33) (class): Incremental builder: accumulate (row, col, value) triplets, then `Build`.
- [`ComplexCsr`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Numerics/Sparse.cs#L134) (class): A complex sparse matrix (real part G, imaginary part B sharing one pattern) - the network admittance matrix Y in sparse form. Built from branch stamps; lets the large-network power flow compute injections and assemble the Jacobian by walking each bus's handful of neighbours instead of a dense nxn sweep.
- [`Builder`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Numerics/Sparse.cs#L146) (class): Declared class; see the source and member declarations for its role.
- [`Ilu0`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Numerics/Sparse.cs#L232) (class): An ILU(0) factorisation - an incomplete LU that keeps the sparsity pattern of the original matrix (no fill). It's a cheap, effective preconditioner: applying it brings BiCGSTAB's effective system close to the identity, so the iterative solve converges in a handful of steps even on a stiff power-flow Jacobian.
- [`BiCgStab`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Numerics/Sparse.cs#L312) (class): Preconditioned BiCGSTAB - a Krylov iterative solver for the nonsymmetric linear systems a Newton step produces. With the `Ilu0` preconditioner it converges fast and uses only sparse mat-vecs, so it scales to tens of thousands of buses where a dense factorisation would not fit.

### src/GridSim.Core/Numerics/SparseBoundedSimplex.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Numerics`. 428 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Numerics/SparseBoundedSimplex.cs).

- [`SparseSimplexStatus`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Numerics/SparseBoundedSimplex.cs#L6) (enum): How `SparseBoundedSimplex.Solve` ended.
- [`SparseSimplexResult`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Numerics/SparseBoundedSimplex.cs#L23) (record): The result of `SparseBoundedSimplex.Solve`: the point (a vertex when optimal), the row duals y = B^-T c_B (the change of the optimal objective per unit of b), the objective c'x and the iterations of both phases. When the status is not Optimal the point is where the method stopped.
- [`SparseBoundedSimplex`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Numerics/SparseBoundedSimplex.cs#L55) (class): A sparse two-phase bounded-variable revised primal simplex for minimise c'x subject to A x = b, lo <= x <= hi (any bound may be infinite; a column with both infinite is free), on the sparse LU (`SparseLu`). It is the vertex solver the branch-and-bound needs (`MilpBranchAndBound`): unlike the interior point method it proves infeasibility (phase one), lands on a vertex (so whole values appear as whole), and has no difficulty with fixed columns or a feasible set with no interior point. `BoundedSimplex` (dense) is left untouched. Method. Nonbasic columns rest at a finite bound (a free one at 0). Phase one adds one artificial per row, signed so it starts at |b - A x_N| >= 0, and minimises their sum; a positive optimum (above 1000 times the feasibility tolerance times 1 + max |b|) proves infeasibility. Because a smaller positive optimum is passed on to phase two with the artificials pinned at zero while still basic, every Optimal point is checked before it is returned: each row's |A x - b| and each column's bounds within `BoundedSimplex`'s post-solve tolerance (1e-6 relative); a point that breaks either comes back `SparseSimplexStatus.NumericalFailure`, never Optimal. Artificials still basic at zero are pivoted out where a real column can take their place (a row where none can is redundant), and are then held at zero. Phase two minimises c'x. Each iteration prices every nonbasic column with y = B^-T c_B (Dantzig: the largest reduced cost of the right sign; ties to the lowest column), takes the entering column's B^-1 a_j, and the ratio test takes the first bound reached (the entering column's own opposite bound gives a bound flip with no basis change; ties to the lowest basis position; a pivot below 1e-9 in magnitude is never taken). After 50 consecutive degenerate steps the entering and leaving choices switch to Bland's rule (lowest index) until a step makes progress, which rules out cycling. Basis. B is factorised by the sparse LU (and B^T for the dual solves), and each basis change appends a product-form eta; the factors are rebuilt from scratch every 50 changes, which bounds the round-off the etas carry. The primal values of the basic columns are recomputed from the factors at each rebuild. Every loop runs in a fixed order, so the result is bit-identical from run to run.
- [`State`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Numerics/SparseBoundedSimplex.cs#L229) (class): The working state: columns, basis, values, bounds and the factorised basis with its eta file.

### src/GridSim.Core/Numerics/SparseInteriorPointLp.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Numerics`. 366 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Numerics/SparseInteriorPointLp.cs).

- [`SparseLpProblem`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Numerics/SparseInteriorPointLp.cs#L8) (record): A linear program for `SparseInteriorPointLp`: minimise c'x subject to A x = b and lo <= x <= hi. A is given as (row, column, value) entries (a repeated cell is summed in the order given); a bound may be infinite (lo = -inf, hi = +inf), and a variable with both bounds infinite is free.
- [`SparseLpStatus`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Numerics/SparseInteriorPointLp.cs#L12) (enum): How `SparseInteriorPointLp.Solve` ended.
- [`SparseLpResult`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Numerics/SparseInteriorPointLp.cs#L28) (record): The result of `SparseInteriorPointLp.Solve`: the primal point, the equality multipliers (y, the dual of A x = b: the change of the optimal objective per unit of b), the bound multipliers (both non-negative, zero on an infinite bound), the objective, the iterations and the final residuals. When `Status` is not `SparseLpStatus.Optimal` the numbers are where the method stopped, not an optimum.
- [`SparseInteriorPointLp`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Numerics/SparseInteriorPointLp.cs#L57) (class): A sparse linear programming solver: Mehrotra's predictor-corrector primal-dual interior point method for the bounded-variable LP (minimise c'x, A x = b, lo <= x <= hi), with each Newton step taken on the augmented system [-(D + rho I) A'; A delta I] solved by the sparse LU (`SparseLu`) after a power-of-two equilibration, and the factorisation reused for the corrector. It is the sparse counterpart of `BoundedSimplex` (dense, a vertex), left untouched: the interior point method scales with the nonzeros, not with rows x columns, which is what the unit commitment and security-constrained OPF of the roadmap need. Method. Bound slacks s = x - lo (finite lo) and t = hi - x (finite hi) with multipliers z and w; the residuals rb = A x - b, rc = c - A'y - z + w, rl = x - lo - s, ru = x + t - hi; the complementarity products s z and t w driven to sigma mu. Eliminating the slacks and bound multipliers leaves the augmented system in (dx, dy) with D = z / s + w / t. The predictor solves with sigma = 0; Mehrotra's sigma = (mu_aff / mu)^3 and the second-order term give the corrector. Steps keep 0.995 of the distance to the boundary, separately for the primal and the dual. rho = delta = 1e-9 regularise free variables and a rank-deficient A; the residuals are recomputed exactly every iteration, so they do not bias the converged point. Stopping. Optimal when the relative primal residual max(|rb|, |rl|, |ru|) / (1 + |b| + |bounds|), the relative dual residual |rc| / (1 + |c|) and the relative gap |c'x - (b'y + lo'z - hi'w)| / (1 + |c'x|) are all at or below the tolerance (1e-9 by default; infinity norms). Every loop runs in a fixed order, so the result is bit-identical from run to run.

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Numerics`. 249 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Numerics/SparseLu.cs).

Unlike an iterative method it solves Jx = b exactly in one pass regardless of how stiff the power-flow Jacobian is (short cables -> huge admittances -> ill-conditioning), which is what the full node-level GDA replica needs. The numeric factorisation lives in `SparseLuFactorization`: for each column, a single sparse triangular solve whose nonzero pattern is found by a depth-first reach, so the work tracks the true post-fill nonzeros. This replaced an older dynamic scheme built on `Dictionary<int,double>` rows that paid hash overhead and re-derived the sparsity pattern on every solve.

### src/GridSim.Core/Numerics/SparseLuFactorization.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Numerics`. 836 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Numerics/SparseLuFactorization.cs).

- [`SparseLuFactorization`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Numerics/SparseLuFactorization.cs#L23) (class): A sparse LU factorisation built by the Gilbert-Peierls left-looking algorithm with partial pivoting, over a fill-reducing column ordering (reverse Cuthill-McKee). Left-looking G-P is the standard fast sparse LU: column `k` is produced by a single sparse triangular solve `L z = A(:,q[k])`, whose nonzero pattern is found first by a depth-first reach over the graph of the already-built `L`. That keeps the arithmetic proportional to the true (post-fill) nonzeros instead of paying the dictionary/hash overhead and per-solve re-symbolic cost of the old dynamic scheme. The factorisation is `L U = P A Q`, where `Q` is the RCM column permutation (`_q`), `P` is the partial-pivoting row permutation (encoded by `_pinv`), `L` is unit lower-triangular and `U` upper-triangular. All factors are stored compressed-sparse-column (CSC); `L` keeps its unit diagonal as the first entry of each column, `U` keeps its pivot as the last.
- [`InverseQuadraticForm`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Numerics/SparseLuFactorization.cs#L414) (class): Evaluates q = sum_p hVal[p] * x[hCol[p]] where x = A^-1 h, for a SPARSE h, giving a result that is BIT-IDENTICAL to the reference hDense[hCol[p]] = hVal[p] (each p, in order); x = Solve(hDense); q = 0; q += hVal[p] * x[hCol[p]] (each p, in order) while doing only the work that can change the answer (October 2026 review, R010/R117). The reference paid, per call, two fresh n-length allocations, two full O(n) permutation passes and full forward and back sweeps over every column of L and U, whatever the sparsity of h. This evaluator differs from it in exactly four ways, each of which provably leaves every bit of q unchanged: No allocation. The caller supplies an all-zero workspace of length n, which is used in pivot-step space directly (h is scattered straight to its permuted slots) and cleared again before returning, so it is all +0 on exit. Forward solve starts at the first nonzero. In the reference, every pivot-step slot below the smallest slot h touches holds +0 and every column j there has multiplier x[j] = +0. An update x[i] -= l*(+0) leaves a nonzero x[i] unchanged and leaves a +0 at +0 (+0 - (+0) = +0 - (-0) = +0 in round-to-nearest), so skipping those columns - and any later column whose multiplier is exactly zero - is bit-identical, signed zeros included (in the forward sweep a zero slot is always +0: an exact cancellation a - a gives +0, never -0). Back solve stops at the last slot the caller reads. Back substitution finalises x[j] at column j and later (smaller) columns only update rows above themselves, so once column kMin (the smallest pivot-step slot of any requested entry) is done, every requested entry holds its final value. A column whose finalised x[j] is exactly zero is not propagated: its updates could only flip the sign of a zero entry. A zero requested entry - whatever its sign - contributes a product of +0 or -0 to q, and adding a signed zero to the accumulator never changes it (q starts at +0; a nonzero q is unchanged by +-0; +0 + (-0) = +0; and a sum that cancels exactly is +0, never -0). Only the requested entries are read back, through the inverse column permutation. Arguments 2 and 3 rely on every factor entry being finite (l*0 would be NaN for an infinite l). The constructor checks that once; if any factor entry is not finite the evaluator falls back to the full reference arithmetic for every call, so even that pathological case is reproduced exactly.

### src/GridSim.Core/Numerics/SparseLuPlan.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Numerics`. 62 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Numerics/SparseLuPlan.cs).

- [`SparseLuPlan`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Numerics/SparseLuPlan.cs#L13) (class): The symbolic record of one Gilbert-Peierls factorisation (`SparseLuFactorization.Factor` with a plan requested): the CSC pattern of A it factored, the column ordering, each column's nonzero reach in the topological order the depth-first search produced, each column's pivot row, and the patterns of L and U. A matrix with the same pattern can then be factored by `SparseLuFactorization.Refactor`, which replays exactly the arithmetic the full factorisation would do (same operations in the same order) without the depth-first searches, and returns null whenever the full factorisation would have chosen a different pivot, so the caller falls back to it. A factorisation from the plan is therefore bit-identical to a fresh one, or not produced at all. Immutable once built; one plan may serve many threads.

### src/GridSim.Core/Physics/Experimental/CarbonTracing.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Physics.Experimental`. 124 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Physics/Experimental/CarbonTracing.cs).

- [`CarbonTracing`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Physics/Experimental/CarbonTracing.cs#L22) (class): EXPERIMENTAL: carbon tracing - "what fuel is each load actually consuming?". It combines `PowerFlowTracing` (which generator's power reached which load) with a per-generator carbon intensity (from the generator's fuel type) to give each LOAD a physics-based carbon intensity: the CO2 attributable to the electricity that generator-tracing says actually flowed to it. Unlike a regional grid-average carbon-intensity figure, this is locational and flow-based - two loads on the same system get different intensities depending on which generators feed them. PROVENANCE: inherits the tracing convention (proportional sharing - an accounting method, not physical electron tracking) and adds per-fuel emission factors. The factors (`FuelCarbon`, tCO2/MWh) are the one carbon table's figures (`Presentation.CarbonIntensityTable`, the same figures the market and machine views use; R145 / R146); real per-plant/metered intensities would need a plant-emissions join (a GB-data follow-up). Generic IEEE cases carry no fuel type, so they fall back to the "other" default - the trace is then structurally correct but the intensities are placeholders. Opt-in via `experimental carbon`.
- [`LoadCarbon`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Physics/Experimental/CarbonTracing.cs#L26) (record): A load's traced carbon: its demand, the CO2 rate attributed to it, and the resulting intensity in grams of CO2 per kWh (the figure carbon-intensity dashboards quote).
- [`CarbonTraceResult`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Physics/Experimental/CarbonTracing.cs#L29) (record): The carbon trace of a solved state.

R145 / R146 (CF4): the free text is classified to Core's one fuel taxonomy (`Model.FuelTypes`, economics reader) and the figure is the ONE figure of that kind in `Presentation.CarbonIntensityTable` (NESO Carbon Intensity Regional Forecast Methodology, May 2024, Table 1, direct combustion; see the table for the source and the kind mapping). This class carries no figure of its own, so the carbon trace, the MACHINE tab and the MARKET tab give the same CO2 for the same dispatch. Non-combusting sources are zero, imports and grid infeeds zero (combustion outside the network), and an unknown / empty type takes the table's "Other" figure (`DefaultTPerMwh`), the case for fuel-less IEEE test systems.

### src/GridSim.Core/Physics/Experimental/ContinuumWaveModel.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Physics.Experimental`. 311 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Physics/Experimental/ContinuumWaveModel.cs).

- [`ContinuumWaveModel`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Physics/Experimental/ContinuumWaveModel.cs#L33) (class): EXPERIMENTAL: the grid as a continuum, viewed through the fluid analogy. The linearised swing dynamics on a network are a DAMPED WAVE EQUATION, M d2(delta)/dt2 + D d(delta)/dt + K_L delta = P_imbalance, structurally the skeleton of Navier-Stokes: an inertial term (M, the 1/2 J w^2 spinning-mass "density"), a dissipative term (D, the damping - the analogue of VISCOSITY, not of inertia), and a restoring term (the synchronising graph-Laplacian K_L, the "elastic"/pressure coupling). The rotor angle delta is the field variable; disturbances propagate across the network as electromechanical waves at a finite speed. The rigorous, checkable content is the MODAL structure: the eigenvalues of the generalised problem K_L phi = w^2 M phi are the network's normal modes - the inter-area electromechanical oscillations (typically 0.1-2 Hz) - and the null mode is the centre-of-inertia. PROVENANCE: this is a modelling LENS, not a claim that the grid satisfies Navier-Stokes. It is a LINEARISATION (small-signal, about the operating point) of the validated nonlinear swing model, so it captures oscillation frequencies and mode shapes, NOT large-disturbance transients, loss of synchronism, or turbulence (the grid's nonlinearity is the sin(delta_ij) pendulum coupling, a different beast from Navier-Stokes advection). It is opt-in (the `experimental wave` verb) and COLLAPSES to the established physics in its degenerate limit: a single machine against an infinite bus reproduces the analytic small-signal frequency w_n = sqrt(w_s P_s / 2H) that `ClassicalMultiMachine` is validated against. The intrinsic-vs-synthetic inertia separation is preserved (M is the real 1/2 J w^2 mass, never a df/dt emulation).
- [`WaveModes`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Physics/Experimental/ContinuumWaveModel.cs#L72) (record): The network's electromechanical normal modes.
- [`MachineAmplitude`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Physics/Experimental/ContinuumWaveModel.cs#L87) (record): One machine's participation in a mode: its signed amplitude (normalised so the largest is +/-1). Machines with opposite signs swing AGAINST each other in that mode - the "areas" the inter-area oscillation splits the system into.

A harmonic penetration state must satisfy the network equations at every order - the nodal current computed from the solved harmonic voltages, `Y(h) V(h)`, must equal the injected harmonic current `I(h)` at every bus. A residual is not an impossible state, it is a SOLVE/MODEL defect (a mis-built Y(h), a lost injection), which is what makes it a useful audit of the harmonic engine. PROVENANCE: EXPERIMENTAL and OFF BY DEFAULT - like `ReciprocityCheck` it is not one of the headline laws, not part of `PhysicsLaws.Audit`, and never in `PhysicsCheckRegistry.HardGateLaws`. It COLLAPSES to a trivial pass in the degenerate limit (a correctly-solved system balances to machine epsilon; an empty source set is vacuously balanced).

A passive network's driving-point impedance is positive-real: `Re(Z_grid(jw)) >= -tol` for all w. A converter that closes a loop with the grid may present a NON-passive band (a negative-real admittance around the PLL bandwidth); that is not itself an instability - the Nyquist test adjudicates it - so this is reported, never gated. Like `ReciprocityCheck` this is NOT one of the ten headline laws, is not part of `PhysicsLaws.Audit`, and is NEVER in the hard-gate set. It reports `LawStatus.Constitutive` when passivity holds and `LawStatus.Violated` (with the offending frequency) otherwise - a diagnostic, not an acceptance gate.

### src/GridSim.Core/Physics/Experimental/PowerFlowTracing.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Physics.Experimental`. 232 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Physics/Experimental/PowerFlowTracing.cs).

- [`PowerFlowTracing`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Physics/Experimental/PowerFlowTracing.cs#L27) (class): EXPERIMENTAL: power-flow tracing - "where did each generator's power actually go?" Given a SOLVED power flow, it decomposes every line flow and every load into the contributions of each generator, by Bialek's proportional-sharing method: at a node, the incoming power is assumed to distribute among the outflows in proportion to those outflows. That single assumption makes the trace a linear system - the upstream distribution matrix A_u built from the ACTUAL solved flow directions, solved once per generator against the sparse LU. The "path of least resistance" is not modelled here; it is already baked into the power-flow solution the trace reads. PROVENANCE: tracing is an accounting CONVENTION, not a physical fact - electrons are indistinguishable, so "which generator's power reached which load" has no unique answer at the electron level. Proportional sharing (Bialek 1996 / Kirschen) is the established, regulator-used convention for loss allocation and transmission-use pricing; this reproduces it. Honest scope: it is a GROSS trace (line flow taken at the sending end, so each generator is allocated its share of losses as the remainder) and assumes the solved flow graph is ACYCLIC in its flow directions (true for the dominant pattern of almost every solved case). GR-497: only a loop that makes A_u singular is detected and reported; a directed loop with gain below one leaves A_u regular, is traced, and still reads `FlowGraphAcyclic: true`, so that flag means "A_u was factorised". Opt-in via `experimental trace`; never on a validated path. With real GB generation/demand/flow data the trace becomes physically meaningful (which northern generator's output reached which southern load).
- [`GenLoadFlow`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Physics/Experimental/PowerFlowTracing.cs#L44) (record): How much of a generator's output (MW) reached a particular load bus.
