### src/GridSim.Core/Physics/Experimental/ReciprocityCheck.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Physics.Experimental`. 85 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Physics/Experimental/ReciprocityCheck.cs).

- [`ReciprocityCheck`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Physics/Experimental/ReciprocityCheck.cs#L24) (class): EXPERIMENTAL, opt-in physical-consistency law: network RECIPROCITY. A network built only from passive RLC elements (lines, shunts, in-phase transformers) has a SYMMETRIC bus admittance matrix, Y = Y^T - a consequence of Lorentz reciprocity. Phase-shifting transformers are the deliberate exception: they are non-reciprocal by design (Yft = -ys/conj(tap), Ytf = -ys/tap differ once the phase shift is non-zero), so the check EXCLUDES phase-shifted branches and asserts symmetry over the rest. A residual there is not a physics violation of the state - it is a MODEL/BUILD error (a mis-stamped branch, a duplicated one-directional entry), which is exactly what makes it a useful build-time audit. PROVENANCE: this law is EXPERIMENTAL and OFF BY DEFAULT. It is not one of the ten headline laws and is not part of `PhysicsLaws.Audit`; a caller opts in (the CLI's `physics-check --experimental`). It COLLAPSES to a trivial pass in its degenerate limit: a phase-shifter-free passive network is exactly reciprocal (residual at machine epsilon), and an empty/single-bus network is vacuously reciprocal. It never gates a state (a reciprocity break is a data defect, not an impossible state), so it is reported as Constitutive/Violated, never in `PhysicsCheckRegistry.HardGateLaws`.

A disturbance at one bus does not reach the whole system at once - it spreads as an electromechanical wave at a FINITE speed (the same physics `PropagationDelay` models and `ContinuumWaveModel` gives the frequency of). This computes, per bus, an amplitude and a PHASE DELAY (time-of-flight from the source), so an animator can draw `amplitude_i * cos(2*pi*f*t - phase_i)` and show the ripple travelling outward at the wave speed - the fluid analogy made visible. PROVENANCE: purely a visualisation aid derived from the linear wave model - the frequency is the dominant inter-area mode, the delay is distance / wave speed, and the amplitude decays with distance. It is not a transient simulation. Opt-in (the map's WAVE mode).

Where the laws answer "is this a valid network state at all?", these answer "does the state stay inside the equipment's capability?" - a generator cannot exceed its reactive capability, a branch cannot exceed its thermal rating, a bus voltage is bounded. A state can satisfy every physical law yet be operationally infeasible (a generator producing more VArs than it physically can), so the constrained estimator's acceptance gate checks BOTH: hard laws plus these capability limits. These are the same inequalities the Ring B active-set backend enforces at solve time; checking them here in the gate is the layered design's backstop and the definition the active-set is built to hold.

### src/GridSim.Core/Physics/PhysicsLaws.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Physics`. 526 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Physics/PhysicsLaws.cs).

- [`PhysicsLaws`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Physics/PhysicsLaws.cs#L30) (class): An independent audit of a solved grid state against the foundational physical laws of an AC power network - the physics-vocabulary sibling of the numeric residual check. Where the solver drives `S = V ? conj(Y V)` to zero by Newton iteration, this RE-DERIVES the same balances from the raw branch data by a different arithmetic path (per-branch pi-model flow accumulation, not the solver's nodal YV product) and reports each law's residual by name. It never re-runs the solver, so a pass is genuine corroboration that the solved voltages satisfy the network laws. GR-494, what is and is not independent: the nodal balance (KCL) and energy laws re-derive their sums by a different path and can fail on a solved state. Law 2 (branch flow) recomputes each branch's flow with the same admittance stamp as the result's line flows, so it can only detect a result that does not belong to the model passed in. Law 7 (KVL around a loop) holds by construction for a nodal-voltage solution (every voltage drop is a difference of two node voltages) and is reported Holds with residual 0 for every state. SCOPE, stated honestly. GridSim is a POSITIVE-SEQUENCE PHASOR model plus an electromechanical frequency layer. That makes the circuit laws (energy conservation, Ohm, Joule, KCL, KVL, complex power) and AC synchronism directly checkable. It is NOT an electromagnetic-field model, so Ampere's and Gauss's laws are not verifiable here - they are embodied CONSTITUTIVELY (a branch's series reactance X is the lumped consequence of Ampere's inductance; a transformer tap ratio and generator internal EMF are the lumped consequence of Faraday's induction) but there is no field to check. Those laws are reported as `LawStatus.Constitutive` / `LawStatus.NotModeled` rather than given a fabricated residual - the same discipline as the rest of the estate.
- [`SpecifiedInjections`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Physics/PhysicsLaws.cs#L523) (record): Bus injections a state is physically bound to, for `PhysicsLaws.AuditAgainst` (R011/R012). `PMw` and `QMvar` map a bus id to its specified net injection (generation minus demand, MW / MVAr); a bus absent from a map leaves that component unconstrained. `Basis` says in plain English where the values come from (for example "the estimator's zero-injection constraints") and is quoted in the law's detail line so a reader can see what KCL was checked against.

### src/GridSim.Core/Physics/SynchronismFromTrajectory.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Physics`. 119 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Physics/SynchronismFromTrajectory.cs).

- [`SynchronismFromTrajectory`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Physics/SynchronismFromTrajectory.cs#L27) (class): N246 (October 2026; Ruling R1, Mark delegated EE calls 2026-10-04): builds the law 9 input (`SynchronismSample`) from a dynamics run's OWN trajectory, so a fault study can score synchronism on what it actually integrated. The criterion. Loss of synchronism is any machine's rotor angle relative to the inertia-weighted centre of inertia (COI) exceeding 180 degrees at any sample of the run: the out-of-step criterion PSS/E and PowerFactory apply to a transient-stability run (an angle past 180 degrees from the COI means the machine has passed the unstable equilibrium of its swing). No frequency band is applied (a fault run's speed deviation is reported, not scored), so the sample is `SynchronismSample.AngleOnly`. Relation to the run's own verdict. `ClassicalMultiMachine.Simulate` declares a loss only past its pole-slip limit (default 2 pi, one full slip) from the same COI. Anything past 2 pi is past 180 degrees, so when the run says UNSTABLE law 9 is always Violated; between 180 and 360 degrees the law is Violated while the run's verdict still says it held. The CLI prints both and says which is which; neither replaces the other. Arithmetic. The COI is formed exactly as the integrator forms it (sum of H_i delta_i over sum of H_i, in machine order, at every stored sample), and the largest |delta_i - delta_COI| is taken over every sample and machine; radians to degrees is one multiplication by 180 / pi. No transcendental function is evaluated, so the figure is the same bits on every CPU and OS. A non-finite angle or speed anywhere gives a non-finite maximum, which the law scores as a loss.

### src/GridSim.Core/PowerFlow/BackwardForwardSweep.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.PowerFlow`. 692 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/PowerFlow/BackwardForwardSweep.cs).

- [`BackwardForwardSweep`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/PowerFlow/BackwardForwardSweep.cs#L50) (class): A backward/forward-sweep (BFS) power flow for radial and weakly-meshed distribution networks - the "two-way" solve. Transmission-oriented Newton-Raphson struggles on feeders with high R/X ratios; BFS is the standard, robust method there. Each iteration is two passes over the feeder tree: Backward (leaves -> source): sum the load/shunt currents up each branch to get the series current flowing through it. Forward (source -> leaves): apply the series voltage drop `V_child = V_parent/tau - Z*I` to update every bus voltage. It requires a single slack (the source) and a connected in-service topology. On top of the plain radial solve it adds two capabilities: Weakly-meshed feeders. A spanning tree is grown from the source and the few extra (non-tree) branches become breakpoints. A breakpoint (loop) impedance matrix is built once by superposition, and each sweep injects compensating breakpoint currents so the loops close (Shirmohammadi-style multi-port compensation). Only a small number of loops is accepted - a densely meshed transmission grid is still declined as "not a distribution feeder". PV / voltage-controlled buses. Non-slack generators that regulate voltage hold their bus at the setpoint |V| by a reactive-power correction each sweep, using the path reactance as the dV/dQ sensitivity, clamped to the generator's Q-limits (a PV bus that saturates reverts to PQ). It falls back to the old "not radial -> non-converged" report only when the network is genuinely unsupported: disconnected, no slack, or too meshed to be a weakly-meshed feeder. Non-regulating generators are constant-power (PQ) injections; loads are constant power unless the bus carries a voltage-dependent `ZipLoad`, which is drawn at the swept voltage exactly as the Newton solvers draw it (`LoadAtVoltage`). Line charging, bus shunts and transformer taps (including non-unity magnitude and phase shift) are carried through exactly: the forward voltage step and backward current accumulation apply the ideal-transformer ratio on the tapped branch (divide V / multiply I by the complex tap, per side), so the converged voltages solve the same MATPOWER pi+tap model the Newton solvers use - not just at unity tap. Same inputs, same physics as Newton (R036/R037, October 2026). The sweep is auto-selected for radial models (`SolverSelector`), so it must not quietly solve a different problem. It honours `PowerFlowOptions.FlatStart` (a warm start from the bus Vm/VaDeg otherwise, as Newton), `PowerFlowOptions.EnforceQLimits` (off = PV buses hold their setpoint with unlimited reactive output, as Newton), `PowerFlowOptions.Cancellation` (checked every sweep) and ZIP loads; it builds each tap with `AdmittanceStamp`'s rule (a ratio of 0 or below means 1, the phase shift is always kept); the slack is held at its own VaDeg; and every bus voltage setpoint comes from the one shared rule `VoltageSetpoint`. Its reactive-limit clamp is continuous (a saturated PV bus comes back off its limit as soon as the voltage allows), which is the converged state of Newton's outer loop with `PowerFlowOptions.RevertQLimits` on.
- [`BranchModel`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/PowerFlow/BackwardForwardSweep.cs#L486) (record struct): Declared record struct; see the source and member declarations for its role.

Each system in the batch is solved by a `CpuSparseLuSolver`, the canonical Newton step solver, so a batched contingency sweep is bit-identical to the one-at-a-time sweep BY CONSTRUCTION: the very same function runs on the very same inputs. Why a fresh `CpuSparseLuSolver` per system is still bit-identical: that solver only caches the reverse Cuthill-McKee ordering, and the ordering is a deterministic function of the sparsity pattern alone (no random tie-break, no state). Recomputing it gives the same permutation the cache would have held, so the factorisation and the solution are the same bits. The cache is a speed device, never a numerical one. The systems are independent, so they run in parallel across the batch; each writes only its own result slot, so the order in which they finish cannot change any number.

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.PowerFlow`. 55 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/PowerFlow/CpuSparseLuSolver.cs).

- [`CpuSparseLuSolver`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/PowerFlow/CpuSparseLuSolver.cs#L22) (class): The default CPU sparse linear solver: the direct sparse LU (reverse Cuthill-McKee ordering + partial pivoting). The reference the GPU sparse backend is validated against. It caches the fill-reducing ORDERING across calls whose matrix has the same sparsity pattern. A Newton-Raphson power flow solves the same-structured Jacobian once per iteration (only the values change as the voltages update); recomputing the RCM ordering - a sort/BFS over the graph - every iteration is pure repeated structural work. Because RCM is a deterministic function of the pattern, reusing it is bit-identical to recomputing it, so this is a speed-only change with no effect on the solution. The pattern is compared by content each call (O(n+nnz), cheap next to the ordering it saves); a changed structure (a Q-limit bus-type switch rebuilds the Jacobian pattern) transparently triggers a fresh ordering. Not thread-safe (GR-490): the cached ordering is per instance and unguarded, so one instance must not be called from two threads at once. Parallel sweeps give each worker its own solver (a factory), as the contingency screens do.

- [`DenseBatchSparseAdapter`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/PowerFlow/DenseBatchSparseAdapter.cs#L20) (class): R071 (October 2026): lets a dense `IBatchedLinearSolver` (the GPU batched LU, or its CPU reference `CpuBatchedLuSolver`) serve the batched contingency sweep, which posts SPARSE systems of possibly different sizes. The systems of one batch are grouped by size (in their batch order), each group is expanded to the dense row-major layout the dense seam takes, and the group is solved in one `SolveBatch` call. Not bit-identical to the canonical sweep, by design and on the record. The dense LU pivots column by column in natural order, the canonical sparse LU in reverse Cuthill-McKee order, so the two solutions of the same system agree to rounding, not to the bit. This adapter is therefore the GPU route into the sweep, held to the same standard as the single-system GPU solvers (which are outside the CPU bit-identity contract); the bit-identical batched route is `CpuBatchedSparseLuSolver`, the default of `Analysis.ContingencyAnalysis.ScreenBranchesBatched`.

### src/GridSim.Core/PowerFlow/DenseLuSolver.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.PowerFlow`. 157 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/PowerFlow/DenseLuSolver.cs).

- [`DenseLuSolver`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/PowerFlow/DenseLuSolver.cs#L24) (class): A dense LU solve (Gaussian elimination with partial pivoting) for Ax = b. Correct and obvious; plenty for the Jacobians of small networks. `SolveInPlace` works directly on the caller's arrays (no copies), so the Newton-Raphson loop can reuse one Jacobian/mismatch buffer set across iterations. When networks get large, a sparse factorisation or a GPU backend can replace this behind `ILinearSolver` without touching the solver. Performance: the elimination runs over a flat, row-major `double[]` copy of the matrix rather than the caller's `double[,]`. 1-D indexing lets the JIT drop the per-access 2-D bounds checks, keeps each row contiguous for cache locality, and lets the inner row-update vectorise through the bit-exact `GridSim.Core.Numerics.SimdKernels.SubtractScaledRow(ref double, int, ref double, int, int, double)` (a separate multiply and subtract per element at every vector width, never a fused multiply-add; D-DOC-209, October 2026: the old DenseLuKernels forwarder had no caller and is gone). The pivot search, row swaps and back substitution keep the original scalar order, so the result is bit-for-bit identical to the textbook version. The factored matrix is written back into `a` on completion, preserving the in-place contract.

### src/GridSim.Core/PowerFlow/DistributedSlackPowerFlow.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.PowerFlow`. 426 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/PowerFlow/DistributedSlackPowerFlow.cs).

- [`ParticipationRule`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/PowerFlow/DistributedSlackPowerFlow.cs#L7) (enum): F22: how the participation factors of a distributed slack are chosen.
- [`DistributedSlackPowerFlow`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/PowerFlow/DistributedSlackPowerFlow.cs#L49) (class): F22 (October 2026): the power flow with a DISTRIBUTED slack. The single-slack Newton engines hand the whole real- power balance (losses and any scheduling error) to the reference bus; here it is shared among the participating units by participation factors alpha_g (sum 1): every unit produces `Pg0_g + alpha_g K`, with K the system imbalance, and the reference bus keeps only the angle reference (its own units take their share like any other). Method: an outer loop around an unchanged engine, like the tap-changer loop (`OltcLoopPowerFlow`). Each pass allocates K to the units, solves with the engine, and reads the reference bus's solved generation: the excess e over its own units' allocation is the part of the imbalance the allocation did not yet cover, so `K += e`, until `|e| <= `ToleranceMw``. At the fixed point every unit produces exactly its allocation, which is the distributed-slack solution (the reference's P equation holds with its share, every other bus's by construction). Since K_new = demand + losses(K) - sum Pg0 and the losses change little with K, the loop contracts quickly (a few passes). Because each pass is an ordinary engine solve, the dense and sparse engines give the same bits here too: their per-solve results are bit-identical, and the loop's own arithmetic is the same plain sequence of operations in model order. Limits. A unit is held within [Pmin, Pmax]: a unit that would leave its range is fixed at the bound and the rest of its share goes to the others in proportion to their factors (water filling). When every participating unit is at a bound and imbalance remains, the result is NOT converged (status MaxIterations) and `LastNote` says why. Several reference buses (N120, October 2026). A model whose reference buses each sit in a separate network island (buses joined by in-service branches) is solved with one imbalance per island: K_i is shared among the participating units of island i only (the factors normalised within the island) and grown from island i's reference bus excess, and the loop settles when every island's excess is within `ToleranceMw`. That is the distributed slack of each island, exactly as if each were solved alone (the islands share no branch, so one island's dispatch cannot move another's balance). Units in an island with no reference bus take no share. Two reference buses in the SAME island stay refused: each fixes its own angle, so the power between them is set by the network, not by the dispatch, and no single imbalance can bring both to their allocations. A model with exactly one reference bus takes the original single-imbalance path, unchanged to the bit. Opt-in: nothing uses this wrapper unless asked (the CLI `pf --distributed-slack`); every existing solve is the single-slack engine, unchanged.

### src/GridSim.Core/PowerFlow/FactsDevices.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.PowerFlow`. 136 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/PowerFlow/FactsDevices.cs).

- [`FactsResult`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/PowerFlow/FactsDevices.cs#L15) (record): One FACTS device's solved state: the shunt element's reactive power into the sending end bus (Mvar) and its current (MVA at unity voltage), the series element's power delivered to the terminal end bus (MW, Mvar), the series voltage (pu) and current (MVA at unity voltage), the active power through the bridge from the shunt to the series element (MW), and whether the shunt current rating limited the shunt element (the sending end bus then not at VSET). Series quantities are 0 for a `FactsMode.Statcom`; for a `FactsMode.SeriesImpedance` device the series element is an ordinary branch and its flow is in the line flows.
- [`SvcState`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/PowerFlow/FactsDevices.cs#L20) (enum): Where a static var compensator ended: holding its bus voltage, fixed at its initial susceptance (its bus inside the band), or at either end of its range.
- [`SvcResult`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/PowerFlow/FactsDevices.cs#L34) (record): One static var compensator's solved state: its susceptance (Mvar at 1 pu), its reactive power at the solved voltage (Mvar), the set-point it held (pu; NaN when it stayed at BINIT) and its state.
- [`FactsDevices`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/PowerFlow/FactsDevices.cs#L80) (class): The steady-state models of FACTS devices (PSS/E FACTS device records, modes 1 to 3) and static var compensators (PSS/E switched shunts with continuous voltage control, MODSW 2), solved with the AC power flow inside `HvdcCoupling`. Shunt element (every mode, when SHMX is above 0). A voltage-controlling source at the sending end bus I holding VSET. Its current is limited to SHMX (MVA at unity voltage): after each AC solve the shunt element's apparent power S_sh is recomputed at the solved voltage, and when |S_sh| / |V_I| exceeds SHMX the source's reactive power is fixed at the largest the rating allows, sqrt((SHMX |V_I|)^2 - P_sh^2) with the sign of the excess, and the bus is released (PQ), the value re-taken at each solved voltage until it settles (a current-limited source). UPFC (MODE 1 with a terminal end bus J). The power-injection model of a lossless UPFC: the series element delivers PDES + j QDES to bus J; the active power it takes from bus I and the series converter's power both come through bus I, so bus I gives up exactly PDES of active power (the shunt converter supplies the bridge power), its reactive power is whatever holds VSET. With no series impedance, the series voltage is V_se = V_J - V_I and the series current I_se = conj(S_J / V_J); the series element draws S_I = V_I conj(I_se) from bus I, so the shunt converter supplies S_sh = S_device - (-S_I), the bridge power is Re(S_J - S_I). After the solve the terminal end voltage band VTMN..VTMX, the series voltage rating VSMX, the series current rating IMX (when above 0) and the bridge rating TRMX are checked: a device outside any of them makes the solve NOT converged, naming the device and the limit (PSS/E then changes the device's operating mode, which GridSim does not guess). A UPFC needs its shunt element (SHMX above 0). MODE 2 with a terminal end bus. The series element is bypassed: I and J are joined by a model branch of PSS/E's zero-impedance reactance, the shunt element a STATCOM at I. MODE 3. The series element is a model branch of impedance SET1 + j SET2 between I and J, with the shunt element at I. Both branches are added by the reader, so here those devices are their shunt elements. Static var compensator. A continuously variable susceptance between every reactor block in and every capacitor block in. Its initial susceptance BINIT is in the bus shunt. With VSWHI equal to VSWLO it holds that voltage; otherwise it stays at BINIT while its bus is inside VSWLO..VSWHI and holds the band edge its bus crossed (the continuous counterpart of MODSW 1's block switching; an interpretation, noted in the manual). While holding, it is a voltage-controlling source of reactive power B V^2 - BINIT V^2 at the set-point; when that would need more than its range, it is fixed at the end of the range (an exact susceptance, so its reactive power follows V^2), the bus released. Each controlled bus must have no generator and no VSC converter in voltage control and must not be the slack bus; such a model is refused, naming the device. Several FACTS shunt elements and static var compensators may hold one bus together: the bus is held at their common set-point and the reactive power its sources supply is shared by RMPCT (PSS/E's "percent of the total Mvar required to hold the voltage" each device contributes), each device's share being its RMPCT over the sum of the RMPCTs of the devices still holding the bus. A device whose share would pass its own limit (current rating, susceptance range) is fixed at that limit and the others share the rest; the reactive power still needed only grows for them, so a device fixed at a limit is never released. Conflicting set-points (two VSETs, or a compensator holding a band edge another device does not hold) are refused or fail loud: one bus cannot be held at two voltages.

### src/GridSim.Core/PowerFlow/FixedPatternSparseLuSolver.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.PowerFlow`. 108 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/PowerFlow/FixedPatternSparseLuSolver.cs).

- [`FixedPatternSparseLuSolver`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/PowerFlow/FixedPatternSparseLuSolver.cs#L32) (class): OPT-IN sparse LU solver that treats the matrix pattern as a function of the CSR STRUCTURE alone: every stored entry is part of the pattern, explicit zeros included. Because the pattern then never depends on the values, the symbolic work of one factorisation (each column's depth-first reach and pivot row, recorded as a `SparseLuPlan`) can be replayed for the next matrix of the same structure (`SparseLuFactorization.Refactor`): about half the cost of a full factorisation on the gb-full Jacobian. The pivot rule. A plan is reusable only while the pivot order holds. Plain partial pivoting moves pivots between Newton steps (8 to 12 columns of the case300 Jacobian at every step, near-ties broken by rounding), so this solver pivots by default with a diagonal preference (`DefaultDiagonalPreference`): a column's diagonal is its pivot whenever its magnitude is at least that fraction of the largest candidate's (threshold partial pivoting, as KLU and UMFPACK offer). On gb-full the plan is then replayed for 8 of the 11 Newton factorisations. Not the default, and not bit-identical to it. The default solver (`CpuSparseLuSolver`) drops exact-zero entries by value before factorising and uses plain partial pivoting. Keeping the zeros changes the order of the depth-first reach, and the diagonal preference changes pivots, so the last bits of every solve differ from the default path's (the two agree to rounding: gb-full voltages within 2.4e-13 pu). Nothing in GridSim uses this class unless a caller constructs it and passes it in (for example `new SparseNewtonRaphsonPowerFlow(new FixedPatternSparseLuSolver())`); every default result is untouched. What it does guarantee. Each solve is bit-identical to a FRESH structural factorisation of the same matrix (same ordering, zeros kept, same pivot rule, full Gilbert-Peierls): a replay produces exactly the fresh factorisation's L and U, or is refused when the pivot search would choose a different row, in which case the full factorisation runs and its plan replaces the old one. So the result never depends on which earlier matrices the instance has seen. Not thread-safe (it caches the ordering and plan per instance), like `CpuSparseLuSolver`.

### src/GridSim.Core/PowerFlow/HvdcCoupling.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.PowerFlow`. 738 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/PowerFlow/HvdcCoupling.cs).

- [`HvdcCoupling`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/PowerFlow/HvdcCoupling.cs#L32) (class): The AC power flow of a model with HVDC links (`GridModel.LccLinks`, `GridModel.VscLinks`): the AC solve and the links' DC solves alternate until the AC solve's inputs stop changing. Each LCC converter is a constant-power load at its bus (`LccDcLinks.SolveLink` from the last AC voltages). Each VSC converter injects its active power (`VscDcLinks.SolveDc`, with any capability reduction of its order); a MODE 1 converter is a voltage-controlling source with its reactive limits (a power-flow-only unit, the bus voltage-controlled), a MODE 2 converter a constant-power injection at its power factor. After each AC solve every VSC converter's apparent power is checked against its rating at the solved voltage and reduced by its weighting (`VscDcLinks.Reduce`) when it exceeds it; reductions only ever tighten. FACTS devices and static var compensators (`FactsDevices`): each shunt element or compensator is a voltage-controlling source at its bus; after each AC solve a shunt element over its current rating is fixed at the reactive power the rating allows (re-taken at each solved voltage until it settles), a compensator whose bus has left its band starts holding the band edge, and one beyond its susceptance range is fixed at the end of the range. A UPFC's series element is the injections PDES + j QDES at its terminal end bus and -PDES at its sending end bus. Induction machines (`InductionMachines`): each a constant-power load at its bus at the slip that meets its schedule at the last AC voltage. Settled when the LCC and induction machine states repeat within 1e-9 (1 + |P|) and no VSC, FACTS or compensator input changed; at most `LccDcLinks.MaxCouplingIterations` AC solves. Failures (no DC state meets an order, the AC solve did not converge, no settling) return the last result marked NOT converged with the reason in `PowerFlowResult.LccNote` (LCC), `PowerFlowResult.VscNote` (VSC), `PowerFlowResult.FactsNote` (FACTS and compensators; also a settled UPFC outside its terminal voltage band or its series or bridge ratings). A model with none of these devices never reaches here.

### src/GridSim.Core/PowerFlow/InductionMachines.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.PowerFlow`. 106 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/PowerFlow/InductionMachines.cs).

- [`InductionMachineResult`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/PowerFlow/InductionMachines.cs#L8) (record): One induction machine's solved state: its slip, the active and reactive power it draws from its bus (MW, Mvar; negative active power for a generator) and its mechanical (shaft) power (MW, positive for a motor).
- [`InductionMachines`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/PowerFlow/InductionMachines.cs#L30) (class): The steady-state model of an induction machine (PSS/E induction machine record, custom design, single cage), solved with the AC power flow inside `HvdcCoupling`. Equivalent circuit (all pu on the machine base MBASE and RATEKV): stator RA + j XA in series with the magnetising reactance j XM in parallel with the rotor R1 / s + j X1, at slip s. At terminal voltage V (pu of RATEKV) the input impedance is Zin = RA + j XA + (j XM || (R1 / s + j X1)); the machine draws S = |V|^2 / conj(Zin) (its reactive power positive when absorbed), the air-gap power is |V|^2 Re(Zp) / |Zin|^2 with Zp the parallel part, and the mechanical power is the air-gap power times (1 - s). At s = 0 the rotor branch is open. Slip. The slip meets the schedule PSET: mechanical power out (PCODE 1) or electrical power in (PCODE 2), positive for a motor and negative for a generator. It is found on the stable branch, between synchronous speed and the slip of peak power: |s| is stepped out from 1e-9 by doubling (at most to 1) until the power passes the schedule, then bisected to the last representable slip. A schedule beyond the peak power at the present voltage (the machine would stall, or a generator run away) has no steady state: the solve fails, naming the machine. Plain arithmetic only, so the result is the same bits everywhere. The machine is a constant-power load at its bus for each AC solve, re-taken at each solved voltage until the powers repeat within 1e-9 (1 + |P|).

- [`ElectedIsland`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/PowerFlow/IslandPartition.cs#L43) (record): GR-055: the balance of one island whose reference was elected by `IslandPartition`.
- [`IslandPartition`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/PowerFlow/IslandPartition.cs#L65) (class): Makes a network with out-of-service branches solvable. A branch opening can split the grid into islands; each island needs exactly one reference (slack) bus or its power flow is singular. This pre-pass detects the connected components over the IN-SERVICE branches and, per island: keeps it if it already has a slack; ELECTS its largest generator bus as the reference if it has generation but no slack; and BLACKS IT OUT (drops its buses/branches from the solve, booking the lost load/gen) if it has no generation. With every branch in service this is a single component containing the original slack - a pure no-op, so a fully-connected model is unchanged (bit-identical solve).

### src/GridSim.Core/PowerFlow/KronReduction.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.PowerFlow`. 191 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/PowerFlow/KronReduction.cs).

- [`KronReduction`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/PowerFlow/KronReduction.cs#L20) (class): Kron (star-mesh) reduction of a bus admittance matrix: eliminate the buses you don't want to keep and fold their effect into the retained buses, so an N-bus network becomes an equivalent network among only the retained nodes (e.g. the generator buses). This is the standard construction behind classical multimachine transient stability and behind physically-derived inter-domain synchronising coefficients: the imaginary part of the reduced admittance between two retained buses is their synchronising susceptance. Uses sequential single-node elimination (Y_ij <- Y_ij - Y_ik*Y_kj / Y_kk), the numerically standard form; equivalent to Y_kept - Y_ke*Y_ee^-1*Y_ek but without forming the inverse.

### src/GridSim.Core/PowerFlow/LccDcLinks.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.PowerFlow`. 213 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/PowerFlow/LccDcLinks.cs).

- [`LccControl`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/PowerFlow/LccDcLinks.cs#L7) (enum): How a two-terminal LCC link ended up being controlled in a solve.
- [`LccLinkResult`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/PowerFlow/LccDcLinks.cs#L23) (record): One two-terminal LCC link's solved state: the DC current (A) and voltages (kV), the firing and extinction angles (degrees), the converter taps, the active power each converter draws from or delivers to its AC bus (MW), the reactive power each absorbs (Mvar), the control mode, and whether a power order became a current order (the inverter voltage below VCMOD).
- [`LccDcLinks`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/PowerFlow/LccDcLinks.cs#L60) (class): The steady-state model of a two-terminal line-commutated (LCC) HVDC link, PSS/E's two-terminal DC model, and its coupling to the AC power flow. Converter equations (per converter, N bridges in series; Eac the open-circuit line-to-line voltage on the valve side of the converter transformer, kV; I the DC current, kA): Eac = |V| x EBAS x TR / TAP (|V| the AC bus voltage in pu, EBAS its base kV, TR the transformer ratio, TAP the tap on the AC side). Rectifier: Vdr = N (k Eac cos(alpha) - (3/pi Xc + 2 Rc) I); inverter: Vdi = N (k Eac cos(gamma) - (3/pi Xc + 2 Rc) I), k = 3 sqrt(2) / pi; Xc, Rc the commutating reactance and resistance per bridge (ohms). Vdr = Vdi + Rdc I (the line resistance). Active power: the rectifier draws Vdr I, the inverter delivers Vdi I (MW). Reactive power absorbed: P tan(phi) with cos(phi) = (k Eac cos(angle) - 3/pi Xc I) / (k Eac), the classical fundamental power factor. Control (the normal PSS/E sequence). A current order is SETVL (A); a power order |SETVL| (MW) is held at the rectifier (SETVL > 0) or the inverter (SETVL < 0). The inverter runs at its minimum extinction angle and its tap is stepped (from the file's tap, by its step, within its limits) to bring the compounded DC voltage Vdi + RCOMP x I as close as it can to VSCHD; under a power order the current then follows from the power and that voltage. If the compounded voltage is below VCMOD, the power order becomes a current order (the order divided by VSCHD). The rectifier's firing angle follows from the voltage it must reach, and its tap is stepped to keep the angle between its limits. If even at the minimum angle with its tap at the limit the rectifier cannot reach the voltage, it sits at the minimum angle and the inverter takes the current, at the order less the margin DELTI, with its extinction angle (and tap) set by the voltage the rectifier can give. A link whose order no angle and tap within their limits can meet fails the solve loud: `SolveLink` throws naming the link, and `Solve` returns a result marked NOT converged with that reason in `PowerFlowResult.LccNote`. Coupling. Each converter is a constant-power load at its AC bus for one AC solve; the DC state is then re-solved from the new AC voltages, and the two alternate until the converters' P and Q change by less than 1e-9 MW (or Mvar) times (1 + |P|), at most 50 times. Deterministic: fixed loops, the AC solve bit-identical as always.

### src/GridSim.Core/PowerFlow/LoadAtVoltage.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.PowerFlow`. 31 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/PowerFlow/LoadAtVoltage.cs).

- [`LoadAtVoltage`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/PowerFlow/LoadAtVoltage.cs#L16) (class): The single rule for "how much load does this bus actually draw at voltage V" (R065, October 2026). A bus with no `Bus.Zip`, or a ZIP whose coefficients do not vary with voltage, draws exactly its nominal `Bus.Pd` / `Bus.Qd` - returned as the stored doubles, untouched, so every constant-power case stays bit-for-bit on the historical numbers. A voltage-dependent ZIP load draws `Pd * PMultiplier(V)` and `Qd * QMultiplier(V)`, the same polynomial the Newton mismatch and Jacobian already use. Before this helper only the Newton mismatch honoured ZIP; the reactive-limit check, the physics audit and the backward/forward sweep all used the nominal load, so an exactly solved ZIP case was reported as violating KCL and its generators' reactive output was mis-measured.

- [`MtdcConverterResult`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/PowerFlow/MtdcLinks.cs#L10) (record): One converter's solved state in a multi-terminal DC link: whether it rectifies, its DC current (A, positive into the DC network), the DC voltage at its DC bus (kV), its firing (rectifier) or extinction (inverter) angle (degrees), its tap, and the active power it draws from (positive) or delivers to (negative) its AC bus (MW) and the reactive power it absorbs (Mvar).
- [`MtdcLinkResult`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/PowerFlow/MtdcLinks.cs#L14) (record): One multi-terminal DC link's solved state: every converter (in file order) and every DC bus voltage (kV, in file order).
- [`MtdcLinks`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/PowerFlow/MtdcLinks.cs#L33) (class): The steady-state model of a PSS/E multi-terminal DC link: line-commutated converters (the two-terminal converter equations of `LccDcLinks`) on a resistive DC network. Control. The DC voltage converter (VCONV) runs at its minimum angle with its tap stepped (from the file's tap, by its step, within its limits) to bring its DC voltage nearest its schedule SETVL (kV); every other converter holds its order: SETVL MW (MDC 1) or A (MDC 2), positive for a rectifier, negative for an inverter, a power order turned into a current by its DC bus voltage. The DC network (link resistances RDC, grounding resistances RGRND) is solved with the voltage converter's DC bus as the reference; the voltage converter takes whatever current balances the network, and rectifies or inverts by its sign. Each order-holding converter's angle then follows from its DC bus voltage and current, its tap stepped to keep the angle within its limits. Not applied. The mode switch voltage VCMOD, the alternate voltage converter VCONVN, the current margin MARG and the participation factor DCPF (which govern what happens when a converter runs out of angle or tap range) are not applied: a converter that would need them fails the solve, naming the converter, rather than be solved with a guess. A converter connected to two DC buses (IDC2) is refused when the file is read.

### src/GridSim.Core/PowerFlow/NewtonRaphsonPowerFlow.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.PowerFlow`. 384 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/PowerFlow/NewtonRaphsonPowerFlow.cs).

- [`NewtonRaphsonPowerFlow`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/PowerFlow/NewtonRaphsonPowerFlow.cs#L30) (class): The Newton-Raphson power flow in polar form. Each inner iteration linearises the bus power-balance equations around the current voltages (the Jacobian), solves for the corrections through an `ILinearSolver`, and applies them. An outer loop enforces generator reactive-power limits: if a PV bus would need more (or less) VARs than its generators can supply, the reactive output is pinned at the limit and the bus is released to PQ - its voltage is then free to sag or rise, exactly as a real machine hitting its excitation limit. The flow is re-solved until no further switching is needed. Bit-identical to `SparseNewtonRaphsonPowerFlow` on the CPU (Mark's ruling 2, October 2026). This engine keeps its own dense admittance, injection and Jacobian assembly, but on the CPU every Newton step is solved and applied by the shared canonical routines (`NewtonShell.SolveStep` / `NewtonShell.ApplyStep`): the dense Jacobian is copied into the same CSR pattern the sparse engine builds and handed to the same sparse LU. The two engines then differ only in assembly, which is exact (same products, same summation order), so every voltage, angle, injection, flow and iteration count matches to the bit. `DenseSparseParityTests` proves it on every bundled case the dense engine can hold. A non-CPU dense backend (the ILGPU / ROCm GPU solvers) is still honoured as given: its factorisation rounds differently by nature, so GPU results are NOT part of the bit-identity contract. It uses the same step damping, voltage floor and non-finite guard as the CPU path.

These cover the parts of a power-flow solve that do not touch the Jacobian/LU representation: aggregating generator/load injections onto buses (the P/Q specs and the flat/warm start), the reactive-power outer-loop bookkeeping that switches a PV bus to PQ when its generators hit a Q-limit, assembling the `PowerFlowResult` (injections, losses, line flows) - and the Newton step itself: the shared unknown numbering, the canonical linear solve and the damped update. Only the Y-bus, injection and Jacobian ASSEMBLY stay in the two solver files. Every helper is a pure function of its inputs, and assembly is exact (same products, same summation order), so on the CPU the two solvers produce bit-for-bit identical results. `DenseSparseParityTests` pins that on every bundled case the dense engine can hold.

### src/GridSim.Core/PowerFlow/OltcLoopPowerFlow.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.PowerFlow`. 64 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/PowerFlow/OltcLoopPowerFlow.cs).

- [`OltcLoopPowerFlow`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/PowerFlow/OltcLoopPowerFlow.cs#L29) (class): An `IPowerFlowSolver` that runs the on-load tap changer (OLTC) outer loop of `SteadyStateSolver` around a Newton engine, so a caller that takes an `IPowerFlowSolver` (the contingency screens, the N-1 sweep, stress and chain) can solve to the same regulated steady state as the default case solve. Why it exists (October 2026, D04). The contingency family used to run the raw Newton engine, with no OLTC loop, while the default case solve (`gridsim <case>`) runs the loop. The post-fault steady state that GB security assessment judges is the state AFTER the Grid Supply Point tap changers have acted (NETS SQSS v2.10, 8 April 2025, section 6.2: "following a secured event, the target voltages at Grid Supply Points should be achieved ... after the operation of Grid Supply Transformer tap-changers"), so the screens now include the loop. With no OLTC records in the model the loop is skipped and the answer is exactly the wrapped engine's, bit for bit (`SteadyStateSolver.Solve` returns `engine.Solve(model, options)` directly). The returned result is the result of the last loop pass, solved on the tap-adjusted model; the model the caller passed in is never changed. Not thread-safe, exactly like `SteadyStateSolver`: one instance per thread. A concurrent call on a shared instance throws `InvalidOperationException` rather than racing.

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.PowerFlow`. 156 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/PowerFlow/SolvedGeneration.cs).

Why this exists: those reports used to print "Generation" as the sum of the POSITIVE bus net injections (`PowerFlowResult.PInjMw` is generation minus demand at each bus). That is not what any generator produces: a generator bus that also carries load contributes only its surplus, and a generator bus whose local load exceeds its output contributes nothing at all. On IEEE case14 it read 0.25 GW against 0.26 GW of demand plus 13.4 MW of losses, i.e. less generation than consumption, which cannot be right. This class reports the actual generator output instead.

### src/GridSim.Core/PowerFlow/SparseKronReduction.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.PowerFlow`. 256 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/PowerFlow/SparseKronReduction.cs).

- [`SparseKronReduction`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/PowerFlow/SparseKronReduction.cs#L60) (class): The Kron reduction of `KronReduction.Reduce`, done on the nonzero pattern of the matrix instead of the full dense array, giving the SAME BITS in every entry of the result (stream P, October 2026: R105, N290, R007). Why. The dense reduction allocates the whole n x n complex matrix (about 200 MB at gb-full's 3,539 buses, about 320 MB for the 4,491-node machine-augmented network of the classical stability model) and visits every active row and column at every elimination step. A network admittance has a handful of entries per row, so almost all of that work and memory is spent on zeros. This class keeps, per row, only the entries that are or become nonzero (the original pattern plus the fill-in of the elimination) and eliminates the same nodes in the same order with the same arithmetic. Why it is bit-identical (the proof). The dense reduction eliminates the non-kept nodes k in ascending index order, and at step k, for every active row i != k with w[i,k] != 0 (the test is `yik == Complex.Zero`, which a signed zero also passes) and every active column j != k, does `w[i,j] -= yik * w[k,j] / pivot` with `pivot = w[k,k]` (its zero-row shortcut is proved and tested to give exactly this per-entry update; see the R126 comment in `KronReduction.Reduce`). Call the PATTERN the set of positions that are stored here: every input cell, its mirror (j,i), every diagonal, and the fill: at step k, every pair (i,j) of active neighbours of k. The pattern is structurally symmetric, so the rows i with a stored (i,k) are exactly the columns of row k. Outside the pattern the dense matrix holds exactly (+0, +0) at every step. Initially, every position that is not an input cell is the default (+0, +0). At step k a position (i,j) outside the pattern can only receive an update when w[i,k] is stored-and-nonzero (otherwise the dense code skips the row), and then w[k,j] must be outside the pattern (else the fill would have put (i,j) in it), so by induction w[k,j] = (+0, +0) and the term is `yik * (+0, +0) / pivot`. With yik and the pivot finite and the pivot nonzero (the pivot test guarantees |pivot| > 0), every product in the complex multiply is a signed zero, so the product is a complex zero, and a complex zero divided by a finite nonzero complex is a complex zero (the divide's denominators are nonzero: in each branch of the scaled division the denominator is c + d*r or d + c*r with |r| <= 1 and no cancellation). Then `+0 - z` is +0 for z = +0 or -0 in round-to-nearest. So the position stays (+0, +0). Inside the pattern every value is the dense value, bit for bit. The same steps k in the same order; the same rows (stored (i,k) with yik != 0, every other row has yik = (+0, +0) by (1) and is skipped in both); for each such row every stored (i,j) with j active and j != k receives `w[i,j] -= yik * w[k,j] / pivot` with the same operands: w[k,j] is the stored value, or (+0, +0) by (1) when (k,j) is outside the pattern, and that zero term is applied here too, as the dense code applies it (it can turn a -0 component into +0, so it is not skipped). Each entry is updated once per step and only from row k and column k, which that step never changes, so the order in which the entries of a step are visited does not matter (the same argument the dense code's R126 comment makes). A fill entry starts at (+0, +0), the dense value by (1), and receives the same update. The pivot test and its failure are the same. The matrix scale is the largest entry magnitude over the input (the positions outside the input are zeros and cannot raise a maximum; with every input finite the maximum does not depend on the visiting order), so the floor is the same double; the pivot is the same value by (2), so the same step fails, with the same message (`KronReduction.NearSingularPivotMessage`). Where the proof needs finite numbers, the dense code itself is run. Step (1) needs yik and the pivot finite. If any input entry is not finite (NaN or infinite), or an elimination step meets a non-finite pivot or a non-finite yik (an overflow), the sparse attempt is abandoned and the matrix is reduced by `KronReduction.Reduce` on the dense array built from the same cells: the answer is then the dense answer by construction. No admittance GridSim builds from a valid model takes that path. Cost. Work and memory follow the fill-in of the elimination in the given (natural) order, which is not reordered: a fill-reducing order (minimum degree, as the sparse LU uses) would change which nodes are eliminated first and so the rounding of every reduced value, and is therefore not used. On a network the fill is far below n x n in the early steps; the last steps, among the kept nodes' neighbours, can densify, and in the worst case (a matrix that fills completely) the cost is that of the dense reduction plus the bookkeeping. Measure at the batch.


- [`SparseNewtonRaphsonPowerFlow`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/PowerFlow/SparseNewtonRaphsonPowerFlow.cs#L21) (class): The same polar Newton-Raphson power flow as `NewtonRaphsonPowerFlow`, but assembled entirely sparsely: a sparse complex Y-bus and a sparse Jacobian built by walking each bus's neighbours. Each Newton step is solved by the direct sparse LU (reverse Cuthill-McKee ordering, partial pivoting; ILU(0)/BiCGSTAB only if the LU reports singular). Memory is O(nnz), which is what lets the full node-level GDA replica - tens of thousands of buses - reach steady state, where the dense O(n^2)-memory path cannot. On the CPU it is BIT-IDENTICAL to the dense engine on every case (Mark's ruling 2, October 2026): both run the one canonical step in `NewtonShell.SolveStep` / `NewtonShell.ApplyStep`, and differ only in exact assembly arithmetic. `DenseSparseParityTests` pins it.

### src/GridSim.Core/PowerFlow/SteadyStateSolver.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.PowerFlow`. 572 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/PowerFlow/SteadyStateSolver.cs).

- [`SteadyStateSolver`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/PowerFlow/SteadyStateSolver.cs#L42) (class): Solves the network to a regulated steady state: a Newton-Raphson power flow with an outer on-load-tap-changer loop. After each solve it nudges every OLTC's tap one step toward its target (raising a controlled bus on the untapped To end by lowering the tap, or one on the tapped From end by raising it, and vice-versa), then re-solves, until the taps settle inside their deadbands - the digital echo of Grid Supply Point transformers holding distribution voltage as load shifts. With no OLTCs it's just the plain power flow. Which transformer, and which OLTCs regulate (N046, October 2026). An `Oltc` record names its transformer and its controlled bus. The record now drives the first branch carrying that name AND having the controlled bus at one of its ends (`MapOltcRecordsToBranches`); only when no same-named branch touches the controlled bus (a remote controlled bus) does it fall back to the first branch of that name, the historical rule. Before N046 the match was by name alone, so with names shared between transformers on different buses (gb-full has 58 such names) a record could step a transformer it does not belong to. An OLTC whose controlled bus is generator-regulated (PV or slack in the model) HOLDS its tap, as the passive plant does (`Assets.PassivePlantFleet`): the machine's AVR fixes that voltage, so no tap position can move it, and regulating it anyway ran the tap one step per pass to its limit. On gb-full 71 records aim at PV buses held at 1.02 pu against a 1.0 +/- 0.01 pu target, and every one of those taps was driven from 1.0 to 1.0999999999999996 (see `TapsHeldAtGeneratorBus`). Generator-regulated as SOLVED (N071, October 2026). The hold is decided from the bus types each converged solve ended with (`PowerFlowResult.SolvedBusTypes`), not only the model's stored types: a PV bus whose units the reactive-limit loop pinned at Qmin / Qmax is a PQ bus in that solve (no AVR holds it), so its tap changer regulates it. Before N071 such a tap stayed held while the bus sat outside its band, and the loop still reported the taps settled. The model's types still decide before the first solve and whenever a solve did not converge. Not thread-safe. A single instance keeps mutable per-solve state (`RegulatedModel`, `OltcPasses`), so it must not be shared across threads. Use one instance per thread for parallel N-1 sweeps. Concurrent `Solve` calls on the same instance are detected and rejected with an `InvalidOperationException`.

### src/GridSim.Core/PowerFlow/SwitchedShuntPowerFlow.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.PowerFlow`. 249 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/PowerFlow/SwitchedShuntPowerFlow.cs).

- [`SwitchedShunt`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/PowerFlow/SwitchedShuntPowerFlow.cs#L14) (record): F22 (October 2026): a discrete switched shunt (capacitor or reactor bank) at a bus, switched in whole steps to keep the bus voltage inside a band. `StepMvar` is the reactive injection of one step at 1 pu voltage (positive = capacitive, negative = reactive), added to the bus's fixed shunt Bs exactly as a MATPOWER Bs (MVAr at 1 pu) is; the bank sits at a whole number of steps between `MinSteps` and `MaxSteps`, starting at `InitialSteps`.
- [`SwitchedShuntPowerFlow`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/PowerFlow/SwitchedShuntPowerFlow.cs#L41) (class): F22 (October 2026): the power flow with discrete switched shunts, as an outer loop around an unchanged engine (the way PSS/E-style discrete shunt control and GridSim's own tap-changer loop work). After each converged solve every bank whose bus voltage is below its band switches IN one step (more capacitive), and every bank above its band switches OUT one step, within its step range; the network is re-solved with the new shunts until no bank moves. A bank that reverses direction is frozen at its current step (it is hunting across a band narrower than one step), which guarantees the loop ends. Each pass is an ordinary engine solve, so the dense and sparse engines give the same bits. `ShuntsSettled` is false when the pass cap stopped the loop with a bank still wanting to move, or when a bank had to be frozen while outside its band; a caller must not report that state as regulated. Opt-in: only used when asked (the CLI `pf --switched-shunts`).

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.PowerFlow`. 28 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/PowerFlow/VoltageSetpoint.cs).

Why "last": it is what MATPOWER does. `runpf` seeds the controlled voltages with `V0(gbus) = gen(on, VG)`, a MATLAB indexed assignment in which a bus index that repeats keeps the LAST value written - so a GridSim solve cross-validated against MATPOWER must use the same rule, and the dense and sparse Newton engines (`NewtonShell.BuildBusSpec`, which overwrites the per-bus value generator by generator) always have. Before this the backward/forward sweep took the HIGHEST Vg at a PV bus and the FIRST generator's Vg at the slack, so the three engines held the same model at three different voltages. A unit that should not regulate (a storage site, for instance) must therefore carry the bus's existing setpoint rather than a placeholder; `Storage.StorageFleet.Apply` does exactly that.

### src/GridSim.Core/PowerFlow/VscDcLinks.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.PowerFlow`. 115 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/PowerFlow/VscDcLinks.cs).

- [`VscConverterResult`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/PowerFlow/VscDcLinks.cs#L10) (record): One converter's solved state in a VSC link: active and reactive power into its AC bus (MW, Mvar; negative when drawn from the bus), its DC voltage (kV), its losses (MW), the active power order it ended with (a power converter's order after any capability reduction; NaN for the DC voltage converter) and whether its MVA or current rating limited it.
- [`VscLinkResult`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/PowerFlow/VscDcLinks.cs#L14) (record): One VSC link's solved state: the DC current (A, positive from the power converter towards the DC voltage converter) and both converters.
- [`VscDcLinks`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/PowerFlow/VscDcLinks.cs#L40) (class): The steady-state model of a two-terminal VSC HVDC link, PSS/E's VSC DC model. DC side. One converter holds the DC voltage (TYPE 1, DCSET kV); the other an active power order (TYPE 2, DCSET MW drawn from its AC bus into the link; negative sends power to the bus). Each converter's losses are max(MINLOSS, ALOSS + BLOSS x |Idc|) (kW, Idc in A), taken from the AC side. With R the DC line resistance and I the current from the power converter towards the voltage converter: the power converter's AC draw P = (Vdc + R I) I + loss(|I|), solved for I in the cancellation-free closed form (the root nearest zero); the voltage converter then delivers Vdc I - loss(|I|) to its bus. AC side. MODE 1 (AC voltage control): the converter is a voltage-controlling source at its bus with its active power fixed, its reactive power between MINQ and MAXQ, holding ACSET pu (the bus becomes a voltage-controlled bus; a reactive limit reached releases it, as for a generator). MODE 2 (fixed power factor): reactive power P x sqrt(1 - pf^2) / pf with pf = ACSET, of the same sign as P for pf > 0. Ratings. The apparent power must stay within min(SMAX, sqrt(3) |V| base kV IMAX / 1000) (either 0 = no limit). When the solved state exceeds it, the active power order and the reactive power are reduced by the power weighting fraction PWF: P' = P (1 - (1 - PWF) k), Q' = Q (1 - PWF k), with k in 0..1 chosen so that P'^2 + Q'^2 is the limit squared (PWF 1 reduces only the reactive power, 0 only the active power). The reduced reactive power caps the MODE 1 converter's limit on that side. Under MODE 2 the reactive power is tied to the active power by the power factor, so both are scaled onto the rating together (the weighting has nothing to choose between). The DC voltage converter's active power is set by the link, so its weighting is taken as 1 (reactive only); if its active power alone exceeds its rating the solve fails, naming the link.

### src/GridSim.Core/Presentation/CarbonFactors.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Presentation`. 232 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Presentation/CarbonFactors.cs).

- [`CarbonIntensityTable`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Presentation/CarbonFactors.cs#L65) (class): THE one table of per-fuel carbon-intensity figures in GridSim (October 2026, R145 / R146; ruled by main under Ruling R1, CF4). Every carbon figure the app paints or computes - the MACHINE tab's stack total, the MARKET tab's grid-intensity read and the experimental carbon tracing - reads ONE figure per fuel from here, so the same dispatch gives the same carbon in every view, and no other file carries a per-fuel carbon literal. Source. NESO (National Energy System Operator), "Carbon Intensity Regional Forecast Methodology", issue May 2024, Table 1 "Fuel Type / Carbon Intensity gCO2/kWh", p.3; the same figures are served by the NESO Carbon Intensity API at `https://api.carbonintensity.org.uk/intensity/factors` (read 2026-10-11): Biomass 120, Coal 937, Gas (Combined Cycle) 394, Gas (Open Cycle) 651, Hydro 0, Nuclear 0, Oil 935, Other 300, Solar 0, Wind 0, Pumped Storage 0. The methodology states (p.1) that the factors cover "CO2 emissions related to electricity generation only" and "are based on the output-weighted average efficiency of generation in GB and DUKES CO2 emission factors for fuels" (its refs [3], Energy Policy 102 (2017) pp.463-475, doi 10.1016/j.enpol.2016.12.037, and [4], DUKES). That is the DIRECT-COMBUSTION intensity of the electricity generated: the fuel's DUKES combustion factor divided by the GB fleet's measured efficiency, per MWh generated, with no upstream (mining, gas supply, plant build) emissions. Why this set. (1) It is the one per-fuel set the GB system operator publishes for GB plant, so the MARKET tab's indicative read is consistent with the measured NESO intensity it is replaced by whenever a lake tick carries one. (2) It is a direct-combustion set (the basis main's Q8 judgement asked for). (3) It is the set the MARKET tab already used (coal 937, CCGT 394, OCGT 651, biomass 120, other 300), which the review identified as the only one of the three old sets with a traceable origin; the MACHINE (0.35 / 0.49 / 0.95) and tracing (0.36 / 0.44 / 0.91 / 0.40 / 0.34 / 0.20 / 0.65) sets had none. Mapping of GridSim's kinds onto the published fuel types (choices recorded here, Ruling R1): Coal (and lignite) = Coal 937; CCGT = Gas (Combined Cycle) 394; OCGT = Gas (Open Cycle) 651. Gas of unstated cycle = Gas (Combined Cycle): the GB gas fleet's output is overwhelmingly combined cycle, and an unstated gas unit in GB data is a CCGT far more often than a peaker. Gas CHP = Gas (Combined Cycle): the table has no CHP row, and the electricity-side efficiency of GB gas CHP is closer to a CCGT's than to an open cycle's (the heat output is not counted against the electricity here). Oil and reciprocating engines (diesel, oil engines) = Oil 935. Biomass = Biomass 120. The one entry that is not direct combustion: the methodology's footnote i says it is "consumption-based" accounting (120 +/- 120 gCO2/kWh, supply-chain emissions), because the stack CO2 of biomass is biogenic and counted as zero by UK carbon accounting. It is kept as published so the whole table stays one published set; it is named (`BiomassTPerMwh`) so a caller that wants pure stack CO2 can see it. Other (and any unclassified fossil fuel) = Other 300. Nuclear, wind, solar, hydro, tidal, pumped storage, batteries, hydrogen: 0 (no combustion). Interconnectors and grid infeeds: 0. Their combustion happens outside the modelled network, so under direct accounting it is not this network's. NESO's Table 1 does print approximate consumption-based import figures (French ~53, Dutch ~474, Belgian ~179, Irish ~458 gCO2/kWh, marked "~" because the forecast weights each link by the exporting country's live mix); they are not used here because they are consumption-based, not direct, and a GridSim interconnector or GSP infeed does not carry its source country. A caller wanting consumption-based totals applies them itself. The methodology PDF is docs/reference/carbon/S325-neso-ci-regional-methodology-v2.pdf. (CF4-F2, N350.) Units. The table is held in t CO2 / MWh (the form the stack total and the tracing multiply MW by); the kg CO2 / MWh form (numerically gCO2/kWh, as NESO publishes it) is DERIVED as 1000 x t. Each derived value is the published whole number exactly: for a decimal t = d / 1000 the nearest double times 1000 lies within 1000 x half an ulp of t, which is always under half an ulp of d (the ulp ratio is at most 1000 / 1024), so it rounds to d. `Cf4CarbonTableTests` pins every one. What moved (R145 / R146, before -> after, t/MWh unless kg): MACHINE CCGT / Gas / CHP 0.35 -> 0.394, OCGT 0.49 -> 0.651, coal 0.95 -> 0.937, biomass 0 -> 0.12, Other 0 -> 0.3; MARKET unknown fossil 450 -> 300 kg; tracing coal 0.91 -> 0.937, OCGT 0.44 -> 0.651, CCGT 0.36 -> 0.394, CHP 0.34 -> 0.394, generic gas 0.40 -> 0.394, oil / recip 0.65 -> 0.935, imports / infeed 0.20 -> 0, biomass 0.12 and unknown 0.30 unchanged. The old per-view constant names below are kept ONLY as names (each is now the one figure of its fuel, not a separate literal), because tests outside this change refer to them by name.
- [`CarbonFactors`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Presentation/CarbonFactors.cs#L197) (class): The per-fuel carbon factors the presentation layer paints, shared by both the WPF view-models and the web session projections so the twins can never drift. Both forms read the ONE figure per fuel in `CarbonIntensityTable` (R145 / R146, CF4): the MACHINE tab's t/MWh and the MARKET tab's kg/MWh of the same fuel are the same number in two units. Keys are fuel names (from the app-local `Fuels` taxonomy, the names `FuelTaxonomy` paints) rather than the app-local `FuelInfo` struct, because that struct is defined separately in each UI project.

### src/GridSim.Core/Presentation/CredibleLossBasis.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Presentation`. 28 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Presentation/CredibleLossBasis.cs).

The 3,600 MW Dogger Bank A+B+C correlated cluster is the TSGB Policy 0021 ("The 1,800 Megawatt Fiction") worst-case scenario; the 1,800 MW figure is carried alongside. N040 (S3, October 2026), what the official documents say: NESO, Frequency Risk and Control Report 2025, For Approval, May 2025 (docs/reference S052), s.4.1 p.10: "The minimum inertia of 102 GVA.s is based on a future largest loss of 1800 MW", and s.7.1: additional response "in preparation for securing the future largest loss of 1800 MW". FRCR 2025 secures BMU-only events (one BMU lost) and does NOT secure simultaneous events (s.6.2, s.7.1), and a correlated multi-unit cluster loss is a simultaneous event. So 1,800 MW is the official future largest loss, not a superseded convention, and 3,600 MW is an unsecured scenario, not the official design basis. The presentation labels say so; the constant names (and the values the tests pin) are unchanged, so no number moves.

### src/GridSim.Core/Presentation/DesktopLaunchArgs.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Presentation`. 216 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Presentation/DesktopLaunchArgs.cs).

- [`DesktopLaunchArgs`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Presentation/DesktopLaunchArgs.cs#L30) (record): The desktop app's (GridSim.Wpf) launch arguments, read and checked in one place so the rules can be unit-tested without a window (D-DOC-074 and D-DOC-142, docs-session findings, October 2026). The two defects this replaces, both in `MainWindow.OnLoaded`: D-DOC-074: the model text was "the first word after the program name that does not start with '-'", so the VALUE of a flag was taken as the model: `--back 30` booted case30, and `--tab OPERATOR` on its own searched the model picker for "OPERATOR" and fell back to the first model. D-DOC-142: a `--zone`, `--back` or `--bridge-source` value that matched no picker entry was dropped without a word, so a typing slip quietly streamed a different zone, start or reconstruction than the one asked for. The rules now: every flag takes its value as the NEXT word (two-token form, as the manual always said), and that word is never the model text. At most one other word may be given and it is the model text. Anything that cannot be honoured is refused with a message naming it (fail loud): an unknown option (including the `--zone=ukpn` one-token form and a wrong-case `--Zone`, which used to be ignored), a flag with no value, a flag given twice, a second model word, a `--back` that is not a whole number, and (in `Resolve`) any value that matches no entry of its picker. The app shows the refusal and closes, like a CLI usage error, rather than open on something the user did not ask for. Presentation only: nothing here touches a computed number.
- [`DesktopLaunchPlan`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Presentation/DesktopLaunchArgs.cs#L200) (record): The launch arguments matched to the app's pickers: an index per given value (null when the value was not given), and every refusal. The app applies the indices only when `Ok` is true.

### src/GridSim.Core/Presentation/ExactInputMemo.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Presentation`. 59 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Presentation/ExactInputMemo.cs).

- [`ExactInputMemo`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Presentation/ExactInputMemo.cs#L24) (class): R131 (October 2026 review, stream P): remembers the exact inputs of the last completed computation, so a presentation surface can skip recomputing when nothing it reads has changed. Why. The web TRIP / DEVICE tab and the TSGB what-if card recompute in `OnParametersSet`, which Blazor calls on every Dashboard render (each live frame and each 4 s presence heartbeat). The TRIP tab's auto mode runs `TsgbSizer.SizeForTargets` (up to 8 growth and 44 bisection swing simulations) plus two more swings every time, although the inertia, demand, loss and the user's inputs have not changed. Why the shown numbers cannot change. The computations are pure functions of their inputs (no clock, no random number, no shared state). This memo reports "unchanged" only when every input is the same to the BIT (doubles compared by their IEEE 754 bit patterns, so +0 and -0, or two NaNs with different payloads, count as different; texts compared ordinally), and the surface then keeps the results of the previous run on those very inputs, which are the results a new run would give. The finding's suggestion, rounding the inputs to display precision before comparing, is NOT used: two inputs that round alike can give different results, so it could show numbers computed from inputs other than the current ones. Use: call `IsUnchanged` before computing (skip when true), and `Remember` after the computation completed. A computation that throws is never remembered, so it runs again next time. Not thread-safe (one memo per component instance, used on its renderer's thread).

```csharp
// line 31

// line 44
```

### src/GridSim.Core/Presentation/FrequencyRiskPresenter.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Presentation`. 278 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Presentation/FrequencyRiskPresenter.cs).

- [`FrequencyRiskPresenter`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Presentation/FrequencyRiskPresenter.cs#L38) (class): The ONE presenter for the NESO RP1 / OPERATOR credible loss and the purchased-time grade ladder, called by both the web projections (`TabProjections.Rp1` / `Operator`, `FuelBreakdown`) and the WPF view-models (`NesoRp1Vm`, `OperatorVm`). Before October 2026 (Q1 / R304) the two shells disagreed: the web used the largest single unit, the WPF the larger of that unit and the largest correlated interconnector group. The rule, grounded in the GB documents (Q1 ruling: "ground it in the real rules"). Source: NESO, Frequency Risk and Control Report 2025, "The Report - For Consultation", March 2025 (the FRCR the NETS SQSS requires NESO to produce): Executive summary (p.4), recommendation 2: "Secure all Balancing Mechanism Unit (BMU) only risks and do not apply additional actions to mitigate all BMU plus Vector Shift (BMU+VS) and simultaneous events". Section 6, Table 1 (p.15): current secured loss group = "BMU-only"; Section 6.1.1 (p.16): "the FRCR policy mandates securing all BMU-only events". Section 6.2 (p.18-19): securing all simultaneous events would need up to 3 GW of DC holding and is not recommended; Section 7.1 (p.27): "Secure all BMU-only events to keep resulting frequency deviations within 49.2 Hz and 50.5 Hz" and "Do not apply additional controls to secure all BMU+VS and simultaneous events". Section 8.1 (p.29): a "unified loss risk policy" covering "the loss risk from individual BMUs or from a NETS group" is only a FUTURE direction needing industry consultation and SQSS Panel approval - not today's rule. So the credible loss NESO secures today is the loss of ONE unit (one BMU). Two interconnectors tripping together at a shared landfall (Sellindge IFA + ElecLink, the North Sea pair) is a simultaneous / multi-BMU event, which FRCR 2025 explicitly does NOT secure. The correlated group is therefore shown as unsecured live context (`CredibleLossView.CorrelatedGroupExceedsSecured` flags when it is the bigger risk), but it never redefines the credible loss. This is the web rule, pinned by `WebProjectionAntiDriftTests.Rp1_CredibleLoss_IsTheSqssSecuredLargestLoss`; the WPF moved to it. What the documents do not set. No document in the repository defines a grade ladder on purchased time; the thresholds below are presentation judgement (Mark's Q10 / Q1 "best judgement"), anchored to the 49.2 Hz secured-event limit above (FRCR 2025 s.7.1) via `StabilityMetrics.LfddWorkingSetpointHz`. The unified ladder is the WPF four-step NORMAL / WATCH / ADVISORY / WARNING ladder with its falling-trend escalation; its colour levels keep the web's existing cuts exactly (green at or above 5 s, amber at or above 2 s, red below).
- [`GradeLevel`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Presentation/FrequencyRiskPresenter.cs#L74) (enum): The colour level a grade is drawn in. Both shells map it to their own brush / CSS class.

- [`CredibleLossView`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Presentation/FrequencyRiskPresenter.cs#L117) (record struct): The credible loss both shells grade against, plus the correlated interconnector group as unsecured context. `SecuredLossMw` is the largest single online unit (FRCR 2025 "BMU-only"); the correlated group is carried for display only.
