### src/GridSim.Core/Presentation/FuelTaxonomy.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Presentation`. 94 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Presentation/FuelTaxonomy.cs).

- [`FuelCategory`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Presentation/FuelTaxonomy.cs#L4) (enum): How a generator's fuel sits in the inertia / decarbonisation picture.
- [`FuelDescriptor`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Presentation/FuelTaxonomy.cs#L8) (record struct): A classified fuel: display name, hex colour, category, and whether it is a spinning (synchronous, inertial) machine.
- [`FuelTaxonomy`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Presentation/FuelTaxonomy.cs#L38) (class): The ONE fuel taxonomy for the presentation layers (R305, October 2026): maps a generator's free-text `Model.Generator.Type` onto display name, colour, category and synchronous/converter split. It used to be copied into the web `Fuels`, the WPF `Fuels` and the map's `fuelColor`, and the copies could drift; the web one now delegates here. Two classifications fixed on the way: Reciprocating engines (`recip`, the canonical type GDA's `FuelMap` gives diesel / oil / gas-engine plant, plus `reciprocating`, `diesel`, `engine`) are synchronous fossil machines - Core's `PoleMap` treats `recip` as a 4-pole synchronous machine. They used to fall through to "Other" (non-synchronous, non-fossil), so their inertia was counted in the total but not the intrinsic figure and their CO2 was not counted as fossil. "gas engine" still reads as Gas (the gas rule is checked first), exactly as before. Hydrogen (`hydrogen`, `fuel cell`, `electrolyser`) is checked BEFORE hydro: the substring test used to read "hydrogen" as synchronous hydro. A hydrogen fuel cell or electrolyser is converter-connected power-to-gas-to-power plant, shown as storage with no inertia. Hydrogen burnt in a gas turbine, CCGT or CHP is caught by those earlier rules and stays synchronous fossil-class plant. R305 rest and N020 (October 2026): the keyword list itself now lives in Core's one fuel taxonomy, `Model.FuelTypes`, shared with the GDA importer, the DC-OPF merit order and carbon tracing, and matches whole words by their start instead of any substring. This class keeps only the display table by kind. What that changed for the shells, exactly: "onshore" (the type data/uk and data/gb-synthetic give onshore wind) shows as Wind (onshore), Renewable, instead of Other (still non-synchronous); "gas turbine" shows as OCGT instead of Gas, and "CHP (Combined Heat and Power)" as CHP instead of CCGT, and a bare "combined" as Gas instead of CCGT (all three still synchronous fossil); "Charcoal" is no longer Coal and "Microwave" no longer Tidal (substring false positives, now Other). No canonical type string changes its synchronous flag; the keywords whose reading would change one are deferred to the frequency / inertia pass (see `Model.FuelTypes`).

### src/GridSim.Core/Presentation/LiveZoneTable.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Presentation`. 149 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Presentation/LiveZoneTable.cs).

- [`LiveZoneTable`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Presentation/LiveZoneTable.cs#L33) (class): N056: the zone table of the interactive live dashboard (`gridsim [case]` with no `--ticks`), for ANY case. Before N056 the table was hard-wired to the GB 10-zone teaching model (`data/uk`): it listed every bus at or above 200 kV and read its "132 kV" column and demand from the bus whose id is that bus's id + 100. On any other case that is wrong in two ways: where no such bus exists the 132 kV column printed NaN, and where one happens to exist (IEEE 118 has buses 1-118, so bus 8 "pairs" with bus 108) it printed an unrelated bus's voltage and demand as if it were the zone's lower-voltage side. The rule now (pure presentation: it reads the model and the solved state, computes nothing new): Rows are the buses at the case's top voltage level: at or above `TransmissionKvFloor` (200 kV) when the case has any; otherwise the highest `BaseKv` present. A case with no bus voltages at all (MATPOWER case14 carries baseKV 0) has no rows and says so in `Note`. A row's lower-voltage partner is a bus joined to it by an in-service branch with a lower, known `BaseKv`. The GB teaching model's convention (partner id = id + `UkPartnerIdOffset`) is honoured first when that bus really is such a neighbour, so `data/uk` reads exactly as before; otherwise the partner is the unique lower-voltage neighbour, and with none or several there is no partner (shown as not applicable, never as another bus's value). Demand is the zone's own demand: the row bus's demand plus its partner's (for `data/uk` the 400 kV buses carry none, so the figure is the 132 kV demand exactly as before). At most `MaxRows` rows, in bus-id order; `Omitted` counts the rest so the display can say so.
- [`Row`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Presentation/LiveZoneTable.cs#L45) (record): One zone row. `LowerVmPu` is NaN when the row has no lower-voltage partner.

Each rule lives here once and both shells call it: FREQUENCY EVENT: strictly `|f - 50| > 0.2 Hz` (the WPF rule). 49.8 Hz and 50.2 Hz are the edges of the GB operational band (`FrequencyLimits.OperationalLowHz` / `FrequencyLimits.OperationalHighHz`), so a frequency ON the edge is still inside the operational limit and is not an event. ### src/GridSim.Core/Presentation/TripWhatIf.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Presentation`. 112 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Presentation/TripWhatIf.cs).

- [`TripWhatIf`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Presentation/TripWhatIf.cs#L26) (class): R148 + N297 (B4, October 2026; Ruling R1: Mark delegated EE calls 2026-10-04): the ONE set of rules the trip and TSGB what-if surfaces use (web TRIP / DEVICE tab, web GEN & INERTIA TSGB card, WPF trip compare), so the same loss gives the same "required device" and the same grades on every tab and shell, at the case's own nominal frequency. R148, before: the web TRIP / DEVICE tab sized the device to 0.5 Hz/s and 49.5 Hz with literals, while the web TSGB card and the WPF compare sized it to 0.125 Hz/s (`FrequencyLimits.RocofLimitHzPerS`) and `FrequencyLimits.StatutoryLowHz`, so one loss gave two different answers on two tabs of one dashboard; the trip tab also hard-coded its 48.8 / 49.5 / 1.0 / 0.5 grade cuts and reference lines. Decision (Ruling R1). The device is sized to the targets the other two surfaces and the CLI (`trip`, `gda` TSGB lines) already use: RoCoF at most `FrequencyLimits.RocofLimitHzPerS` (0.125 Hz/s, the legacy loss-of-mains setting, the strictest RoCoF any GB relay was ever set to: the conservative design target this app's inertia thesis, the dynamic MIF and the RP1 tab all quote) and the nadir held at the statutory low edge (ESQCR 2002 regulation 27, 49.5 Hz at 50 Hz). The 0.5 Hz/s figure had no source. The grade cuts are named here: a RoCoF above `FrequencyLimits.RocofLimitModernHzPerS` (1 Hz/s, the post-ALoMCP LoM setting, EREC G99 Issue 2 Table 10.1) is an alarm, above `RocofWarnHzPerS` a warning; a nadir at or below the LFDD first stage is an alarm, below the statutory edge a warning. N297, before: these surfaces ran their swing at the GB 50 Hz and graded against the absolute GB edges for every case, so on case9 (60 Hz since D2) they disagreed with CLI `trip`. Now the study runs at the case's nominal (`StudyConfig`) and grades against the GB bands about it (`FrequencyBands`, B2's convention). At 50 Hz every number and text is the one the WPF compare and the TSGB card printed before.
- [`Level`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Presentation/TripWhatIf.cs#L58) (enum): The grade of one what-if read-out. Each shell maps it to its own style (web css "alarm" / "warnv").

- [`UnitRampHistory`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Presentation/UnitRampHistory.cs#L18) (class): Frame-to-frame memory of each generator's output, for the MECHANICAL / machine-engineer ramp readouts (web `MechanicalService` and WPF `MachineEngineerVm`). Each unit is identified by its INDEX in `GridModel.Generators`, checked against its bus and name. It used to be keyed by `Generator.Name`, which is not unique: gb-full has many units sharing a name ("- chp" x18 above 10 MW, "- other" x25, "Bolney 132kV chp" at 20.26 and 246.05 MW). Within one frame the second namesake was diffed against the first one's output, so a steady operating point showed ramps of tens of MW/min every frame (and the WPF torsional-pulse counter grew for ever). The index is unique and stable while the topology is unchanged; the bus/name check means a different unit at the same index (a model swap that slipped past a `Reset`) starts with no history instead of a phantom ramp.

### src/GridSim.Core/Protection/AlarmLogCsv.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Protection`. 95 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Protection/AlarmLogCsv.cs).

- [`AlarmLogCsv`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Protection/AlarmLogCsv.cs#L21) (class): Reads a real sequence-of-events / alarm log for `SequenceOfEvents.CrossReference` from CSV (R095). Format (UTF-8, one header line, then one alarm per line): `at_s,device,from,to,description`. `at_s` is seconds from the event start (t = 0; map a real alarm's UTC to it first), a finite number in invariant culture. `device` is the ANSI device id as logged (for example `51` or `21-Z1`), non-empty. `from` and `to` are the branch's end-bus ids; a non-branch alarm (bus voltage or frequency) has both 0 and takes no part in the branch-trip match. The description is free text and is everything after the fourth comma, so it may itself contain commas. Blank lines and lines starting with `#` are skipped. Fail loud. A wrong header, a missing field, a time that is not a finite number, a non-integer or negative bus id, exactly one of `from` / `to` being 0, or an empty device each throw `InvalidDataException` naming the line, rather than dropping the alarm (a silently dropped alarm would turn into a false "predicted, not observed").

### src/GridSim.Core/Protection/Coordination/OvercurrentCoordination.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Protection.Coordination`. 259 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Protection/Coordination/OvercurrentCoordination.cs).

- [`OvercurrentCurve`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Protection/Coordination/OvercurrentCoordination.cs#L10) (enum): The standard time-current characteristic (TCC) families an inverse-time overcurrent relay can be set to. The IEC forms are `t = TMS * k / ((I/Is)^alpha - 1)` (IEC 60255-151); the IEEE forms are `t = TD * (A / ((I/Is)^p - 1) + B)` (IEEE C37.112). Definite-time operates after a fixed delay for any current above pickup.
- [`OvercurrentElement`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Protection/Coordination/OvercurrentCoordination.cs#L36) (record): One inverse-time / definite-time overcurrent element - a curve family, a pickup current `Is` (in the same unit as the fault currents it is evaluated against, amps or per-unit) and a time dial. For an IDMT curve `TimeDial` is the IEC time-multiplier setting (TMS) or the IEEE time dial (TD); for a `OvercurrentCurve.DefiniteTime` element `DefiniteTimeSeconds` is the fixed delay.
- [`GradingResult`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Protection/Coordination/OvercurrentCoordination.cs#L46) (record): A coordination check between a primary (downstream) and backup (upstream) element at a common fault current. `MarginSeconds` is `backup - primary` operating time - the grading margin - and `Coordinated` is whether it meets the required coordination time interval with the primary operating first.
- [`OvercurrentCoordination`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Protection/Coordination/OvercurrentCoordination.cs#L75) (class): Inverse-time overcurrent (ANSI 51) coordination - the shared time-current-curve (TCC) library and the grading / selectivity-margin checks that GridSim lacked (the existing `TimeOvercurrentRelay` hard-codes a single IEC standard-inverse curve to flag a relay on a solved state; it does not grade one relay against another). Everything here is a pure closed form of the standard curve equations, validated to machine epsilon. The operate times are functions of a supplied fault current (the current the element sees). Deriving each relay's current contribution from the network - the per-branch split of the fault current computed by `ShortCircuit.Iec60909` / `FaultAnalysis` - is available from `Iec60909.BranchFaultCurrents`; callers pass that current in (R095: this doc used to call the coupling "a later slice"). Keeping the current an input keeps this library exact and independent of the operating point.

### src/GridSim.Core/Protection/FaultAnalysis.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Protection`. 807 lines. [Implementation](../../src/GridSim.Core/Protection/FaultAnalysis.cs). **Pre-existing local modifications: this link targets the working tree.**

- [`FaultType`](../../src/GridSim.Core/Protection/FaultAnalysis.cs#L10) (enum): The fault type. `FaultAnalysis.ThreePhase` solves the balanced fault on the positive-sequence network; `FaultAnalysis.Unbalanced` (F21, October 2026) solves the unbalanced faults on the three sequence networks.
- [`BranchSequenceCurrents`](../../src/GridSim.Core/Protection/FaultAnalysis.cs#L26) (record): F21: one branch's sequence currents during an unbalanced fault, at each end (pu on the system base, phase a reference, flowing INTO the branch at that end), with the derived phase, residual and negative-sequence magnitudes a relay measures.
- [`UnbalancedFaultResult`](../../src/GridSim.Core/Protection/FaultAnalysis.cs#L51) (record): F21 (October 2026): the result of an unbalanced fault study (`FaultAnalysis.Unbalanced`). Sequence quantities are phase-a referenced, pu on the system base. `PositiveSequenceState` is the faulted positive-sequence network state (bus voltages and branch flows); the protection overlay evaluates its phase elements on the PHASE currents and voltages built from the sequence quantities (N117, October 2026: it used to read this positive-sequence state alone) and its earth-fault and negative-sequence elements on `Branches`.
- [`ConverterWithoutFaultInfeed`](../../src/GridSim.Core/Protection/FaultAnalysis.cs#L92) (record): N118 (October 2026): a converter-interfaced unit an unbalanced fault study gives no fault infeed (see `UnbalancedFaultResult.ConvertersWithoutFaultInfeed`): its bus, name and rated MVA (its machine base).
- [`FaultResult`](../../src/GridSim.Core/Protection/FaultAnalysis.cs#L96) (record): The faulted network state: the collapsed voltages and elevated branch currents produced by a fault, plus the fault current itself and the per-bus differential current a busbar relay would see.
- [`ConverterFaultInfeed`](../../src/GridSim.Core/Protection/FaultAnalysis.cs#L109) (record): A converter-interfaced unit's state during the fault: its terminal voltage, its injected current (pu on the system base, and as a multiple of its own rated current), the active/reactive split, and whether it sits on its current limit.
- [`FaultAnalysis`](../../src/GridSim.Core/Protection/FaultAnalysis.cs#L132) (class): Balanced three-phase fault analysis by the classic Thevenin / bus-impedance superposition. From the PREFAULT solved voltages it builds the fault-study admittance (network Ybus + loads as constant- impedance shunts + generators as their subtransient reactance to ground), solves one column of the bus impedance matrix for the fault bus, and superposes the fault: `If = V0_k / (Zth_kk + Zf)`, `V_faulted = V0 - Zbus[:,k].If`. The faulted branch currents then drive the protection overlay, so the current/voltage/distance/differential elements operate on a real fault - the demonstration the passive assessment needed. Generator subtransient reactances are synthesised (a generic X"d, since the model does not carry machine reactances) and provenance-noted; the whole thing is positive-sequence, so only the three-phase fault is represented (an earth fault is reported not-representable). Converter-interfaced generators (`Generator.IsConverterInterfaced`: batteries, PV, wind, VSC HVDC) are not given an X"d: they are current-limited injections following the grid-code fast fault-current characteristic (see `SolveWithConverters`), so their infeed is capped near rated current instead of the several-times-rated an X"d source would claim. The fault admittance is factored on the sparse engine (`FaultNetworkSystem`) at every size, so a small case and gb-full run the same arithmetic (N233, October 2026: the old dense path up to 1,500 buses is gone).

### src/GridSim.Core/Protection/FaultNetworkSystem.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Protection`. 233 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Protection/FaultNetworkSystem.cs).

- [`FaultNetworkSystem`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Protection/FaultNetworkSystem.cs#L35) (class): A factored fault-study admittance matrix: the network `YBus` (or any supplied cells) plus a sequence of diagonal shunt stamps (machine reactances, loads as impedances), factored once and solved for as many right-hand sides as a study needs (a Zbus column, a converter-injection response, ...). One engine at every size (N233, Mark's determinism rule 2026-10-04: identical bits on every solver path). Every fault network is factored on the real 2n-expansion sparse LU (`RealExpandedComplexSolver`), the same stack the harmonic study and the RMS network run, whatever the bus count. Until October 2026 a network of up to 1,500 buses was factored on the dense complex LU (`DenseComplexLuSolver.FactorDense`) and a larger one on the sparse LU. The two solve the same matrix (the sparse cells are bit for bit the dense build's nonzero cells) but they are different algorithms (complex partial pivoting against a real-expanded LU with its own ordering), so they agreed only to a few units in the last place (at most 4.818E-15 relative over Ik'', ip, Ib and Ith on case118, measured by DOC-4). Two answers to one question break the rule, so the size switch is gone, exactly as the power flow lost its dense / sparse switch at N057: a 9-bus case and gb-full now run the same arithmetic. The few-ulp moves this made in the small-case pins are recorded once, in the tests, under "Moved 2026-10 (N233, ...)". Networks above 1,500 buses (gb-full) were already sparse, so their results are bit for bit unchanged. The dense LU survives only as a test oracle (`DenseReferenceScope`): an independent algorithm the tests cross-check the sparse answers against, to a stated tolerance. No production code path can select it (the scope is internal and only the test project opens it), so it is not a second engine. Singular systems fail loud (R285, October 2026): the sparse factor reports a singular matrix and this throws. (The dense oracle clamps a vanishing pivot to 1e-14 rather than stopping, so every dense solve is checked against the matrix it came from, and a solution that does not satisfy `Y x = b` to a backward-stable residual is rejected with the same "singular" error. That check only reads the answer.)
- [`Restore`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Protection/FaultNetworkSystem.cs#L56) (class): Declared class; see the source and member declarations for its role.

### src/GridSim.Core/Protection/ProtectionAssessment.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Protection`. 97 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Protection/ProtectionAssessment.cs).

- [`ProtectionAssessment`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Protection/ProtectionAssessment.cs#L19) (class): A passive protection-simulation overlay. Given a SOLVED state it evaluates a library of relay elements (voltage 27/59, frequency 81U/81O, RoCoF 81R, loss-of-mains 78, over/under/thermal current 50/51/37/49, distance 21, reverse power 32, busbar differential 87, and honestly-not-checkable earth/negative-sequence 50N/51N/21N/46) and reports where each WOULD operate and why - so a run can conclude, without ever altering the solve, "protection simulation suggests relay 51 on branch X would operate (2.1x rated, trips in 1.3 s)". It is deliberately not a certified protection study - real relay settings are unobtainable, so the pickups are generic standard-practice values (grounded only for the statutory frequency band and the modern RoCoF limit), and elements a positive-sequence model cannot evaluate are reported not-checkable rather than fabricated. It never calls the solver or mutates the model/result.

### src/GridSim.Core/Protection/ProtectionCascade.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Protection`. 243 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Protection/ProtectionCascade.cs).

- [`CascadeStep`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Protection/ProtectionCascade.cs#L10) (record): One rung of a protection cascade: the relay that operates, the branch it opens, and the state of the network after that branch is removed and the flow re-solved.
- [`CascadeResult`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Protection/ProtectionCascade.cs#L24) (record): The propagation of a protection event through the network: the ordered trip sequence and why it stopped.
- [`ProtectionCascade`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Protection/ProtectionCascade.cs#L41) (class): A passive, read-only "what-if" cascade: it does NOT touch the caller's solve. Starting from a prefault state it repeatedly assesses the protection overlay, trips the branch element that would operate FIRST (shortest inverse-time), opens that branch in a COPY of the model, re-solves, and re-assesses - so a single overload can be followed as it propagates ("relay 51 on A opens it -> B overloads -> relay 49 on B opens it -> the system splits"). It stops when nothing else would trip, the re-solve fails (a split / blackout - the honest terminal state), or a step cap is hit. This is the propagation counterpart of the single-state assessment: same relay library, chained through topology. Branch-tripping elements only (thermal 49, overcurrent 50/51, distance 21); voltage/frequency elements shed or trip infeed rather than open a line and are left to the active layer.
- [`RestoreFullSolveFlow`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Protection/ProtectionCascade.cs#L188) (class): Declared class; see the source and member declarations for its role.

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Protection`. 770 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Protection/ProtectionRelays.cs).

Yields every operating location plus, for context, the single closest non-operating one - so the report can state both "would fire on bus X" and "nearest to firing: bus Y at 92%".
- [`ProtectionRegistry`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Protection/ProtectionRelays.cs#L22) (class): The set of relay elements the assessment runs, in a FIXED order (the order verdicts are produced in). D-DOC-224 (October 2026): this comment used to say "ordered device-number ascending", which the list is not (49 and 50 / 51 / 21 come before 81U, and 87 before the 50N / 51N / 21N / 46 group). The order is kept exactly as it is, because the verdict list and every report built from it follow it; it groups the elements as voltage (27, 59), power (32), branch current (37, 49, 50, 51), impedance (21), system frequency (81U, 81O, 81R, 78), busbar (87) and the sequence-quantity elements last.
- [`VerdictCollector`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Protection/ProtectionRelays.cs#L44) (class): Shared helper: track operating verdicts and the single closest non-operating one.
- [`UnderVoltageRelay`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Protection/ProtectionRelays.cs#L63) (class): 27 - Undervoltage. Vm below the pickup: a depressed bus (voltage-collapse precursor).
- [`OverVoltageRelay`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Protection/ProtectionRelays.cs#L87) (class): 59 - Overvoltage. Vm above the pickup: light-load / Ferranti overvoltage.
- [`DirectionalPowerRelay`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Protection/ProtectionRelays.cs#L111) (class): 32 - Reverse/directional power. A generator absorbing real power (motoring).
- [`UnderCurrentRelay`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Protection/ProtectionRelays.cs#L139) (class): 37 - Undercurrent. A branch in service carrying essentially NO current: a de-energized / open-ended circuit. Tested against an absolute floor, so a normally lightly-loaded line (a small but real current) is not flagged - only an effectively dead one.
- [`ThermalOverloadRelay`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Protection/ProtectionRelays.cs#L174) (class): 49 - Thermal overload. Branch loading above its rating, with a first-order thermal replica for the operating time.
- [`InstantaneousOvercurrentRelay`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Protection/ProtectionRelays.cs#L213) (class): 50 - Instantaneous overcurrent. |I| above a multiple of rated current (a close-in fault magnitude); definite/instantaneous operation.
- [`TimeOvercurrentRelay`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Protection/ProtectionRelays.cs#L246) (class): 51 - Time (inverse-time) overcurrent. |I| above pickup, operating time from the IEC 60255 standard-inverse curve t = TMS.0.14 / (M^0.02 - 1).
- [`DistanceRelay`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Protection/ProtectionRelays.cs#L293) (class): 21 - Distance / impedance. The apparent impedance V^2/conj(S) seen by the relay at EACH end of the line, tested against three forward zones scaled from the line's own series impedance (load encroachment shows here as a heavily-loaded line whose apparent impedance shrinks into zone 3). One verdict per line, from the end that operates in the fastest zone (or, if neither operates, the end closest to operating), so the result no longer depends on which way round the branch is stored (R041, October 2026: only the From end used to be evaluated). On a tie the From end is reported.
- [`EndView`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Protection/ProtectionRelays.cs#L375) (record struct): What one end's relay sees: its apparent impedance, whether that is in the forward direction, the zone it falls in (null = none) and its signed margin to the outer zone (> 0 = operated).
- [`UnderFrequencyRelay`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Protection/ProtectionRelays.cs#L411) (class): 81U - Underfrequency. The run's minimum frequency (or the steady operating frequency) below the statutory pickup.
- [`OverFrequencyRelay`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Protection/ProtectionRelays.cs#L468) (class): 81O - Overfrequency.
- [`RocofRelay`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Protection/ProtectionRelays.cs#L498) (class): 81R - RoCoF. The run's peak rate-of-change-of-frequency against the modern ALoMCP limit. Needs a dynamic run; reports not-checkable against a steady state.
- [`VectorShiftLomRelay`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Protection/ProtectionRelays.cs#L528) (class): 78 - Vector shift / loss-of-mains. A voltage-angle jump (or RoCoF) past the pickup - the islanding-detection element. Needs a dynamic run.
- [`DifferentialRelay`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Protection/ProtectionRelays.cs#L564) (class): 87 - Busbar differential. The KCL current residual at each bus; a converged solve balances power so this is ~machine-epsilon - the element bites only under an injected internal fault, reported honestly as secure with the largest residual shown.
- [`GroundFaultRelay`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Protection/ProtectionRelays.cs#L607) (class): 50N/51N/21N/46 - Ground/earth and negative-sequence elements. Over a positive-sequence state (a power flow, or a balanced fault) there is no zero- or negative-sequence quantity to measure, so the element is reported not-checkable rather than given a fabricated verdict (unchanged). F21 (October 2026): when the context carries an unbalanced fault study (`ProtectionContext.Sequence`), the four elements are evaluated on its branch sequence currents and bus sequence voltages: 50N instantaneous earth fault: the larger end residual |3 I0| over `ProtectionSettings.EarthFaultInstantaneousMultiple` x rated current. 51N time earth fault: residual over `ProtectionSettings.EarthFaultTimeMultiple` x rated, time from the IEC standard-inverse curve (the 51 element's curve) at `ProtectionSettings.EarthFaultTms`. 46 negative sequence: |I2| over `ProtectionSettings.NegativeSequenceMultiple` x rated, definite time `ProtectionSettings.NegativeSequenceTimeS`. 21N earth-fault distance (lines only): at each end, for each phase p, the residual-compensated loop impedance `Z = V_p / (I_p + k0 3 I0)` with `k0 = (Z0L - Z1L) / (3 Z1L)` (the textbook earth-loop measurement), tested against the 21 element's forward zones; the end and phase in the fastest zone decide. Pickups are generic (`ProtectionConfidence.Generic`, [VERIFY] in `ProtectionSettings`).

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Protection`. 291 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Protection/ProtectionTypes.cs).

- [`ProtectionLocation`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Protection/ProtectionTypes.cs#L4) (enum): Where a relay verdict sits in the network.
- [`ProtectionConfidence`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Protection/ProtectionTypes.cs#L13) (enum): How much weight a verdict's SETTING carries. The operating quantities are always computed from the solved state; this grades the pickup it is compared against. Real relay settings are unobtainable, so the honest default is `Generic` - a standard-practice value - with the grounded frequency/ RoCoF limits marked `Grounded` and the elements a positive-sequence model cannot evaluate marked `NotCheckable` rather than given a fabricated verdict.
- [`RelayVerdict`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Protection/ProtectionTypes.cs#L30) (record): One relay element's verdict on one location, over the solved state. `Operate` is the headline "would this relay pick up"; `Basis` is the plain-language reason ("Vm 0.74 pu below the 0.80 pu undervoltage pickup"). `Margin` is the signed distance past pickup in the quantity's own units (positive once operated). `TimeToTripS` is the inverse-time operating time where the element has a curve (null for definite-time / not-applicable).
- [`ProtectionTrajectory`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Protection/ProtectionTypes.cs#L51) (record): A summary of a dynamic run, supplied when one is available so the frequency-derivative elements (RoCoF, loss-of-mains vector shift, over/under-frequency excursion) have something to evaluate. When null, those elements report `ProtectionConfidence.NotCheckable` against a steady state rather than inventing a transient.
- [`ProtectionSettings`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Protection/ProtectionTypes.cs#L81) (record): Generic, settable relay pickups. Frequency and RoCoF limits are the grounded GB statutory / modern- ALoMCP values; the 27 / 59 voltage pickups are the G99 Issue 2 Table 10.1 interface-protection settings (S3, October 2026), still graded Generic because a real transmission bus has no such relay; everything else is standard-practice generic (a real scheme is graded per site and is unobtainable). Overrides let a caller sweep a stricter setting to ask "what would a tighter relay do".
- [`ProtectionReport`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Protection/ProtectionTypes.cs#L219) (record): The full protection assessment over one solved state: every relay verdict, and the subset that would operate. Never mutates the model or result - it is a read-only overlay.

### src/GridSim.Core/Protection/SequenceOfEvents.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Protection`. 133 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Protection/SequenceOfEvents.cs).

- [`AlarmEvent`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Protection/SequenceOfEvents.cs#L12) (record): One row of a real, timestamped sequence-of-events (SOE) / alarm log: a protection operation on a branch. Map a real alarm's absolute UTC to `AtSeconds` (seconds from the fault t=0) before cross-referencing. Non-branch alarms (bus voltage/frequency) can be logged with `From` = `To` = 0 and are not matched against the branch-trip cascade.
- [`SoeMatchKind`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Protection/SequenceOfEvents.cs#L15) (enum): How one event lines up between the predicted cascade and the observed alarm log.
- [`SoeEntry`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Protection/SequenceOfEvents.cs#L28) (record): One reconciled entry between prediction and observation.
- [`SoeCrossReference`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Protection/SequenceOfEvents.cs#L38) (record): The reconciliation of a predicted cascade against a real alarm log.
- [`SequenceOfEvents`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Protection/SequenceOfEvents.cs#L61) (class): Cross-references a PREDICTED protection cascade (`CascadeResult`) against a REAL timestamped alarm log, so an analyst can see where the physics reproduced the event and - more usefully - where it diverged. A predicted trip with no matching alarm means the model over-predicted; a real branch-trip alarm the cascade never predicted is where the model is missing something; a matched pair that arrived out of the predicted order flags a sequencing error. The cascade orders trips by relay operating-time rank rather than wall-clock, so matching is by branch identity and relative order, not exact timing.

### src/GridSim.Core/Protection/ShortCircuit/Iec60909.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Protection.ShortCircuit`. 2267 lines. [Implementation](../../src/GridSim.Core/Protection/ShortCircuit/Iec60909.cs). **Pre-existing local modifications: this link targets the working tree.**

- [`ShortCircuitObjective`](../../src/GridSim.Core/Protection/ShortCircuit/Iec60909.cs#L13) (enum): Whether the voltage factor `c` is chosen for the maximum short-circuit current (equipment duty, breaker rating) or the minimum (protection-sensitivity checks). IEC 60909-0 Table 1.
- [`PeakFactorMethod`](../../src/GridSim.Core/Protection/ShortCircuit/Iec60909.cs#L26) (enum): N134 (CF3, October 2026): how the peak factor kappa of a three-phase duty is found (IEC 60909-0:2001 subclause 4.3.1.2; IEC 60909-0:2016 subclause 8.1.2 "Multiple-fed short circuit", checked against the 2016 contents list, [VERIFY] 2026-10-11. IEC 60909-0:2026 Edition 3.0 now exists and its numbering is unchecked).
- [`UnbalancedFaultType`](../../src/GridSim.Core/Protection/ShortCircuit/Iec60909.cs#L45) (enum): The unbalanced short-circuit types, each a different connection of the sequence networks.
- [`SteadyStateBasis`](../../src/GridSim.Core/Protection/ShortCircuit/Iec60909.cs#L62) (enum): D-DOC-097 (October 2026): how the steady-state short-circuit current `Iec60909.Duty.SteadyIkKa` (and with it the thermal factor n inside `Iec60909.Duty.ThermalIthKa`) was obtained, so a reader can tell an exact value from a bound. In every case the number reported is Ik'' (plus any converter share) and n = 1; what differs is whether IEC 60909-0 says that IS the steady-state current.
- [`Iec60909`](../../src/GridSim.Core/Protection/ShortCircuit/Iec60909.cs#L134) (class): IEC 60909-0 short-circuit duty study - the standards calculation a protection or switchgear-rating engineer needs, distinct from the operating-point superposition of `FaultAnalysis`. The two differ deliberately: 60909 drives the fault from a single equivalent voltage source `c*Un/sqrt(3)` at the fault location, with all other sources shorted and loads neglected, rather than superposing on the solved prefault voltages; it reports the family of standardised currents over time - the initial symmetrical `Ik''`, the peak `ip`, the DC component `idc`, the symmetrical breaking `Ib`, the thermal-equivalent `Ith` and the steady-state `Ik` - through the standard factors `kappa, mu, m, n`, not a single fault-current magnitude. The network entry points (`ThreePhase`, `LineToLine`) assemble the positive-sequence Thevenin impedance. `ThreePhase` applies the near-to-generator breaking factor mu per machine through the IEC 60909-0:2016 multiple-fed formula (R095), so its `Ib` equals `Ik''` only when every machine is far from the fault; its steady-state `Ik` stays `Ik''` (lambda deferred). The unbalanced entry points keep `Ib = Ik''`, as the standard directs for unbalanced faults (no flux decay is taken into account, IEC 60909-0:2016 subclause 9.2 "Unbalanced short-circuits", within clause 9 "Calculation of symmetrical breaking current"; checked against the 2016 contents list, [VERIFY] 2026-10-11, N066 / N236; the earlier citation of 10.2 was wrong, clause 10 is the DC component). The duty formulae themselves (`PeakFactor`, `ThermalDcFactor`, `FromThevenin`, `FromSequenceImpedances`) are pure and validatable against the IEC closed forms to machine epsilon. The near-to-generator AC-decay factors are provided as pure closed forms too - the synchronous breaking factor `BreakingFactorMu` (`mu`) and the asynchronous-motor factor `MotorBreakingFactorQ` (`q`) - with `SynchronousBreakingCurrentKa` applying `mu` for a single-machine fault. The impedance-correction factors `GeneratorCorrectionKg` (`K_G`) and `TransformerCorrectionKt` (`K_T`) are closed forms too, correcting a machine or transformer impedance before it enters the fault network. F21 (October 2026): the power-station-unit factors `PowerStationUnitCorrectionKs` (`K_S`) and `PowerStationUnitCorrectionKso` (`K_SO`) are added, and `ApplyCorrectionFactors` applies K_G / K_S / K_SO / K_T to a copy of the model on request (the generator rated power factor is the caller's input, since the model carries none); the duty methods themselves are unchanged and still study the model as given. Still deferred, and noted rather than silently assumed: the steady-state factor `lambda` (`Ik = lambda * IrG`), which the standard reads from machine-dependent graphs (2001 Figures 18/19, 2016 Figures 15/16) rather than a closed form. The multi-machine breaking current is delivered: `PartialThreePhase` decomposes a fault into the per-machine partial currents (each with its own `mu_i * Ik''_i`) and reports the fleet total by the meshed-network formula, the same value `ThreePhase` reports (N049). The unbalanced faults are wired end-to-end from the model: `LineToLine` through the positive/negative networks, and `SingleLineToGround` / `DoubleLineToGround` through the zero-sequence network (`ZeroSequenceThevenin`) built from the transformer winding connections.
- [`CorrectionApplied`](../../src/GridSim.Core/Protection/ShortCircuit/Iec60909.cs#L378) (record): F21: one impedance correction applied by `ApplyCorrectionFactors`.
- [`CorrectionReport`](../../src/GridSim.Core/Protection/ShortCircuit/Iec60909.cs#L382) (record): F21: what `ApplyCorrectionFactors` did: the corrected model, each correction, and the elements it could not correct (with why).
- [`Duty`](../../src/GridSim.Core/Protection/ShortCircuit/Iec60909.cs#L509) (record): The full IEC 60909 duty at a fault, currents in kA (and the driving `Ik''` in pu).
- [`BreakerRating`](../../src/GridSim.Core/Protection/ShortCircuit/Iec60909.cs#L538) (record): A switchgear device's short-circuit ratings (IEC 62271 / IEEE C37), to check a computed `Duty` against - the rated maximum voltage (kV, line-to-line), the peak making current, the symmetrical breaking current, and the short-time withstand current over its rated duration (kA rms). GR-124: `BreakingAsymKa` is the optional rated ASYMMETRICAL breaking current (kA rms, the IEC 62271-100 `I_sc sqrt(1 + 2 (dc%)^2)` figure). When it is given the check also tests the DC (asymmetrical) breaking duty `sqrt(Ib^2 + idc^2)`; NaN (the default) leaves that check out and says so in `BreakerAdequacy.AsymmetricalChecked`.
- [`BreakerAdequacy`](../../src/GridSim.Core/Protection/ShortCircuit/Iec60909.cs#L551) (record): The adequacy of a breaker against a duty: each rating checked, with the signed kA margin (rating minus demand, so `>= 0` is adequate) and the overall verdict. GR-606: `RequiredVoltageKv` is the highest system voltage the rated voltage was compared with. GR-124: the asymmetrical (DC) breaking check is made only when the rating carries one (`AsymmetricalChecked`); otherwise `AsymmetricalOk` is true and its margin NaN.
- [`MachinePartialCurrent`](../../src/GridSim.Core/Protection/ShortCircuit/Iec60909.cs#L1221) (record): One source's contribution to a three-phase fault: its partial initial symmetrical current (kA and pu), its rated current, the near-generator factor `mu` for its own contribution ratio, and the partial symmetrical breaking current `mu * Ik''_g`. A converter-interfaced source (`IsConverter`) is a current source: its share is `I_skPF * |Z_kj| / |Z_kk|` with `mu = 1`.
- [`FaultContribution`](../../src/GridSim.Core/Protection/ShortCircuit/Iec60909.cs#L1230) (record): A three-phase fault decomposed into the per-machine partial currents that feed it, with the totals. Each machine's own `MachinePartialCurrent.BreakingIbKa` is its single-fed `mu_i * Ik''_i`; the fleet `TotalBreakingIbKa` is the meshed-network (multiple-fed) breaking current that `ThreePhase` reports, bit for bit (N049), so it is generally NOT the sum of the per-machine values.
- [`SyncPartial`](../../src/GridSim.Core/Protection/ShortCircuit/Iec60909.cs#L1300) (record struct): One synchronous machine's partial current for a three-phase fault (R095): its partial initial current (pu and kA), its rated current (kA), its near-generator factor mu, its single-fed breaking current mu * Ik''_G (kA), and `VoltageRatio`, the magnitude of the initial voltage difference across its subtransient reactance relative to the equivalent source, `|dU''_G| / (c Un / sqrt 3) = |I_G| X''d / c` (pu), which the meshed-network breaking current weights its decay by. #165 (bug hunt 2026-11-01): that is `|V_G| / c` only when no unit transformer is modelled; with one, the network bus voltage V_G also holds the transformer drop, which the weight used to include (X''d 0.2, XT 0.15, mu 0.7 at the fault bus: deduction 0.300 Ik''_G instead of 0.171 Ik''_G, so Ib was 0.129 Ik''_G too low).
- [`BranchFaultCurrent`](../../src/GridSim.Core/Protection/ShortCircuit/Iec60909.cs#L1385) (record): One branch's through-current for a three-phase fault at the study bus: the from- and to-end current magnitudes (kA and pu). A protective relay on that branch measures its own end's current, so this is the fault current an overcurrent element on the branch sees - the input a coordination study (`Coordination.OvercurrentCoordination`) needs from the network.
- [`ZeroSeqBranchKind`](../../src/GridSim.Core/Protection/ShortCircuit/Iec60909.cs#L1668) (enum): F21: how one branch appears in the zero-sequence network.
- [`ZeroSequenceNetwork`](../../src/GridSim.Core/Protection/ShortCircuit/Iec60909.cs#L1685) (record): F21: the zero-sequence network: the admittance stamps in order, which buses have an earth path, the series adjacency, and each branch's own element (kind and admittance) for its zero-sequence current.
- [`ConverterInfeed`](../../src/GridSim.Core/Protection/ShortCircuit/Iec60909.cs#L1965) (record struct): A converter-interfaced unit in the positive-sequence fault network: its IEC 60909-0:2016 source current `I_skPF = k * I_rG` (pu on the system base), its rating, and the transfer impedance `Z_kj` from its bus to the fault bus.
- [`PositiveNetwork`](../../src/GridSim.Core/Protection/ShortCircuit/Iec60909.cs#L1973) (class): The positive-sequence fault network seen from one fault bus, with synchronous machines as X''d shunts and converter-interfaced units split out as current sources. `UpliftPu` is the IEC 60909-0:2016 converter term `sum_j |Z_kj| * I_skPF,j`: the three-phase current is `(c + UpliftPu) / |Z_kk|` (in pu, source `c*Un/sqrt(3)`).

- [`HostingLocationResult`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Qsts/HostingCapacity.cs#L124) (record): The hosting capacity at one candidate bus.
- [`HostingResult`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Qsts/HostingCapacity.cs#L133) (record): The study result: one row per candidate, in candidate order.
- [`HostingCapacity`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Qsts/HostingCapacity.cs#L148) (class): Hosting capacity: the largest PV (or added load) at each candidate bus before a constraint is broken, by bisection on the size in MW. Each size is judged by the snapshot method (regulated power flows at stated demand and resource levels) or by the QSTS method (the whole time series). A constraint the base case already breaks counts only where the resource makes it worse (strictly larger excess), so an existing problem does not mask the hosting limit and is not blamed on the resource. Search. Size 0 must pass (it is the base, with base violations excluded by construction); MaxMw is tried next: if it passes the capacity is reported as at least MaxMw. Otherwise the bracket [pass, fail] = [0, MaxMw] is halved (mid = lo + (hi - lo) / 2) until hi - lo <= ToleranceMw. Deterministic: the same sizes are evaluated in the same order on every run; for a limit that is monotone in the size the true capacity lies in [HostingMw, FailingMw]. Candidates are independent scenarios and may run in parallel, each with its own engine; results land by index, so the answer does not depend on the thread count.
- [`BaseRun`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Qsts/HostingCapacity.cs#L254) (record): The base runs (size 0): one per snapshot, or the one time series.

### src/GridSim.Core/Qsts/InvariantProblemList.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Qsts`. 59 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Qsts/InvariantProblemList.cs).

- [`InvariantProblemList`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Qsts/InvariantProblemList.cs#L15) (class): Bug #193 (2026-11-01): the list a study's Validate method collects its refusal messages in, formatting every interpolated number with the INVARIANT culture. The messages used to be built with plain string interpolation, which formats doubles in the current culture, so the same refused study said "got 0,5" on a de-DE machine and "got 0.5" elsewhere: the same run wrote different bytes per machine. An interpolated message (`p.Add($"... {x} ...")`) binds to the handler overload below, which formats with `CultureInfo.InvariantCulture`; a plain string literal binds to `Add(string)`. Call sites read exactly as they did with a `List<string>`.
- [`InvariantMessageHandler`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Qsts/InvariantProblemList.cs#L37) (struct): Bug #193: the interpolated-string handler behind `InvariantProblemList.Add(ref InvariantMessageHandler)`: the standard handler, fixed to the invariant culture.

### src/GridSim.Core/Qsts/QstsEngine.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Qsts`. 1388 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Qsts/QstsEngine.cs).

- [`QstsEngine`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Qsts/QstsEngine.cs#L31) (class): Quasi-static time series engine: runs a `QstsStudy` on a case as a sequence of power flows, one per step, warm-started from the previous step, with the controllers acting and their state carried between steps. Reuse. Every solve is a call to the `IPowerFlowSolver` given (the sweep, dense or sparse Newton); QSTS only builds the model each solve sees. Step 0 is never warm-started, so a one-step run with nothing varying is the single power flow of the case, bit for bit. Steady mode solves each step with the existing steady-state loops (`SteadyStateSolver` around `SwitchedShuntPowerFlow`), carrying taps and bank steps forward. Timed mode runs the controllers of this file; the order within a step is (1) advance the timers and storage energy over the elapsed interval, (2) build the step's model (profiles, devices, carried taps and banks, warm start), (3) solve, then repeat: continuous controllers (inverters, storage) to a fixed point, else capacitor banks that are ready, else tap changers that are ready, re-solving after each action, until nothing acts or a cap is reached, (4) record the step and judge it. Re-solves within a step start from the step's starting voltages, as the existing tap loop's passes do. Determinism. A run is strictly sequential, devices act in model order, ordering never depends on a hash, and the only transcendental (the inverter response lag) goes through `DetMath`, as does the LDC phasor. Not thread-safe: one engine per thread (the hosting-capacity study runs one per scenario).
- [`RunState`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Qsts/QstsEngine.cs#L62) (class): Declared class; see the source and member declarations for its role.
- [`StepBase`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Qsts/QstsEngine.cs#L379) (class): Declared class; see the source and member declarations for its role.

- [`ReplayResult`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Replay/ReplayValidator.cs#L24) (record): The outcome of validating an event replay against its recorded headline metrics.

Runs `FrequencyDynamics.Simulate` on an event's recorded pre-event inertia/demand and losses+actions with NO device, then checks the simulated RoCoF/nadir against the `RecordedOutcome`. When a 1-second NESO trace is attached it also computes a per-sample RMSE (aligned on the loss instant; the path is data-gated - dormant until a real trace is dropped in). It cross-checks the implied inertia via `InertiaEstimator` and scores with `FrequencyLimits.Assess`. Only a `ReplayVerdict.Reproduced` baseline should unlock a counterfactual: reproduce reality first.
- [`TraceComparison`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Replay/ReplayValidator.cs#L316) (record struct): Per-sample RMSE between the simulated trajectory and the recorded NESO trace, aligned so the sim's first loss instant lines up with the sample nearest `GridEvent.WhenUtc`. Returns null when no trace is attached (the data-gated path). Reading the trace enforces the horizon guard via `NesoFrequencyCsv`.

### src/GridSim.Core/Scenarios/H0StudyEngine.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Scenarios`. 240 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Scenarios/H0StudyEngine.cs).

- [`H0StudyGeneratorInertia`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Scenarios/H0StudyEngine.cs#L11) (record): One untransformed generator's inertia contribution, so a sidecar can recompute E for any scale.
- [`H0StudyCell`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Scenarios/H0StudyEngine.cs#L22) (record): One evaluated cell of the H=0 sweep: a fixed (sync-inertia scale, GFM fraction, corner) triple and the outcome. The real and virtual inertia are kept in SEPARATE fields - `SystemInertiaGvaS` is REAL (1/2)Jw^2 that enters E; `VirtualInertiaMwS` is the grid-forming fleet's virtual control inertia Ev, which enters ONLY the forming denominator (`EffectiveFormingInertiaMwS`), never the real budget. RoCoF/nadir fields are `NaN` (an explicit "undefined" sentinel) when the cell is `FormingDependent` - a genuine H=0 grid with no grid-forming source forms nothing, so those quantities are not physical numbers to be plotted.
- [`H0StudyResult`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Scenarios/H0StudyEngine.cs#L53) (record): The full H=0 study result: the passed baseline gate, the untransformed inertia table, and every cell. R287 (B4, October 2026): the loss figures. `TotalExogenousLossMw` is |sum of every exogenous loss step| (it was called `LargestLossMw`, which it is not); `RocofSettingLossMw` is |sum of the loss steps in the first `Events.GridEvent.RocofSettingWindowSeconds`|, the dP of every cell's `H0StudyCell.BareInertiaRocofHzPerS`; `LargestSingleLossMw` is the largest single step.
- [`H0StudyEngine`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Scenarios/H0StudyEngine.cs#L94) (class): The fleet-routed twin of `ScenarioEngine` for the H=0 counterfactual. Where the scenario sweep floors a scalar E, this routes every cell through the authored per-asset fleet (`AssetFrequencyDynamics`) over a RECONSTRUCTED grid model, applying two model-level transforms per cell: scale the real synchronous inertia (`GridInertiaTransforms.ScaleSynchronousInertia`) and set the grid-forming fraction of the converter fleet (`GridInertiaTransforms.SetGfmFraction`). Wiring Workstream A's grid-forming FORMATION path is what makes "GFM holds at H=0" a real physical result rather than a flag: the GFM fleet is re-interpreted as a virtual former (Ev/Dv, via `FormingAggregate.FromFleet`) that enters the forming denominator, and is EXCLUDED from the active fleet so its contribution is counted exactly once. The grid-following units stay in the fleet and keep tripping into the Loss-of-Mains cascade. At scale==0 with an adequate GFM fleet the forming denominator is 0(real)+Ev(virtual) > 0, so a bounded RoCoF is FORMED (GFM holds); at scale==0 with an all-GFL fleet nothing forms the frequency and the cell is `H0StudyCell.FormingDependent` with NaN RoCoF (GFL cannot hold) - the real bifurcation. The transforms and this engine are ADDITIVE: `ScenarioEngine`, `FrequencyDynamics` and `AssetFrequencyDynamics` are untouched, so every existing validated path stays byte-identical.

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Scheduling`. 41 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Scheduling/AnalysisJob.cs).

- [`AnalysisJob`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Scheduling/AnalysisJob.cs#L15) (class): One unit of post-solve analysis the cycle scheduler can dispatch onto a worker. A job is a stable description of work (identified by `Id`) executed against whatever `CycleContext.Frame` is current when it runs - so a Low job that is deferred and picked up two cycles later re-screens the same elements against the fresh state, never a stale one. Divisible work (a full N-1 sweep) is expressed as many small jobs with stable ids (`n-1:lp:0`, `n-1:lp:1`, ...); the scheduler's Low-tier rotation then rolls coverage across cycles. There is no per-job internal fan-out: a job runs on a single worker and does any re-solving serially, because the scheduler already owns the cross-job parallelism.

### src/GridSim.Core/Scheduling/CycleScheduler.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Scheduling`. 264 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Scheduling/CycleScheduler.cs).

- [`CycleScheduler`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Scheduling/CycleScheduler.cs#L21) (class): Fans a fixed set of post-solve analysis jobs out across a worker pool once per cycle, against one shared immutable frame. The contract the whole design rests on: High always completes. Every High job runs to completion each cycle, never cancelled at the deadline - so the essential view is always current even when the cycle runs long. Low is best-effort and rotates. Low jobs are admitted only while the core-ms budget lasts, run under the wall-clock deadline, and any not served this cycle keep their place at the front of the rotating pool so a later cycle covers them - no starvation. Not re-entrant. `RunCycle` owns the rotating Low pool and must be called serially (one cycle at a time) - which is exactly how `CycleRunner` drives it. The fan-out within a cycle is parallel; the cycles themselves are sequential.

### src/GridSim.Core/Security/ISecretStore.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Security`. 192 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Security/ISecretStore.cs).

- [`ISecretStore`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Security/ISecretStore.cs#L20) (interface): The seam through which a service resolves a secret it needs (a key-ring certificate password, a feed credential, a message-bus connection string) - NCSC CAF B3 "data security / secrets management". The point is that no service reads a secret straight from plain configuration or a committed file: it asks the secret store, and a deployment chooses the backend. GridSim defines the seam; the deploying party supplies the backend, exactly as with `IAuditSink` and `IIncidentSink`. GridSim ships `EnvironmentSecretStore` (secrets from environment variables, the current source) and `CompositeSecretStore` (try a chain). A deployment that wants secrets out of the environment supplies its own store backed by an OS keychain, Windows DPAPI, or a vault - without pulling a third-party dependency into the estimator core (Core stays on the base class library only, which is itself a supply-chain assurance property). Not a secret: the GridSim licence key is signed, not encrypted (its fields are inspectable by design), so it is not a confidential secret and does not need this store; the key-ring certificate password and any feed credential do.
- [`SecretStoreExtensions`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Security/ISecretStore.cs#L31) (class): Convenience helpers over `ISecretStore`.
- [`NullSecretStore`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Security/ISecretStore.cs#L43) (class): A secret store that holds nothing. The honest default when no store is configured: every lookup misses, so a caller falls back to whatever it did before (for example reading configuration directly).
- [`EnvironmentSecretStore`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Security/ISecretStore.cs#L68) (class): Resolves secrets from environment variables (base-class-library only). A logical name such as `Auth:KeyCertificatePassword` is tried as given and in the ASP.NET double-underscore form (`Auth__KeyCertificatePassword`), so it matches how the host already surfaces configuration secrets. Only the ':' separator is mapped, as ASP.NET does: `Bridge:API_KEY` is read from `Bridge__API_KEY`. The older form with every '_' and '.' doubled (`Bridge__API__KEY`) is still read when it is the only one set; when BOTH are set the lookup throws `InvalidOperationException` naming both variables (GR-719), which stops a web host that reads the secret at start-up. An empty or whitespace value is treated as absent (an unset secret, not an empty secret).
- [`DirectorySecretStore`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Security/ISecretStore.cs#L129) (class): Resolves secrets from files in one directory, one secret per file: the layout of Docker / Compose secrets (`/run/secrets/<name>`), Kubernetes secret volumes and systemd credentials (`$CREDENTIALS_DIRECTORY`). The secret then never appears in configuration or the process environment, where any child process and many diagnostics can read it. A logical name such as `Auth:KeyCertificatePassword` is looked up as the file `Auth__KeyCertificatePassword` (the ASP.NET form) and then as given if that is a valid file name. One trailing newline is removed (secret files are usually written with one); an empty file counts as absent. Fail loud on set-up, never on a miss. The directory must exist when the store is built (a typo in the setting must not silently mean "no secrets"). A name that could leave the directory (a path separator or `..`) is refused. A missing file is a normal miss, as the `ISecretStore` contract requires.
- [`CompositeSecretStore`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Security/ISecretStore.cs#L168) (class): Tries each store in order and returns the first hit. A deployment puts its most trusted backend first (an OS keychain or vault) and `EnvironmentSecretStore` last as the fallback.

- [`RoleGuard`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Security/RoleGuard.cs#L69) (class): The fail-loud role gate for GridSim's service operations (NCSC CAF B2 identity and access control). It mirrors `RestrictionReview.AssertPermitted` in spirit: a typed throw at the service seam, never inside the inner solver loop where it would cost per-iteration overhead and pollute the numerics. Additive to, never a replacement for, the forward-inference guard. The two gates are independent: the guard consults no role and has no bypass, so even an `OperationRole.Administrator` cannot make the engine process data newer than the 169 h horizon. Access control narrows WHO may run the filter; it never widens WHAT the filter may see. Neither gate can weaken the other whichever runs first. Every denial is recorded as a security event when an audit log is supplied, tying B2 to C1.

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Simulation`. 81 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Simulation/GcScope.cs).

- [`GcScope`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Simulation/GcScope.cs#L21) (class): Scoped control over the garbage collector for compute-heavy or real-time sections. The GC can't be turned off outright for a long-running process, but: `LowLatency` switches to `SustainedLowLatency` for the scope - full blocking gen2 collections are deferred, so a replay or live loop runs without GC stutter. Safe to hold for a long time; collections still happen, just not the disruptive ones. `NoGc` uses a true no-GC region for a bounded burst of work: pre-reserve a byte budget and the GC won't run until it's spent (then it resumes). Use only around finite batches - never an open-ended loop. Both return an `IDisposable` that restores the previous mode.
- [`LatencyScope`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Simulation/GcScope.cs#L39) (class): Declared class; see the source and member declarations for its role.

- [`GdaReplayResult`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Simulation/GdaReplayLoop.cs#L23) (record): The full offline state-estimation pass over a historical demand series. `Provenance` is `ProvenanceTag.DerivedFromRecorded` for a plain reconstruction and `ProvenanceTag.Counterfactual` when hypothetical storage was added - a "what if a battery had been there" run on real history is a conclusion, never an input to another replay. GR-854 (November 2026): a passive-plant replay whose modelled plant actually changed a tap ratio or derated a rating in some step is `ProvenanceTag.Interpolated` (recorded inputs augmented by modelled plant behaviour: usable to improve fidelity, never an event source); one whose plant changed nothing stays DerivedFromRecorded, and storage keeps Counterfactual, which wins.
- [`GdaReplayLoop`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Simulation/GdaReplayLoop.cs#L39) (class): The historical grid state estimator. Replays a `GdaTimeSeries` through a validated steady-state power flow: for each historical timestamp it derives the operating case (`GdaTimeStep.ApplyTo` -> demand scaled, slack re-balanced), warm-starts from the previous solve, solves, and records the reconstructed state (voltages, losses, convergence). Because the input series is horizon-checked and the loop calls `ForwardInferenceGuard` again at ingestion, it can only ever reconstruct the PAST - offline state estimation, never nowcasting. An `onSolved` hook lets a caller dump each solve's full math via `SolveExport`. With `passivePlant: true` the model's bound passive plant (delayed OLTC taps, thermal derate; see `Assets.PassivePlantFleet`) runs step to step (R058).

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Simulation`. 61 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Simulation/HybridMultiRateScheduler.cs).

- [`ScheduledUpdate`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Simulation/HybridMultiRateScheduler.cs#L8) (record): One scheduled estimator update at an instant, tagged SCADA (the slow robust WLS) or PMU (the fast linear estimator).
- [`HybridMultiRateScheduler`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Simulation/HybridMultiRateScheduler.cs#L34) (class): EXPERIMENTAL (R095). The hybrid multi-rate scheduler for a SCADA + PMU state estimator. SCADA telemetry arrives slowly (~5 s) and PMU synchrophasors fast (~0.5 s), so the intended estimator runs a robust nonlinear WLS at each SCADA instant and a fast linear PMU estimate at each PMU instant between them (about nine linear updates per SCADA cycle). This interleaves the two rates onto one ordered schedule - SCADA wins a coincident instant. Deterministic (derived from the periods, no wall-clock read). Status: the schedule itself is tested (`HybridMultiRateSchedulerTests`), but NOTHING drives it yet: no engine, CLI verb or front end calls `Schedule` (this summary used to say "which the resident engine drives"; `RealtimeEstimatorEngine` does not use it). It is a SCADA/PMU estimator utility, not part of the frequency / inertia dynamics. To leave experimental it needs: (1) a caller that runs the robust WLS at each SCADA update and `Estimation.LinearPmuStateEstimator` at each PMU update, seeded from the last SCADA state; (2) the one PMU path prerequisite still open (it was listed in a "technical chapter 18.6" that no longer exists, D-DOC-155; the mapper is described in technical ch. 33, C37.118 synchrophasor ingest), the mapper-to-estimator adapter (the C37.118 decoder fixes R046 / R293 / N061 and the angle re-referencing to the estimator's slack R295 are done; D-DOC-219 corrected this list); (3) an end-to-end test of the interleaved run on a replayed stream, including the no-future invariant (no update reads telemetry stamped after its instant); (4) a CLI or resident-engine surface. GR-848: an `end` before `start` and mixed `DateTimeKind` values are refused (they used to give an empty or mis-stamped schedule silently). TEST-ONLY today (GR-848). Kept for its tests and for the estimator above; no production code may call it until that estimator exists. Removal is not proposed.

### src/GridSim.Core/Simulation/InfeedSelection.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Simulation`. 65 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Simulation/InfeedSelection.cs).

- [`InfeedSelection`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Simulation/InfeedSelection.cs#L25) (class): Picks the generator an operator "trip" should remove: the largest unit that is ACTUALLY GENERATING right now. Shared by the WPF map (right-click / T key) and the web map (right-click / T key) so both shells trip the same unit for the same frame. The rule, in plain English: Only live output counts (`Generator.Pg` > 0). Nameplate (`Generator.MBase`) is never used: on gb-full the national slack balancer carries a 266,425 MVA nameplate at 0 MW, and 1,072 voltage-control devices carry 2,880 MVA nameplates at 0 MW, none of which is an infeed that can be lost. Power-flow-only devices (`Generator.PowerFlowOnly`: the slack balancer and voltage-control units) are skipped even when the solve has given them output, because they are not physical plant. Tripping one would inject the solver's balancing residual as a "loss of infeed". Ties are broken by model order (the first unit in `GridModel.Generators` wins), so the choice is deterministic for a given model. When nothing qualifies the result is `null`, and the caller must say so ("no generation to trip") rather than fall back to some other figure.

- [`LiveSim`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Simulation/LiveSim.cs#L44) (class): Drives the GB model through a day: each tick advances a clock, scales demand to the day/night curve, re-dispatches and re-solves to a regulated steady state. Frequency is modelled as a small mean-reverting wander about the model's nominal (50 Hz for a GB case) - the way the real system frequency constantly drifts as supply and demand chase each other. The swing integrator is driven by a random ambient imbalance each tick plus any unit-trip deficit (which secondary restoration decays); the tick-to-tick change in demand does not drive it (re-dispatch meets demand on every tick). N273 (October 2026 review, stream B2; Ruling R1: Mark delegated EE calls 2026-10-04): the swing runs at the model's own nominal frequency (`GridModel.FrequencyHz`), and the bands the shells grade the frequency against are `Bands`, the GB bands about that nominal (`FrequencyBands.ForNominal`). Before, the live loop ran every case at the GB 50 Hz, so the WSCC 9-bus case (60 Hz since D2) was integrated at the wrong speed and shown against 50 Hz bands. Every 50 Hz case runs exactly as before. Lives in Core (uses only Core types) so it can be unit-tested without the WPF app.

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Simulation`. 162 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Simulation/RealtimeEstimatorEngine.cs).

- [`RealtimeEstimatorEngine`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Simulation/RealtimeEstimatorEngine.cs#L24) (class): A resident, guard-safe streaming state estimator. It pulls a measurement window, refuses anything newer than the historical horizon, warm-starts from the previous estimate, runs the validated `WlsStateEstimator`, and emits a frame - continuously, for the lifetime of the process. This is real-time engineering - streaming ingest, a resident loop, warm-started sub-cycle cadence, resilience - on guard-permitted-age or replayed data, exactly as `UnderstandingRestrictions.md` permits. It is a filter, not a predictor: every emitted state is stamped at its window's time (present/past), never a future-dated claim about the real grid. Wall-clock pacing (the sub-cycle clock via `Frequency.ReplayController` / `Frequency.RocofUpsampler`) is a host concern; the engine itself processes each window as it arrives so it stays deterministic and testable. Every window's timestamp passes `ForwardInferenceGuard.RejectFuture` before it is ever estimated - a window newer than the horizon is recorded and skipped, never processed, so the resident service is structurally incapable of nowcasting.
- [`RealtimeEstimatorOptions`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Simulation/RealtimeEstimatorEngine.cs#L124) (record): Knobs for a `RealtimeEstimatorEngine` run.
- [`RealtimeEstimateFrame`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Simulation/RealtimeEstimatorEngine.cs#L153) (record): One emitted real-time estimate, stamped at its window's (present/past) state time.
- [`RealtimeRunSummary`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Simulation/RealtimeEstimatorEngine.cs#L156) (record): What a `RealtimeEstimatorEngine.Run` did over its stream.

### src/GridSim.Core/Storage/AgeingModel.cs

Namespace: `GridSim.Core.Storage`. 149 lines. [Implementation](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Storage/AgeingModel.cs).

- [`AgeingModel`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Storage/AgeingModel.cs#L18) (class): Semi-empirical capacity fade (`AgeingParameters`), advanced step by step alongside the cell: calendar fade `k_cal A(T) f(SoC) sqrt(days)`, integrated through time-varying stress by the equivalent-time method (the fade so far maps back to an equivalent age at the present stress); cycle fade on charge throughput: 20 % over `N80` equivalent full cycles, scaled by temperature (Arrhenius) and C-rate. The total updates `CellModel.CapacityFade`, which shrinks capacity and grows resistance. Depth-of-discharge-aware cycle fade over a whole run is available from a rainflow count (`Rainflow`, `CycleFadeFromRainflow`).
- [`Rainflow`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Storage/AgeingModel.cs#L107) (class): Rainflow cycle counting (ASTM E1049-85, three-point method) of a SoC (or any) history.

- [`CellModel`](https://github.com/MarkS0485/GridSim/blob/b0ff2fc47f46df9cc5724f5b336c858651fa9527/src/GridSim.Core/Storage/CellModel.cs#L15) (class): The equivalent-circuit state of one (representative) cell: state of charge, the two RC polarisation voltages, temperature and accumulated ageing. Current is positive on discharge. V_t = OCV(SoC, T) - I R0(SoC, T) - V1 - V2 V_k' = -V_k / tau_k + I R_k / tau_k (k = 1, 2; exact zero-order hold per step) SoC' = -I_eff / (3600 Q) (I_eff: Peukert on discharge, coulombic efficiency on charge) Resistances scale with temperature (Arrhenius) and with ageing (resistance growth); capacity with fade.
